title: How to Extract Audio From a Video in Canva Easily 2026
transcription: Hi there! Welcome to PMN Online. In this video, we are going to cover how to extract audio from a video in Canva. Have you ever found yourself with a video and all you wanted was just the audio part? Whether it's for creating a podcast, using it as background music, or even for narration purposes, extracting audio can be quite a daunting task. But here at PMN Online, we're going to make this process a breeze using Canva's intuitive platform. By the end of this video, you'll have a clear understanding of how to seamlessly separate the audio from any video, all within Canva's user-friendly interface. So, let's dive into it right away. The first step on our journey is to get over to Canva. So, open up your favorite web browser and head to canva.com. If you already have an account, simply log in. For those of you who are new to Canva, don't worry, signing up is free and takes only a minute or two. Canva isn't just a tool for designing, it's a versatile platform for a variety of creative tasks, including video editing. It's definitely worth setting up an account if you plan on working on creative projects regularly. Once you're logged in, you'll see the Canva dashboard. Look for the create button, which is usually right at the top. Clicking this will open up a wide array of design options. Since we're focusing on video today, make sure to select the video option. This sets up a new video project for you, unlocking all the tools you'll need for both video and audio editing. Now that your blank video project is ready, you'll want to navigate to the elements tab on the left-hand side of the screen. This section is a treasure trove of resources, featuring everything from graphics and stickers to videos and audio clips. Take a moment to explore if you like, but for our purpose today, we're going to focus on selecting a video. You can choose a stock video provided by Canva, or upload your own video to work with. For practice, feel free to use any sample video you can find. After you drop your chosen video onto the timeline, you might also want to experiment with adding a separate audio track. This could be useful if you want to compare the original audio from the video with a different sound or music track. You can find the audio section either in elements or from the left sidebar. Just like you added the video, you can add an audio track underneath it. Canva's platform allows you to layer and arrange these tracks, giving you the freedom to get as creative as you like. Now let's move on to the main event: extracting the audio from your video. Once you've got your video loaded in, look closely at the timeline beneath your video slides. You'll notice a colored line, which represents the audio linked to your video clip. To extract this audio, simply click on that colored line. This action will highlight the audio, making it active. Press the delete key on your keyboard. Just like that, you've separated the audio from the video timeline, leaving you with just the visuals or combining with any other audio track you've added. If you wish to export only the audio, you can mute the video visuals or adjust the export settings to fit your needs. The process is as simple as it sounds, and with Canva's platform, it's much less intimidating than it might seem. Remember, if you make a mistake, you can always use the undo button to reverse any action. It's all part of learning, so don't hesitate to go through the steps until you feel comfortable with them. title: Lenny's Growth Assistant
transcription: This assistant answers questions from 300 podcast episodes. Watch what happens when I ask it something those episodes don't cover. It refuses. That refusal is the hardest thing in this project, and it isn't a prompt instruction, it's enforced in code. Lenny's Podcast is hundreds of interviews with product and growth leaders. The insight you need is in there, but it is scattered. A question like, "How do I know I have product market fit?" gets answered by a dozen guests who disagree with each other. Search gives you fragments. A general chatbot gives you a fluent answer with invented attribution. I wanted both synthesis and sources. Still on the local model, it retrieves from Postgres using hybrid search, vector similarity fused with full-text ranking, and then answers only from what came back. Every claim carries a bracket, and every bracket resolves to a real episode and a named guest. If it can't cite it, it doesn't say it. A cloud model will follow an instruction like "only use these excerpts." A 1-billion-parameter local model won't. Asked that cooking question, it answered from its own memory and attached a citation to an unrelated excerpt so the answer looked sourced. So, scope became code. These rules only ever see the retrieval evidence, never your question, which means they can't quietly turn into a banned topic list. Three cheaper approaches failed first. I even asked the model to judge its own grounding. Two out of six, and in one case, it answered, "Yes, this is answerable," while its own reason said the excerpt didn't discuss the topic. There are four skills, and a three-tier router decides which one runs. Cheap pattern matching goes first. "Build me a dashboard" never needs a model call at all. Only genuinely ambiguous requests reach the LLM classifier, and that classifier also rewrites the search query because a conversational question makes a poor embedding. You can watch it decide in the logs: the skill, the tier, the confidence, and then the retrieval fan-out underneath. The second skill writes "Ship 30 for 30" essays: strong hook, short paragraphs, bolded phrases so it can be skimmed, a clear takeaway at the end, and citations running through it. This one measured at 1,301 words against a 1,250-word target, nine bold phrases, 10 bullets, five sources. The third skill generates artifacts. Asked for a dashboard, and it writes a complete HTML document that renders right here, sandboxed in an iframe. It never leaves the application. On the local model, the layout is deterministic. The design system comes from the app, and things like an empty table or a mismatched column count get repaired in code. So, a small model can produce a thin page, but not a broken one. The local model has real limits, and they are written down, including a claim in my own README that turned out to be wrong once I retested it. FastAPI, React, Postgres with pgvector, Claude, and Ollama behind a single interface. 182 tests. Thank you for watching.

title: Can AI reliably detect empathy? Trustworthy AI for empathy detection in text and video
transcription: Trustworthy AI methods that solves key barrier in empathy detection. One of the key challenge is inconsistent labels when those data has been labeled by human raters. To solve this, I present my work using large language model that shows consistent performance improvement over traditional method. This particular approach has been already published in EACL 2024 conference. Next, I address this inconsistent labels through an uncertainty-aware language modeling. The key benefit of this approach is that we get the uncertainty of the model on top of the prediction. So we know when the AI model is confident on its prediction and when it is not. Just to demonstrate this approach, here is a quick video. So, let's say someone is saying, "A month after Hurricane Matthew, 1,800,000 Haitians urgently need food." And in response, if someone else says, "My heart just breaks for the people who are suffering." Now, let's see what my model says, the amount of empathy here, and what is its confidence. So, as we can see here, it shows that it, it is around 80, and this is its confidence interval. Now, for the same interactions, same stimuli, that "A month after Hurricane Matthew," if someone says, "I see, but this doesn't sound too worrisome to me." Let's see what is the prediction from my model. And... and as we can see here, the prediction is roughly around 30 or so. So, that is the demo of my model, and everyone can try this through this link. Next, I addressed the third key barrier, which is addressing privacy when detecting empathy from video. My method does not require the raw video footage, but it works with summary statistics features from the video, so the end result is privacy-aware. Overall, as Karl Pearson said, "that which is measured improves." So, if we can measure empathy, we can find ways to improve it. And so our social interaction, for example, whether it is a human-robot interaction, or patient-doctor interaction, or spousal relationships, we can improve empathy among different scenarios, including imp- increasing empathy of people with low empathetic skills. Thank you.

title: How To Use Claude For Research Writing - Easy Guide (2026)
transcription: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to use Claude for research writing. We'll start by asking for an outline. Open a new chat, state your research topic clearly, and share your goal, audience, and any constraints like word count or required sections. Then ask Claude to propose a detailed outline with logical headings and subheadings. If you already have a structure in mind, mention it so Claude can adapt. Don't hesitate to request alternatives or a more detailed version if the first pass feels too broad. Next, ask for key points and summaries for each major section. You can say you want the core arguments, crucial concepts, and the types of evidence to include. If you have readings or notes, paste excerpts and ask for concise, accurate summaries with the main takeaways. This creates a solid content map before any drafting begins and helps prevent gaps or repetition later. With the scaffolding ready, have Claude generate the introduction, body, and conclusion. For the introduction, request a clear context, a precise thesis statement, and a brief roadmap of what follows. For the body, ask for well-structured paragraphs that each develop a single idea supported by reasoning or data, and include transitions that guide the reader. For the conclusion, ask for a synthesis that reinforces the thesis and highlights implications without introducing new claims. Specify tone, reading level, and any terminology you want emphasized. Now, paste your own text and ask Claude to improve the writing. Be explicit about your goals, improve clarity, tighten sentences, enhance coherence, and preserve your original meaning. And if you want, ask for side-by-side revisions or brief explanations of major edits so you learn from the changes. You can repeat this as you refine each section. When you're ready for citations, ask Claude to add them in the required style, such as APA or MLA. Provide the actual sources or references you intend to use and request accurate in-text citations and a properly formatted reference list. Remind Claude to cite only the materials you supply, and always verify final citations against your institution's style guide. Then ask Claude to proofread. Request a careful pass for grammar, punctuation, consistency in tense and voice, and alignment with your style requirements. Ask it to flag awkward phrasing and suggest smoother transitions and to call out any redundancy or unclear logic. Finally, combine and finalize. Merge the polished sections, then ask Claude to smooth transitions, ensure a unified voice, check the structure against the outline, and tighten the title and headings. Once everything reads cleanly and aligns with your goals, you're ready to export and submit with confidence.

title: State of the Field report
transcription: In a collective quest to transform agri-food systems equitably and sustainably, we face a daunting challenge: analyzing the contributions of millions of scientists to inform future decisions. How can we keep up with the massive research output? With millions of publications across over 35,000 journals and technical reports, the task seems overwhelming. Finding ways to map and synthesize research into actionable evidence is a significant undertaking. The Juno Evidence Alliance's groundbreaking report introduces a new approach to review and evaluate scientific publications within agri-food systems. Using AI methods, the report evaluates 6.3 million scientific titles, abstracts, and metadata from 2010 to 2023. By aligning research with policy objectives, we guide inclusive and equitable decisions across food systems, and find solutions from scientists in hunger and climate crisis-affected countries. Together, we can use science to find solutions to transform agri-food systems. Join us in this important journey.

title: 30th Anniversary of Ecohydrology at UNESCO and 20 years of UNESCO Ecohydrology Demonstration Sites
transcription: This year marks a significant moment for the UNESCO IHP as we celebrate the 30th birthday of ecohydrology at UNESCO and 20 years of UNESCO ecohydrology demonstration sites. Today, we reflect back from foundations of the science in Poland to the current global influence of ecohydrology. Ecohydrology rose to answer the fundamental question of how to deal with ecosystem problems in the aquatic environment. As Professor Zalewski, director of the European Regional Centre for Ecohydrology, realized that environmental protection alone is not enough. Hence, by studying the mechanisms that regulate the environmental processes through the interactions between the biota and the water system, ecohydrology was born. With water as a driver for all life, the protection and resilience against challenges in the current climatic context, such as pollution, scarcity, management, and drought, is essential. Thus, the second part of ecohydrology is finding and implementing solutions. From the design of experiments in laboratories to the implementation of real systems, research in ecohydrology looks for nature-based solutions to tackle different problems worldwide. To highlight successful implementations of NBS based on ecohydrological values at the water basin scale, UNESCO has supported the formation of 66 demonstration sites. These span 36 countries across all six continents and are excellent case studies for the ecohydrological approach to water management. This network has developed thanks to the UNESCO demonstration site program that brings together researchers, local governments, and communities from all across the world. Examples include the ecological engineering of Las Dunas in the Cahuayumac microbasin in Peru, the natural migration and remediation of watersheds and lagoon ecosystem in Ghar El Melh, Tunisia, wastewater treatment wetland system in Asmelabad, Pakistan, and the Birmingham urban ecohydrological urban observatory in the Upper Tame catchment in the United Kingdom. Another key development is the international Ecohydrology & Hydrobiology Journal aimed at increasing understanding of water-biota interplay and how this knowledge can be used for decision-making tools. The scope aims to address the priorities of the international initiatives, such as the Millennium Development Goals and the UNESCO IHP. With 26 volumes, the journal incorporates climate change, water quality, pollution, and sustainability, and the latest developments of ecohydrological understanding. The importance of ecohydrology will continue to grow with the need to reduce consumption and alleviate pressure on the environment as climate change will bring about new water challenges. With water being a key element of all aspects of life, these 30 years mark only the beginning. To continue building a resilient future, we look to the youth of today. The Ecohydrology Youth Network brings together young people and aims to support the engagement and the development of ideas within the ecohydrology field. With over 500 members, the network connects young scientists, promotes ecohydrological solutions, and exchanges ideas. The future of ecohydrology is looking bluer and greener. And on that note, happy 30th anniversary of ecohydrology and 20 years of ecohydrology demonstration sites.

title: Antibiotics Exposure Within 6 Months is not Associated with Increased Prevalence of SIBO
transcription: Hi, my name is Dr. Gillian Barlow, and I'm here to talk about my poster about antibiotic resistance and the small bowel. Prolonged or repeated use of antibiotics, particularly in early childhood, can negatively impact the gut microbiome and lead to antibiotic resistance. In addition, antibiotic use has been suggested to contribute to the development of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, or SIBO. However, most of these studies were performed using stool samples. So in this study, we explored the impact of antibiotic use in the small bowel, which is central to nutrient absorption, immune function, and hormone regulation. To do this, we collected duodenal aspirates from subjects undergoing upper endoscopy via our REIMAGINE study and isolated the microbial DNAs and sequenced them. We also plated some of each sample to determine which ones had SIBO, and compared medical histories to see which subjects had used antibiotics in the last six months. In total, 1,052 subjects were analyzed, of whom 214 had taken antibiotics in the last six months. Importantly, we found there was no significant difference in the prevalence of SIBO in subjects who had or had not taken antibiotics. In addition, there were also no differences in duodenal microbiome diversity or richness between the two groups. However, we did find significant differences in antibiotic resistance profiles. Comparing antibiotic resistance ontology, or ARO phenotypes, we found that two were more common in subjects who had taken antibiotics in the last six months. The first was proteins modulating permeability to antibiotics, which confers resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics, that would include penicillins, cephalosporins, and carbapenems. And the second was genes altering cell wall change, which confers resistance to a broad range of antibiotics. Lastly, as far more of the subjects in our antibiotics group were female, we broke the results down by sex. However, we found that there were no differences in the ARO profiles in male versus female subjects. So, what are our take-home messages? Taking antibiotics in the last six months is not associated with an increased prevalence of SIBO, and does not appear to affect microbiome richness or diversity in the small bowel. However, subjects who had taken antibiotics in the last six months did have increased prevalence of antibiotic resistance phenotypes that confer resistance to a broad range of antibiotics, and specifically to beta-lactam antibiotics. These differences were not significantly different between male and female subjects. Thank you for listening to my poster. Please check out all of the other research that the Mast Group is presenting at DDW 2023.

title: Edinburgh Neuroscience  - about us
transcription: Edinburgh Neuroscience is a network connecting more than 600 brain and mind researchers at the University of Edinburgh. We're one of the largest groupings of neuroscientists in Europe, and home to a broad church of scientists looking at every aspect of the brain and how it develops and functions from the beginning to the very end of life. We are interested in what makes us tick, what keeps us on a healthy trajectory, and what makes things fall apart. What are the mechanisms underlying neurological disorders, and how can we repair, reverse or halt the damage caused by them? These are the questions we want to answer. Our researchers are spread across four campuses and many subdisciplines embedded in the different colleges of the university, and so we, Edinburgh Neuroscience, strive to integrate this community to foster collaboration and an open progressive research culture. We facilitate sharing of perspectives and approaches to ensure we are considering all aspects of a brain disorder right through from the molecular level to the real-life experiences of those impacted. To do this, we organise events throughout the year that showcase research from PhD students who are just beginning their research careers through to world leading experts designing life-changing therapies and interventions. We promote equitable professional development and work practices and celebrate our successes. We provide a forum for discussion so that our community can debate and explore what matters to them. This can be anything from research policy, open science, equality and diversity, funding, to facilities and public engagement, and how these affect us. We're always open to ideas and questions from inside or outside of our network, so if you'd like to keep in touch, please drop us a line via our email address or connect with us on social media.

title: "Personalized for Patients, Precise for Clinicians" — Yuan Lew on CGP | Biomarkers Conference 2026
transcription: Hello, my name is Yuan, and I have stage 4 EGFR-positive cancer of lung origin. I would like to invite you to join us for the virtual Fourth Annual Pan-Tumor Biomarkers Conference on June 18th to 19th, 2026. Let's talk about comprehensive genomic profiling, or CGP, and why this is so important and central to the discussions we'll be having. CGP is a laboratory technique that uses a small amount of biological sample to look at hundreds of genomic changes inside cancer cells. These changes can provide information on how best to treat your cancer by targeting areas where the cancer is vulnerable. CGP is known to be especially important for patients with advanced cancers or rare types of cancer. CGP informs our medical team on how to optimize our treatment approaches for best survival, and more importantly, better quality of life. Couple this with treatment plans of our own personal priorities, cancer care is becoming personal. This is important to us as we move towards how to empower patients more in making decisions that affect our health. Personalized for patients, precise for clinicians.

title: Proteomics of the Small Bowel Lumen Shows Anti-Microbial Immune Activation in Response to SIBO
transcription: Hello, I'm Nathan Hendricks. I'm a specialist at MAST. I'm here to talk about my poster, which is looking at the proteomics of SIBO. So, I'm looking at SIBO, which is Small Intestinal Bacterial Overgrowth. It's a GI disorder which occurs when you have certain select species that are overabundant. Uh people have looked at the sequencing, uh genomics of SIBO, um but nobody's really explored the proteomics of SIBO. So we're going to look at the protein makeup of people with or without SIBO, and see what sort of diagnostic or prognostic markers there are there. So, we're looking at small bowel lumen aspirates from the REIMAGINE study. Uh so we took 20 microliters of these aspirates, and it's important to note that this is the centrifuged aspirate, it's not the tissue. And we took 20 microliters of that and we processed it uh by trypsin digestion to prepare it for proteomics analysis. We took these processed samples and we analyzed them um with data-independent acquisition on the ZenoTOF 7600. So, of the proteins we see, we see many IgGs, uh which is something we might expect to see in SIBO, and we also see Defensin A1 and Defensin A3 are one of the most significantly upregulated proteins in SIBO. And this all matches with what you would expect to see in a immune response to infection. So, if we look at the particular pathways that are in this dataset, we have many proteins that are part of the neutrophil degranulation pathway. And this highlights that there is a specific neutrophil response occurring to SIBO in the lumen. So, to summarize some of the important results we see, uh we see immunoglobulins and defensins in our protein dataset, which is something that we would expect to see in response to bacterial overgrowth. Uh we also see uh a lot of activation of the neutrophil uh degranulation pathway and proteins related to neutrophils, and this all suggests that we are seeing neutrophil uh activation in response to SIBO. So, thank you for listening to this summary, and thank you for checking out my poster. Uh I hope you check out all the other posters and presentations that we have from MAST at the 2022 DDW.

title: The Absolute Quantification of Gram-Negative Bacteria in Older Subjects with SIBO and GI Symptoms
transcription: Hi. My name is Ava from the MAST program. And in this study, we're looking at how aging impacts the small intestinal microbiome and its relationship to gastrointestinal symptoms. We know that small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, or SIBO, becomes more common as people get older. But what we're still unclear about is why. Whether it's driven by an increase in total bacterial load or shifts in the microbial composition, or even both. So our aim in this study is to determine if there's a relationship between aging, absolute small bowel microbial loads, microbial community structure, and gastrointestinal symptom severity. To address this, we analyzed duodenal aspirate samples from subjects in the REIMAGINE study. These were patients undergoing upper endoscopy without colon prep. We grouped subjects by age and used metagenomic sequencing to quantify absolute microbial abundance, so not just relative composition, but actual bacterial load. What we found is total bacterial load increases significantly with age, and the prevalence of SIBO rises as well. At the same time, microbial diversity declines in older age groups. When we looked more closely at microbial composition, we found that key Gram-negative bacteria, particularly Escherichia coli and Klebsiella species, increase progressively with age in patients with SIBO. These changes were consistent and significant across all age groups. Then we looked at how this relates to symptoms. In subjects over the age of 50, those with SIBO reported significantly greater symptom severity, including diarrhea, bloating, and abdominal pain. Importantly, these symptoms were strongly associated with the abundance of specific bacterial groups, such as Escherichia and Fusobacterium, rather than bacterial load alone. And also, in older subjects without SIBO, increased bacterial load did not correlate with symptom severity. So simply having more bacteria isn't enough to explain symptoms. It really depends on the microbial composition. So overall, our findings suggest that aging is associated with increased bacterial load and reduced diversity, but symptom severity in older adults is more closely linked to specific microbial signatures rather than total load alone. This highlights the importance of using absolute microbial quantification to better understand, diagnose, and potentially treat SIBO, especially in aging populations. Thank you so much for taking the time to listen to my poster, and be sure to check out the rest of our posters from the MAST program here at DDW. Take care.

title: KSQA: Dr. Julie Magarian Blander (Inflammation Resolution)
transcription: Hi! I'm Julie Magarian Blander, one of the scientific organizers for the upcoming Keystone Symposium on Inflammation Resolution: Emerging Concepts, Mechanisms, and Disease Insights. Inflammation is our body's essential defense against infection and injury. But when it doesn't resolve properly, it drives so many chronic diseases like autoimmune disorders, cardiovascular problems, neurodegeneration, cancer, and even the processes behind aging. Now, in this meeting, we'll dive into the latest advances in how inflammation actually winds down. Things like signals from dying cells and damaged tissues, the crucial roles that myeloid cells and T cells play in tissue repair and immunosuppression, neural controls of the process, and ways in which aging disrupts these mechanisms. Ultimately, it's about translating these discoveries into therapies that can finally address unresolved inflammation at its core. Earlier ones like the 2022 event paired with tissue fibrosis, or the 2018 focus on resolution mediators, were great at laying foundations. But this time, we're pushing boundaries with a parallel conference on Tumor Microenvironment: Identifying Drivers of Progression and Resistance. There will be shared keynotes, joint talks, meals, and poster sessions. And through these, we will explore how failed inflammation resolution in tumors essentially hijacks normal repair pathways to fuel cancer growth. Chronic inflammation doesn't operate in isolation. In cancer, unresolved inflammation interferes with the repair processes, and drives tumor progression and resistance to treatment. By pairing these two conferences, we're reflecting the real biology. Inflammation and the tumor microenvironment are intertwined. If you're passionate about bridging basic science with disease insights, this is where you will see how unresolved inflammation links to tumor progression and beyond, inspiring the next wave of research that could change patient lives. Visit keystonesymposia.org for details on abstracts, registration, and award. We look forward to seeing you in Whistler.

title: ASX drops as renewed US-Iran attacks drive oil price higher | Finance Report | ABC NEWS
transcription: The mood on the Australian share market has turned gloomy again, with the ASX down 0.8% due to falls in almost every single sector. Though, it was particularly bad for mining. One reason why is because oil prices have shot up above 90 US dollars a barrel again, as the US and Iran were only able to manage a few days without resorting to violence. So, if you've been asleep for the past week or so, you really haven't missed all that much, apart from oil prices surging to really scary levels, then plunging on hopes of peace, and then rising again as those hopes were very quickly dashed. And there was yet another sell-off across tech and AI stocks like Meta, or Facebook, after revealing its cash flow has fallen off a cliff from 8 and a half billion to 784 million US dollars in just a year. So, there are major concerns it's been spending way too much money on AI infrastructure which may not pay off. Though, shares of Microsoft soared in after-hours trade, after its Azure cloud computing division saw revenue growth of 43%, which is quite the increase. And in Seoul, Samsung shares were all over the place, despite revealing a massive 20-fold increase in quarterly profit, due to insatiable demand for its AI chips. So, the net result, big falls across the South Korean market and on Wall Street. The US market, in particular, was hit hard by the Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates on hold. As ridiculous as that may sound, it's because markets have decided the new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh may have a credibility problem, as so far, he's been all talk, but no action, when it comes to how hard he claims he'll be fighting inflation in the US. And finally, the Aussie dollar is a little bit weaker at 69 and a half US cents. And that's finance.

title: AI Spending In Focus for Meta, Microsoft Earnings
transcription: Gil Luria of DA Davidson staying bullish on Microsoft going into the results, and writing Microsoft will be the key earnings report of the entire season. Capex guidance for fiscal '27 will determine the direction of the market. Gil joins us now for more. Gil, key question then: why is this the key one? Why this one name? Why is it so important? For a couple of reasons. One, this is Microsoft's fiscal year-end, so they're going to guide for 12 months, for a full year, and they'll give us an hard number. So we'll be able to pin down how fast that capex growth is, at this point. Is it growing even faster than Azure? Or is it growing slower than Azure? Will be the key question. And the other reason is Microsoft has been the responsible adult in the room around capex for the last couple of years. It It was about a year and a half ago that when we were worried about the direction of AI, that they actually did step back capex a little bit. So that's why investors are looking to them to see if if they're going to blink. They're more likely than Google, Amazon, Meta, etc., to blink. And that's why investors are are trepidatiously walking into this earning is if Microsoft says they're reining in capex, that's going to be tough for the AI trade. We don't think they're going to say that. Do you think that increasingly, as capex has to go up regardless of some of the pushback that you're seeing in capital markets, do you think that the better investment thesis is shifting to the bond space, to the credit space, and away from, say, buying the equity? Well, to the extent that the bonds for for these mighty companies, Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, are starting to trade at a discount, that does seem like a a relatively safe bet here because these companies are incredibly creditworthy, and they all have the ability to stop capex on a dime. They could go to a fraction of their current run rate and still grow their business. They just believe, and they're trying to show us evidence, that this investment is showing a return. But if, at some point, they decided that it is not, they'll scale back capex, and their cash flows will skyrocket. That's why these companies are more creditworthy than almost every country in the world. It's because their flow of cash is very reliable. It's It's almost like a global tax that these big companies have. Therefore, any discount to their debt is probably attractive. Does it help them that you're seeing dislocation in some of the semiconductor names and pushback, potential competitive pressures, coming from elsewhere when it comes to manufacturing some of the components? Oh, it gives them a little bit more operating leverage vis-a-vis the chip companies. But realistically speaking, none of these companies is going to buy chips from China. And if that's the concern about competition, that's not that much of a a leverage point against Nvidia, Broadcom, Micron, etc. Those companies will continue to get this 75% gross margins as long as we continue to ramp the data center build-out. But they'll they'll certainly try.

title: Did Jim Carrey Send Doppelgänger to Accept Award? Truth REVEALED
transcription: Merci à ma merveilleuse famille. à ma fille Jane. et à mon petit-fils Jackson. Je vous aime. Je vous aime maintenant et pour toujours. Jim Carrey, is that you? Because the internet's convinced it's a doppelganger or even a clone. There's magic in the universe. Yeah, fans questioning if Jim's newish look is some sort of magic trick after the 64-year-old debuted longer locks, seemingly lighter eyes, and a fuller face at the César Awards in Paris where he was given a top honor. Merci à ma sublime compagnie. Mina. Je t'aime Mina. That's Jim on stage thanking his daughter, grandson, and girlfriend, but internet sleuths just aren't having it. His updated appearance sparking a wild rumor that it was actually someone else who was there in Jim's place. Yeah, get ready. Let's do this. Then Alexis Stone, a transformative makeup artist known for impersonating celebs in public, entered the chat, posting this likely AI image of a face mask and teeth, signaling to his 1.4 million Instagram followers it was him impersonating Jim. But not so fast. Boom! Somebody stop me! A rep for Jim confirms to ET it was indeed just Jim who attended the award ceremony. And if you need more proof, a representative from the César Awards tells us Jim was there with his loved ones, longtime publicist, and 12 close members of his inner circle. And calls all the fuss online a non-issue. I have to pinch myself, honestly. I mean, I'm the, the proof that, you know, manifestation, you know, is, is real. There, you know, I, I sat up on Mulholland Drive looking out at Lankershim Boulevard, and, uh, and dreaming up my life as it was going to be, and I was going to be one of the biggest actors in the world, and I was going to do movies that reintroduced themselves to several generations of people. The people that grew up with the game are 40 and 50, and they now, and they also grew up with me, and, uh, now they're bringing their kids to see me, and I got that goodwill for another 20 years now, and, and it's just like winning the lottery. It's wonderful.

The article suggesting the plan could require the US and Israel to petition Iran's neighbors to restrict or close border crossings, which would limit exports and imports to the country. Earlier today, the media pressed President Trump as to how Iran still has enough missiles and military capability to continue to attack US bases and ships in the region and how he might respond. transcription: రక్తసిక్త పిశాచ కొరియన్ కనకరాజు దెయ్యం ఆవాహయామి... కనకరాజు ఆవాహయామి. నాయనా... నువ్వు చెప్పినట్లే వచ్చి కూర్చున్నాను నాయనా... మంత్రం చెప్పు. ఆ.... ఓం.... వీడికి ఇప్పుడే పోవాలి... మా తోపు మా బలవంతుడు.. అనంతపురం కే ఒక రారాజు.. మన కనకరాజు. పెనుగొండలో మీ అంతటి పెనువాంపం ఎప్పుడూ చూడలేదు మేడం. bloody mass people, బాబోయ్, అన్యం. అవునురా.. నాకు ఈ కంపెనీలో పనిచేస్తుంది కదా. ఆ కొరియా వాళ్ళతో మాట్లాడి మాట్లాడి నేర్చుకుని ఉంటాదిలే... సుగం తో... యా బాస్ పాటరా ఇది. ఆ భాష ఏంది డాక్టర్? నాశం.. ఏముందిలే కనక, సచ్చెపోద్దొచ్చిందని మలయాళం మాట్లాడతాన్నావా. అట్లెక్కడున్నావ్ నాయనా? ఏదో ఒకటి చెయ్యి. ఏందిరా చేసేది? నేను చెప్పేది దానికి అర్ధం అయితా లేదు, అది చెప్పేది నాకు అర్ధం అయితా లేదు. కమ్యూనికేషన్ గ్యాప్ రా అబ్బాయ్. ఈ అవతారం ఏందిరా? ఈ పచ్చ బొట్టు ఏంది? నా మీసం ఏది? జాతరలో కోడిపుంజుని తయారుచేసినట్టు తయారుచేసినారు. ఎదురుకి తోలబోతున్నావ్... లే లేదు కిషోర్ అన్న... ఏలవేందిరా. భద్రంగా దాచిపెట్టినాను కనక. బుధవారం బుధవారం గోర్లు కూడా కత్తిరిస్తున్నాను. ఆ కాయ చెప్పమ్మ... మీ సన్నా, మనోడు అనుకున్నాను సార్. ఎవడవు నువ్వు? ఇంటికి వెళ్ళాలని ఉంది అన్న. ఎవడ్రా వీడు బిగ్ బాస్ కంటెస్టెంట్ లా ఇట్లా అడుక్కుంటాడు? సుగం జ్యోత్స్నా... మీకు దండం పెట్టేస్తా స్వామి, కనీసం సబ్ టైటిల్స్ అయినా వేయండిరా రేయ్. అహోబిలం లక్ష్మీనరసింహ స్వామి సాక్షిగా చెప్తున్నా.. వాడు నరకానికి పోకుండానే నరకం ఎట్లుంటాదో చూపిస్తానా కొడుక్కి. I'll kill you. అయితే వాడికి కూడా తెలియాలి.. నేను ఎలాంటి వాడినో అని. ఒకే శరీరంలో ఇద్దరు కోపిష్టులు ఉంటే... ఇంకెన్ని కష్టాలు వస్తాయో ఏంటో... కొరియా! కొరియా! కొంపతీసి ఈయన గారు మరిపోయారా? చైనా! చైనా! కొరియనే కన్ఫామ్.

title: PRESSURE - Official Trailer [HD] - Only In Theaters May 29
transcription: The final decision on the timing of D-day will be mine and mine alone. Call General Eisenhower. Tiger was a training op, dress rehearsal for D-day. They walked right into it. One mistake, just that one mistake. Ike, you have to stop doing this to yourself. What's done is done. Group Captain Dr. James Stagg, here at the express request of General Eisenhower. Do we have a date yet for the invasion, sir? D-day is in 61 hours from now. This is the largest seaborne invasion in history. Fate of the war, thousands of lives hinge on this. I need a forecast. Churchill tells me you're the best meteorologist in the country. Get me the latest readings from every single base within 2000 miles of Normandy. The invasion is confirmed for Monday, Monday, Monday. Oh, they won't like this. We are faced with a succession of two aggressive storms. Are you absolutely certain? D-day will be calm and sunny. I couldn't disagree with that more. If D-day is canceled, we will lose this war. The final decision on the timing of D-day will be mine and mine alone. If you invade tomorrow, they're going to be washed away. 300,000 men with families that they may never see again. Why should I trust you? We must face the facts! The facts, however frightening they may be! If we delay, the enemy will be ready and waiting. They'll slaughter every single last one of us. The storms that I'm talking about are real, and the wrath of nature is real.

title: Examining the legal process behind Fauci diaries release
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription:
I want to bring in CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson with more on this. First of all, I feel like we're going way back in time. It's amazing how Senator Rand Paul got the legal authority to obtain Dr. Fauci's personal journal. Your thoughts on that?

So, obviously, this does feel like it's from the wayback machine. We know that Senator Rand Paul is looking into the origins of the coronavirus as we just heard. We know that Senator Rand Paul does have subpoena authority when it comes to subpoenaing people or information if there is a legitimate legislative purpose for that subpoena. In addition, there's reporting that these diaries or parts of them were actually found on government databases, and so, that it was federal government agencies, specifically HHS, that provided this information to Senator Rand Paul. And so, I think that's how you see that we've come to having this discussion now and how Anthony Fauci's private diaries moved from obviously just being his to now being in the public square.

Sure. Can anyone's personal diary or journal be subpoenaed, and is there anything that is just off-limits?

So, absolutely, there are tons of reasons why, you know, rest assured, everybody at home, it is not the case that the Senate can wake up one morning and say, "You know who I'm really curious about?" So, as we mentioned before, when it comes to congressional subpoenas, both the House of Representatives and the Senate, you need to have a legitimate legislative purpose for that subpoena. You need to have a good reason behind saying, "We want information or testimony from you." In addition, when it comes to private diaries, that might be different from what we're talking about here where reporting indicates that at least many of these entries were on government servers. So, if you want to keep your information private, you know, don't log it on your workplace computer or your workplace internet systems. And then finally, of course, there are privileges that people can assert and there are general privacy concerns. So, it is not just the case that you write something down, and it could at some point be subject to a conversation that you and I have.

All right, and just lastly, are we confusing diaries with just medical information that he was noting if it wasn't in his own personal diary at home type of thing?

So, that's a great question, and I think my answer would be I don't think there's a legal definition of privacy. So, what there is a difference of course, excuse me, of diary. What there is, of course, a difference between is something that maybe I write at home about my personal impressions of people at work versus what I write during the course of my job. Those two things obviously are different. In what we're talking about with respect to the information that's been released with Anthony Fauci's journals or diaries, I think is a mix between personal and professional. We see both of those.

Yeah, fascinating. All right, Jessica Levinson, appreciate the information. Thank you.

title: diary cinematic video | how journaling can change your life
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Today at 9:15 a.m. I wrote something in my diary that I have never admitted to anyone, not even my bird, not even to myself. Dear diary, here are the things I never say out loud. I miss people, I know I shouldn't. I tell everyone I'm okay, but some nights, I'm not. Day by day, nothing feels different for me, but when I look back, everything has changed. I have mastered the art of saying I'm fine because explaining the truth felt heavier than hiding it. When the room gets quiet, my thoughts don't. Old conversations replay like music in my head. Memories, they hit harder. It gets loud inside my head with words I wish I had said. And some endings, well, they don't come with explanations. They say, your problems begin to lose their weight, the moment you write them down. So, I did. I wrote the messy parts, the overthinking, how exactly I felt at those particular moments, things that keep me awake. Well, the pain didn't disappear, of course, but it didn't feel so heavy anymore. And, I realized something. Honesty with yourself changes everything because in the end, you are the creator of your life. So tell me, if no one was watching, how would you live tomorrow?

title: Journal with Me: Master Your Mindset (in 2026)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: There is this poem that says our soul is the sail of our life and how our soul is set determines how our life goes. Have you believed the lie that the winds matter more than your sail? The winds around us are ferocious forces, that is for sure. But they are not what guides us. Darling, the winds change with seasons, with tempests, and those who forget their sail are surely at the wind's mercy, tossed and directionless. Raise your sail, dear one. With it, you will use the winds to set the direction, the course of your life. Happiness, bliss, shalom, peace exists in one place—inside of you—and in one time—right now. This ancient wisdom is your sail. You are the gatekeeper, the manager of your sacred space. Therefore, commune daily with her. Ask, "How is she?" For as she goes, so does the rest of life. And when we get tempted to wrench that soul into conforming, into behaving, into lockstep with every other soul, we must remember that she is a wild spirit, that her dreams are not meant for others' validation, that she sways the oaks and sends cracks through Earth's tectonic plates when she realizes the power and beauty of her sail. These two things can be true at the same time: treacherous winds are blowing and your soul is set on peace, hope, love, and joy.

गंदा होता है, या मेरे जैसे लोग ज्यादा पैसा नहीं कमाते, तो चाहे आप दिन में कितनी भी मेहनत कर लो, रात को वही बिलीफ सिस्टम एक्टिव हो जाता है। इसलिए आज की रात मोटिवेशन की नहीं है, आज की रात रीसेट की है। मैं चाहता हूं कि आप इस वीडियो को सोते वक्त सुनो। कोई एफर्ट नहीं, कोई विजुअलाइजेशन प्रेशर नहीं, बस सुनते रहो। अब अपनी आंखें बंद करो, एक गहरी सांस लो और धीरे-धीरे छोड़ दो। इमेजिन करो जैसे आप पूरे यूनिवर्स के बीच में हो, तारों के नीचे, बिल्कुल सेफ। और मैं धीरे-धीरे आपके सबकॉन्शियस से बात करूंगा। आज रात हम पुरानी मनी स्टोरी को रिलीज कर रहे हैं। अपने मन में बोलो, बिना आवाज के भी चलेगा। जो भी बिलीव्स मैंने पैसा लेकर कैरी किए, जो डर, गिल्ट या गिल्ट के साथ आए, मैं उन्हें आज... रिलीज करता हूं। फील करो जैसे कोई हैवी वेट चेस्ट से निकल रहा हो। अब मैं आपके सबकॉन्शियस को एक नई आइडेंटिटी दे रहा हूं। रिपीट मत करो, बस सुनो। पैसा मेरे लिए सेफ है, पैसा मेरे लिए नेचुरल है, मैं पैसा संभाल सकता हूं, मैं पैसा ग्रो कर सकता हूं, मैं पैसा डिज़र्व करता हूं। अगर बीच-बीच में नींद आए, परफेक्ट, क्योंकि सबकॉन्शियस को वही चाहिए। आज रात आप एफर्ट से नहीं, वर्दिनेस से अट्रैक्ट कर रहे हो। इमेजिन करो कि यूनिवर्स आपको पुश नहीं कर रहा बल्कि सपोर्ट कर रहा है। जैसे अपॉर्चुनिटीज नेचुरली आ रही हैं, लोग मदद कर रहे हैं, आइडियाज फ्लो हो रहे हैं, आपको प्रूव नहीं करना पड़ रहा, बस रिसीव करना पड़ रहा है। और अब तीन शब्द मैं आपके सबकॉन्शियस में प्लांट कर रहा हूं- मैं रेडी हूं। रेडी फॉर मनी, रेडी फॉर पीस, रेडी फॉर ग्रोथ। कल सुबह जब आप उठोगे, कुछ ड्रामेटिक नहीं होगा, लेकिन एक चीज बदलेगी, आपका अंदर का रिलेशनशिप पैसों के साथ और वही छोटा सा शिफ्ट 2026 को अलग बना देगा। याद रखना, डिसिप्लिन आपको एक्शन देता है, लेकिन आइडेंटिटी आपको रिजल्ट देती है। और आज रात आपने अपनी आइडेंटिटी अपग्रेड की है। बस इस ऑडियो को सुनते हुए सो जाओ, यूनिवर्स का काम शुरू हो चुका है। अगर यह वीडियो आपके दिल को थोड़ा सा भी शांत करे, या आपको लगे कि यह सिर्फ सुनना नहीं बल्कि महसूस करना था, तो प्लीज इस वीडियो को लाइक करो, चैनल को सब्सक्राइब करो और इसे उन लोगों के साथ शेयर करो जो मेहनत तो कर रहे हैं, लेकिन अंदर से थक चुके हैं। कमेंट में title: A message from Jet Li
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Hi, I'm Jet Li. Welcome to my YouTube channel. I learn how to training my body for many years. Maybe you know, I was eight years old learning martial arts, trained the body. I spent 37 years to learn how to training my mind. Here, I want to share more how to training the mind, why is very important, because now I'm very peaceful, I hope you too. You know, a lot of people only want to share the shiny part, but I want to share both. I'm just like a normal people when I was young. I'm struggling, I got a lot of pressure, I want to fight, I want to be successful. But what is the successful? We need more famous, more power, more things. But if you fight for that, if you don't understand, in the end of the day, you're still fighting. I want to talk to you guys more stories how to training martial arts, if you interested, I can share. How to make action film, or in the future, how to helping people. Oh, that's wonderful, because we are global family living on Earth. I'm retired, nothing to do, but I really want to use my life journey and the experiences to share with you, make your journey easier, happier, and healthier.

title: I don’t chase I attract
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I don't chase, I attract. Everything finds its way back. I don't stress, I don't fight. My whole life is flowing right. I breathe in peace, I let go fear. What is mine is already here. I don't want, I don't wait. The universe knows my fate. I love money, and money loves me. Financial freedom running to me. I get paid to exist, just be. Everything flows so effortlessly. I am happy, I am wealthy. I am glowing, I am healthy. I am magnetic, can't you see? Everything comes naturally. I don't need to check the 3D. I trust myself, I trust the unseen. Everything comes at the perfect time. I want it and it's already mine. I don't rush time, I let it flow. What is for me already knows. I don't chase dreams, I don't pretend. Everything meets me in the end. I love money, and money loves me. Financial freedom running to me. I get paid to exist, just be. Everything flows so effortlessly. I am happy, I am wealthy. I am glowing, I am healthy. I am magnetic, can't you see? Everything comes naturally. I slowed my breath, I changed the tone. Started acting like it's already done. Now I choose what I assume. Life says yes to every move. If it's mine, it won't pass me by. It finds its way, I receive the sign. I love money, and money loves me. Financial freedom running to me. I get paid to exist, just be. Everything flows so effortlessly. I am happy, I am wealthy. I am glowing, I am healthy. I am magnetic, can't you see? Everything comes naturally. I always get what I want, I always get what I need. title: "What It Sounds Like" Huntrix | Live Action Music Video | KPop Demon Hunters | Song Cover | IRL Sony
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription:
Nothing but the truth now.
Nothing but the proof
of what I am.
The worst of what I came from.
Patterns I'm ashamed of.
Things that even I don't understand.
I tried to fix it. I tried to fight it.
My head was twisted.
My heart divided.
My lives all collided.
I don't know why I
didn't trust you
to be on my side.
I broke into a million pieces
and I can't go back.
But now I'm seeing all the beauty
in the broken glass.
These scars are part of me,
darkness and harmony.
My voice will be the light.
This is what it sounds like.
Why did I cover up
the colors stuck inside my head?
I should have let the jagged edges
meet the light instead.
Show me what's underneath.
I'll find your harmony.
The song we couldn't write.
This is what it sounds like.
Stop this song.
We're shattering the silent.
We're rising, defiant,
shining in the quiet.
You're not alone.
We listen to the demons.
We let them get between us.
But none of us are out here
on our own.
So we were cowards,
so we were liars,
so we're no heroes,
we're still survivors.
The dreamers, the fighters.
No lying, I'm tired.
But dive in the fire
and I'll be right here
by your side.
We broke into a million pieces
and we can't go back.
But now we're seeing all the beauty
in the broken glass.
These scars are part of me,
darkness and harmony.
My voice will be the light.
This is what it sounds like.
Why did we cover up
the colors stuck inside our head?
Get up and let the jagged edges
meet the light instead.
Show me what's underneath.
I'll find your harmony.
Fearless and on the fire.
This is what it sounds like.
G-Crew.

The growth of the global game at this T20 format has been brilliant. Moments to savour and remember. Celebrate India, you absolutely deserve it.

transcription: सवेरे समय का शो देखा, उसमें उसने कहा कि... स्टैंड-अप कॉमेडियन और यूट्यूबर समय रैना लगातार चर्चा में बने हुए हैं। वजह है उनका नया स्टैंड-अप स्पेशल 'स्टिल अलाइव'। इस नए यूट्यूब वीडियो में समय ने अपनी जिंदगी के सबसे मुश्किल दौर के बारे में खुलकर बात की। साथ ही उन्होंने यह भी बताया कि टफ फेज में सिर्फ दो लोगों ने उनका साथ दिया, जिन्हें वो इंस्टाग्राम पर भी फॉलो करते हैं - राखी सावंत और दीपक कलाल। पूरे शो के दौरान समय ने राखी सावंत और दीपक कलाल की काफी टांग खींची और उन पर जोक्स भी किए। लेकिन इसके बावजूद दीपक कलाल इमोशनल हो गए और उन्होंने एक वीडियो शेयर करते हुए कहा... ...उसने कहा कि, अब आप आपके पापा के... को स्क्रेच करो, तो कूपन निकलेगा। कोई बहुत... कूपन आपको निकलेगा। इसीलिए मैं पापा को कहूंगा आई लव यू पापा, क्योंकि मैंने हमेशा मम्मी को ही बोला आई लव यू। लेकिन मेरे पापा की उम्र भी 85 है, और मैं कहूंगा आई लव यू पापा। लव यू पापा। कमेंट सेक्शन में बताइए क्या समय रैना देश के नंबर वन कॉमेडियन बन चुके हैं? यस और नो।

transcription: Woh mujhe disrespect kar rahe hain, toh unke sath baitha hua hai? Meri kya izzat chal rahi hai bahar? Main todi hui hoon Yogesh. Dekh lo ek bar, tere ko disrespect karegi toh uske sath baithna jaake room mein. Kaisa lagega? Yaar ab tere case mein... Tum logon ko kuch bhi lage, iske chot lagi hai, main yahan pe tha, uske chot lagi hai, dekh thodi bahut chinta mujhe bhi hai bhai, main uske sath... Yaar chinta hai toh usi ke paas ja, mere paas mat aa. Chal chhod. Ruru, yeh itni gandi-gandi baatein, meri galti nahi thi. Maine kuch bola nahi, maine kuch lada nahi. Woh jab mereko disrespect karti hai, toh tu kahan tha? Tu mereko jaa-jaa kyun kar raha tha? Because... Tu mere sath kyun nahi aaya? Tune mujhe kya bola? Yogesh ko samjha le, main iska muh tod dungi, yeh kar dungi. Aur mujhe pata hai tu kar sakti hai... Toh tujhe mere sath aana chahiye tha na? Tu usko baith ke sympathize kar raha hai. Woh 20 din ka jo connection tha na usko chhod, tu toh sath mein tha na... kya mere andar se char din mein sab khatam ho jayega? Jo connection tha sab khatam ho jayega? Toh theek hai. Theek hai. Theek hai. Theek hai. Woh wali baat... Theek hai, theek hai, mat kar, mere liye jo samajhna, jaao. Meri disrespect koi karega tu khada rahega... Yeh jaao-jaao wali cheez na Ruru, us din karni chahiye thi jis din aayi thi. Jaao us din bolna chahiye tha, abhi nahi... Meri disrespect hui hai aur tu... Main tere sath hi khada hoon, puri duniya ko pata hai. Haan woh... Main tere sath hi khada hoon, puri duniya ko pata hai. Kahan khada hai? Jaa... jaa... jaa... Main Ruru ko bas ek hi point bol raha tha, Ruru, at this point, Ruru ke paas main hoon, mere paas aap ho. Jo teesra banda, yaani Akanksha jiske sath main tha abhi tak, uske paas kaun hai? Doston, Akanksha pad gayi hai akeli. Koi nahi hai Akanksha ke defense ke liye. Is feeling se Akanksha ka ho gya hai emotional breakdown. Kya aane wale episode mein kya Yogesh dega Akanksha ka fir se sath, toh kya hoga yeh janne ke liye channel ko subscribe zaroor kijiye.

title: Journal Reading 010 | Trust Your Journey, It Was Carved For You
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: There was a point in time, earlier on in my spiritual awakening journey, when I was concerned with growth and getting better. Not that I don't want to grow now because of course I do, but in the beginning, the pursuit of growth was all-consuming. It was ego-driven. I went to the gym regularly, I meditated, I read self-help, spiritual books, and took notes. I even took up coaching others in an attempt to ditch the nine-to-five scene. None of the habits stuck for more than a few months, but I would always come back to them the following year. Like I said, it was ego-driven. I wanted to do better because, deep down, I felt I wasn't good enough. I felt behind in life, like I should be further along. And although that way of pursuing growth and self-improvement served its purpose, I now understand it's not the best way. Actually, I would even go as far as to say as adding habits to your daily routine for the sole purpose of getting better is the very thing that keeps you from getting better. Often times, our pursuit for better is rooted in social validation. We want to be liked, we want to be accepted, we want to be seen in a particular light. And the problem doesn't come from not being noticed or liked. Often times, along these sorts of external focus journeys, we are seen and liked, but we aren't seen and liked for who we actually are. I believe a better way to improve oneself is not to download a bunch of habits influencers have said that have changed their lives, but to do more of the things you enjoy. Lean into yourself, and forget what the internet says is good or bad. If running is what you love, then run because you love it, not because you think in three months you'll be a different person. If you genuine- if you genuinely enjoy having a couple of beers at the end of the day, have a couple of beers. The biggest lie the self-improvement space sold us was that there's something wrong with who we are, and that we need to fix it. There is nothing wrong with who you are or where you are at in life. title: Finding True Abundance | Journal Reading 019
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Good morning, YouTube. Today's journal reading was written on March 17th, 2026, and in this one, I kind of explore ideas of abundance, and I think that's a theme that maybe I've wrestled with a lot throughout my life. Anyway, here it goes. Abundance is found in nothing. Abundance is found in knowing enough. As I write this, I'm sitting back in our brown leather recliner we found sitting outside our dumpster when we first moved here. That probably sounds gross, but it was in good shape, and we needed some furniture. That was roughly six years ago. There was a time in my life where material abundance and worldly status mattered to me. It was something I chased. Where I was, or what I had, was never enough. I needed more. I needed to progress. But then something changed. I don't know when it happened, or why, or what triggered it. All I know is one day, all that once mattered seemed trivial. Among the spiritual community, there's a decent amount of talk about abundance, the law of attraction, and manifestation. If only we align our thoughts and energy with the life and success and the material we desire, all we imagine will be ours. Whether there's any truth to that, that doesn't really matter to me. What does matter to me is why our lives, where we are at this—where—lah, where we are at any given moment is not enough for us. I think we all have ideas in our head of what it means to be abundant and successful, and likely more often than not, those ideas are filled with lavish material items and social recognition from our fellow man. It's what I thought. It's what I chased. But I've come to understand that that's not true abundance. That's not what true success is. True success and abundance is looking around at your life just at it—just as it is right now, and seeing all that you have, all that you've accomplished this far. If you live in America, odds are you have everything you need, plus some. You have a roof over your head, food in the fridge, people who love you. Recognizing the value in all of that you already have is true abundance. Knowing enough in a world that is constantly telling you to go for more, to go for better, is a superpower. It's abundance. Knowing enough is not a lack mindset. It's peaceful sustainability. It's the mindset of the richest people on earth.

category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Bullet journaling accepts that every day is different rather than trying to impose the same structure each time. This makes it flexible and able to handle whatever comes up. The main point is that bullet journaling embraces chaos with a system that can change as needed. A daily log has not set amount of space, use what you need that day. Some days may take just one page, others more. The monthly log has two pages, one for the calendar and one for tasks. Write events, tasks and notes on the calendar page next to each date. List tasks for the month on the other page. If a task is for a different month, write it in the future log, then add future tasks to the next month's log when that month starts. You can make custom pages for specific topics like health goals or a hobby. Use the index at the front to keep track of all your pages and collections. List the topic and page numbers. Keep adding to the index as needed. This flexible approach accepts that every day is different. The system can grow and change along with your need.

title: Just do the right thing. The rest doesn’t matter.#Selflessness#PersonalGrowth#selfimprovement
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: On action and duty. Great ideas from the book Meditations by Marcus Aurelius. Just do the right thing, the rest doesn't matter. That quote is basically saying focus on what you can control, and let go of what you can't. Here's what that breaks down to. 1. Just do the right thing. This is the part you can control. It's about your own choices, your own actions, and your own character. Is it kind? Is it honest? Is it helpful? Does it align with who you want to be? Your job is to figure out the right, decent, ethical thing to do in a situation and then do it. That's your duty. 2. The rest doesn't matter. This is the part you can't control, so don't let it paralyze you or stop you from doing your duty. What other people think of you for doing it, whether you'll get credit or even be thanked, whether it will be successful or work out perfectly, how hard or scary it feels. The outcome, sometimes, you can only control your effort, not the final result. Think of it like this. You see someone drop their wallet. The right thing is to pick it up and give it back to them. So you do it. The rest, that doesn't matter. Whether they are suspicious of you, whether they say a heartfelt thank you or just grunt, or whether you're late to your next appointment because you stopped. You did your part. The rest was out of your hands. In a nutshell, pour your energy into being a person of good action. Don't waste your energy worrying about the noise, the results, or the opinions that follow. Your peace comes from knowing you did what you should, not from how the world reacts. It's a call for integrity over image, for courage over comfort, and for focusing on your own behavior in a world you can't control.

title: If You Can't Stop Scrolling, Watch This

transcription: Have you ever picked up your phone for just one minute and somehow lost an entire hour? You're not alone. The average person spends hours scrolling every day. Six: Go for a walk. A short walk can boost your mood, clear your mind, and improve your health. No fancy equipment needed, just step outside and start moving. Five: Learn one new skill. Spend 15 minutes learning a language, practicing an instrument, or watching a tutorial. Small daily improvements can lead to massive results over time. Four: Call someone you care about. Instead of watching strangers online, connect with real people in your life. A simple conversation can strengthen relationships and make someone's day. Three: Write down your thoughts. Push-ups, stretching, yoga, or a quick workout—anything that gets your body moving. Your future self will thank you. One: Work on a goal—that project, business idea, skill, or dream you've been putting off. Spend just 20 minutes on it today. Progress beats endless scrolling every single time. The next time you reach for your phone, ask yourself, "Do I want entertainment for a moment or progress that lasts?" If you found this helpful, don't forget to like, subscribe, and share it with someone who spends a little too much time scrolling.

title: How to Build Habits That Actually Stick
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You're not failing when it comes to habits. You're just starting too many at once. Most people don't struggle because they're lazy. They struggle because they try to change their entire life overnight. They want to wake up earlier, start working out, eat healthier, drink more water, meditate, journal, read more, spend less time on their phone, all at the same time. And for a few days, it feels exciting, but then everything falls apart. Not because you're incapable, because your brain can't sustain that much change all at once. If your habits never seem to stick, the problem isn't motivation. It's the way you're trying to build them. Most habits fail because there's no structure behind them. People rely on motivation instead of systems. They tell themselves, "I'll work out after work tomorrow. I'll start eating healthier in a few days. I'll remember to do it." But vague habits don't survive real life because life gets busy, you get tired, your routine changes, your motivation drops, and if there's no repeatable structure, the habit disappears with it. Another mistake people make is setting the barrier too high. They think, "If I'm going to work out, I'm going to do 1 hour. If I'm going to read, I need to read an entire chapter. If I'm going to meal prep, I need to fix my entire diet." Eventually, your brain starts resisting it, not because the goal is bad, because the effort required feels too big to repeat consistently. That's why intensity usually fails. It asks too much before consistency exists. If you want a habit to stick, make it smaller, smaller than you think it should be. Make it so easy your brain has no reason to avoid it. Want to start working out? Don't commit to an hour. Commit to putting your shoes on and doing 5 to 10 minutes. Want to read more? Read one page. Want to meditate? Sit down for 30 seconds. Your goal in the beginning should not be full transformation. It should be repetition because repetition creates familiarity and familiarity lowers resistance. You're not trying to prove how disciplined you are. You should be trying to teach your brain that this is something you do now. Another thing that helps is attaching your habits to something that already exists. Instead of saying, "I'll do it later," anchor it to something specific. After I brush my teeth, I'll stretch. After work, I'll take a walk for 10 minutes. After making my coffee, I'll journal for a few minutes. The less decisions your brain has to make, the easier consistency becomes. That's what systems do. They reduce friction. Here's the part that nobody likes hearing. Consistency is supposed to feel boring sometimes. Social media makes change look exciting and intense, but real progress usually looks repetitive, quiet, simple, unimpressive. A lot of people quit because a habit no longer feels exciting. But habits that last aren't built on excitement. They're built on repeatability. You don't need perfect days. You need enough days repeated over time. Missing one day isn't failure. Starting over every single week is. The goal isn't to become a different person overnight. The goal is to create a system that you can maintain over time. If you want habits that actually stick, stop trying to change everything at once. Make the habit smaller. Remove friction. Repeat it consistently. Build structure around it. Because consistency is not built through intensity. It's built through repetition. Small actions repeated daily will always beat out massive effort that only lasts a week. Until one day, they become automatic. If this helped, subscribe. I'll be breaking down systems for your lifestyle so you can actually build something that works.

title: Aurora Innovation: Business Review Highlights Q4 2025 with Co-Founder & CEO Chris Urmson
transcription: 2025 was a really big year for us. We launched our driverless trucks for the first time. We've been operating them day in and day out. Q4 continued to be great progress for us. We are, as of January, to over 250,000 driverless miles, which is nearly triple the mileage we had in October, increasing our revenue 25% quarter-over-quarter. And of course, we did all this while maintaining a perfect safety record and perfect on-time record. Our latest release unlocks our ability to operate driverlessly in the rain, in the fog, and in heavier wind. This unlocks really meaningful utilization gains because in the past, the Aurora Driver had been blocked from operation up to 40% of the time because of weather. This release also unlocks driverless operation between El Paso and Phoenix and complete bidirectional driverless operation between Fort Worth and El Paso. Fort Worth to Phoenix is a big deal because it's a 1,000-mile lane, and that 1,000 miles means that a person can't drive that in a single day within their hours of service limits. It means that the Aurora Driver is now offering a superhuman benefit to our customers. This year, we're really going to see our generalized AI approach unlock some rapid expansion. We expect to be operating across the Sun Belt this year, going to customer endpoints, really serving the need of our customers. That's going to start with one of the leading US carriers and their endpoint in Phoenix. We're also going between a sand mine and a customer site in Midland for Detmar. Detmar is a great example of how endpoints unlock value for customers. The Aurora Driver is going to be operating 20 hours a day for Detmar, hauling frac sand for their oil and gas industry customers on this 60-mile lane that's mostly freeway, effectively doubling the productivity of their assets. On top of that, we're going to be running from Laredo to Dallas, hauling berries for Driscoll's for Hirschbach. And we're going to end the year with over 200 trucks operating driverlessly day in and day out. Our new fleet's going to come online in Q2. It's going to be on the International LT platform, and we're not going to have to have an observer on board. With Volvo, we've really entered the industrialization phase. We're working with the New River Valley factory, where the first VNL with the Aurora Driver installed has come off the line, and that's really setting us up for the future. This is the foundation you need to really deliver product at scale. Looking further ahead to our third-generation system, we continue to make great progress on Novia. This hardware generation is really going to enable scale, allowing us to produce tens of thousands of trucks. We ended 2025 in a really strong position with $1.5 billion on our balance sheet. We anticipate that'll fund operations until we achieve positive free cash flow in 2028. Scaling over 200 trucks means that we're going to be able to generate somewhere between 14 and 16 million dollars of revenue this year. That's a 400% increase year-on-year. We're seizing the opportunity to transform logistics, one of the most important industries on the planet, and we're well on our way to having tens of thousands of Aurora-driven trucks on the road.

title: Insurers' Shifting Priorities - Pricing Modernization Webinar Clip
transcription: Okay, so this data comes from our annual survey of insurers on the factors that shape their IT investment priorities. So last year, and in most prior years, the number one thing is growth. If it'll help me grow, I will spend money. But this year, the picture changed noticeably. Growth, as you can see, moved down to third place, while data and innovation emerged as the leading priorities. In fact, last year, data wasn't even in the top five, and so here it is, number one, without even being something that we saw last year. Now, that does not mean that growth and efficiency are no longer important, because nearly all insurers, 98%, still said growth was a big area of focus in 2026. But what's changing is how they're thinking about achieving it, right? Increasingly, insurers are seeing data as the foundation for growth, innovation, and operational improvement. And so these priorities, they're no longer really separate initiatives, they're deeply interconnected, they're increasingly dependent upon each other. So, growth, number one thing that carriers are focusing on. But at the same time, the market environment is changing. Now, this comes from a study of policyholders who had a personal auto claim in the last two years. And we picked personal auto because we were looking at the claims experience. And personal auto is kind of homogeneous when it comes to claims, as opposed to something like, you know, general liability. Anyway, we found that 25% of those who had a claim loved their carrier so much after the claim that they would pay more to stay. But half of all policyholders with a claim told us that they were actively looking for lower premium elsewhere, or had already moved. So, policyholders shopping at historically high rates. And in that environment, the goal can't just be how low can you go to keep your customers, right? Or to attract new customers. That approach always creates long-term profitability challenges. So, the real question is, what is the right price for this specific customer based on their individual risk profile? Now, when insurers rely on broad rating bands, they increase the likelihood of adverse selection, right? Because the lower-risk customers are more likely to leave in search of pricing that more adequately reflects their actual risk, while the higher-risk customers are more likely to stay because they're getting a lower price than they should be paying. And this is why pricing precision matters so much right now, like not only for attracting the customers who are actively shopping, but also for retaining the ones already in your portfolio.

title: Disconnected Management Systems Are Undermining Strategy Execution
transcription: Here we're focusing on strategy and performance, right? And when we talk about strategy and performance, there is a series of corporate processes that are part of this big umbrella that we call strategy and performance corporate processes. So we have governance, we have succession management, we have project management, audits, balanced scorecards, ISOs, certifications, innovation management, KPIs, OKRs, budgets and so much more, right? I'm not going to go through all of these. The idea is there is a number of practices or processes or management models that have, that interact with each other and we call corporate management. And each one of these can have a software to support that practice, right? So you can have a software for OKRs, for example, another software for your BIs or your dashboards or your balanced scorecard, another software for your Scrum projects or task management and so on. So for each of these practices, we have a whole ecosystem of softwares to support that practice, right? And what we've been seeing in organizations is that as you adopt an app or a software for each of these practices, they stop interacting with themselves. This should be practices that are make sense independently, but they're also part of a management system, and they should interact with each other. But when you have apps or softwares for each of these, they stop talking to each other. They start acting as silos of information, right? And this is the reality that we see in most organizations. If we take a look at this chart, this chart is the number of app SaaS apps, on average, for each organization, right? So the average number of SaaS apps. And we see that in 2015, we had only 8 SaaS apps, on average, for an organization. And this jumped to 80 in 2020 in just 5 years, then to 130 in 2022. This is the phenomenon that we call SaaS sprawl or app sprawl, right? It was the proliferation of SaaS applications in organizations, and it just boomed, right? From, in 7 years, from 8 to 130. And all of these specialized apps came about and companies adopted them, and for each activity, each management practice, you had an app for that or you have an app for that. But this created big problems in the organizations, right? Managing SaaS is a new problem for IT. So there are so many providers, that managing it all is a huge problem. And integrating it all is a huge problem. So if you have 8 SaaS applications, and you buy the 9th, okay, you're going to integrate, you know, this new SaaS application with 8 others to connect the information. transcription: Recession risk is rising fast and could hit within weeks. Will geopolitical tensions and inflation push the global economy over the edge right now? Energy prices are not just a headline. When energy costs rise, businesses face higher expenses and often pass those on to consumers. This causes people to cut back on spending, creating a feedback loop that weakens economic growth. This dynamic is a key reason economists are so worried about inflation's lingering impact on the economy in 2026. Top economist Mohamed El-Erian has issued a stark warning. He says the global economy faces a critical eight-week window to prevent a recession. The trigger is the reopening of a crucial oil route currently disrupted by geopolitical tensions. If this route stays closed, energy supplies tighten further, pushing costs higher and escalating recession risks worldwide. Another leading economist, Mark Zandi, agrees recession risks are rising significantly. He estimates about a 40% chance of recession this year. However, Zandi still sees a path to avoid it, especially if geopolitical tensions ease. The key challenge is managing inflation, which remains elevated even if tensions cool. Investors are already feeling the pressure. Zandi warns the S&P 500 could fall by as much as 30% as the market adjusts to the real economic risks behind inflated stock valuations. This signals a painful correction ahead for many portfolios as the economy deals with these pressures. Even if geopolitical tensions ease and energy routes reopen, elevated prices are expected to persist. Zandi estimates this will cost the average household roughly $1,400 a year. This ongoing inflation squeeze means families will feel the impact directly through higher everyday expenses. What this means for you is clear: the next two months are critical. Energy prices and geopolitical events could shape your financial future. You might face higher costs and a volatile stock market. Staying informed and cautious with spending and investments is key. Subscribe now for the latest updates to help you navigate these uncertain times.
