title: Introducing Claude Fable 5
transcription: Today we're launching Claude Fable 5. The most capable model we've ever released to the public. Fable 5 is a mythos class model with safeguards that make it ready for general use. We didn't broadly release our previous model with this level of capability because when we finished training and testing it, we saw that the model, Claude Mythos Preview, was finding thousands of cybersecurity vulnerabilities. A model that can find flaws like that can also be used to exploit them. So instead of releasing it, we handed it to the people who protect the world's critical software and put it to work fixing the holes before someone could break through them. It was the right call for the moment, but it was never the goal. We believe powerful AI should be safe and accessible. That's why we went to work on Claude Fable 5. Every Claude model has safeguards to keep it from doing harm. Fable needed more cautious ones than anything we've built before. Our safety systems for Fable 5 automatically review requests that touch on high-risk areas like cybersecurity or biology. Those requests are then redirected to Opus 4.8. We do that intentionally so people can continue to benefit from the capabilities of a powerful model like Fable without the cyber and biology risks that come with it. The safeguards are broad today, but we'll keep refining them so that they're better at allowing safe requests. We built Claude Fable 5 for your most ambitious work. It can stay with a problem far longer than any model before it. It's highly autonomous and can operate for days without intervention. And it's not just coding. It can take on projects in finance, research, economics, law - complicated tasks that used to need constant supervision. So point it at something that matters. title: Company Culture | Simon Sinek
transcription: So, I think the concept of leadership is one of the most misunderstood concepts in business, quite frankly. We think about leadership as a rank or position, like "I'm in leadership." The question is, are you a leader? Leadership is the awesome responsibility to see those around us rise. It is a skill set that needs to be learned and practiced. Most of us, the way we have achieved our leadership position or rank is because we were good at the job. The problem is that's not your job anymore. You know, when we're super junior, the organizations we work for give us tons of training how to do our job. Some of us go to college and how to do our job. If you're an architect, you have to go to school to learn how to be an architect. And if you're really good at your job, they'll promote you until you reach a position where you're now responsible for the people who do the job you used to do. But they don't teach us how to do that. And so the reason we get managers and not leaders is because we don't get taught how to do our new job called leadership. When leaders take themselves on, when leaders uh become students of leadership, you'll find that all of the traditional metrics that we try and push and, you know, and drive every day, go up. Productivity goes up. Engagement goes up. Uh uh innovation goes up. Um I think it's very funny, I love uh I love organizations that when they write their values on the wall, you know, it's like, integrity, innovation, you know, honesty. By the way, if you have to write honesty on the wall, you've got bigger problems. Um But those those things are not things you can do. Those are the result of things. You can't walk into someone's office and say, "Lynn, a little more a little more innovation from you today, please." Like, what are you supposed to do? And so, it's not a value. A value is is is a behavior. And the better we understand our values and the better we incentivize to behavior, the stronger your culture. And the stronger your culture, the more innovation you get, the more integrity get, the more productivity you get, the more uh uh engagement you get. My favorite definition of culture is culture equals values plus behavior. So, values, number one, needs to be written as verbs. It's not integrity, it's do the right thing. It's not innovation, it's find a new way to solve a problem. It's not honesty, it's tell the truth. Which are which are behaviors and we can incentivize and reward to those behaviors. And the people who are best at embodying those values, those are the ones that we should promote into leadership positions because those are the ones that set the example of of how we how we work here.

title: UKREiiF 2026: 'Where the smart money is moving' panel discussion
transcription: So, we're here at UKREIIF this year, talking all things living UK real estate. The current environment for living real estate in the UK is one with viability challenges and concerns. We've got rising build cost inflation, increased regulation, economic difficulties. What there also is, is a huge amount of opportunity. There is pent-up demand, there is under supply, there is no shortage of debt available, there is capital being deployed. It is a huge time for opportunity. The smart money is moving primarily into affordable housing, I would say, though how you define that depends on a number of factors, but clearly the biggest risk to any investment strategy is take-up and demand at this moment, and so through various lenses people are trying to make sure that whatever it is that they're investing in or developing is affordable for the end user, so that the project is viable long-term. I think there's quite a lot of opportunity for living product, because there is a fundamental requirement and demand for good quality accommodation across all the living sectors, asset classes. Especially when there is a bit of an affordability gap. So, those that can deliver product that meets that demand are going to be very well placed. 2026, for me, has also been the year of co-living. We're seeing more institutionalisation of co-living, in terms of an accepted asset class for co-investors. So, I think the opportunities at the moment, very much from a housebuilders point of view, are in the land market. Slightly longer-term strategic sites, gray belt, something where you can work with a landowner to really maximize the number of homes on a site, and really go out there and get a planning consent. I believe that the opportunities in the living sector lie in working in partnership, both with local governments, local councils, with developers, with capital, trying to bring everybody together to achieve the ultimate goal of delivering more housing for the country. I think the smart money in living is moving to affordable with a small 'a'. That's how we deal with the viability concerns. That's where some degree of public subsidy can unlock delivery. I also see there's huge opportunities in partnerships becoming platforms, with long-term sustainable partnerships between registered providers, developers and investors to unlock delivery at scale.

title: Inside the Cigna Healthcare Broker Connect & Insight Forum 2026 | Corporate Event Highlights
transcription: Welcome to the Cigna Broker Insight Conference 2026. We are really grateful to have you here. Thank you for joining us. It's great to see so many, uh, familiar faces, uh, here with us. Delighted to have you here to host for what we hope is an engaging, insightful, and enjoyable conversation. Since the opening of our expanded office in May, many of you and your teams have been in with us, have spent time with us through workshops and different working sessions. The collaboration during those sessions and the feedback you have shared has been incredibly valuable to us. And I'm happy to confirm that Africa continues to be a key growth market for us. Our commitment here is long-term, deliberate, and strategic, and Kenya sits right at the heart of that journey. As advocates for improving health, we've been conducting annual insight studies that help us better understand the key aspects of people's health and well-being in order to improve the vitality of those we serve. The data that I will present today reflects a sample of over 500 people in Kenya and over 11,000 globally, and those are not necessarily Cigna customers, but are really a cross-section of of the society. I'm sure you, you will agree with me, because both health and vitality are foundational for thriving individuals, for thriving families, thriving communities, and they help foster, ultimately, a healthy economy, a healthy workforce, and a healthy society. The true value of any health solution is only ever revealed in a moment of crisis. And in that moment, what people desperately need is not just coverage. They need to know that someone is there, someone who knows their name, someone who picks up the phone, and someone who comes to them. Cigna Africa is that someone. We pass our love back to your teams in the offices, please pass our love to them, and we look forward to partnering. Thank you very much. I have been honored to be your MC tonight, and we look forward to seeing more of you in the coming events. Asanteni sana.

ऑपरेटिंग मार्जिन 7.34 आपको जाता हुआ, मतलब नेट मार्जिन कंपनी का 7.34 देखने को मिल रहा है। तो साल-दर-साल तो बढ़ा है लेकिन क्वार्टरली बेस पर आपको गिरते हुए देखने को मिल रहे हैं। ईपीएस की बात करते हैं तो देखिए पिछले क्वार्टर में ईपीएस ₹1.77, पिछले साल ₹4.26, अभी देखते हैं तो ₹4.12 आपको जाता हुआ देखने को मिल रहा है। तो ओवरऑल देखा जाए तो नंबर कुछ ख़ास नंबर टाइप के नहीं देखने को मिल रहा है, क्योंकि रेवेन्यू देखते हैं तो रेवेन्यू आपका 5% के आसपास बढ़ते हुए देखने को मिल रहे हैं। मार्किट का अनुमान भी इतना ही था तो रेवेन्यू आप कह सकते हैं रेवेन्यू में कोई दिक्कत नहीं है, रेवेन्यू तो चलेगा। लेकिन खर्चे फिर से इस क्वार्टर में ज्यादा आपको देखने को मिल रहे हैं। खर्चे ज्यादा होने की वजह से कंपनी का ऑपरेटिंग प्रॉफिट आपको साल-दर-साल गिरते हुए देखने को मिल रहा है। नेट प्रॉफिट आपको बढ़ते हुए देखने को मिल रहा है, क्योंकि बहुत सारे एडजस्टमेंट इसके अंदर आपको देखने को मिल रहे हैं। देखते हैं मार्किट इस पे कैसे रिएक्ट करता है। वीडियो पसंद आए तो लाइक कीजिएगा, साथ ही साथ चैनल को सब्सक्राइब जरूर कीजिएगा। धन्यवाद।

transcription: नमस्कार, आप देख रहे हैं बिस्तख और मैं हूं आपके साथ चिराग ठाकुर। देश की दिग्गज आईटी कंपनी टाटा कंसल्टेंसी सर्विसेज यानी कि टीसीएस ने गुरुवार को अपने चौथे तिमाही के नतीजे जारी किए, जिसमें कंपनी का प्रदर्शन मजबूत रहा। कंपनी का कंसोलिडेटेड नेट प्रॉफिट सालाना आधार पर 12% बढ़कर ₹13,718 करोड़ पहुंच गया। पिछले साल इसी तिमाही में यह ₹12,224 करोड़ था। कंपनी ने ₹31 प्रति शेयर का फाइनल डिविडेंड घोषित किया है। इससे निवेशकों को सीधा फायदा मिलेगा। टीसीएस का ऑपरेशन से रेवेन्यू 10% बढ़कर ₹70,698 करोड़ हो गया है। कंपनी को यह फायदा ऐसे समय में हुआ है जब आईटी सेक्टर आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस में नए-नए बदलाव के कारण उतार-चढ़ाव भरे दौर से गुजर रहा है। इस कारण कंपनी के शेयरों में हाल में बड़ी गिरावट आई थी। टीसीएस ने इस तिमाही में 12 अरब डॉलर की कुल डील वैल्यू यानी कि टीसीबी हासिल की है। जिसमें तीन बड़ी मेगा डील शामिल है। कंपनी की विकास दर में आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस की भूमिका सबसे अहम रही है। कंपनी की सीओओ आरती सुब्रमण्यम के अनुसार FY26 एआई अपनाने के मामले में एक निर्णायक साल रहा। चौथी तिमाही में कंपनी का सालाना एआई रेवेन्यू 2.3 अरब डॉलर के पार निकल गया है। टीसीएस ने अपने हाइपरवोल्ड निवेश के जरिए ओपनएआई, एएमडी और एबीबी जैसी दिग्गज कंपनियों के साथ रणनीतिक हाथ मिलाया है। कंपनी ने इंटरप्राइज ट्रांसफॉर्मेशन, डिजिटल इंजीनियरिंग और क्लाउड मॉर्डनाइजेशन जैसे क्षेत्रों में मजबूत डील्स हासिल किया है। कंपनी ने माना की वैश्विक आर्थिक चुनौतियां बनी हुई हैं लेकिन ग्राहकों का टेक्नोलॉजी निवेश पर भरोसा मजबूत है। नतीजों के ऐलान से पहले बीएसई पर टीसीएस का शेयर 1.09% की तेजी के साथ ₹2587.75 पर बंद हुआ। एक्सपर्ट का मानना है कि शानदार मार्जिन और एआई क्षेत्र में कंपनी की बढ़ती पकड़ आने वाले समय में स्टॉक को और मजबूती दे सकती है। इसके अलावा, टीसीएस ने 1 अप्रैल से सभी ग्रेड के कर्मचारियों के लिए सालाना सैलरी बढ़ोतरी लागू करने का ऐलान किया है। हालांकि, इस बार कितनी बढ़ोतरी होगी इसका खुलासा नहीं किया गया है। खास बात यह है कि कंपनी एक तरफ सैलरी बढ़ा रही है तो दूसरी तरफ कुल कर्मचारियों की संख्या में सालाना आधार पर कमी भी देखने को मिली है। हालांकि, इस बार सबसे बड़ा सवाल यही है कि सैलरी में कितनी बढ़ोतरी होगी। कंपनी ने अभी तक हाइक का परसेंट स्पष्ट नहीं किया है। पिछले साल FY25 में टीसीएस ने सैलरी हाइक में करीब 5 महीने की देरी की थी और सितंबर 2025 से इसे लागू किया गया था। उस समय औसतन 4.5% से 7% तक की बढ़ोतरी दी गई थी। जबकि बेहतर प्रदर्शन करने वाले कर्मचारियों को डबल डिजिट हाइक मिला था। आप टीसीएस के नतीजों के बारे में क्या सोचते हैं, कमेंट करके हमें जरूर बताएं और बने रहे बिस्तख के साथ।

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 explained: How the new 48-team format works
transcription: For years, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has talked about getting more countries involved at a World Cup. That push finally took shape in January 2017 when football's governing body voted to expand the tournament from 32 to 48 teams. Under the new format, there will be 104 matches at this World Cup. That's 40 more than at Qatar 2022. Those games will be played across 16 host cities in the USA, Mexico, and Canada. That's a huge change from the compact 2022 tournament in Qatar where a fan could realistically attend two or even three matches in a single day. The 48 teams will be split into 12 groups of four. The top two from each group plus the eight best third-placed teams will move into a new 32-team knockout phase. From there, the tournament runs through the round of 32, the round of 16, quarterfinals, semifinals, and then the final. By the time we get to the decider at MetLife Stadium in New York, New Jersey, on July the 19th, the champions will have played eight matches. That's one more than the seven required by Argentina when they won Qatar 2022.

बिलो एस्टीमेट है कंपनी का रिवेन्यू। ऑपरेटिंग प्रॉफिट आपका साल दर साल क्वार्टर दर क्वार्टर गिरता हुआ देखने को मिल रहा है। नेट प्रॉफिट बढ़ा है और मार्केट के एस्टीमेट से बेहतर है लेकिन एक्सेप्शनल आइटम की वजह से बेहतर है। तो मिक्स टाइप के नंबर है, बाकी देखते हैं मार्केट इसपे कैसे रियेक्ट करता है। वीडियो पसंद आए तो लाइक कीजिएगा, साथ में साथ चैनल को सब्सक्राइब जरूर कीजिएगा। धन्यवाद।

title: The 2026 FIFA World Cup explained in 2 minutes
transcription: The stage is set for this year's FIFA Men's World Cup, with the opening matches kicking off tomorrow. The tournament, held every four years, will be unlike any before it. Here's why. Firstly, it will be the biggest World Cup in history, the most complex one yet. For the first time ever, the tournament will be shared across three countries: the United States, Canada, and Mexico, and matches will be played across 16 cities. The competition is expanding, too. Instead of the traditional eight groups, this year's tournament will feature 12, made up of four teams each. 48 national teams will compete, instead of 32. With more teams in the mix, the road to glory could be tougher to predict. The expansion means a record number of matches. Teams will play 104 matches over 39 days, making it the longest ever World Cup run. With more teams involved, there could be more opportunities for underdogs to make their mark. Among those returning to the World Cup include the Democratic Republic of Congo, Haiti, and Iraq, while four debutants are getting their boots on the pitch for the first time. They are Uzbekistan, Jordan, Curacao, and Cape Verde. But staging the World Cup across three countries brings major logistical challenges. Some teams could end up traveling thousands of kilometers between venues, crossing borders and time zones. FIFA has grouped matches regionally to reduce travel, but long journeys may still be unavoidable for teams that progress deep into the tournament. And depending on where they're playing, the climates could be different, from the high altitude of Mexico City to Miami's heat and humidity. To manage that, FIFA has mandated cooling and hydration breaks during matches. Next, technology will play a bigger role than ever before. Every player will have a digital avatar to remodel on-pitch actions. These changes make it easier for officials to see what would go on during fast or obstructed plays, so they can provide more accurate calls for offsides or potential handballs. And then, of course, there are the stars. This could be the last dance for several legends. Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed this will be his last World Cup. Argentina's Lionel Messi and Croatia's Luka Modrić are also widely expected to be making their final appearances on the game's biggest stage. For football's greats, one final bow. For a new generation, a chance to make history. The road to World Cup glory is about to begin.

title: Hear from Afroman after the verdict in his civil trial
transcription:
Outside this Adams County courthouse, the sound of victory.
After a jury sided with the musician Afroman, whose real name is Joseph Foreman, after a days-long civil defamation trial. Afroman, speaking to WCPO right after the verdict.
I didn't win. America won. America still has freedom of speech. It's still for the people, by the people.
...the jury finds in favor of the defendant.
Seven Adams County Sheriff's deputies sued the musician. They argued Afroman used security video from a 2022 raid of his home and put it in music videos using deputies' likeness without permission.
There's damage to reputation, there's pain and suffering, there's public humiliation. There's everything you saw and heard from these detectives, from the witness stand.
This raid taking place nearly a year ago following search warrants related to possession and trafficking in drugs and kidnapping. The rapper was never charged. Along with using the surveillance video in multiple music videos, including in the song "Lemon Pound Cake", the deputies also say Afroman called them thieves and pedophiles among other things on social media.
I didn't go down here and sue the police department. I fixed up the damages they made, and I sung songs about them to raise money to do it. They were unapologetic.
The deputies wanted Afroman to pay $3.9 million in damages.
We got about a total of 250 pieces given out. This is the last one, and I'd like to give it to you.
Supporters of Afroman coming from near and far, with a message both verbally and symbolically.
For me, this isn't really about Afroman, it's about free speech. So, when someone like Afroman stands up for my free speech by using his talents, his musical talents, to fight the corrupt system, we gotta come out and support him.
I'm glad thing, you know, things went my way. But if they would have took it all from me, I was happy about all the love I was getting from everybody. After them people kicked my kicked my door in.
In Adams County, Jay Warren, WCPO 9 News.
When life give you lemons, you make lemon pound cake.

transcription: दोस्तों, IPL 2024 की स्टार्टिंग से पहले आज हम सभी लोगों को CSK की टीम का रोर इवेंट देखने को मिला था। जहाँ पर करंटली यह रोर इवेंट हमें चलता हुआ नज़र आ रहा है, इसमें हमें सबसे पहले तो चेन्नई सुपर किंग्स की टीम के जितना भी पुराना बैच था जिसमें मैथ्यू हेडन उनके साथ ही सुरेश रैना, अंबाती रायडू, हरभजन सिंह जैसे बड़े-बड़े प्लेयर्स फोटोशूट का हिस्सा बनते हुए नज़र आए थे। दरअसल, CSK की टीम जिन्होंने काफी सारे रिकॉर्ड ऑलरेडी बना दिए हैं, उन सभी प्लेयर्स को यहाँ पर सम्मानित किया गया था। इसके बाद, CSK के रोर मैच में हमें लाइव महेंद्र सिंह धोनी, संजू सैमसन और उसके साथ ही शिवम दुबे की काफी ज्यादा रॉयल एंट्री चेपॉक स्टेडियम में देखने को मिली। जिस तरीके से RCB का अनबॉक्स इवेंट होता है, कुछ उसी तर्ज पर काफी ज्यादा हाइप और क्रेज़ हमें देखने को मिला पूरी तरीके से जैम पैक्ड स्टेडियम। चेपॉक स्टेडियम में करंटली हमें देखने को मिल रहा है जहाँ पर MSD की एंट्री पर लोग काफी ज्यादा इमोशनल भी हो गए थे। इसके साथ ही, अभी हमें करंटली इसके बाद यहाँ पर एक मुकाबला भी देखने को मिलने वाला है जिसमें जो इनकी पास्ट की इलेवन है, जिसमें काफी बड़े-बड़े लेजेंड्स मैथ्यू हेडन, सुरेश रैना, रॉबिन उथप्पा, हरभजन सिंह जैसे प्लेयर्स पार्टिसिपेट करेंगे और जो करंट इलेवन है, उसमें महेंद्र सिंह धोनी और उनके साथ ही इनके करंट प्लेयर्स के बीच में हमें मुकाबला देखने को मिलने वाला है। तो CSK... आप लोग बताना क्या आप लोगों के हिसाब से इस साल CSK की टीम IPL का टाइटल जीतेगी या फिर नहीं?

title: MI Practice Match Highlight 2026 | MI Intra Squad Practice Match 2026 | Rohit Batting MI Camp 2026
transcription: दोस्तों IPL 2026 के एडिशन के लिए फाइनली मुंबई इंडियंस का भी प्रैक्टिस कैंप यहां पर शुरू हो चुका है जहां पर मुंबई की टीम ने भी आज इंट्रा स्क्वाड प्रैक्टिस मुकाबला खेला था। अपनी स्क्रीन पर देख पा रहे होंगे जहां पर रोहित 11 और शार्दुल ठाकुर 11 बनाकर यहां पर प्रैक्टिस मुकाबला खेला था। शार्दुल 11 ने टॉस जीतकर पहले बल्लेबाजी का फैसला किया था। शार्दुल 11 की तरफ से रोबिन मिंज़ इसके साथ ही राज अंगद बावा यहां पर बैटिंग करने आए थे। रोबिन मिंज़ ने यहां पर 32 गेंदों में 66 रन की ताबड़तोड़ पारी खेली थी। राज अंगद ने यहां पर 30 रन केवल 14 गेंदों में बनाए थे बेहतरीन शुरुआत दी थी। इसके साथ ही मयंक रावत ने 45 रन 29 गेंदों में बनाए थे और गेंद के साथ 34 रन देकर एक विकेट भी लिया था। इसके साथ ही शार्दुल ठाकुर ने फिनिशिंग टचेस दी थी, 10 गेंदों में 23 रन बनाए थे, दो विकेट लेकर 45 रन देकर दो विकेट भी इन्होंने लिए थे। मयंक मार्कंडेय ने 30 रन देकर एक विकेट लिया था। दीपक चाहर ने यहां पर 34 रन देकर एक विकेट लिया था। इसके साथ ही यहां पर 198 रन 9 विकेट पर 20 ओवर में यहां पर शार्दुल 11 ने बनाए थे। दरअसल बॉल बाय बॉल इसके साथ ही जो फास्ट हाईलाइट है वो टेलीग्राम पर हम पोस्ट कर चुके हैं, तो फटाफट आप डिस्क्रिप्शन बॉक्स खोलकर टेलीग्राम चैनल को ज्वाइन कर लें। वहां पर सभी टीमों के लाइव प्रैक्टिस गेम भी चलते हैं, इसके साथ ही हर मैच की हाईलाइट सब कुछ वहां पर प्रोवाइड कर रहे टेलीग्राम पर। इंट्रा स्क्वाड मुकाबले भी देखने को मिलेंगे तो डिस्क्रिप्शन बॉक्स खोलकर आप टेलीग्राम चैनल पर पहुंच जाएं। फिर रोहित की टीम टारगेट का पीछा करने आई थी। रोहित की तरफ से यहां पर रोहित शर्मा ने बेहतरीन शुरुआत दी, नमन धीर ने उनके साथ ओपन किया था। नमन धीर ने 27 गेंदों में 51 रन बनाए, जबकि रोहित शर्मा यहां पर 43 गेंदों में 95 रन पर नाबाद थे जहां पर एक छक्का तो 121 मीटर का रोहित ने लगाया था। अपनी स्क्रीन पर देख पा रहे होंगे, इसके साथ ही दानिश मेलवार ने नाबाद 19 गेंदों में 34 रन बनाकर फिनिशिंग टचेस दी थी तो रोहित शर्मा 11 ने 199 रन चार विकेट पर केवल 17.5 ओवर में ही स्कोर कर लिया था। अभी विदेशी खिलाड़ियों ने टीमों को ज्वाइन नहीं किया है, केवल इंडियन प्लेयर इस मुकाबले का भाग हैं। इसके साथ ही रघु शर्मा ने तीन विकेट लिए यहां पर चार ओवर में 31 रन देकर। इसके साथ ही अश्विनी कुमार ने 23 रन देकर दो विकेट लिए और मोहम्मद इजहार ने बेहतरीन गेंदबाजी करी 21 रन देकर तीन विकेट चार ओवर में लिए थे, तो इस प्रकार से ये मुकाबला था। इस मुकाबले की कंप्लीट हाईलाइट हमने टेलीग्राम पर डाल दी है और भी बाकी टीमों के जो प्रैक्टिस चल रही है वो सब कुछ टेलीग्राम पर हम प्रोवाइड कर रहे हैं तो आप फटाफट टेलीग्राम चैनल को ज्वाइन कर लें और आप कमेंट करके बताइए और कौन सी टीमों की आप इंफॉर्मेशन जानना चाहते हो।

title: CSK Intra Squad Practice Match 2026 || CSK Practice Match 2026 Highlight | CSK Practice Today
transcription: दोस्तों, IPL 2024 के एडिशन के लिए अभी चल रहे प्रैक्टिस कैंप में चेन्नई की टीम ने आज इंट्रा-स्क्वाड प्रैक्टिस मुकाबला खेला था जहाँ पर MS Dhoni 11 बनाकर और ऋतुराज गायकवाड 11 बनाकर यहाँ पर प्रैक्टिस मुकाबला खेला गया था, जहाँ पर MSD 11 ने पहले टॉस जीतकर गेंदबाजी का फैसला किया था, ऋतु 11 को यहाँ पर पहले बल्लेबाजी कराई थी जहाँ पर ऋतुराज गायकवाड 11 से पहले गायकवाड ने यहाँ पर ओपन किया था, उनके साथ अरावली अवनीश पटेल ने ओपन किया था। दोनों ने ताबड़तोड़ शुरुआत करी जहाँ पर गायकवाड ने 30 गेंदों में 59 रन की बेहतरीन पारी खेली थी, इसके साथ ही यहाँ पर अरावली पटेल ने यहाँ पर 39 गेंदों में 90 रन की विस्फोटक पारी खेली थी। संजू सैमसन नंबर तीन पर आये थे, 18 गेंदों में 46 रन इन्होने बनाए थे, इसके साथ ही यहाँ पर घोष ने, रामकेश घोष ने यहाँ पर 18 रन 10 गेंदों में बनाए थे, इसके साथ ही 28 रन देकर एक विकेट भी लिया था, इसके साथ ही मुकेश चौधरी ने 32 रन देकर एक विकेट लिया था। श्रेयस गोपाल ने यहाँ पर 39 रन देकर तीन विकेट लिए थे और ऋतुराज गायकवाड 11 ने 20 ओवर में 226 रन 8 विकेट पर बनाए थे, बड़ा स्कोर बनाया था। MSD 11 जब टारगेट का यहाँ पर पीछा करने आई तो इनकी भी शुरुआत बेहतरीन रही थी जहाँ पर आयुष माथुर और सरफराज की बेहतरीन ओपनिंग जोड़ी थी। आयुष माथुर ने 45 रन 20 गेंदों में बनाए थे, सरफराज ने 40 गेंदों में 90 रन की पारी खेली थी। विस्फोटक ओपनिंग साझेदारी थी, जबकि यहाँ पर कार्तिक शर्मा नंबर तीन पर आये थे, 12 गेंदों में 30 रन इन्होने बनाए थे और एम एस धोनी ने यहाँ पर 45 रन 20 गेंदों में नाबाद पारी खेली थी, इसके साथ ही प्रशांत वीर भी 35 रन 16 गेंदों में बनाकर नाबाद रहे थे और 19.1 ओवर में 227 रन 5 विकेट पर बनाकर MSD 11 ने ये मुकाबला जीत लिया था जहाँ पर खलील अहमद ने 30 रन देकर दो विकेट लिए थे। राहुल चाहर ने 28 रन देकर चार विकेट लिए थे, इसके साथ ही इस मुकाबले की जो कम्पलीट 10 मिनट की हाईलाइट है वो हम टेलीग्राम पर डाल चुके हैं। बाकी टीमों की भी जो रोज़ इंट्रा-स्क्वाड प्रैक्टिस मुकाबले हो रहे हैं, सारी हाईलाइट्स टेलीग्राम पर आ रही हैं। टेलीग्राम पर लाइव मुकाबले भी आ रहे हैं तो आप फटाफट डिस्क्रिप्शन बॉक्स खोलकर टेलीग्राम चैनल को ज्वाइन कर लें, इसके साथ ही आप कमेंट करके बताइए आप कौन सी टीमों के आख़िर और इंट्रा-स्क्वाड प्रैक्टिस मुकाबलों की जानकारी चाहते हैं, आप कमेंट जरूर करें।

title: Marco Rubio Rails Against 'Globalist Bureaucrats' At ICC And 'So-Called International Law'
transcription: For 250 years, Americans have governed ourselves as a free and sovereign people. We choose our own leaders, we determine our own laws, and when we're accused of a crime, we stand for judgment before a jury of our own peers. This is the essential and indispensable feature of our form of government. It is the foundation of our shared way of life. But today, powerful people in faraway places want to take that away from us. They believe that they should be in charge of your laws, of your country, your life, and they don't care whether or not you agree. Halfway across the world, there's an institution that calls itself the International Criminal Court. Maybe you've heard of it, maybe you haven't. But chances are you don't know the names of its judges, of its prosecutors, or its president, and you shouldn't have to. But as we speak, the ICC and its friends are waging a war against our country, not with bullets or missiles, but with statutes and compacts and the force of so-called international law. When the ICC was born 24 years ago, they told us that it was merely a narrow backstop, a global court that would step in to prosecute only the gravest offenses, things like genocide and war crimes, and only when a nation's courts were unable to prosecute them on their own. But the truth is, it was something far more radical and extreme. It was a global tribunal staffed by unelected globalist bureaucrats who claim their power is almost unlimited. The danger of this global court has only continued to grow. Today, it threatens every aspect of our political and legal system. Border patrol agents removing violent criminals from our country, American Marines risking their lives to defend our homeland, prosecutors working to dismantle terrorist plots to attack and kill Americans. If we stand idle, all of them would be at the mercy of foreign judges thousands of miles away, facing the constant risk of prosecution and even imprisonment for the so-called crime of defending their own country. The American people never agreed to any of this, and they never will. Read the words of our Declaration of Independence. We fought a revolution against a foreign power transporting us beyond seas to be tried for pretended offenses. Independence is our birthright. We will never let foreign bureaucrats take that away from us. This administration will not sit by as the ICC and its allies seek to threaten our people. If they believe they can deprive us of our sovereignty, we will teach them the full meaning of American resolve.

transcription: I'm Katie Tarasov, here at Nvidia's annual GTC Developer Conference in San Jose, California, where CNBC will have live coverage throughout the event. I'm on the showroom floor where hundreds of companies are showing off products powered by Nvidia's chips and technologies, including a lot of robotics. 110 robots here, almost every single company in the world, I can't think of one that are building robots, is working with Nvidia. Humanoid robots from companies like Unitree, Booster, and LimX greeted me on the way in today. But the star event was, of course, CEO Jensen Huang's keynote. I just want to remind you, this is a tech conference. Nvidia's graphics processing units, GPUs, have proven absolutely crucial for powering generative AI, making the Silicon Valley giant the first ever to reach a $5 trillion market value last year. But now, agentic AI is shifting compute needs, and Nvidia is shifting strategy to match. It showed off a rack filled only with its central processing units, CPUs, at GTC this week. The more modest host chips usually act in a supporting role for GPUs but have suddenly found themselves in the limelight, creating an industry-wide renaissance as Nvidia says CPUs could be the next bottleneck for AI. Huang unveiled a new Groq language processing unit in his keynote Monday, built on technology acquired with Nvidia's largest purchase to date, $20 billion for Groq's assets in December. The new LPU has a single core, purpose-built for speeding up the GPU. It's expected to ship in the third quarter of 2026 and be integrated into a brand new rack dedicated to housing 256 of the new chips, increasing the token-per-watt performance of Rubin GPUs in the neighboring Vera Rubin rack 35 times. We united, unified two processors of extreme differences: one for high throughput, one for low latency. It still doesn't change the fact that we need a lot of memory. He also gave a sneak peek of this: Nvidia's Hyper architecture that will be available in the next Vera Rubin Ultra rack-scale system shipping in 2027. It totally changes the game for rack-scale systems by flipping the compute trays on their side to allow extreme density and much lower latency. Huang also met with reporters for a private Q&A session Tuesday. We've been, um, licensed for many customers in China for H200. That's right. transcription: Hi everyone. I am Anand Singh, Chief Security and Strategy Officer at Symmetry Systems, and this is my daughter, Aarushi Singh, undergraduate researcher and security practitioner. And honestly, we're not here to give you a standard, dry lecture. We're actually just here to finish an argument we started last Tuesday. It wasn't an argument, Aarushi. It was a spirited debate. Alright, well, that's why our session is called Cyber Family Feud, but this isn't about old versus young. It's about the clash between builders and accelerators. Exactly. And I represent the builders. We dig into the logs, optimize for failure modes, and frankly, we know where all the bodies are buried. And I represent the accelerators. I treat LLMs like junior engineers because I want to build security directly into the pipeline and move fast. Which is great until the automation is wrong. We can't forget how to actually reason through a problem when the quick fixes fail, which is why I am right, Aarushi. No, I'm right. See, this is the problem that most security teams are facing right now. The builders and the accelerators are speaking two entirely different languages. In our session, we are going to show you how to manage these two mindsets into what we call the Centaur model. We'll talk about how builders need to own the "why," the trust boundaries, and blast radius. And accelerators own the "how," the scaling, the automation, and the enforcement. If your security team feels disconnected, come join us. We'll give you a three-to-six months roadmap to get them operating on the same mission. So Aarushi, top answers on the board. Name the best way to get your builders and accelerators to stop fighting and actually secure your architecture. Well, they just need to come to our session at the RSA Conference. title: RSAC 2026 Conference Quick Look: The Impact of Security Usability Challenges in Cloud Environments
transcription: Hi everyone, my name is Alex Sierra and on behalf of myself and Alex Pinto, my co-presenter, I want to talk to you about a session CLS W09: The Impact of Security Usability Challenges in Cloud Environments. The point of this talk is we're going to be looking at a dataset that involves security posture checks on a variety of cloud providers, especially the hyperscalers: AWS, Azure, GCP, and OCI (Oracle Cloud Infrastructure). And we're going to correlate the UX decisions that they have made in the way that users can set up infrastructure, can set up credentials, can set up storage, with security outcomes. We're going to see how much, and if and how much, the way that the cloud providers decided to design their UI and their architecture are leading users to make more or less security mistakes. We feel like this is important for cloud providers and for people designing systems in general to understand the impact of their user experience design in security. Plus, we provide a series of practical recommendations for organizations, for companies, in the way that they use those cloud providers to minimize the impacts that those UX decisions have on their security posture. Hope to see you all there.

title: RSAC 2026 Quick Look: Model Collapse and Idiocracy: Ensuring the Future of AI Stays Intelligent
transcription: What if the biggest threat to AI isn't hackers? What if it's AI slowly getting dumber? We're told AI is getting smarter than humans, that it's evolving past us, but what if the opposite risk is just as real? What if AI stops learning from actual human intelligence? And what if the most powerful technology we've ever built starts averaging itself into mediocrity? That may sound like satire and in the movie Idiocracy decline took 500 years, but in AI, it might take five. Hi, I'm Diana Kelly, CISO at Noma Security. And at RSA conference 2026, I'm talking about model collapse and why it's a security issue, not just a research curiosity. We've fed AI the entirety of human wisdom, centuries of science, literature, engineering, medicine. But high quality human data is finite. At the same time, the internet is filling with AI generated content at industrial scale. And when systems start learning from degraded copies of their own output, something subtle happens. They forget the edges, diversity shrinks, nuance fades, and accuracy erodes. And in security, the edges are often where the real threats live. Detection gets harder, misinformation scales, and the attack surface expands. In the movie Idiocracy they kept insisting everything was fine, while trying to water their crops with the sports drink Brawndo. The real warning question though from that movie was, can a society recognize and act on its own decline while it is happening? We have the same choice now with AI. In this session, I'll share practical strategies to protect and steward the human signal, how to anchor models to real human data, how to prioritize edge cases instead of averages, and how to keep humans in the loop and govern synthetic data responsibly. The human signal built the first generation of AI. Whether AI survives the next generation is up to us. Join me at RSA Conference 2026 in person or online and let's ensure the future of AI stays intelligent.

title: Kevin Baum - Next Generation in AI Research IJCAI-ECAI 2026
transcription: Hi, I'm Dr. Kevin Baum and I lead the research group for Responsible AI and Machine Ethics at the German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence. Being a philosopher and computer scientist, I work on a problem that sounds simple, but that might be one of the most important ones in our lifetimes. The alignment problem. Put simply, it is about getting AI to do what we want in ways we find acceptable. But that framing actually hides the hard part. We live in a pluralist society and we do not agree on what we want or on what counts as acceptable. So aligning AI with human values is more than a technical challenge, it's a sociotechnical one under deep normative uncertainty. At bottom of it, it's a political problem. Whose values, decided by whom, and why? My group works on that challenge from a philosophical and a computer science point of view. We build architectures that make AI reason explicitly about norms and values, resulting in normatively competent systems that can act for the right reasons, state those reasons, and let human challenge and refine them, and we ground all that in philosophical theory. Here's why it matters. AI systems are becoming agents, making decisions in hospitals, courtrooms, and classrooms. The answer is not smarter machines, it is normatively more competent ones. Doing the right things for the right reasons, guided by real humans and keeping responsibility where it belongs.

transcription: As you've also heard, uh, coronary physiology continues to be underutilized, and there's probably a number of reasons. And we also now have randomized clinical trial data from Japan. 400 patients in the provisional trial across 13 Japanese sites looking at intermediate lesions. title: PulseCast: Highlights in Leukemias From the 2025 ASH Annual Meeting
transcription: Amir Fathi, a leukemia specialist at Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, Massachusetts. I was fortunate to attend the American Society of Hematology meeting this last December in Orlando, Florida, where multiple presentations covering a series of topics in myeloid malignancies were provided. It was an exciting meeting. There were multiple exciting presentations. Among them, we presented the results of PARADIGM, a phase 2 randomized study that compared intensive induction chemotherapy to less intensive azacitidine and venetoclax in fit, traditionally induction-eligible patients. The study met its primary endpoint: event-free survival was better for patients who received azacitidine and venetoclax. There were also multiple secondary endpoints that were important. The rate of overall response, composite remission, was significantly higher in patients who received azacitidine and venetoclax. Patients who received azacitidine and venetoclax also tolerated treatment better, with less incidence, with lower incidence of grade 3 or higher bleeding or infectious complications, decreased time in the hospital, as well as decreased admission during their initial course to the intensive care unit. There was also better quality of life and better patient-reported outcomes. This opens the field to potentially introducing less intensive therapies for patients that are traditionally thought to receive intensive chemotherapy, the long-term standard of care in AML, which allows tolerability, safety, but also allows them to move on to curative modalities such as stem cell transplant. There was also a series of presentations on the combination of azacitidine and venetoclax and targeted therapies, such as gilteritinib, the FLT3 inhibitor, as well as multiple menin inhibitors, such as ziftomenib. These data, although early, show significant promise also in patients with acute myeloid leukemia. I look forward to future meetings and ongoing progress in myeloid malignancies. Thank you.

title: Diary Entry I Wanted To Share With ALL Footballers...
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I wanted to share with you guys a diary entry that I wrote during a time that felt like nothing was going smoothly. And you might want to save this video for later because someday you're going to need it. Recently, I've been questioning why nothing in my life seems to be going smoothly. I've been playing football at a high level for years, training harder than everybody else, taking it more seriously than ever before. And still, I'm sitting here with no confirmed answer about where I'm playing next season. Football is competitive, I understand. I have been trying to get my European visa for the past year. I made three different applications and eventually left the country hopeless. And just two days after leaving, they called me for the acceptance meeting. Just two days after I'm out of the country, probably just bad timing, right? I graduated school with a top 1% mark, went to the best university in my country, signed with a professional club, and made a system so strong it changed the lives of 300 players remotely worldwide. And yet, parents are still skeptical to work with me and delay for months just to say no. Probably just a bad coincidence, right? This might be unrelated, but I even approached a trusted brand of dental braces, and halfway through the treatment, I was the first client in company history who had manufacturing issues, so I had to restart the process. And when they sent me the new one, the package got held at customs, and now I have no idea where the $4,000 worth of dental braces are. Just simple procedures that were initially planned to run smoothly and take a few months to complete are now becoming a headache because it's taking a few years to overcome. This is the side of football, the side of life that nobody ever talks about. Every single year without fail, I go through a season like this, a stretch where nothing seems to click, where it feels like the universe itself has turned against me. And here's the lesson I learned from this and what I wanted to share with you guys today. The toughest battles in life are given to the strongest warriors, not because life is cruel but because life is precise. The moment you decide to achieve something amazing, the moment you decide to become a professional footballer, the universe will place you in difficult situations to see what you're made of, to see whether you'll push through to the other side or whether you'll make excuses, blame the system, and quietly walk away from your dream like most people do. Most footballers quit before the breakout even happens, not because they weren't talented enough but because they stopped one season too early. And here's a harsh truth: for the majority of your life, you're going to be in the fight, you're going to be grinding, uncertain if it's going to work out, waiting for the right moment, pushing through the season when nothing feels fair. And then all of a sudden, for a small percentage of your life, everything is going to start to click. You're going to be playing your best football, your confidence is going to be untouchable, the doors are going to start opening up. And that moment right there, that moment is only beautiful because of everything that came before it. The goal in football or in life is not to avoid the hard season. The goal is to refuse to leave before the season ends. So, if you're in it right now, keep training, keep building, keep showing up every single day for your standards when everything around you feels like it's not. You will only fail the moment you decide to quit, and that's a guarantee. So, do not stop and keep pushing till the end.

title: How to Create a Line of Credit Account in QuickBooks Online (Step-By-Step) [2026 guide]
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to create a line of credit account in QuickBooks Online. Having a line of credit account set up in QuickBooks is essential for tracking borrowed funds and repayments accurately within your financial records. Whether you're managing a small business or keeping personal finances in order, this process will help you stay organized and ensure your books are complete and up to date. If you don't already have a QuickBooks Online account, you can use the link in the description to sign up and get started. Now, let's dive into the steps. First, start by logging into your QuickBooks Online account and navigating to your dashboard. Look to the top right corner of the screen where you'll see a small gear icon. This is your settings menu. Go ahead and click on it to open the options. From the dropdown menu that appears, you'll need to scroll down and select the option labeled "Chart of accounts." This is where all your accounts are managed and organized within QuickBooks. Once you're on the chart of accounts page, look towards the upper right corner of the screen again and click the button labeled "New." This will allow you to create a new account. Next, you'll need to enter a name for the account you're setting up. You can choose something straightforward like "Line of Credit," or use a name that better suits your specific needs. It's helpful to pick a name that makes the account easily recognizable when you're reviewing your records later. After naming the account, it's time to assign the correct account type. In the dropdown menu for account type, select "Long-term Liabilities." This category is appropriate because a line of credit typically represents a financial obligation that spans longer than a year. Once you've set the account type, move to the detail type field. From this list, choose "Notes Payable." This detail type is the most accurate for a line of credit, as it represents loans or borrowings that need to be repaid. Finally, click the "Save" button to complete the process and create your new line of credit account. Once saved, the account will appear in your chart of accounts list, and you'll be able to use it to track transactions related to your line of credit. And that's it! You've successfully created a line of credit account in QuickBooks Online. If you found this video helpful, please like and subscribe.

title: Video 3: Why is sharing your radiotherapy treatment story important to you?
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: It's been really important to me all along to share my story of my treatment, my diagnosis, my treatment and my recovery, to whoever will listen, to be perfectly honest. My first desire was to tell fellow patients, and I was interviewed by a radiation oncologist. My answers to my, her questions were recorded, and those videos have been shared by doctors and other cancer team members to thousands of people who've been diagnosed with a head and neck cancer. And I'm just so grateful that clinicians have seen the value of sharing a patient's story. I think there's no substitute for a patient who's about to have radiotherapy to hear the story of a fellow patient, not only just describe what the treatment's like and the recovery's like, but just to see a patient who's survived, who's survived cancer. Because I think so many of us when we get that cancer diagnosis, we're just full of anxiety and fear, and there's nothing as reassuring as seeing a patient who's gone through it and come out the other side. But I also think it's good for cancer team members to see these videos because it, it exposes them to the emotional and psychological impact of a cancer diagnosis and the treatment. And if they can hear the patient's story, empathize, uh, understand emotionally, feel some of those feelings, I think they're much more likely to do research and make an effort to help us psychologically, which I think is as important as survival.

title: I Called My Parents and Said "I Need Help" | Logan's Story
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Before treatment, I was I was broken. I had a lot of depression, anxiety and was using drugs and alcohol to mask all that, to cope with it. I just remember feeling so hopeless. I just broke down and I called my mom and I called my dad and I said, "I need help." I remember at that moment I I still didn't feel great but I felt for the first time that I might be headed in the right direction. In terms of choosing this treatment center, I remember there was a family friend that we had. She said, "If I had a family member going through what Logan's going through, there's only one place I would send them and that was Providence." I think walking around the center and talking to different staff, you know, a lot of the clinicians made me feel like I was understood for the first time in a in almost forever. It was also fun, too. I think that's something I didn't expect is the idea that I can work on myself and I can do the tough things and I can have the groups where I tear up and I can go into individual session and talk about things I haven't talked about but at the same time with all my peers and and even a lot of the staff I was just laughing and I was having a good time. Life now is great. I don't worry people anymore. Soon after graduating Providence, I got hired and I really just started to find my purpose and find my life. The advice I would give someone that's still struggling is stop digging. Find the people in your life who care about you and ask them for help. The answers to the questions that people might have of what happens after treatment, answer themselves when you just give into the experience. So, ask for help. Uh stop digging. title: Blue Monday
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription:
Let's talk therapy. My name is Rafal Kolary from Edinburgh Taxi Therapy.

Blue Monday, it is a concept that the third Monday of January, it's been named the most depressing day of the year. This is the time when people usually struggle with paying the bills, as well as they struggle with the New Year's Eve resolution and how December went for them.

After Christmas, after New Year's Eve, we feel that our motivation is a little bit lower. Then, when we look outside, the weather, it's not the best one. This is not Gran Canaria, Tenerife or any other hot spot. It's Scotland. It's raining, it's gloomy, and we are affected by that.

Money pressure have huge impact on how we feel. Obviously, the Christmas finished, the New Year's Eve is over. We are back to reality. We are back to making sure that we need to cover our daily expectations, have enough money for food, have enough money for our life, and then the money are not coming because it's still almost middle of January. That's when the anxiety, low mood, depression might come to the picture.

In regards to seeking the support, you might feel that your mood is low, the anxiety is there. You do not feel well about yourself, and your self-esteem is being affected. However, you do not have to wait for the crisis to kick in. Sometimes it's better to work with the prevention. It's better to make sure that everything is fine. This is the perfect moment to look for the support.

It's important to find a space, a safe space, confidential one, where you would be able to explore your feelings and understand what is going on in your life.

My personal reflection in regards of the Blue Monday is, this is the moment when it's time to get out from the house. It is the moment to introduce some exercises, enjoy the sun while you can catch it, spend some times with your friends, and if this doesn't help, maybe look for the support like Edinburgh Taxi Therapy, or any other psychologists which are available in your neighborhood.

title: Just a little flower and talk therapy for my fellow moms... #Shorts #lindseybosway
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: My two boys are napping. I have my coffee and I'm going to use just Trader Joe's flowers and make a little arrangement. Let's chat motherhood. After I had my first baby, I think looking back on it, I had more postpartum anxiety than I even knew at the time. And I did not feel like myself for like 15 months. And part of that was just like no creative drive, no desire to really do anything outside of motherhood. And when I had my second, it was definitely better, but I just remember one day he was like 12 months old and I was like, "Oh, I want to make a flower arrangement." And I was like, "Oh gosh, I'm coming back." But it is wild. So, if you're not there yet, if you just had a baby and you feel like you're not yourself, I promise it gets better. And one day you'll feel like doing something again that requires energy. But it's okay if right now you just want to nap when your baby naps. So, I just made a little grid here. That'll make it easier to stick our flowers in. And once I started doing flowers when they were napping, I feel like I have so much more energy on the days that I do it. I think it's just like using your brain for something other than motherhood, and it gives me like a jolt of energy. And often times, when we're dealing with our babies or toddlers, it's such chaos. And I just find arranging flowers to be so peaceful and meditative once you really get into it. I always think about that one creator who talks about getting her pink back. And, you know, it went viral or whatever, but it's so true. And when you're a first time mom, you have no perspective on the fact that it does come back. Your second time around is a little easier because you know what's going on, and you know that it's okay to feel that way. But it can be really jarring when you have your first baby, and you don't understand that it's temporary. It really is. Like my biggest piece of advice that I give friends is just to try to remember in motherhood that everything is temporary. It's looking really pretty, but we have a lot of space to fill in. A few finishing touches here. I also think, in motherhood, it is okay if one day you want to make this huge, amazing arrangement, and the next day you don't want to. You put your kids to bed, and you spend the next hour in your bed. It's just okay. That's how it goes. And you know what I've stopped doing? Bullying myself for that. Just let myself relax. I don't ever go to a space of shame. Because you know what's not relaxing? Sitting down, trying to relax, and worrying about the fact that you're relaxing. Here she is. She's whimsical. She's fall. I love her.

title: Deepening Self-Awareness: Practical Activities and Reflections #selfgrowth #mentalhealth #selflove
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Self-awareness helps us better understand the thoughts, emotions, and patterns that shape our lives. Here are three simple ways to deepen your self-awareness. Number one, journaling your thoughts. Sometimes clarity begins when you finally see your thoughts on paper. Number two, sitting quietly with your emotions, not avoiding them, not distracting yourself, just noticing them. Number three, asking yourself difficult but honest questions: "What triggers my stress?", "What patterns keep repeating in my life?" At American Behavioral Clinics, we believe self-awareness is one of the most important steps toward emotional wellness and personal growth. Because self-awareness isn't about perfection. It's about noticing, understanding, growing. American Behavioral Clinics, helping people better understand themselves, one step at a time.

title: The Bright Side of AI
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: With all the AI gloom and doom, I often forget how cool AI actually is. Like, what a technology, what a time to be alive. You know, like, I often have this heaviness about it, and more of this, "I gotta use this. I gotta make this work. I need to catch up with with the trends and everything, not to fall behind." And what I lose sight of sometimes is how amazing this technology is, and I just, today, I had this case of, hey, you can, you can use AI to analyze your thought patterns, like your personal thought patterns, and not only can you understand how you think, but obviously also where your blind spots are, and and how you can improve your thinking, and how, what are, what the patterns are, and this, getting this awareness about yourself, in all kinds of areas, obviously professionally, how you make decisions, but but also in private, it's such an amazing feat, to be honest. This technology didn't exist. Like, how would you else, like, get to this? Like, of course, if you do therapy for 10 years, which nobody wants, and and I'm not really a fan of it, still, there's this other person processing it, and you probably not get to the root of it. Now, you can upload hours, hundreds of hours of you interacting in in Zoom calls, whatever it is, and you can have AI analyze, find out your thought patterns, even like making your thoughts visible to yourself. And I just thought, how amazing, and this is just one use case, obviously. There's so much to be had also with this technology. It's scary. It's It puts a pressure on myself, and I guess on you as well, but it's also fabulous, and this is my, my little reminder to myself, and maybe to you, that if you, if you set aside this, this pressure, this, this fear maybe even, and and let in the, the possibilities and the opportunity a little bit more, it could be tremendously fun to interact with this technology, and and all the, the beautiful things that can come from that. transcription: Anatomy of sadness. Feet of gloom, heart of contempt, stomach ailing, consuming, intestines disposing. Ears curved but not bent, hearing words of one cent. Chest broad with pain. You can call me Built because my tears fall like rain. Teeth yellow with fear. Grinding joy, genitalia of a hermaphrodite. Warm, moist womb of misery. Penis, a knife. Soul torn to shreds like that of a goat's bite. Nose aware of the stench of foulness filling the air. Arms and legs long, no power, no strength. Keeps me weak, unable to carry on. My hair's not nappy, but woolly like Jesus's, who just like me was at times unhappy. Waited for a resurrection three days too long, but my angels sing a melancholy song. My mind full of thoughts getting heavier. My eyes change color like the leaves in fall, and glow like a cat's when night falls.

title: You Don’t Have To Be Okay Right Now (Listen to This)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Hey, I don't know what you're going through right now, but I have a feeling it's been heavy, not just one thing, but everything at once. Your thoughts, your emotions, the pressure you put on yourself, it's a lot, and maybe you've been telling yourself that you should be handling it better, that you should be stronger than this. But listen, you don't have to be okay right now. You don't have to have everything figured out. You don't have to pretend that nothing is bothering you. You're allowed to feel overwhelmed, you're allowed to feel tired, especially if you've been holding everything in for so long. And I know your mind might not stop going over the same thoughts again and again, thinking about everything that could go wrong or everything you wish you did differently, but not every thought you have is telling you the truth. Sometimes, your mind is just exhausted. So, just for a second, take a breath with me, slowly in and out. You don't need to fix your whole life tonight. You don't need to solve everything all at once, just focus on this moment, just getting through right now, that's enough. And even if it doesn't feel like it, you're doing better than you think. You've made it through days that felt impossible before. You're still here, and that matters more than you realize. So, if today felt like too much, if you felt overwhelmed, if you felt like you were falling behind, just know this, you're not alone in that feeling, and you don't have to carry it all perfectly. You don't have to be okay, you just have to keep going, one moment at a time.

title: Are You Okay... Really?
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: We ask it out of habit every single day, but we rarely listen for the truth. "How are you? Are you okay?" "Yeah, I'm fine." It's the ultimate American defense mechanism. We live in a culture that glorifies the grind, praises independence, and tells us to "fake it till we make it." So when things get heavy, our language shrinks. We reduce an entire ocean of burnout, anxiety, and quiet exhaustion into a single automatic wall. "Have you been crying?" "No, just tired." "Just tired." It's the perfect cover-up. Because nobody questions it. In a world where everyone is exhausted, it's easy to hide. But there's a massive difference between needing sleep and being tired of waking up feeling empty. Depression doesn't always look like tears or dramatic breakdowns. In reality, it looks like complete isolation. It's sitting in a crowded room in New York or a quiet suburb in Ohio, surrounded by people, yet feeling entirely invisible. It's building walls so high that even the people who love you can't reach you. "Do you want to talk about it? You can tell me anything." "No, there's nothing to talk about." When someone pushes you away, it's rarely a rejection. Most of the time, they literally just don't have the words. How do you explain a profound sadness that has no specific cause? How do you tell your family or your friends that your life looks great on paper, but feels completely hollow inside? So they say "No," hoping you'll leave them alone, but secretly praying that you won't. They don't need a lecture, they don't need a motivational speech, toxic positivity, or a 10-step plan on how to fix their life. "Do you want a hug?" "Yeah." Sometimes saving a life doesn't take a hero, it doesn't take the perfect words. It just takes the willingness to sit in the dark with someone. The most powerful thing you can say to someone who is drowning isn't "I understand." It's simply, "I'm here, and you don't have to carry this alone." Right now, millions of people are fighting battles they don't talk about. And ironically, the people who spend all their energy checking on everyone else are often the ones drowning the fastest. Do me a favor today. Don't just send a casual text asking "How's it going?" Call someone, look them in the eyes, break through the automatic answers. Because you never truly know how heavy a burden is until you offer to help hold it. Check on your people today.

title: Inside the Mind of Someone Who Feels Alone | Deep Narration About Loneliness
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Sometimes the loneliest feeling isn't when you're alone, it's when you're surrounded by people and still feel like you don't belong. The room is full of voices, laughter, conversations, noise, but somehow, none of it reaches you. You smile when they look at you, you nod like you're listening, you say you're fine, because it's easier than explaining what's going on inside your head. Sometimes you hold your phone, staring at the screen, wanting to text someone, but not knowing who would understand. You start typing, then delete everything, because how do you explain a feeling you don't even understand yourself? Outside, the world keeps moving. People walk with purpose, cars pass by. Everyone seems to be going somewhere. And you wonder why you feel stuck in the same place, every single day. Loneliness isn't always silence. Sometimes it's noise that doesn't include you. Sometimes it's laughing with people, but feeling nothing inside. Sometimes it's going home and realizing, no one really knows how you feel. You sit in your room, the lights are off. The only sound is your own thoughts, and they don't stop. You ask yourself questions: Why do I feel like this? Why can't I connect? Why does everything feel so far away? But even on days like this, when the silence feels too loud, a small part of you is still there. Still breathing, still trying, still hoping. And sometimes, that's enough. Sometimes, making it through the day while feeling alone is already a victory. And maybe tomorrow feels lighter. Maybe not easier, but a little less heavy. And that small difference can keep you going. You can follow for more simple psychology explained.

Uh and forgive the like little history lesson here, but I found this super interesting. Uh there's this thing called the Jevons paradox. Uh back in the 1800s, this guy William Jevons, he noticed that when steam engines were getting much more efficient, right? We like crossed this threshold where steam engines were getting super super efficient. So the hypothesis was, hey, we're going to use less coal. Well, what happened was people didn't use less coal, the tech was so good that there were more and more steam engines. So everybody got a steam engine and total coal use exploded, right? So how does that relate to this? Well, we're seeing the exact same thing in fundraising right now. As the friction of giving goes down, the initial cost of entry is smaller. The volume of committed donors is really booming. And so donors aren't pulling back, they're moving faster, committing a little bit differently. Smaller upfront gifts don't necessarily mean lower donor value. Organizations that are winning in 2026 will build their revenue architecture around how donors are actually giving today. title: How To Create a Winning Pitch Deck | Experienced Voices
transcription: Hello, I'm Jean Gray, publisher of American Entrepreneurship Today. Welcome to this special video tutorial from our Experienced Voices podcast series. A great pitch deck doesn't just show data. It tells a compelling story. It is the single most important asset you have when raising capital. Today we're breaking down the eight essential elements that captivate investors and turn that maybe into a yes. Let's dive in. Every successful company starts by identifying a genuine pain point. Don't just list facts, tell a story. Who is hurting and why is the current way of doing things broken? Make the investor feel the friction of the status quo. If they don't feel the pain, they won't value your medicine. Now present your solution. This is where you introduce your product or service as a hero of the story. Focus on the benefits, the so what, not just the technical features. Show, don't tell. A quick demo or a high-quality product render works best here to make your vision feel real. Investors want to back big wins. This is your chance to show the scale of the opportunity. Clearly define your TAM, your SAM, and your SOM. Use credible third-party data to prove that this market is not only large but growing. Prove that this is a venture-scale opportunity worth their time. How do you turn this into a profitable machine? Briefly explain your revenue model. But more importantly, show your traction. Whether it's user growth, pilot programs, or revenue milestones, show that your theory has been validated by the market. Traction is the ultimate risk reducer. Never say you have no competition. It implies you haven't done your research. Acknowledge the landscape, then clearly articulate your unfair advantage, or moat. Why are you different, and why is that difference defensible? Focus on why you win, not just where they fall short. Investors bet on jockeys, not just on horses. Highlight why your team has the unique expertise to execute this vision. Then pivot to the ask. Be transparent. How much are you raising, and what specific milestones will this capital unlock? Be confident, clear, and focused on the future. Finally, wrap up with a summary of your vision. One powerful sentence that captures the future you're building. Thank your audience, and leave them with a clear next step, whether that's your website, an email link, or a direct invite to a demo. The deck is your foot in the door. Now it's time to walk through it. I hope you found our funding tutorial helpful. Please like, share, and subscribe so we may bring more content supporting your entrepreneurial journey. Check out our full Experienced Voices podcast series. Look for more segments that help you start, fund, and grow your business.

title: The Perfect 60-Second Startup Pitch (Investors Will Remember)
transcription: The perfect 60-second startup pitch. Imagine you step into an elevator with your dream investor. You have exactly 60 seconds before the doors open. Would you know what to say? Most founders make one big mistake. They try to explain everything about their business. The truth is, your goal isn't to close the investment in 60 seconds. It's to make the investor want another conversation. Here's a simple framework that works. First, start with the problem. What pain are you solving? Keep it simple and relatable. If the investor doesn't understand the problem, they won't care about the solution. Next, explain your solution. In one sentence, describe what your company does. Avoid technical jargon or long explanations. If someone outside your industry can't understand it, it's probably too complicated. Then, explain why now. Why is this the right time for your business? Maybe a new technology has made your solution possible. Maybe customer behavior has changed. Maybe the market is growing rapidly. Investors want to know why this opportunity exists today, not 5 years ago. After that, share your traction. You don't need millions in revenue, but you do need evidence that you're making progress. That could be paying customers, user growth, partnerships, pilot programs, or even a growing waitlist. Traction reduces uncertainty and builds confidence. Finally, finish with the opportunity. Don't end by asking for money. Instead, leave the investor wanting to learn more. Give them a reason to schedule a second meeting. Remember, a great pitch doesn't answer every question. It answers just enough to create curiosity. If an investor walks away wanting to know more, you've done your job. The best founders don't overwhelm investors with information. They tell a clear story, communicate confidence, and make their business easy to understand. Because at the end of the day, investors don't invest in the longest pitch, they invest in the clearest one. If you found this video helpful, subscribe to the Pitch Network for more practical advice on fundraising, networking, and building startups that investors want to back.

title: The 5 Things Angel Investors Look for Before They Invest
transcription: How angel investors actually decide to invest. Imagine you've spent months, maybe even years, building your startup. You finally get a meeting with an angel investor. You walk in, deliver what you think is the perfect pitch, and they pass. So what happened? The truth is, angel investors aren't just investing in ideas. They're investing in founders. They're investing in execution. And most importantly, they're investing in the probability that your business can succeed. Here are the five things they're really looking for. First, the founder. This is by far the most important factor. Investors know that startups rarely go exactly according to plan. Markets change, products evolve, and unexpected problems come up all the time. They're asking themselves one simple question: Can this founder figure it out? A great founder is resilient, adaptable, and able to execute even when things don't go as planned. Second, the problem. Is it a real problem that people genuinely want solved? Or is it just a nice idea? The bigger and more painful the problem, the more valuable the solution becomes. Great businesses solve expensive problems, not minor inconveniences. Third, the market. Even an incredible product has limited potential if it's built for a tiny audience. Investors look for large growing markets because they want companies that can scale. If the opportunity isn't big enough, neither is the return. Fourth, traction. One of the biggest myths is that you need massive revenue before investors will take you seriously. That's simply not true. What investors really want is evidence that people care. That could be growing users, paying customers, partnerships, a waiting list, or strong engagement. Any sign that the market is responding positively reduces the risk of investing. And finally, why you? What's stopping another company from copying your idea tomorrow? Maybe it's your experience, maybe it's your technology, your network, your community, or simply your ability to execute faster than everyone else. The strongest startups don't just have a great idea. They have a compelling reason why they're the best team to bring that idea to life. At the end of the day, angel investing is all about reducing risk. Every customer you gain, every milestone you hit, and every problem you solve gives investors one more reason to believe. Because investors don't invest in certainty, they invest in confidence. title: Inside the VC Mindset: What Makes a Pitch Win

What is crucial if you want a VC to fund your business idea? First, what is a VC? VC stands for Venture Capitalist. A VC is someone who gives money to new businesses they believe can grow big. Instead of getting paid back like a loan, they receive part ownership of the business. If the business succeeds, they succeed, too. Because of that, VCs don't invest in just any idea. They invest in ideas that are clear, realistic, and ready to grow. That's where the winning pitch formula comes in. First is the problem. You must clearly explain a real pain point people actually have. Second, the solution. What is your product or service, and how does it work? Third, the value proposition. Why is your solution better or different from others? Fourth, the market. Who is this for, and how many people need it? Fifth, the business model. How does your idea make money? Next is traction. You don't need perfect numbers, but you need to show you understand costs and revenue. Then there's the ask. How much money are you asking for, and what are you offering in return? Finally, vision and scale. Show how your idea can grow bigger in the future. If you can clearly explain all 10 of these, a VC is much more likely to listen. Thanks for watching. title: Why Didn't Robinhood Blame AI for Layoffs?
transcription: Why didn't Robinhood blame AI for layoffs? Robinhood is still cutting about 290 jobs, even as the company reports growth, and CEO Vlad Tenev left AI out of the memo entirely. The company is still shrinking its workforce while saying the business is growing, so the message is blunt. The cuts are about the company's structure, not a public AI excuse. That silence stands out because many tech companies have started using AI language in layoff announcements. Amazon, Block, Coinbase, GitLab, and Intuit have all used similar logic around leaner teams, less bureaucracy, and fewer silos. Robinhood chose not to join that script. Instead, the note pointed away from AI and toward a broader internal reset. That analyst view reinforces the point. In other words, if AI was already part of the machine, it could not be the easy excuse for the cuts. The company's internal message had to point somewhere else. This is why the Robinhood memo is getting attention beyond one company. Tech firms are under pressure to justify layoffs at the same time AI tools are being sold as efficiency machines. Robinhood's choice suggests that the AI blame game may be losing credibility fast. If a company already uses AI broadly, saying AI caused the cuts starts to sound like a cover story, not an explanation. Robinhood cut 10% of its staff, about 290 jobs, but skipped the AI script that many peers now lean on. The real takeaway is simple. title: Which Accounting Roles Face Ai-Related Layoffs Affecting You?
transcription: The first accounting roles hit hardest by AI are those focused on routine data entry. Tasks like inputting invoices, receipts, and basic bookkeeping are now automated by advanced software. This reduces errors and speeds up processes, but it means these jobs are shrinking fast. If your role is mostly manual data input, AI could replace it soon. Next up are roles dealing with transaction processing and reconciliations. AI algorithms can quickly match transactions, flag anomalies, and even perform initial audits. This reduces the need for humans to do repetitive checks. Accountants focused on these basic functions are seeing layoffs as companies invest in AI tools to cut costs. Junior auditors often perform routine tests on financial data. AI systems can now analyze vast data sets faster and more accurately, identifying risks and inconsistencies. This automation means fewer junior auditors are needed for standard audits, though experienced auditors still focus on complex and judgment-based tasks. Despite AI layoffs, roles requiring complex judgment, strategic thinking, and client interaction remain strong. Senior accountants, financial analysts, and consultants rely on skills AI cannot easily replicate. The takeaway is clear: upskilling toward advisory, strategy, and technology management will future-proof your accounting career. Subscribe for daily answers to questions you didn't know you had.

Tonight, new political turmoil. Alabama and Tennessee are the latest states rushing to redraw congressional districts after a Supreme Court ruling that further weakened voting rights. CBS News Congressional Correspondent Nicole Killion has the latest. Nicole.

Six months out from the midterms and the redistricting wars are intensifying for control of Congress after a recent Supreme Court ruling rolled back a key part of the Voting Rights Act. The Supreme Court's 6-to-3 decision to strike down Louisiana's congressional map hits right in the heart of Cleo Fields' seat. The district was created, first of all, Louisiana's minority population, black population, is over a third of the state. The Democrat represents the sixth congressional district, which slinks from Shreveport to Baton Rouge. But the high court ruled the newly drawn majority-minority district was an unconstitutional gerrymander since it was based on race. Congressman Troy Carter represents the other majority-minority district in New Orleans. It can wipe out both of our seats. We can, realistically, end up having six congressional districts with no African-American or Democratic representation. Ahead of early voting this weekend, Louisiana officials suspended House primary elections slated for November until the state can redraw its map. I don't think that it's going to result in a loss of minority representation, and I think that we have to give the—the people a chance to draw their districts the way the people want to see them drawn. Before the Supreme Court ruling, at least seven states had already passed new congressional maps as part of mid-decade redistricting. Now, several Southern states are using the High Court's decision to justify changes before the midterms, including Florida, Alabama, and Tennessee. It was really not about, you know, that little seat in Louisiana. It's about redistricting all over the nation. It's about the voting rights of people all over the nation. While these new moves by Southern states could potentially net more Republican seats, Democrats are vowing to fight back and are looking to other blue states that could possibly change their maps in the 2028 cycle. Jericka. Nicole Killion, thank you so much.
