title: Supreme Court appears skeptical of mail-in ballots that arrive after Election Day
transcription: The Supreme Court just finished hearing arguments in a major case that raises questions about the legality of mail-in voting. And the conservative justices appeared skeptical about allowing states to count ballots that are mailed on time, but arrive after Election Day. The court's ruling could upend the voting process in more than a dozen states just months before this November's midterm elections. NBC News legal affairs reporter Gary Grumbach joins us now. So, Gary, this case stems from an election law in Mississippi, so walk us through it and what we've heard so far from the justices. Yeah, the oral arguments were supposed to be about whether postmarked ballots by Election Day could be accepted after Election Day, but it really turned into a debate on a variety of different election-related topics, from who is actually delivering that ballot to the state, topics about like ballot harvesting, to conversations about potentially people being able to recall their votes. For example, if you were to send something in via FedEx, could you tell FedEx, "Oh no, I actually want that back"? And then there was conversations about the length of time the state allows a voter to be able to get their ballot in and have it count. So, for example, some states do a week, some states do 21 days. Conservative Justice Samuel Alito, predictably, was pretty upset about all of this. He said, "We used to have Election Day, now it's election month or election months," guys. Gary, if the Supreme Court does rule in favor of the RNC and Mississippi's GOP, what does that essentially mean more broadly for the rest of the country when it comes to these midterms? So, Mississippi was the state that was arguing this and defending their own law, but there's 13 other states that have similar laws, so this would be a very significant thing for almost half the country here in terms of whether or not ballots would be allowed to be counted after Election Day. You have a map there that shows states, both red and blue states, that we're looking at there. And it also specifically relates to some of these military ballots, right? Folks that are serving overseas in our military, especially right now, uh may not be able to get their ballots in on time even though they are postmarked by Election Day. We will have to see exactly how the justices write this opinion, which we should be getting it by the end of June. We thank you for watching, and remember, stay updated on breaking news and top stories on the NBC News app or watch live on our YouTube channel.

title: Supreme Court weakens the Voting Rights Act after 61 years
transcription: The US Supreme Court dealt a blow to the landmark Voting Rights Act on Wednesday after knocking out a major pillar of the law that had protected against racial discrimination in voting and representation. In the six decades since it was signed, the Voting Rights Act became one of the most consequential laws in the nation's history, preventing discrimination against minorities at the ballot box. It also helped elect Black and Hispanic representatives at all levels of government. But on Wednesday, the Supreme Court hollowed out the landmark civil rights era law by striking down a majority Black congressional district in Louisiana. That ruling could provide an open door for political mapmakers to undermine minority representation. The Voting Rights Act was signed into law by President Lyndon B. Johnson on August 6, 1965, five months after the Bloody Sunday attack on civil rights marchers in Selma, Alabama, gave momentum to the bill. Wherever there is discrimination, this law will strike down all restrictions used to deny the people the right to vote. In recent years, AP reporter Gary Fields sat down with some of the people who were pivotal to the birth of the Act. After having talked to these individuals and to a number of other people about why voting rights was so important, the reason for why they were so important then hasn't changed now. In a democracy or a republic such as ourselves, the vote is the thing that you have that is the coin of the realm that allows you to say I'm a full participant in this society, in this endeavor that we call the United States of America. The question now is what comes next for minority representatives and the communities they represent.

title: Supreme Court Steps In After Judge Orders Trump Arrested Live—Emergency Appeal Changes Everything.
transcription:
The sealed 94-page leak: What nobody is connecting yet.

A sealed 94-page federal grand jury transcript leaked Tuesday night, and the legal fallout is already escalating. Federal grand jury testimony is classified as secret under Rule 6 of the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure, meaning this document was never supposed to exist in the public domain. Yet, at 11:47 p.m. on Tuesday, the full unredacted transcript hit ProPublica's servers. Someone on the inside broke protocol to leak it, which is a federal felony in itself. However, the true significance lies within the contents of the testimony, specifically, brand new sworn statements provided by former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson during an undisclosed session in January 2026. Unlike her previous public appearances, this fourth session under oath involved different prosecutors, different targets, and crucial documentary evidence. On page 12 of the transcript, when asked if she maintained personal knowledge of White House communications, Hutchinson revealed that she kept a personal record comprising text message screenshots, calendar entries, and three handwritten journals. Because these were maintained as personal records, rather than official government property, they fall outside standard executive privilege claims and cannot be shielded as easily. Hutchinson essentially created her own paper trail, which has now become central to the prosecution's case. The transcript lays out a detailed timeline of post-election strategy. Page 18 introduces Exhibit 47, a November 9, 2024, text message from Mark Meadows instructing Hutchinson to establish a direct line with former DOJ official Jeffrey Clark and then Michigan Senate Majority Leader Mike Shirkey. Page 23 details a November 11th conference call arranged by Hutchinson featuring Donald Trump, Mark Meadows, Jeffrey Clark, Mike Shirkey, Rudy Giuliani, an Arizona State Senator, and Hutchinson herself. According to her testimony, the explicit topic of the call was developing strategies to delay election certification in Michigan and Arizona, focusing directly on disrupting the certification process, rather than pursuing standard court challenges.

title: [HIGHLIGHT] How DEVO Created the “Whip It” Sound (The Real Story) - From EP 379
transcription: Robert Margouleff is memoir Shaping Sounds, Stevie Wonder, DEVO, the Synth Revolution and My Life Behind the Music. You describe DEVO as wanting to put an alien head on an R&B body. What did that phrase mean to you in, in musical terms? Well, uh, just as a quick aside, the thing is this, the, the DEVOs love R&B. They grew up listening to R&B. So when I came on board, I made really sure that the bottom end of their records was really R&B. There was, the band was a small band. It was not meant to have lots of overdubs. It was, should be, it was a simple band. Everyone played their part, one part each, right? When they played together, it was an ensemble. But it was more like a string quartet. It was tight and it was together, but it had an R&B bottom end. And I made very sure that that stuck, that the bottom end, the kick in the bass, were the R&B, had the R&B feel. And then they put the, the monster on the top. But it was an R&B body with a, with an alien head. That's what DEVO is. Yeah. When you first heard it, do-do-do-do-do, ping, dow, were you thinking? Five up, two down. Da-da-da-da-da, five notes. Bam-bam, two notes down. Very simple, very easy to remember, very impulsive feel. Those guys are marvelous. Mark is a marvelous songwriter. Jerry knows how to really write the lyrics. Jerry is a real politician. And you know, he just had a baby last year or the year before. And he's, He's pushing 70. But they also had that genius in the idea of the, uh, image, you know, the look. Yeah. When you look at their live show, you can, when you look at their live show, you really realize how really tight and highly organized they are. They are absolute geniuses at this stuff. All we had to do is just not drip stuff all over them, sugar coating and syrup and bullshit, and just let them play their instruments and play out, and maintain their impulsive energy. And by bringing them into the control room, I was able to do that, and allow the cross talk and the energy and everything else to really fulfill itself, super loud and quad in the control room.

title: How Indie Creators Are Building Shows With Shorts
transcription: Vertical short-form animation used to feel to me like this weird side quest. Like something you did for the algorithm, but not for your actual career. But lately, I've been seeing indie animators use shorts to quietly build entire worlds. Characters, shows, fan bases, momentum. So today, I want to break down the storytelling formats that are actually working and how you can use them for your own projects. Because here's the truth: most of us don't get to make a full series right away. We don't get handed a season order and a budget and a team. We build things slowly. And shorts are how a lot of creators are doing that right now. They help you test ideas, grow an audience, prove there's really something there. They're not throwaway content. They're like micro-pilots, proof of concepts. I've been doing this storytelling thing for a while now, in studios and independently. And the creators who are really winning in short form aren't just posting random clips. They're actually telling tiny, strategic stories. Hi, I'm Emily Brundige, and I create cartoons for a living. Over the past decade, I've pitched and sold eight original animated shows. Most recently, I created my own original animated show, Goldie, for Apple TV. It's been nominated for two Emmys, including Best Writing. When I look at the shorts that turn into long-term fandoms, I see the same three storytelling models that really work. They seem simple, but structurally, they're doing something very smart. Let's start with the most classic storytelling format. Self-contained stories. Mummy Joe is a great example of this. Every short is its own tiny episode: beginning, middle, and end. Nothing carries over, so you can click on any one, and you're not lost, you're just in. Why does this work? title: Audio Files: Lessons NOT YET Learned
transcription: The Tech on Demand podcast brought to you by GrowerTalks. Audio Files Episode 76. Lessons Not Yet Learned. From the February 2026 issue of Green Profit magazine, written by Bill McCurry, narrated by Bill Calkins. Lessons Not Yet Learned. Philip quadrupled his dad's operations during his 23-year term as CEO. He invested in new operations, dramatically improving results. At 46, Philip died unexpectedly. Alex, his 20-year-old son, assumed control of the organization. Not everyone felt this was the right choice. Alex dismissed those who wouldn't get on board. He wisely continued the investments in new technology, results in even greater success than his father had achieved. By the time of Alex's unforeseen death at 33, the organization was 10 times the size it had been at his father's death. 5 years later, that organization had deteriorated to substantially smaller than when Philip ran it. Alex was toasted and written about as one of the greatest leaders in history. He was probably the first PR-based autocratic personality with no true leadership beyond misleading publicity and fear. Beginning in 343 BC, Aristotle tutored Alex for 3 years. Today we call him Alexander the Great. Based on the outcomes for his organization, team, and citizens, he should be called Alexander the Goof. At his deathbed, generals asked Alexander, "Who shall lead us?" Alexander replied, "Whoever is the strongest." The reality is Alexander would leave behind only fighters and no trained leaders. None of the generals were taught anything but rampaging, knocking heads, and killing. They had no understanding of negotiation, compromise, or leadership. The generals fought each other for elevation to Alexander's position. As a result, that era's Greek empire withered away in civil wars, rebellions, disintegration, and loss of power and influence. Alexander didn't expect to die young and didn't plan or train for succession. His leadership style was complete control. He neither trained his possible successors nor shared any information with them. His iron-handed rule gave no thought for the future.

title: Audio Files: Lessons NOT YET Learned
transcription: How many unexpected deaths of owners have meant the end of a garden center, the elimination of all employee jobs, erosion of family wealth and inheritance? What's our lesson? When a well-known garden center operator dies, the sad news speeds through our industry, but what we rarely hear about is what happens to that garden center later. As a business advisor, I hear from many of the heirs when it's almost always too late. The most common situation is that the owner refused to share the true economic reality with the next generation. It makes no difference if that next generation is related by blood or is an unrelated employee. Many bosses don't share the good, the bad, the ugly of financial statements. Numerous new managers have said to me, "I've never seen a set of financial statements before." What does this all mean? Mid-managers thrust into CEO roles are worse. The boss frequently said, "We're short of cash, we can't do what you suggest." Then the keys to the kingdom and the checkbook are thrust into their hands. They see the amount of dollars in the bank and immediately come to the likely incorrect conclusion that the boss lied. They don't understand the seasonality of cash flow and spend the cash without grasping the ramifications. Needing cash, they painfully learned lenders don't write loans to managers who don't understand that garden centers have seasonal cash flows. When selling or attempting to retire, owners without a strong leadership team find they don't have a business to sell. They have inventory that's worth half what the owner thinks it is. The fixtures and equipment are usually worth a quarter or less of the owner's estimate. They may have real estate, but if the operations can't be run without the current owner, they don't have a business. All they have to sell is a job and the physical assets. It's a sad but consistent story. You may be good at making things happen, but what's the future when you're not here? Perhaps history may call you the great, but if you fail, your employees, your town, and even your family might remember you as... the goof. The End. We hope you enjoyed this episode of Audiofiles, from the Tech On Demand podcast brought to you by GrowerTalks. Please take a minute to leave us a positive review. It'll help us reach more greenhouse, garden center, and CEA professionals.

title: Hydration Breaks at FIFA World Cup 2026: The commercialization of climate adaptation?
transcription: There is an ongoing tension between climate action and the commercials of sport. We talk about this a lot. Sustainability is prioritized by sports organizations until it butts up against performance or commercial issues. We see this a lot, I don't think that's particularly, don't think that's particularly controversial to say. But sport is around performance and of course in 2026 it's around commercials. So, this is not breaking news. However, what I think we are seeing here is probably the first example of a climate adaptation leading specifically and directly to commercial opportunity. So, high temperatures are forcing hydration breaks. That's a visible sign of climate impact in elite sport. Even fans watching from home are seeing these climate adaptations now in real time. So, they are going to see a hydration break. The advertising that overlays shows how climate change is driving an intersection with broadcasting business models. It's creating new conversations around how climate adaptation is monetized or communicated as well. This is breaking new ground in structuring commercial content around health and safety pauses, and it's a model that could spread to other sports, especially as climate-driven interruptions become more common. I think for me this is a moment to explore how commercial imperatives and climate adaptation intersect in sport governance. You're going to have your own views about whether this is right or not. Would we love to see these hydration breaks happening like brought to you by the climate crisis? Yes. Is that going to happen? Probably not. Could we encourage these breaks, where they are connected to climate adaptations to be aligned with perhaps climate-positive organizations, or perhaps campaigns or information around the climate crisis? Yes, could we use it as an educational opportunity? I'd love it. What we're seeing already is this commercial adaptation, so we'll see what happens after this. I think there is massive opportunities for discussion around this and what it means, and I think we'll see a lot more about that over the summer.

What does the science actually say about whether social media is ruining our attention spans? Personally, I'm finding it a lot harder these days to sit down and read a book or watch a movie without scrolling on my phone, and it's those short vertical videos that feel particularly addicting. And recently, the science YouTuber, Joss Fong, posted a really great explanation on her channel, How To, where she dove into what the existing science can tell us about whether that brain rot is real, or if it's all just in our fearful heads.

In this conversation about attention spans, there's a phrase that I keep hearing, which is "brain rot". What do we actually mean by that phrase "brain rot"? What are we actually thinking is happening to ourselves and what is happening to ourselves?

I think what people mostly mean when they talk about brain rot is a kind of low-quality internet content on mostly algorithmic social media feeds, probably primarily these short-form video feeds, but also things like on Reddit or Twitter. I think people imply a low quality, but also they're implying a certain effect that they have on, that this is having on our minds.

So it's the content and the impact of the content.

And I think what we hear from a lot of people is, "I used to be able to read books and now I can't. I used to be able to watch movies, um, and now I can't." The story starts in 1769 with a French engineer named Nicolas-Joseph Cugnot, who built what is widely considered the first self-propelled vehicle. transcription: He built a three-wheeled vehicle powered by a gasoline engine, and in 1886, he patented it, making it the first officially recognized automobile. His invention wasn't just a machine; it was a turning point in history. But Benz wasn't alone. Around the same time, another German inventor, Gottlieb Daimler, was developing his own gasoline-powered vehicles. Daimler focused on improving the engine itself, making it smaller and faster, while Benz created the first practical car. Daimler helped make cars more powerful and adaptable. And we can't forget Bertha Benz, Karl Benz's wife. In 1888, she secretly took the first long-distance road trip, solving mechanical problems along the way. Her journey proved that the automobile was more than just an experiment; it was a practical invention. Meanwhile, in the early 1890s, an important development was taking shape in France. Panhard and Levassor introduced what became known as the Système Panhard. They placed the engine at the front of the car and used rear-wheel drive, a layout that became the blueprint for most modern cars. By the early 20th century, the competition had spread worldwide. In the United States, Henry Ford revolutionized the industry by introducing assembly line production, starting in 1913, making cars affordable for all.

title: Cessna Crash Layton Utah, Southwest Flight 512 Honolulu Diversion, Beijing Tower Crash Deliberate
transcription: Despite the ongoing review, the FAA stresses that current rules remain unchanged. Under 14 CFR Part 120 and 49 CFR Part 40, marijuana is a prohibited substance for all safety-sensitive aviation personnel, and a verified positive THC test continues to disqualify a pilot from holding an FAA medical certificate, regardless of state legalization status. While the agency is working towards scientifically defensible impairment thresholds, stopping short, for now, of adopting a fixed abstinence window comparable to Transport Canada's 28-day rule, its zero-tolerance stance holds, with federal regulations superseding state cannabis laws. Chinese authorities on July 2nd released findings concluding that the Beijing Tower crash involving a light aircraft was a deliberate act. Officials stated the pilot acted for personal reasons, classifying the event as a case of endangering public safety after reviewing recovered diary entries and other evidence. The underlying incident occurred June 26th, when an Aurora SA60L light sport aircraft struck the CTCC tower in Beijing's Chaoyang District. The collision killed the pilot, identified as 66-year-old Liu, and injured 13 people on the ground. According to reports from Bloomberg and the Washington Post, investigators found that Liu, a freelance Beijing resident, had documented suicidal thoughts prior to the crash. Early reports from the BBC and other outlets had raised questions about whether mechanical failure or pilot error might have been factors. The official finding now confirms the strike was intentional. Following the incident, China imposed a nationwide ban on light aircraft flights. The event has raised significant questions about aviation security in the capital, as the aircraft penetrated heavily restricted airspace before striking the tower. Further details regarding the flight path and any specific security breaches remain limited, as initial state media disclosures were brief. That's all we have for today. title: History Buffs: The Odyssey Impressions
transcription: Hey, history buffs, it's Nick Hodges here. Now, I know my niche is reviewing historical movies and TV shows, but today, I'm going to make an exception. I just got back from Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, arguably the most talked about movie of 2026. People were already divided on it before they'd even seen it. Well, now I have, and I'm going to answer the question everyone's asking: Is this a movie you're going to like? Well, that depends. How much do you care about Greek mythology, or more specifically, how much do you care about Homer's Odyssey? Do you expect this movie to follow that story beat for beat, and if it doesn't, how much is that going to bother you? Because if all you care about are the monsters, I can tell you right now you're getting the Cyclops, the Laestrygonians, the witch Circe, the Sirens, Scylla, and Charybdis. They're all there. Strangely, though, there are almost no gods. Okay, we're probably entering spoiler territory here, but if you don't mind minor spoilers, Odysseus never speaks to Hermes, Aeolus, or Poseidon. The only god he ever interacts with is Athena, and even she is presented more like a hallucination than an actual goddess. Which doesn't really make much sense to me because there's definitely magic in this movie. Circe genuinely turns Odysseus's men into pigs. Calypso's in the movie too, but she isn't a goddess. She's just a mortal woman who rescues Odysseus and feeds him lotus leaves. There's no temptation of immortality like there is in the original story. If you're wondering how Christopher Nolan handles the gods, the answer is he mostly doesn't. Poseidon never appears. The closest the film gets is, after the Cyclops is blinded, he cries out to Poseidon, and Odysseus's crew conclude that the Cyclops must be his son. That's about as explicit as it gets. And yet, a little later, Odysseus literally travels to Hades and speaks to the dead. Tiresias is there, his fallen comrades from Troy are there, so the afterlife is definitely real. But the Olympian gods? Apparently, that's where Christopher Nolan draws the line. Now, what are the monsters like in the movie? Well, to be honest, the Cyclops is really disappointing. He never talks to Odysseus and his men, he just walks into the cave, seals the entrance, eats a few of Odysseus's men, and then goes straight to sleep, not considering these tiny humans a threat at all. In the original story, it's much more interesting. Odysseus actually talks to the Cyclops, he gets him drunk on wine, and then blinds him while he's asleep. By cutting all of that out, Nolan's Cyclops just comes across as an idiot. I

title: History Buffs: The Odyssey Impressions
transcription: primary. They even wear black armor. The worst offender is definitely Agamemnon. He looks like Batman with a predator spine running down his back, in the baking hot Mediterranean sun. And it's not just the costumes, there's Viking influence all over this movie, the witch Circe drinks out of those horn shot glasses you can buy from the Grimfrost website, Odysseus even sails around in a Viking longship, specifically this one, which completely breaks the illusion that we're meant to be in ancient Greece. Now, I know why Christopher Nolan picked it, he wanted a real seaworthy ship they could actually sail. Fair enough. But there are reconstructed Greek galleys, too, he could have used one of those instead. Another thing I didn't like was the design of the Trojan horse. What do you think when I tell you that it doesn't have wheels? Seriously, every depiction of the Trojan horse we've ever seen puts it on wheels, even the ancient Greeks imagined it that way. The famous Mykonos vase from the 7th century BC shows the Trojan horse with wheels. I mean, it makes sense, right? How else were the Trojans supposed to get it back to the city? Well, in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, they drag it across the plain on logs with ropes while the Greeks hiding inside are being thrown from side to side. It's ridiculous. What I will give Christopher Nolan credit for is that he actually shot on location in Greece, Italy, Malta, Morocco, Iceland. That part is genuinely immersive and it looks fantastic. But overall, going back to the question I asked at the start, is this a movie you're going to like? Well, if you care about Greek mythology as much as I do, probably not, because when I watch a movie based on a story I love, I'm constantly anticipating those iconic moments. I'm sitting there thinking, "Oh, this is the bit with the Cyclops. I can't wait to see what they've done with it," or, "This is where Odysseus meets Circe," or, "This is the journey to Hades," but more often than not, when those moments finally came, I was left feeling disappointed, because many of the changes Christopher Nolan made left me wondering, why? Why make the gods ambiguous but the monsters, magic, and the afterlife all real? Why cast the movie this way? Why dress everyone up like Vikings? Why give Odysseus a Viking longship when reconstructed Greek galley ships already exist? I spent too much of the movie asking why Christopher Nolan had made these decisions, instead of getting swept up in the adventure. But I will admit that this could just be a me problem. It really boils down to how much do you care? Do you enjoy Christopher Nolan's take on The Odyssey, or do you think I'm being pedantic? Let me know in the comments, love to hear your thoughts.

title: Should Barcelona Be Afraid of Jose Mourinho? | History Repeating at Real Madrid? | AT Podcast
transcription: ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോ റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിലേക്ക് വരുന്നതിൽ ബാഴ്സലോണ പേടിക്കണം എന്ന് പറയുന്നവരുണ്ടല്ലോ. ശരിക്കും ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോ വരുന്ന ഈ വർഷം, അതായത് 2023 മുതൽ നോക്കുകയാണെന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ ഒരു ചരിത്രത്തിനെയൊക്കെ അടിസ്ഥാനപ്പെടുത്തിയാണ് നമ്മൾ സംസാരിക്കാൻ പോകുന്നത്. ആദ്യമേ പേടിക്കണോ എന്ന് ചോദിച്ചു കഴിഞ്ഞാൽ നമ്മൾ ഹിസ്റ്ററിയെ ബേസ് ചെയ്തിട്ടുള്ള ഒരു കാര്യമാണ് പറയാനായിട്ട് പോകുന്നത്. ഇതിങ്ങനെയൊക്കെ തന്നെ സംഭവിക്കണം എന്ന് നിർബന്ധമൊന്നുമില്ലെങ്കിലും പലപ്പോഴും ഫുട്ബോളിൽ ഈ ചരിത്രമാവർത്തിക്കുകയാണല്ലോ എന്ന് പറയുന്ന പോലെ ഒരു സംഭവത്തെക്കുറിച്ചാണ് നമ്മൾ പറയാൻ പോകുന്നത്. ബാഴ്സലോണ ശരിക്കും ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോയെ പേടിക്കണോ? ഇതാണ് ടോപ്പിക്. അപ്പൊ എന്തായാലും നമ്മൾ വിഷയം വിഷയമായിട്ട് സംസാരിക്കുന്നതിനു മുൻപായിട്ട്, നിങ്ങൾക്ക് നമ്മുടെ കാര്യപരിപാടികൾ യൂട്യൂബിൽ ഇഷ്ടപ്പെടുന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ എന്തായാലും യൂട്യൂബിൽ ഒന്ന് സബ്സ്ക്രൈബ് ചെയ്തു കൂടെ കൂടുക. നമ്മളങ്ങനെ 9000 സബ്സ്ക്രൈബേഴ്സ് ആയിരിക്കുകയാണ്. ഇനി 10 കെ യിലേക്ക് അടുത്തോണ്ടിരിക്കുകയാണ്. സോ നിങ്ങൾ ഫോളോ ചെയ്യുകയാണ്, സബ്സ്ക്രൈബ് ചെയ്യുകയാണെന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ അത് പെട്ടെന്നാവും എന്ന് ഓർമ്മിപ്പിച്ചുകൊണ്ട്, വെൽക്കം ടു 80 പോഡ്കാസ്റ്റ് ഫുട്ബോൾ ക്ലബ്ബ് ആൻഡ് ദിസ് ഈസ് ആർ ജെ ആറ്റപ്പൻ. ആദ്യം തന്നെ പറയാനുള്ള ഒരു കാര്യം എന്ന് പറയുന്നത് 2010 ൽ സ്പെയിൻ വേൾഡ് കപ്പ് അടിക്കുന്ന ഒരു സമയമുണ്ട്. അതുകഴിഞ്ഞു കഴിഞ്ഞാൽ നേരെ അടുത്ത സീസൺ റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിലേക്ക്, അതായത് ആ അടിച്ച വർഷത്തെ സീസൺ തുടങ്ങുന്നത് ഈ പറയുന്ന പോലെ തന്നെ ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോയോടൊപ്പമാണ്. അതായത് 2010 മുതൽ 2013 വരെക്കുമാണ് ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോ ദി സ്പെഷ്യൽ വൺ റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിൻ്റെ ഹെഡ് കോച്ച് ആയിട്ട് വന്നിട്ടുള്ളത്. ആൻഡ് ഇതിൻ്റെ ഇടയിൽ തന്നെ നമ്മൾ ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോയെ കുറിച്ച് എപ്പോഴും പറയുമ്പോഴും ഈ റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിൻ്റെ ഈയൊരു ചെറിയ സമയം എന്ന് വേണമെങ്കിൽ പറയാം, അല്ലെ? ഒരു മൂന്ന് വർഷം. അല്ലെങ്കിൽ നാല് വർഷം എന്ന്, നാല് വർഷം കൺസിഡർ ചെയ്യാൻ പറ്റില്ല പക്ഷേ എന്നാലും അങ്ങനെ. മൂന്ന് സീസൺസ്. ഈ മൂന്ന് സീസൺ കൊണ്ട് എങ്ങനെയാണ് റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിനെ ഈ പറയുന്ന പോലെ തന്നെ ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോ മാറ്റിയതെന്ന് വച്ച് കഴിഞ്ഞു കഴിഞ്ഞാൽ അത് ട്രോഫികളുടെ നമ്പർ വെച്ചിട്ടോ, വിന്നിങ് പെർസെൻ്റേജ് വെച്ചിട്ടോ, എൽ ക്ലാസിക്കോയിൽ അടിച്ചിട്ടുള്ള ജയങ്ങൾ വെച്ചിട്ടോ ഒന്നുമല്ല. പകരം ഹി വാസ് ബിൽഡിങ്. നമ്മുടെ ടോണി സ്റ്റാർക്ക് അയൺമാനിലൊക്കെ പറയുന്ന ഒരു സാധനമില്ലേ, ഐ ആം ദി മെക്കാനിക് എന്ന് പറയുന്ന പോലെ തന്നെ ഹി വാസ് ദി മാൻ ഹു ഡിസൈൻഡ് റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡ് എന്ന് വേണമെങ്കിൽ പറയാം. അതായത് രമണാ, എങ്ങനെയാ പറയാന്ന് വച്ചുകഴിഞ്ഞാൽ ആ ഒരു മൂന്ന് സീസൺ കൊണ്ട് റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിനെ ശരിയായ റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡ് ആയിട്ട് മാറ്റാൻ ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോയ്ക്ക് സാധിച്ചു എന്നുള്ളതാണ് ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോയെ സംബന്ധിച്ചിടത്തോളവും റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിനെ സംബന്ധിച്ചിടത്തോളവും ജോസെ മൌറീന്യോയുടെ സമയം പുള്ളിയുടെ പേര് വെച്ചുതന്നെ നമ്മൾ പറയുകയാണെന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ ഒരു സ്പെഷ്യൽ വൺ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ ഒരു സ്പെഷ്യൽ സീസൺ ആയി മാറുന്നത് എന്നുള്ളതാണ്. അത് എന്തുകൊണ്ടാണ് എന്ന് ചോദിക്കുകയാണെന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ, ഞാൻ ആ പറഞ്ഞ സമയം കൊണ്ട് തന്നെ പറഞ്ഞു വരികയാണ്. സ്പെയിൻ വേൾഡ് കപ്പ് അടിച്ചു കഴിഞ്ഞു കഴിഞ്ഞിട്ട് ബാഴ്സലോണയുടെ കാര്യമെടുത്ത് നോക്കുകയാണെന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ പിന്നെ അങ്ങോട്ട് ബാഴ്സലോണ യൂറോപ്പ് ഭരിച്ചിരുന്ന സമയമാണ്. എന്ന്

title: Should Barcelona Be Afraid of Jose Mourinho? | History Repeating at Real Madrid? | AT Podcast
transcription: ആരാണ് പേടിക്കേണ്ടത് എന്നുള്ളതാണ് കണ്ടോ. അപ്പോ നിങ്ങൾക്ക് എല്ലാവർക്കും ഉള്ള ഒരു സംശയമായിരിക്കും എന്തൊക്കെയാണ് ഈ എട്ട് ട്രോഫീസ് 2010 മുതൽ 13 വരെയും ബാഴ്സലോണക്ക് അടിക്കാൻ സാധിച്ചിട്ടുള്ളത്. അതായത് രണ്ട് ലാലിഗ, ഒരു കോപ്പ ഡെൽ റെയ്, ഒരു സ്പാനിഷ് സൂപ്പർ കപ്പ്, ഒരു യുഇഎഫ്എ സൂപ്പർ കപ്പ്, അതുപോലെതന്നെ ഫിഫ വേൾഡ് കപ്പും ആൻഡ് ഒരു ചാമ്പ്യൻസ് ലീഗും ഈ സമയത്ത് അടിച്ചിട്ടുണ്ടെന്നുള്ളതാണ് അതായത് എട്ട് ട്രോഫീസ് ഇരുപത് ട്രോഫീസ് അടിച്ചിട്ടുണ്ട് കേട്ടോ. എന്നാൽ അതേ സമയം റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിന്റെ കാര്യം എടുത്തു നോക്കുകയാണെന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ ഒരു ലാലിഗ, ഒരു കോപ്പ ഡെൽ റെയ് ഞാൻ പറഞ്ഞില്ലേ ഫൈനലിൽ തോൽപ്പിച്ചുകൊണ്ട് ആൻഡ് ഒരു സ്പാനിഷ് സൂപ്പർ കപ്പും മാത്രമാണ് അതായത് മൂന്നേ മൂന്ന് ട്രോഫീസ് ആണ് ഈ സീസണുകളിൽ മൂന്ന് സീസണുകളിലായിട്ട് ജോസെ മൊറീഞ്ഞോയുടെ അണ്ടറിൽ റയൽ മാഡ്രിഡിന് എടുക്കാൻ സാധിച്ചിട്ടുള്ളത്. പല പ്ലെയേഴ്സിനെ അന്നും ഈ പറയുന്നതുപോലെ തന്നെ പിന്നീട് അങ്ങോട്ട് ആ ഒരു ലെഗസിയിലേക്ക് കൊണ്ടുവന്നതും അതിനു തുടക്കം ഇട്ടതും ഈ പറയുന്നതുപോലെ തന്നെ ജോസെയാണ് എന്നുള്ളത് ഒരു കാര്യം തന്നെയാണ്. ഒരു ബാഴ്സ പെർസ്പെക്ടീവിൽ തിങ്ക് ചെയ്യുകയാണെന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ ഈ ചരിത്രം ആവർത്തിച്ചു വരികയാണെന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ അതുപോലെയൊക്കെ സംഭവിക്കും എന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ അങ്ങനെയൊന്നും സാധ്യത ഉണ്ടെന്നും ഇല്ലെന്നും ഒന്നും പറയാൻ പറ്റില്ല നമുക്ക് വെയിറ്റ് ചെയ്തുതന്നെ കാണണം. പെപ് ഗ്വാർഡിയോള അല്ല ഹാൻസി ഫ്ലിക്ക് എന്നുള്ളത് മറ്റൊരു കാര്യമുണ്ട്. രണ്ടുപേരുടെ പ്ലേയിംഗ് സ്റ്റൈലിലും വ്യത്യാസങ്ങളുണ്ട്. രണ്ടുപേരുടെ ഫിലോസഫിയിലും വ്യത്യാസങ്ങളുണ്ട്. പക്ഷെ എന്തൊക്കെ പറഞ്ഞു കഴിഞ്ഞാലും ഈ പറയുന്നതുപോലെ അതാണ്, എന്ന് വെച്ചുകഴിഞ്ഞാൽ ബാഴ്സലോണയ്ക്കുള്ള ഒരു മറ്റ് പ്രത്യേകതയായിട്ട് എനിക്ക് എപ്പോഴും തോന്നിയിട്ടുള്ളൊരു കാര്യം എന്ന് പറയുന്നത്, ഈ വലിയ സൈനിങ്ങുകൾ നടത്തിയ സമയങ്ങളെല്ലാം ബാഴ്സലോണയ്ക്ക് വലിയ ഫ്ലോപ്പുകൾ ഉണ്ടായിട്ടുള്ള സീസണുകളാണ്. എന്നു വെച്ചുകഴിഞ്ഞാൽ അത് ചാമ്പ്യൻസ് ലീഗിൽ ആയിക്കോട്ടെ ലാ title: Trump v3.0 | The Most Viral Content Creator | StandUp Comedy by Rahul Dua | 2026
transcription: उसका थोड़ा विटामिन कम है। या उसका पोटैशियम ज़्यादा आया है, क्या चक्कर क्या है उसका? रोज़ सुबह कोई अजीब बात कर दे। है ना? ऐसे ही लगता है ना? है ना? यही तो आप रह गए। आप उसका विज़न ही शेयर कर पा रहे। आप लोगों को पर्सपेक्टिव बदलने की बहुत... देखो, I know the general sentiment is कि बहुत इरैटिक आदमी है, रोज़ सुबह उठ के नई फुद्दू बात करता है। मैं कह रहा हूँ कंसिस्टेंट देखो कितना है। रोज़ सुबह उठ के एक नए सिरे से एक नॉवेल, स्टेट ऑफ़ द आर्ट, फुद्दू बात सोचना। और फिर उसको करने का जिगरा रखना। आर्ट है, कला है ये। पूरी दुनिया का फ़न लगा के रखा है, उसके चक्कर में बिग बॉस की रेटिंग नहीं आ रही है। हाँ, हाँ! सही? आंटियां इंडिया में टाइम पे सो जा रही हैं। कि नींद पूरी कर लेते हैं, कल सुबह मज़ा आएगा। It is not easy being the President of United States, it becomes very lonely at the top. Poor guy is lonely. He is out there to make friends, दोस्त बनाने निकला है वो। अब... अगर रास्ते में कहीं थोड़ा बहुत तेल मिल रहा है... उसमें प्रॉब्लम क्या है? पर दोस्ती में कोई कॉम्प्रोमाइज नहीं देखो, बिल्कुल कोई, कोई फॉर्मेलिटी नहीं करता दोस्ती में। वेनेजुएला का प्रेसिडेंट बताओ निकर-ट्रैकसूट में उठा लाया है। ये रहे यार यहाँ आके। दिल का कितना साफ़ है। कितना जो दिल में है, ज़ुबां पे है। बीच में माइंड का कोई रोल ही नहीं है। आप देखो, अरे! यार नहीं, हेलो, एक सेकंड। माइंड का क्यूँ हो रोल भी, दिल... माइंड तो बाहर है। उसकी पीआर टीम... मर गई कह-कह के। कि नहीं-नहीं, वेनेजुएला वॉज़ इन अ स्टेट ऑफ़ अनरेस्ट, उनकी गवर्नमेंट उनके लिए काम नहीं कर रही थी, डिस्टर्ब स्टेट थी, इसलिए हमको इंटरवीन करना पड़ा। कह रहा है चुप हो जाओ बिल्कुल, झूठ नहीं बोलो अब तुम। भैया, मैं बताता हूँ, इनको नहीं पता। हम उनको वेनेजुएला तेल के लिए जाना था। हमारे हेयर फ़ॉल हो रहा है, रिसीड हो रही। सीधी बात करना है, बिल्कुल कुछ छल-कपट, छलावा कुछ है ही नहीं उस आदमी के पास। आधी बात बताता है। पूरी नहीं बताता। कि, "You have to figure the fuck out."

title: PRESSURE | STAND-UP COMEDY BY SHARON VERMA
transcription: But yeah, what is this photo-woto lene ki trip? Main toh har cheez ki photo leti hoon, khana dekha photo le li, sunset dekha photo le li. Main toh trip ko ekdum Netflix documentary jaisa hi treat kar rahi thi ki kin gadho ke sath aayi hoon. Kal ko aa gayi Sharon files. Har cheez is evidence, evidence, evidence, evidence. Aur ye teeno mera mazaak uda rahe hai yaar, ye teeno keh rahe hai, "Dekho na, photo li hai, abhi reel pe dalegi, story pe lagayegi, followers ko dikhayegi." Aisa keh ke mujhe embarrassed aur chhota feel karane ki koshish kar rahe hai. Aur phir gaadi mein keh rahe hai "sunset ki jo photo li thi bhejna zara. Story pe lagani hai." Story pe lagayi bhi, niche likha hai "My click." Maine waha scuba diving bhi ki. Scuba diving ki hai aap me se kisi ne? Aapne ki hai sir? Kahan pe ki thi aapne? Dubai? Kaisa tha experience aapka? Fun? Haan, technicalities pe chale gaye aap. Expect a simple answer from a man. I'll explain. Nahi nahi, aap bahut sahi ho yaar. Mera, mera itna waahiyat experience tha yaar kyunki maine scuba diving peer pressure mein ki. But, I did not realize that all my peers were under pressure. Peer toh bol hi nahi paa rahe hai ek dusre ko aur main itne pressure mein hoon, main, main itni anxious hoon main instructor ko keh rahi hoon, "Ma'am, mujhe toh tairna bhi nahi aata". Woh kehti hai, "Ma'am, aap bilkul chinta mat kariye, mujhe bhi nahi aata". Kamaal! Do behen, dono grahan. Khud se panic anxiety mein apna manage kar rahi hoon, guys, all by myself kyunki I realized Indians ko sirf ek cheez karni hoti hai to start enjoying. Bas ek cheez karni hoti hai. Payment. Saath hazaar jo kate mere bank account se, maine kaha, "Aaj ek ek machhli dekh kar jaungi. Do chaar turtles toh ghar aayenge mere sath. Nemo kahan hai? Saale ko main dhoond dungi." Kya bill phada, bhai saab! Saath hazaar plus GST plus PTSD.

title: HOW OUR INDIAN EDUCATION SYSTEM FAILED US | StandUp Comedy by Rahul Dua | 2026
transcription: मैं तो CBSE में पढ़ा हूँ right तो CBSE में 6th class में algebra हमारा introduce हुआ है तो हमारी class teacher maths पढाती थी वह अपना लगी हुई है। बच्चों से लेकर teacher तक किसी को X नहीं मिल रहा है। अपना लगी हुई है। तो मुझे समझ नहीं आ रहा है मेरे को ऐसा लग रहा है कि जब X मिल जाएगा बता देगी यह। तो मैं अपना अपने दोस्त से बात करनी शुरू, मैंने अब मैं बात करनी शुरू करी ही है, मैंने तो hello का 'है' बोला, 'है'। मेरे यहाँ आकर चौक बजा चौक। रविंद्र जडेजा ने मुझे खड़ा किया। मुझे मुझे मुझे मैडम ने खड़ा किया। मुझे खड़ा करके कहती, कहती, 'बात क्यों कर रहे हो?' मैने कहा 'बात क्यों कर रहे हो' का क्या मतलब है? बात इसलिए कर रहे हैं क्योंकि man is a social animal. बिना बात किए उससे रहा नहीं जाता, societal construct है यह। यह अभी तो पढ़ाया मैडम moral science में। मैम however obviously in absolutely no mood for any sort of explanation, मैडम ने मुझे 5 मिनट पूरी class के सामने अच्छे से झाड़ा है जो है। और 5 मिनट डांटने के बाद मुझसे कह रही, 'You have wasted 5 minutes. There are 60 students in the class. You have in total wasted 300 minutes.' मैने कहा 'मैम, मैम, time has been wasted in parallel. Not in series. मैम, you have disturbed 60 students. I was at max going to disturb one. That too for 5 seconds only. ओए टिफिन बचा है? नहीं बचा, ओहो that's it.' तो मैम, maths भी ख़राब है, logic भी ख़राब है आपका। और moral science के तो हाल हम देख ही लिए हैं। Zero civic sense. I believe that the Indian schooling system is horrible. या तो गलत पढ़ा रहे हैं या unnecessary पढ़ा रहे हैं। English हमें गलत पढ़ाई हुई। अंग्रेजी मुहावरे आधे अधूरे पढ़ा के छोड़ रखे हैं। I recently got to know that 'Jack of all master of none' is an incomplete proverb.

title: Dhurandhar Film Joke | Stand-up Comedy Clip| Ft. Amit Maharana Saini
transcription: धुरंधर देखी है आप लोगों ने? हाँ लगभग सभी ने, हाँ ठीक करा देख ली। मैंने भी देखी थी, इतना झूठ दिखा रखा ना उस पिक्चर में भाई। सही में शुरू में तो मुझे पता ही नहीं चला था। मैंने देख ली थी ऐसी ही, कि चार-पांच एक्टर हैं तो बढ़िया ही होगी पिक्चर और बढ़िया लगी मुझे। पर फिर एक दिन ऐसा हुआ, मेरा एक दोस्त है, नदीम उसने मुझे ध्रुव राठी की वीडियो भेजी और मुझे फ़ोन करके कह रहा, अबे वीडियो देख जो मैंने भेजी तुझे है। वो तो एक प्रोपेगैंडा फिल्म है, कुछ भी सच नहीं दिखा रखा उसमें। मैंने कहा सच नहीं दिखा रखा? तो भाई मैंने देखी वो जर्मन सिटीजन की वीडियो। वो खुद झूठ बोल रहा है उसमें। कह रहा बर्फ में कत्लेआम दिखा रखा बर्फ में, भाई पूरी पिक्चर में एक भी सीन बर्फ में लड़ाई का नहीं है। बर्फ वो सिर्फ गिलास में डाल रहे, और कहीं बर्फ नहीं और ये मुझे फ़ोन करके कह रहा तुम्हारा तो कोई भी काट देता है अंधभक्तों। मैंने कहा भाई इसमें काटने वाली क्या बात है, हमें तो बढ़िया लगी पिक्चर और रही बात काटने की तो सुन भाई नदीम। देख हमारा तो बचपन में नहीं कटा अब तो क्या ही कटेगा। नहीं कुछ बच्चों के साथ होता है स्कैम ये। देख वो रही चिड़िया, वो रही, वो रही, वो रही, ए उड़ गई, उड़ गई, नीचे साँप। अरे! भाई तुम समझ नहीं रहे। देखो दो साल का बच्चा है छोटा सा, उसके हाथ में डेढ़ लाख का मोबाइल है महंगा मोबाइल है ३०-३५ हज़ार की सिर्फ डिस्प्ले है। अब उसके हाथ से लेना हो गिरा ना दे तो क्या करना पड़ेगा? तब चिड़िया ही काम आती है। हाँ, तुम कहीं और पहुँच गए थे। पर फिर भी मुझे बुरा लगा यार कि मैं कैसे नहीं पकड़ पाया वो झूठ। तो मैंने दुबारा पिक्चर देखी वो। कितना झूठ दिखा रखा भाई आदित्य धर ने उसमें। पाकिस्तान में गलत दिखा दिया बताओ डांस। पाकिस्तान में! हैं? और वहाँ पे वो गार्ड रणवीर सिंह को रोक के बोलता है अन्दर सिर्फ कपल की एंट्री है।

title: EVERYTHING You Need To Know About The New WEGOVY PILL
transcription: It's 6:20 in the morning. You're half awake. Your brain is chanting one word: coffee. Now, plot twist: your new weight loss pill looks you in the soul and says, "Not yet. We need 30 minutes alone with water." Welcome to 2026 where Wegovy is now a tablet, needle-free, but it's not rule-free. Today, we're doing the great trade: the weekly shot versus the daily pill. Not which one is better online, which one fits real humans with real mornings and real habits. Quick note: this is education, not personal medical advice. Talk with your clinician before starting or switching any GLP-1 medication. And one more thing, as an obesity medicine doctor, most of my patients have been successful with weight loss by simply going low-carb, keto, or carnivore, but the reality is there are some people who need help, and that's why I made this video. All right, five rounds, scoreboard style, and I'll drop lesser-known facts that most influencers won't mention. Fast, clear, and practical for you. Round one, let's talk about convenience. Weekly shot: once a week, any time of day, with or without meals. Daily pill: once a day, but it comes with terms and conditions. FDA label rules in human language: empty stomach, morning, water only up to 4 oz, swallow whole, then wait at least 30 minutes before food, drinks, or other oral meds. Lesser-known fact: the tablet includes an absorption helper called salcaprozate sodium, abbreviated SNAC. Score: shot gets round one for pure convenience. Shot, 1; pill, 0. Round two, compliance. Will it actually do this? The coffee test: can you delay coffee for 30 minutes most mornings? If yes, the pill may fit. If your coffee is basically your therapist, the weekly shot may be your peace treaty. Lesser-known fact: the pill has a three-month ramp to maintenance. Day 1 through 30, 1.5 mg. 31 through 60, 4 mg.

If you're the type who wakes up already late, this can feel like trying to assemble IKEA furniture in the dark. Score: tie. Shot one, pill one. Round three: let's talk about effectiveness. Does it work? Yes. In the New England Journal of Medicine trial report, weight change at 64 weeks was about 13.6% with oral semaglutide versus 2.2% with placebo. Let me make that real. If someone weighs 250 pounds, 13.6% is about 34 pounds. That's not "I skipped dessert twice." That's biology is changing. And summaries of the same program note that with strong adherence, averages and big loss percentages can look even better. Lesser known fact: the FDA label notes that 25 milligram tablet can produce average blood concentrations comparable to the 2.4 milligram weekly injection, but with higher variability person to person. Translation: two people can take the same pill and their bodies can see it differently. That's why follow-up matters. Score: tie. Shot two, pill two. Let's go to round four, where we talk about side effects. Most people know the headline: GI side effects, including nausea, constipation, diarrhea, stomach discomfort can happen with GLP-1s, pill or shot. Lesser known fact: a lot of side effects are dose-plus-behavior. Big portions, greasy meals, alcohol, eating fast can turn mild nausea into a full-time job. So here's my side-effect survival kit for week one through week 12: smaller meals, slower eating, protein first, and don't let hydration slip, especially if nausea or diarrhea show up. Also, strength training matters, because the goal isn't just less weight, it's less fat while protecting muscle. Now, the serious warnings matter too. The label includes warnings like pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, dehydration-related kidney injury, and a box warning about thyroid C-cell tumors with contraindications in people with personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2. Score: tie again. Shot three, pill three. Round five: cost and coverage.

title: How Jumping Rope Changes the Human Body.
transcription: The 5-minute jump rope will help you burn fat, create strong and powerful legs, and have you feeling younger than you actually are. This jump rope right here cost me about $5 on Amazon. Cheap, simple tools can have the greatest effect on your body. There's a study that shows jump rope is just as good at improving cardiovascular fitness as running. I am not here to argue that jump rope is any better than running, but there are some unique benefits to jump rope. Number one, you can plainly see on the screen right now. I can't go jogging down the street leaving my boys here to fend for themselves, but I can get 5 to 10 minutes of jump rope in while they play on their scooters around me. It can be the non-runner or parents' weapon to getting into incredible shape in the comfort of your backyard. Now, I assume that jumping rope originated with boxing, but that was only when it was popularized in America. Jump rope started as a fun game for kids way back in ancient Egypt, China, and Greece and Rome. It was brought to America by the Dutch, and eventually turned into an exercise that athletes, especially boxers, still utilize today. Why? Well, it comes down to one quality: rhythm. Boxers have found that the rhythmic, quick feet required to jump rope translates great to their sport. This is a lost quality in modern-day fitness. Many people sit on machines, lay on benches, losing that rhythmic quality that most of us had when we were younger. Here's a few things you probably didn't know about rhythm. Number one is that our brains crave it. It's why we love music. It's why dancers are the most embodied athletes. Rhythmic movement increases coordination, triggers the parasympathetic nervous system, and even increases heart rate variability. Rhythm, combined with bouncing on your feet, strengthens the vestibular system. This improves balance, coordination, and spatial awareness, all things that we slowly lose as we age. And a benefit that you won't find listed on Google is that all these qualities combined result in somewhat of a natural high. And the more competent you become with the rope, the more you experience these elevated feelings. But we also lose muscle and bone density as we age, and the less that we physically train, the easier it is to deteriorate. Most people know to do some resistance training and some cardio, but 90-something percent of the population are missing out on the benefits of plyometrics. Plyometrics are quick, explosive movements that involve lengthening the muscle and then quickly shortening it. And every time you land and rebound, it's three times your body weight in that moment. This has incredible effects on strengthening muscles, connective tissue, and bones. It's a quality that can literally keep you younger, and I think jump rope is the easiest way to safely maintain it. These small doses of impact result in a very strong frame. Skipping rope strengthens your whole lower body structure, and specifically your quads, glutes, and calves. You develop legs that are good at being active, translating well to activities like hiking, cycling, and running. And ask any orthopedic doctor. title: How Jumping Rope Changes the Human Body.
transcription: Pick up basketball game with your friends? Snap! The Achilles goes. Jump rope is one of the most effective preventative measures against lower leg injuries. It'll protect you, but also turn your feet and ankles into springs as they should be used. Let's talk fat loss. There's no one exercise that's going to get you shredded. Creating a good physique is just as much about resistance training, nutrition, sleeping well. But when it comes to conditioning, burning calories, and increasing the metabolism, I've found the jump rope to be one of the best tools in my toolbox. The study I mentioned earlier found that 10 minutes of jumping rope was equal to a 30 minute jog. There's some controversy around this topic and there's another study that seems to disprove it, but I think it still speaks to just how effective jumping rope is for conditioning the body. Anecdotally, for me, when I've made the daily or every other day habit of doing 5 to 10 minute jump rope sessions, I've seen the lowest body fat percentages. But I'm a fan of focusing on performance and functionality, and getting a great physique as a side effect. George Hackenschmidt, one of the original strongman bodybuilders of physical culture, was jumping over chairs into his eighties. This is a strong testament to simple exercises and tools that can slow down the aging process. Most of you guys know, for the last 30 days, I've done 100 bodyweight squats and 50 pushups per day. And the last piece of this routine is a five minute jump rope. But I was nowhere near starting with a full five minutes. I hadn't jump roped much this year at all, so just reaching one minute was challenging. My calves were burning, my lungs were working so hard to get enough air. Even my shoulders were starting to hurt. But after I trained and trained, it obviously became easier. After 100 squats and 5 minutes of jumping rope a day, my legs are in incredible shape. Strong and springy with full mobility. Let me break down how to get started. Start a stopwatch on your phone, and skip the rope for 30 seconds. Look, if you're just starting out, it's not going to be pretty. You're going to look uncoordinated, and even feel a little silly. My best advice is to start slower than you think you should. Breathe through your nose to not make you speed up, and every time the rope hits your feet, just know it's helping you get better. After you jump for 30 seconds, rest for 30 seconds. Then repeat this until the 5 minutes ends. Now, your goal over the 30 days is to start working longer than you rest. Skip for 45 seconds with a 30 second break, then 60 seconds. If there's a day you're feeling really good, test yourself. Go for 2, 3 minutes, you might even surprise yourself and do the full 5. So, this challenge is very simple. Every day, starting today, January 1st, set a 5 minute timer on your phone and skip the rope as much as you can for 30 days straight. Screenshot this, and keep it handy. And guys, just a quick note, these three challenges are meant to be motivation to kick off this new year right. Pushups, squats and jump rope only took me 15 minutes total. They're time efficient for the busy parent. It's not how I'd recommend to train year round, but it's minimalist. You'll see results, and it will motivate you through this last part of winter. Training at 2 years old, huh? I appreciate all you guys so much, and I look forward to an amazing 2022. Yeah!

transcription: नमस्कार, मैं हूँ डॉ श्वेता आड़ात्या लिमिटलेस ब्रेन लैब से। तो आज हम बहुत ही एक सीक्रेट पे बात करते हैं। अगर आप दो या तीन मिनट में सोना चाहते हैं जो कि एक बहुत बहुत बहुत इंपॉर्टेंट सी प्रॉब्लम चल रही है। इतनी बड़ी मुश्किल हो चुकी है इंसोम्निया, यानी की नहीं सोने का प्रॉब्लम। सो बहुत सारे लोग ये प्रॉब्लम में है और अगर आप मॉनिटर करते हैं, चाहे वूप से मॉनिटर करते हो, ओरा रिंग से मॉनिटर करते हो, यूम से करते हो, कोई भी ऐसी मोडालिटी से मेजर करते हो और आप देखते हैं कि आपको डीप स्लीप जो है वो अच्छे से नहीं आ रही है, देन दिस इज़ द ट्रिक व्हिच विल वर्क फॉर यू। ये एक ऐसी ट्रिक है जिसमें ये केवल दो चीजें करने से मात्र से, मेरे पर्सनल पेशेंट्स में बहुत बहुत बहुत चेंजेस आए हैं। मेरे पर्सनली पेशेंट्स ने भी ये अनुभव किया है, मेरे रिलेटिव्स ने अनुभव किया है, मेरे फ्रेंड्स ने अनुभव किया है, तो ये एक एक्सपीरिएंशियल चीज है, जरूर करके देखिएगा। इसमें सोने से पहले आपको दो चीजें करनी होगी। सो सोने से पहले की बात आई एम श्योर स्लीप की बहुत सारी टॉक्स आपने सुनी होंगी कि अंधेरा होना चाहिए, कोल्ड थोड़ा सा टेंपरेचर होना चाहिए, वेटेड ब्लैंकेट, जो आप चादर ओढ़ते हो वो पतली नहीं, मोटी सी होनी चाहिए, कामिंग के लिए 15 से 20 मिनट तक कम से कम लाइट का एक्सपोजर, ब्लू लाइट वगैरह नहीं होना चाहिए, या तो आप फोन में फिल्टर्स फिट कर सकते हो, रीडिंग कर सकते हो, कोई भी ऐसी चीज करें जहां पर आपको एक्स्ट्रा लाइट का एक्सपोजर ना हो, अंधेरा बिल्कुल डार्क रखें, कोई भी एक्सरसाइज, एक्टिविटी, कैफ़ीन, स्टिमुलेंट्स ऐसी कोई भी चीज ना करें कम से कम दो घंटे तक। तीन या चार घंटे की दूरी रखे आपके लास्ट मील और सोने पे। ये सारा कुछ तो 100% आपने सुना होगा और कई सारे ऐसे लोग होंगे आप में से जिन्होंने ये सब कुछ कर भी लिया होगा लेकिन नींद जो है अभी नहीं आती है। सो पहले तो ये समझते हैं कि नींद नहीं आना 40 टू 45% में, यस, बहुत ही बड़ा नंबर है, 40 टू 45% में ये जेनेटिक हो सकता है। तो आपके पूर्वज, आपके जो मां बाप हैं, आपके वालिद हैं, वो नहीं सो पाते हैं इसकी वजह से भी आपको नींद नहीं आती है। सेकंड थिंग इस देयर इस एंग्जायटी, फीयर, वरी कुछ ना कुछ चलते रहता है दिमाग में उसकी वजह से नींद का प्रॉब्लम हो सकता है। अब आपको करना क्या है? transcription: पूरी दुनिया में इस वक्त भारत में चल रही इंडिया एआई समिट 2026 की चर्चा हो रही है क्योंकि एआई के इस सबसे बड़े महाकुंभ में एआई के वर्तमान यानी प्रेजेंट से लेकर भविष्य तक यानी फ्यूचर तक का पूरा रोड मैप तैयार हो रहा है। एआई की दुनिया के ग्लोबल लीडर से लेकर तमाम देशों के हेड्स तक यानी नेशन हेड्स तक इस वक्त दिल्ली में मौजूद हैं। लेकिन क्या मोदी सरकार का प्लान सिर्फ एआई सबमिट तक सीमित है? क्या यह कहना सिर्फ काफी होगा कि यह सिर्फ एक एआई समिट है? यह भारत की पहचान है क्या? आज इस पर मैं विस्तार से बात करने वाला हूं। व्यूअर्स, नमस्कार। आपने सोशल मीडिया पर एआई को लेकर बहुत सारी बातें सुनी होंगी और बहुत सारी एजेंडे और प्रोपेगैंडा देखे होंगे। कोई कह रहा है एआई समिट पे यह नहीं है, कोई कह रहा है एआई समिट पे वह नहीं है। लेकिन मैं आपको बता रहा हूं भारतीय एआई समिट का मतलब क्या है, इसके मायने क्या हैं और सत्य और तथ्य में मैं आज बात करूंगा प्रधानमंत्री मोदी के मिशन, विजन और डेडीकेशन की। इसमें कोई दो राय नहीं है कि मोदी सरकार के प्लान के मुताबिक भारत दुनिया के सबसे बड़े एआई समिट को बहुत ही स्मूथली पूरा कर रहा है। थोड़े इधर-उधर की अगर हम ऊपर-नीचे की बात छोड़ दें तो ओवरऑल इसको 100 में से 90-95 नंबर मिल रहे हैं। लेकिन प्रधानमंत्री मोदी की सोच इससे कहीं दूर तक है। भारत में इस वक्त 20 से अधिक देशों के राष्ट्र प्रमुख यानी प्रधानमंत्री और राष्ट्रपति मौजूद हैं जिनमें फ्रांस के राष्ट्रपति इमैनुएल मैक्रों, ब्राजील के राष्ट्रपति लूला दा सिल्वा, स्पेन के प्रधानमंत्री पेड्रो सांचेज़, क्रोएशिया के प्रधानमंत्री, स्विट्ज़रलैंड के राष्ट्रपति, फिनलैंड के प्रधानमंत्री, ग्रीस के प्रधानमंत्री शामिल हैं। इन सबकी भारत में एक साथ मौजूदगी ये साफ-साफ बता रही है कि मामला सिर्फ एआई समिट तक सीमित नहीं है जनाब क्योंकि ये बात बहुत दूर तलक जा रही है। कैसे? अब बताता हूँ।

transcription: हूं आपको। क्योंकि अब बात ग्लोबल साउथ की ताकत की हो रही है। और इसे लीड करने के लिए भारत पहली कतार में कैसे खड़ा है, वो समझिए। लेकिन यह सब इतनी आसानी से नहीं हो रहा है। खुद प्रधानमंत्री मोदी इसके लिए परिश्रम की प्रकाशता कर चुके हैं और कर रहे हैं और इसे समझने के लिए आपको प्रधानमंत्री के पिछले तीन दिन की दिनचर्या यानी रूटीन मैं बता देता हूं। फ्रांस के राष्ट्रपति इमैनुएल मैक्रॉन 17 जनवरी यानी मंगलवार को मुंबई पहुंचे और प्रधानमंत्री मोदी भी इसी दिन मैक्रॉन के साथ बाइलेटरल के लिए मुंबई पहुंचे। दोपहर सवा तीन बजे के करीब दोनों नेताओं ने मुंबई के लोक भवन में बैठक करी, जिसमें डिफेंस, एआई, ट्रेड, इनोवेशन जैसे बड़े मुद्दे शामिल थे। यहीं से प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने वर्चुअली कर्नाटक में एयरबस H125 हेलीकॉप्टर की असेंबली लाइन का उद्घाटन भी कर डाला। इसके बाद 18 जनवरी की सुबह दिल्ली में प्रधानमंत्री मोदी के कई कार्यक्रम थे। इसलिए मुंबई में सारे काम निपटाने के बाद प्रधानमंत्री मोदी 17 जनवरी को ही दिल्ली लौट आए। 18 जनवरी को प्रधानमंत्री मोदी का कार्यक्रम और भी टाइट पैक था। दिल्ली के हैदराबाद हाउस में प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने दो देशों के राष्ट्राध्यक्षों के साथ बाइलेटरल मीटिंग करी। इसके अलावा प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने गूगल के सीईओ सुंदर पिचाई और सन माइक्रो सिस्टम के को-फाउंडर विनोद खोसला से भी मिले। कोई भी सामान्य आदमी इतनी मीटिंग के बाद चाहता होगा कि थोड़ा आराम कर लें। आप और मैं चाहते हैं, लेकिन इस सोच के बिल्कुल उलट दिन भर सारे काम निपटाने के बाद शाम 7:00 बजे प्रधानमंत्री मोदी भारत मंडपम पहुंचे, जहां एआई समिट चल रहा था। यहां भी प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने तमाम ग्लोबल लीडर्स से मिले और उनका एआई समिट में औपचारिक स्वागत किया। अब आती है 19 जनवरी, तो सुबह करीब 9:30 बजे प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने भारत मंडपम पहुंचकर इंडिया एआई समिट 2023 का औपचारिक उद्घाटन कर दिया। एआई इंपैक्ट समिट में अपनी स्पीच दी और दुनिया को बताया कि भारत को एआई में भय नहीं बल्कि भाग्य और भविष्य दिखाता है। इसके बाद प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने लीडर्स प्लेनरी में भी हिस्सा लिया। दोपहर होते-होते प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने यूएई, नीदरलैंड, स्विट्जरलैंड और ग्रीस के साथ बाइलेटरल मीटिंग पूरी करी। आप देश याद करिए कितने सारे। मैं एक बार फिर रिपीट कर देता हूं आपके लिए, आप नहीं काउंट कर पाए होंगे। रिपीट

title: India AI Summit 2026 Leads the World | PM Modi’s Vision Shapes the Future
transcription: मीट करता हूँ। सुनिए एक बार। यूएई, नीदरलैंड, स्विट्जरलैंड और ग्रीस के साथ बाइलेटरल मीटिंग पूरी करी। इसके बाद प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने 50 से ज्यादा ग्लोबल सीईओ के साथ सीईओ फोरम में हिस्सा लिया। सोचिए ये सारा काम मात्र एक दिन में हुआ है और पूरे तीन दिन का हिसाब देखा जाए तो राष्ट्र सेवा के लिए प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने दिन रात एक कर दिया। इसमें कोई दो राय नहीं है। एक सिर्फ एक सामान्य एआई सबमिट नहीं है। यह उसके साथ-साथ भारत की इमेज बिल्डिंग है। भारत की ग्लोबल पावर को दर्शाता है, भारत आज कहाँ खड़ा हुआ है, वो बताता है। इतने सारे राष्ट्राध्यक्ष, इतना बड़ा ग्लोबल एआई सबमिट और इसके लिए इंटरनेशनल पार्टिसिपेंट्स क्या-क्या बातें कर रहे हैं, ये आपको मैं एक-एक करके गिनाता हूँ। इस सबमिट के साथ-साथ भारत की छवि में किस तरह से चार चांद लगे हैं, ये आप फ्रांस के राष्ट्रपति मैक्रॉन, इमैनुएल मैक्रॉन की जुबानी सुन लीजिए। सुनिए। The CEO of Alphabet is Indian. The CEO of Microsoft is Indian. India does not just participate in global innovation, India leads it. साफ है कि किसी भी देश की तरक्की यूँ ही बैठे-बिठाए नहीं हो जाती। देश का मान और सम्मान यूँ ही नहीं बढ़ जाता, ये सब तब होता है जब देश का लीडर राष्ट्र हित में अपना तन-मन-विजन सब कुछ राष्ट्र प्रथम वाले मिशन के साथ झोंक देता है। शायद तभी दुनिया के बड़े-बड़े दिग्गज ये कहते हैं कि मोदी के नेतृत्व में भारत बिल्कुल सही दिशा में आगे बढ़ रहा है और सोचिए, मजाक उड़ाने वालों को क्या है, उन्होंने तो हर चीज का मजाक उड़ाया। डिजिटल पेमेंट का मजाक उड़ाया, मेक इन इंडिया का मजाक उड़ाया। आज भारत में हो रहे एआई सबमिट का भी मजाक उड़ा रहे हैं। जिनकी दुकान काम नहीं दुकान मजाक उड़ाने से चल रही हो, उन्हें अच्छा लगता है, लेकिन एक व्यक्ति लगातार उसकी दिनचर्या बताने की प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी की दिनचर्या मुझे बार-बार आपको बताने की आवश्यकता नहीं है, लेकिन एक व्यक्ति लगातार देश के मिशन में लगा हुआ है और इस एआई सब, इस एआई का लाभ हमें आने वाले दशकों में मिलेगा, तो इसीलिए ये भारत के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है, गर्व करने की बात है, सेलिब्रेट करने की बात है और इसमें छोटी-छोटी खामियां लगाकर तूफान खड़ा करना से कुछ हासिल नहीं होने वाला। जय हिंद, वंदे मातरम। गर्व करिए।

title: Gemini Spark | I/O 2026 Keynote
transcription: Let me show you how Spark works with some examples from my personal life. So here we are, we have the new Gemini app. It's been completely redesigned. We'll talk about that later in the show, and I want to take you into Spark here. And what you can see immediately is a dashboard with all the different tasks that I have going on in the background. It allows you to check in on these things, and I'll paste in a task right off the bat. This is a pretty straightforward example, but it's so useful. "Help me draft an email to the team, compile everything about our recent Gemini Live launches, and wins from the last week, use /ghostwriter." So there's a few things happening here. Compile everything. This goes across Docs, email, your chat, and grabs the most important information that you need for this update. It also is going to use all of the stuff you've seen in the time period of the last week with the /ghostwriter. That's a personal skill that I've written so the email sounds like me. And what's great is that with Spark, you can upload your favorite skills you find online. So we're going to let this run in the background. You can see it's already started doing various tool calls. And I'm going to switch over to another one from our personal life. We're planning a big block party. And you can see here, this is a pretty complex prompt. We want help grabbing all the RSVPs, keep a list of who's bringing what, remember to email those neighbors who haven't signed up yet. And what's amazing here is Spark will go through step-by-step. Look at all these steps, all the time it saves you going through, and again, work across the various skills and apps that you have. And what's really amazing is it'll break it down and also be able to generate files for you. So the first one here, this is a live RSVP tracker right in Google Sheets. You can see that it shows who's confirmed and who hasn't. What's amazing about this is it'll actually update because it's connected to Gmail. So when L. Thompson, row eight, RSVPs, it'll update, which is pretty amazing. The other thing is it keeps track of all the different guests, as well as sending follow-up reminders to who hasn't signed up yet. So again, this will happen, it'll create the drafts, and under my control, I can send them. And then finally, what the prompt did is it created a hype deck for the block party. And you can see, creates right in Google Slides, perfectly integrated. And you can see it even pulls in things like our giant bounce house that's going to be in the cul-de-sac. Now, all of this is happening in the background and under my control.

transcription: And what's amazing is Gemini can even go a step further and pull out things like your neighborhood homeowner's association won't let you set this up before Friday afternoon at June 5th. That's pulling from a file in my Google Drive. So, it's incredibly helpful about how it pulls it all together. Now, that's Spark working on a laptop. Spark is also amazing on the go, and it works across both Android and iPhone. So here you can see on my phone here, I'll open it up and I can go into Spark. You see both of the tasks we just went through, they sync across all your devices, which is so helpful. And Spark is amazing at just brain-dumping things on your mind. If you're super busy, it's almost you can just throw tasks over your shoulder, Spark'll catch them, and then run with them. So watch this. Start a few threads for me. The first one, find all the upcoming meetings with Sundar, and turn them all hot pink so I don't miss them. The second one, last night I met our new neighbor, John. Write a note to him and his family, invite them to our block party because they weren't on our list originally. The third one, create a document with the top things my wife and I need to do for the kids before the end of the school year. Categorize it by deadline and priority, make it easy to digest, I don't want to miss anything. Alright, so we'll send that in, and you can see at the speed of my voice, it's taking that one task, and it will capture all of that context as fast as I can talk. It starts out as a single thread here, and in the background, it's actually going to go through and break those down into individual tasks. Now, I can just put my phone away and get on with my day, and Spark works in the background for me. We'll check in later to see how it's doing. You can see, this is one of the first times we've been able to put a phone down and let it keep working on the I/O stage, it's great. Because we're prioritizing safety, we're rolling out Gemini Spark deliberately to trusted testers this week, and as a beta for US Google AI Ultra subscribers next week. We want this new type of help to be in as many hands as possible. So to do that, we're introducing a new Ultra plan for $100 a month. Sri Lanka has a coastline of approximately 1,340 kilometers, a striking natural asset for a small island nation. This extensive coastline supports rich biodiversity, fisheries, and coastal livelihoods, but it also places the country at the forefront of climate change impact, such as sea-level rise, erosion, and marine pollution. These coastlines and marine and coastal ecosystems are not only of immense value for heritage conservation, but also play a vital role in fisheries, tourism, and a wide range of socioeconomic activities that sustain communities and contribute significantly to national development. Sri Lanka also holds at least 88 square kilometers of mangrove ecosystems, which are among the most important blue carbon habitats in the region. These mangroves play a vital role in storing carbon, protecting shorelines from erosion, and serving as nurseries for marine biodiversity. Sri Lanka's marine and coastal ecosystems are among its most valuable natural assets. They sustain livelihoods, protect biodiversity, and support national resilience. Yet, these ecosystems, like in most other places in the world, are undergoing pressure from climate change, pollution, and the ongoing degradation of critical habitats. Meeting these challenges demands more than awareness, and it requires coordinated, science-based action at every level.

title: Ryan Short | Keynote Speaker on Place Branding | CivicBrand
transcription: There's this Latin phrase, probably won't say it right, but I think it's "esse quam videri." It means "to be rather than to seem." Said by Cicero a long time ago. In 1893, North Carolina made it part of their seal and their motto. And I think the spirit of it is hopefully pretty obvious, but it's like, it's not something you say. It's something that you do, right? If you say you're about something, it should show up in your, your policies and your budgets and your actions, not just your marketing campaigns and the words that you say. I was talking to director of Arts and Culture Department for a city, and they, he, they had done a council workshop. It's kind of day-long thing where they're going to, you know, like councils do. The whole first half of the day, budget cuts. What are we cutting? Public art, zero. His department just got gutted, ripped apart, everything. "Where can we cut? Where can we cut? Where can we cut?" to where he's like, "I don't even have anything left to cut." Because there's, there's important stuff: fire, safety, public safety, like real things that like, we can't cut those things, so we're going to cut the art and the culture and some of these things first, right? These are the nice-to-have things, and times are tough, nobody wants to do it, but we got to be adults. We got to, you know, make the hard choices. And people get that. I think smart people get that. But then at the close of the council workshop, "Let's end on a positive note. Budget talk wasn't fun. Let's have a new mission statement, vision statement for the city." They kind of brainstormed ideas. What are we all about? Art and culture was front and center. "This is what we're about: art and culture." And he stood up, he's like, "Are you kidding me? We just spent the whole day gutting arts and culture, our reality, to then just go put it on a little poster and say, 'We're about arts and culture.' That is the opposite of "to be rather than to seem." That is, we want to seem like we're about arts and culture, but we're not really about arts and culture.

title: Minimizing Tech Turnover in Conferences & Festivals | Cut E-Waste, Reuse Gear & Recycle Responsibly
transcription: Welcome. Today we're exploring how conferences and festivals can minimize technology turnover, reducing costs, extending equipment life, and supporting sustainability across every stage of event design and production. Today's events rely heavily on technology, from digital signage to mobile apps to interactive displays, all designed to elevate audience engagement. But rapid upgrading cycles push many devices out of service long before the end of their usable life. This constant replacement adds financial pressure, creating higher purchasing, storage, and transport costs. With smarter planning, events can maintain quality while utilizing existing equipment more efficiently and sustainably. Tech turnover often stems from a desire to impress with the newest gear, even when older equipment is still functional. This perception-driven cycle leads to high volumes of discarded tablets, displays, LED panels, and networking devices. Replacing equipment too frequently strains event budgets and contributes to growing e-waste streams. Each discarded device contains materials that require proper disposal through licensed recyclers to avoid environmental harm. Strong inventory management helps reduce unnecessary replacements. By keeping accurate records of equipment age, usage, and condition, event teams can clearly determine when upgrades are truly needed. Asset management systems allow devices to be rotated across multiple events, extending their lifespan. These tools also reveal when a piece of equipment can be repaired or refurbished instead of being replaced outright. With better visibility, purchasing decisions become smarter, more cost-effective, and more sustainable. Modular equipment is one of the most valuable strategies for reducing turnover. Interchangeable components allow lighting, audio boards, and AV systems to be repaired easily without replacing entire devices. Firmware upgrades can also extend the useful life of older equipment. Interoperability ensures older and newer devices function together, preventing unnecessary full system upgrades. Planning for modularity reduces both long-term costs and the environmental footprint of constant tech replacement. Not every event requires brand-new technology. Many attendees care far more about meaningful content and clear audiovisual output than the generation of the device being used.

title: Shettima Urges Governors on Economic Growth | Senate Approves E-Transmission | 2026
transcription: This is Megastar Magazine TV. Hello and welcome to Megastar Magazine TV. My name is Monique Agbey. In the news, Vice President Kashim Shettima urged governors of the 36 states, ministers, and other public officials to pursue an inclusive economic growth model that filters down to the everyday lives of Nigerians. Shettima spoke in Abuja while delivering the keynote address at the opening of the National Economic Council, NEC, conference, a two-day retreat of governors and key stakeholders aimed at strengthening national economic coordination and accelerating inclusive growth. The Vice President warned that the government's mission would remain incomplete if progress does not translate into dignity, opportunity, and hope for citizens across the country. The Senate has approved the electronic transmission of election results to the Independent National Electoral Commission's results viewing portal, while permitting manual collation to serve as a backup where technology fails. The decision followed a reconsideration of a disputed clause in the Electoral Act Amendment Bill during an emergency plenary on Tuesday. The upper chamber stopped short of making electronic transmission compulsory and also rejected the provision for real-time upload of results. Under the reviewed section, presiding officers at polling units are to electronically transmit results to the IReV portal after voting and documentations are completed. The amendment, however, provides that where electronic transmission cannot be carried out due to communication or network challenges, the manual results sheet, form EC8A, will become the primary basis for collation and declaration. The Court of Appeal sitting in Abuja held that the Senate acted within its powers when it suspended the lawmaker representing Kogi Central, Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, for misconduct. The court held that the suspension did not violate the senator's parliamentary privileges or her constitutional rights. The court set aside the contempt proceedings and the 5 million Naira fine earlier imposed on the lawmaker over an unprofessional apology she directed at Senate President, Godswill Akpabio.

title: Multi-Objective Evolutionary Design of Molecules with Enhanced Nonlinear Optical Properties
transcription: Hi, my name is Gamrich, and I'm here to talk about our GECCO project called the Multi-objective Evolutionary Design of Molecules with Enhanced Non-linear Optical Properties. So, NLO materials are essential for mainly telecommunications infrastructure, and we look at specifically the device called an electro-optic modulator, which modulates a beam of light. So, we're looking at NSGA-II, MAP-Elites, MoAM, mu-lambda, and then simulated annealing. So, a mix of QD and multi-objective optimization algorithms, and then some single-objective ones. How we encode molecules is using SMILES. We limit our molecular search space to organic atoms, and we employ these seven mutation operators, and we do not use crossover in our evolution. And you can see how symbols are used to encode molecules. We evaluate the properties which we're optimizing using quantum chemistry, and specifically the Hartree-Fock level of theory with the PySCF library. So, our multi-objective algorithms maximize the beta over gamma ratio, which is important for frequency conversion. We target a range of 100 to 500 atomic units for linear polarizability. Our HOMO-LUMO gap, we target a range of 2 to 4 electron volts. And then our energy per atom, we try to minimize, and this promotes stability in the molecule. And then our single-objective algorithms simply optimize the beta-gamma ratio. So, each algorithm evaluates approximately 2,000 molecules across 20 independent seeds. title: Why We Will Never "Cure" Cancer
transcription: In 1971, Richard Nixon signed the National Cancer Act and declared war on cancer. The language was deliberate: a war with a target date, the way you'd talk about landing on the moon. 55 years later, cancer still kills about 10 million people a year worldwide. We didn't lose that war through lack of funding. The United States alone has poured well over $100 billion into cancer research since that signature. We lost it because the enemy was never a single enemy. That's the part the fundraising campaigns skip. Cancer isn't a disease. It's a category closer to infection than flu. Breast cancer alone splits into at least four molecularly distinct diseases that happen to grow in the same organ. Lung cancer, pancreatic cancer, leukemia: different biology, different mutations, different behavior, filed under one word because they share a symptom: cells that won't stop dividing. Asking for a cure for cancer is a little like asking for a cure for infection. Which infection? Which mechanism? Which host? Point one: The enemy evolves faster than you can aim. Here's the detail oncologists live with and rarely get to explain on camera: a tumor isn't one clone of identical cells. Peter Nowell described this back in 1976 in a paper called "The Clonal Evolution of Tumor Cell Populations," and the idea has only gotten scarier with better sequencing. A single tumor is a population: genetically diverse, competing internally, mutating with every division. Give it a drug, and you're not killing the tumor. You're running a selection experiment. The cells sensitive to the drug die. The handful that happened to carry a resistance mutation before treatment even started now have the whole tumor to themselves, no competition left. Six months later, the cancer comes back, and it comes back immune to the exact drug that shrank it. This is why remission and cure are different words. Oncologists know the difference intimately.

title: Why We Will Never "Cure" Cancer
transcription: Patients often don't find out until the relapse scan. Point two, cancer is a numbers game you were built to eventually lose. The British epidemiologist Richard Peto noticed something strange in 1977. If cancer were just bad luck accumulating with every cell division, then whales should be riddled with tumors. They mostly aren't. Neither are elephants. This is called Peto's paradox, and one leading explanation is that elephants independently evolved roughly 20 extra copies of a tumor suppressor gene called TP53, giving their cells a much more aggressive self-destruct button. Humans got one working copy. We are, cellularly speaking, running a budget security system in a body that lives 70, 80, 90 years, trillions of cell divisions, each one a fresh roll of the dice on a catastrophic copying error. You are not unlucky if you get cancer, given enough divisions, it is closer to a statistical inevitability than an anomaly. The real question was never whether the system fails, it's how long it takes to... Point three, the environment isn't a bystander, it's a co-conspirator. For decades, the assumption was that cancer research meant studying the tumor cell in isolation, understanding its mutations, and building a drug that recognized them. That framework produced real wins and also a wall. Tumors don't grow in a vacuum, they recruit blood vessels through a process called angiogenesis, they hijack immune cells that are supposed to be hunting them, and they physically remodel the tissue around them into something more hospitable to malignancy and more hostile to treatment. Judah Folkman spent much of his career arguing that starving a tumor's blood supply could stop it, and angiogenesis inhibitors did eventually reach the clinic. They rarely cure anything on their own because the tumor has other routes. Cut off one supply line and clonal diversity, the same mechanism from point one, finds another. Point four, the immune system was the plot twist, and it still isn't the ending.

title: Why We Will Never "Cure" Cancer
transcription: In 2018, Jim Allison and Tasuku Honjo won the Nobel Prize for a genuinely new idea. Instead of attacking the tumor directly, release the brakes your own immune system was already wearing. Checkpoint inhibitors like the ones that came out of their work have produced results that looked like science fiction in advanced melanoma, some patients with metastatic disease going into durable remission for years. This is the closest oncology has come to the word cure in a modern sense. But, it works spectacularly in a minority of patients and barely at all in most. Nobody fully knows why one person's tumor is legible to their immune system and another's is invisible to it. The variable isn't just the cancer, it's the individual immune history of the person carrying it, built from a lifetime of infections, genetics, and exposures nobody tracked closely enough to model. Layer these four problems on top of each other and you get the actual shape of the wall. The disease isn't one disease. The tumor that responds to treatment today is genetically a different tumor by the time it relapses. The body's natural defense against malignancy is a compromise, not a guarantee, inherited from an evolutionary process that only ever needed you to survive long enough to reproduce. And the environment surrounding the tumor is actively working against whatever drug you throw at it. There is no single lock, which means there was never going to be a single key. What's actually happened since 1971 isn't failure, it's a quiet shift in the target. Five-year survival rates for many cancers have climbed substantially. Some, like childhood leukemia, have gone from near certain death to majority survival. The war on cancer didn't produce a surrender, it produced something closer to a very long, very expensive stalemate, fought disease by disease, mutation by mutation, patient by patient, with victories that don't generalize and defeats that teach you something anyway. Somewhere in the last five decades, the goal quietly moved from curing cancer to managing it, and almost nobody announced the change out loud.
