title: The Smile Nobody Questioned (New Spoken Words 2026)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I got really good at smiling. So good, that nobody noticed the war happening behind my eyes. I laughed loud, showed up, answered messages with "I'm good". Even cracked jokes while my chest felt like it was carrying a thousand pounds of silence. And the scary part is, after a while, even I started believing the performance. See, depression doesn't always look like darkness. Sometimes it looks like being tired all the time for reasons sleep can't fix. Sometimes it looks like staring at the ceiling at 3:00 a.m. replaying every mistake like your mind signed a contract with regret. Sometimes it sounds like, "You're not enough! You're falling behind! Everybody else figured life out except you!" And you begin to drown in thoughts nobody else can hear. That's the thing about invisible pain. People only notice broken bones, not broken spirits. So you learn survival tricks. You become the therapist friend who secretly needs saving. You become the strong one because strong people aren't allowed to collapse. You disappear into music, into work, into scrolling endlessly at night, hoping distraction feels something like peace. But silence, silence is dangerous. Because when you sit alone long enough, you meet every version of yourself you tried to outrun. The insecure child, the abandoned heart, the exhausted soul. And one day, I realized I wasn't just fighting depression. I was fighting the version of me that believed I had to earn love by suffering quietly. I thought healing meant never hurting again. But healing is actually waking up and choosing to stay, even when your mind tells you to disappear. Healing is messy. It's crying in parked cars, it's canceling plans to breathe, it's admitting, "I'm not okay." before your breaking point introduces you to the ground.

Without it, everyday activities, such as walking, writing, or even sleeping, could shift the bone fragments out of place. By holding the bone steady, the cast creates the stable conditions needed for healing. Within the next week or two, the reparative phase becomes the dominant stage of healing. Specialized cells called chondroblasts produce cartilage, forming a soft callus that bridges the gap between the broken ends of the bone. This soft callus acts like a temporary scaffold, but it is still relatively weak. Because the cast prevents excessive movement, the soft callus can develop without being disturbed. Several weeks later, another group of cells called osteoblasts begins replacing the soft callus with a hard callus made of new bone tissue. These cells deposit minerals such as calcium and phosphates into the developing bone, making it stronger and more rigid. Throughout this stage, the cast continues to protect the healing bone from external forces that could interfere with recovery. Once the fracture has healed sufficiently, the cast is removed using a special vibrating cast saw that cuts through the plaster without harming the skin. అంటున్నారు. ఈరోజు మన వీడియోలో ఎవోర్ ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్ కి సంబంధించిన వేరియంట్స్ ఏమున్నాయో? ఇందులో ఉన్న టెక్నికల్ స్పెక్ట్స్ ఏంటి? ఫీచర్స్ ఏంటి? కంప్లీట్ డీటెయిల్స్ ని ఈరోజు మన MVS ఆటో తెలుగు ఛానల్ లో తెలుసుకుందాం. నమస్తే, నేను మీ కృష్ణ చైతన్య మండేలా. మీరు చూస్తున్నారు MVS ఆటో తెలుగు. ఎలక్ట్రిక్ వెహికల్ రంగంలో అడుగుపెట్టాలనుకుంటున్నారా? కానీ ఎక్కడి నుంచి ప్రారంభించాలో అర్థం కావడం లేదా? సరైన ఈవి డీలర్షిప్ ఎంపిక నుంచి, లాభదాయకమైన ఛార్జింగ్ స్టేషన్ ప్లానింగ్ వరకు, మీ అవసరానికి సరిపోయే ఈవి వెహికల్ సెలెక్షన్ నుంచి, కాలేజీ ప్రాజెక్టులకు టెక్నికల్ గైడెన్స్ వరకు, ప్రతి దశలో మీకు తోడుగా ఉంటుంది, ఈవి కుర్రాడు. అనుభవంతో కూడిన నిపుణుల సలహా, స్పష్టమైన మార్గదర్శకం, సరైన నిర్ణయానికి నమ్మకమైన సహాయం. ఈరోజే స్క్రీన్ పై కనిపిస్తున్న వాట్సాప్ నెంబర్ కు మెసేజ్ చేయండి, మీ ఈవి ప్రయాణాన్ని ఆత్మవిశ్వాసంతో ప్రారంభించండి. సో ఎవోర్ కి సంబంధించిన ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్ డిజైన్ అయితే ఇలా కనిపిస్తుందన్నమాట. ఇది వచ్చి EX 2S అనే ఒక పేరుతో అయితే ఈ బైక్ ని అయితే మార్కెట్ లోకి అయితే రిలీజ్ చేశారన్నమాట. సో మీకు సైడ్ ప్రొఫైల్ అయితే ఇలా కనిపిస్తుంది. సో కలర్ ఆప్షన్స్ కూడా ఉన్నాయి. రెడ్ కలర్, అలానే బ్లూ కలర్, బ్లాక్ కలర్, గ్రే కలర్ ఇలా మొత్తం ఫోర్ కలర్ ఆప్షన్స్ లో అయితే అందిస్తున్నారన్నమాట. సో ఇందులో వీళ్ల టాప్ ఎండ్ వేరియంట్ వచ్చి 5 కిలోవాట్ల బ్యాటరీ ప్యాక్ కెపాసిటీతో 260 కిలోమీటర్ల వరకు IDC రేంజ్ అనేది కంపెనీ వాళ్ళైతే క్లెయిమ్ చేస్తున్నారు. అలాగే ఈ ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్ లో 114 కిలోమీటర్ల టాప్ స్పీడ్ కూడా లభిస్తుంది అనేది చెప్తున్నారు అన్నమాట. ఇక బైక్ పరంగా చూసుకున్నట్లయితే కాస్త పెట్రోల్ బైక్ లుక్ లాగానే కనిపిస్తుంది అన్నమాట. ఒక్కొక్క యాంగిల్ లో మనకి బైక్ అయితే ఇలా కనిపిస్తుంది అన్నమాట. సో ముందు వెనక కూడా మీకు డిస్క్ బ్రేక్స్ తోనే ఈ ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్ అయితే లభిస్తుంది. ఇక చార్జర్ చూసుకున్నట్లయితే ఫ్రంట్ సైడ్ మీకు బూట్ స్పేస్ లాగా ఉంటుంది. దాన్ని ఓపెన్ చేస్తే మీకు చార్జర్ కేబుల్ అయితే తీసుకుని మీరైతే చార్జింగ్ అయితే పెట్టుకోవచ్చు అని చెప్తున్నారు అన్నమాట. అలానే వీళ్ళు చెప్తున్న విషయం ఏమిటంటే ఫాస్ట్ చార్జింగ్ అవుతుంది. ఎవ్రీ మినిట్ కి 1.2 కిలోమీటర్లు చార్జింగ్ అయితే చేసుకోవచ్చు అనేది చెప్తున్నారు అన్నమాట. అలానే 15 ఆంప్స్ వాల్ అవుట్లెట్ దగ్గర అయితే మీరు చార్జింగ్ పెట్టుకుంటే ఇంత ఫాస్ట్ గా అయితే చార్జింగ్ అయితే చేసుకోవచ్చు అనేది క్లైమ్ చేస్తున్నారు. అలానే ఈ బైక్ లో మొత్తం ఫైవ్ రైడ్ మోడ్స్ అయితే లభిస్తాయి అనేది చెప్తున్నారు అన్నమాట. ఇందులో మీకు ఎకో, సిటీ, ప్యామ్ ప్లస్, స్పోర్ట్స్, అపెక్స్ మొత్తం ఐదు మోడ్స్ లో అయితే మీకు ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్ అయితే లభిస్తుంది అని చెప్తున్నారు. దీంట్లో మీకు 10.5 కిలోవాట్ల పీక్ transcription: చేస్తున్నారన్నమాట. ఈ బైక్‌లో మీకు బ్యాటరీ ప్యాక్ అనేది ఇక్కడైతే ఉంటుందన్నమాట. అలానే ఇందులో వీళ్ళు చెప్తున్నదేంటంటే యాక్టివ్ కూలింగ్ అనేది లభిస్తుందని చెప్తున్నారు, IP67 ప్రొటెక్షన్ కూడా ఈ పర్టికులర్ బ్యాటరీ ప్యాక్ కి లభిస్తుందని చెప్తున్నారు. ఇక ఈ ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్‌లో ఇంకొక ఇంట్రెస్టింగ్ ఫీచర్‌ని కూడా వీళ్ళు యాడ్ చేసినట్టు అయితే చెప్తున్నారు. దీని పేరేం చెప్తున్నారంటే SYFT అని ఒక ఫీచర్ అన్నమాట. సో వాస్తవానికి ఇదొక గేర్‌లెస్ బైక్. అంటే ఇందులో ఎటువంటి గేర్లు అనేవి మీరు యూస్ చేయాల్సిన అవసరం లేదు. బట్ వీళ్ళు ఏం చెప్తున్నారంటే ఒక పెట్రోల్ బైక్ ఫీల్‌ని కంటిన్యూ చేయాలనే ఉద్దేశంతో ఆర్టిఫిషియల్‌గా గేర్స్ కింద అయితే ఏర్పాటు చేసామనేది చెప్తున్నారన్నమాట. ఇక్కడ మీకు ఆ గేర్ లాగా ఉంటుంది. అంటే మనం నార్మల్ బైక్ నడుపుతున్నప్పుడు అక్కడ క్లచ్ నొక్కి మన గేర్స్ చేంజెస్ చేస్తాం కదా, సేమ్ అలాగే పెట్రోల్ బైక్ ఫీల్ ఇవ్వడం కోసం కింద మనకి గేర్ లాంటిదయితే ఇస్తారన్నమాట. బట్ నిజానికి ఇది గేర్ కాదు. ఇక్కడ ఏంటంటే ఒక టార్క్‌ని కంట్రోల్ చేసే ఒక సిస్టమ్ అన్నమాట. సో మీకు ఇంకా డీటైల్‌గా ఎక్స్‌ప్లైన్ చేయడం కోసం ఒక ఇమేజ్ అయితే జనరేట్ చేశాను. ఇప్పుడు మీరు ఇది పర్టికులర్ గేర్‌ని మీరు ఎప్పుడైతే ఫుట్ లెవల్‌ని మీరు అడ్జస్ట్ చేసుకుంటూ ఉంటారో, అంటే ఫస్ట్ మోడ్ సెకండ్ మోడ్ కింద అయితే చేంజ్ చేసినప్పుడల్లా మీరు ఇచ్చిన త్రాటిల్ ఏదైతే ఉంటుందో అది ఒక కంట్రోలర్‌కి వెళ్లి ఆ కంట్రోలర్‌లో అది ఏం అర్థం చేసుకుంటుందంటే ఇక్కడ మీరైతే కాలు దగ్గర ఉన్న ఫుట్ లెవల్‌లో మీరైతే చేంజెస్ మోడ్స్ పెట్టారో దానికి తగ్గట్టుగా టార్క్ అనేది అడ్జస్ట్ అవుతుందని చెప్తున్నారు. సో డిఫరెంట్ టార్క్స్ అనేది మీకు అయితే అందిస్తుందని చెప్తున్నారన్నమాట. ఇక్కడ గేర్స్‌, క్లచ్‌లు, ట్రాన్స్‌మిషన్ అయితే లేదు బట్ ఏంటంటే రియల్ బైక్‌కి ఎలక్ట్రిక్ ఒక టచ్ అయితే ఇస్తున్నారన్నమాట. ఉదాహరణకి మీరు ఫస్ట్ గేర్ ఆన్ చేస్తే మాక్సిమం టార్క్ అయితే లభిస్తుంది, సెకండ్ గేర్‌లో మరింత స్మూత్‌గా వెళ్తుంది, థర్డ్ గేర్‌లో బ్యాలెన్స్‌డ్ పవర్, ఫోర్త్ గేర్‌లో రిలాక్స్డ్ పెర్ఫార్మెన్స్, ఫిఫ్త్ గేర్‌లో హై స్పీడ్ ఫీల్ ఇలాంటి డిఫరెన్స్ చేంజ్ అయితే వస్తుంది. దీనికి వీళ్లొచ్చి 250 Newton-meter ఇన్‌స్టాంట్ వీల్ టార్క్ అనేది ఈ ఎలక్ట్రిక్ బైక్ యొక్క మోటర్ అనేది అయితే జనరేట్ చేస్తుందని చెప్తున్నారన్నమాట. సో దీనికి ఈ పర్టికులర్ ఓవరాల్ టెక్నాలజీకే వీళ్ళు ఇస్తున్న పేరు ఏంటంటే SYFT అనే ఒక షార్ట్ ఫామ్‌ని అయితే వీళ్ళు అయితే పిలుస్తున్నారన్నమాట. ఇక బైక్ ముందు భాగంలో చూసుకున్నట్లయితే మీకు ఇంటెలిజెంట్ అండ్ కనెక్టెడ్ ఫీచర్స్ అయితే ఉన్నాయి అని చెప్తున్నారు. కాల్స్ మరియు వాట్సాప్ సింక్ ఫీచర్స్ అయితే ఉన్నాయని చెప్తున్నారు, లైవ్ క్రికెట్ స్కోర్స్ ని కూడా మీరైతే చూసుకోవచ్చు అని చెప్తున్నారు. దీనితో పాటుగా స్మార్ట్ జియో ఫెన్సింగ్ ఆప్షన్ కూడా ఉంటుంది. అంటే మీరు బైక్‌ని పర్టికులర్ రేడియస్‌లో లాక్ చేసుకున్న తర్వాత ఎవరైనా బైక్‌ని మూవ్ చేస్తే మీకు అలర్ట్స్ అయితే వస్తాయన్నమాట. అలాంటి ఫీచర్ కూడా మీకు ఈ బైక్‌లో అయితే లభిస్తుంది. ఇక్కడ రేంజ్ రియల్ రేంజ్ ప్రిడిక్టర్ కూడా ఈ బైక్‌లో అయితే లభిస్తుంది, బ్యాటరీ పర్సంటేజ్ అయితే చూపిస్తుంది అన్నమాట. దాంతోపాటుగా బ్లూటూత్ title: 260 km Range- Avore Electric Bike Launch India - Mvs AutoTelugu
transcription: టైమరు, అలాగే డేట్, అలాగే మీకు సెట్టింగ్స్ ఇవన్నీ డీటెయిల్స్ కూడా మీకు ఇన్స్ట్రుమెంట్ క్లస్టర్ లో అయితే చూడొచ్చు అనమాట. ఇక్కడ 4G కనెక్టివిటీ ఇంటిగ్రేటెడ్ అనేది ఈ పర్టికులర్ బైక్ లో అయితే ఇస్తున్నట్లుగా చెప్తున్నారు. అలాగే బైకు ముందు భాగంలో చూసుకున్నట్లయితే ప్రొజెక్టర్ హెడ్ ల్యాంప్ అయితే లభిస్తుంది అనమాట. అలాగే వీళ్ళు యూస్ చేస్తుంది వచ్చి PMSM మోటార్ ని అయితే యూస్ చేస్తున్నారు. అలాగే అలాయ్ వీల్స్ కూడా ఈ పర్టికులర్ బైక్ లో అయితే లభిస్తుంది అనమాట. ముందు వెనుక కూడా డిస్క్ బ్రేక్స్ తో ఈ బైక్ అయితే లభిస్తుంది. ఇక ఇతర ఫీచర్స్ చూస్తే ఫాల్ ట్యాంపర్ అలర్ట్స్ అనమాట. ఇన్కేస్ మీ బైక్ కనుక కింద పడితే దానికి సంబంధించిన అలర్ట్స్ కానివ్వండి, క్రాష్ కి సంబంధించిన అలర్ట్స్ కూడా మీకు మొబైల్ కి అయితే సింక్ చేసుకోవచ్చు అనేది చెప్తున్నారు. వెహికల్ డయాగ్నోస్టిక్స్ మరియు TPMS ఫీచర్ కూడా ఈ బైక్ లో అయితే లభిస్తుంది అని చెప్తున్నారు. అలాగే ఫుల్ స్టాక్ నావిగేషన్, ఇంకా ట్రిప్ డేటా ను కూడా మీరు ఈ బైక్ కి సంబంధించిన ఇన్స్ట్రుమెంట్ క్లస్టర్ లో అయితే చెక్ చేసుకోవచ్చు అనేది చెప్తున్నారు. జియో ఫెన్సింగ్ గురించి మీకు ఆల్రెడీ చెప్పాను. అలాగే ఈ బైక్ లో మీకు మొబైల్ యాప్ కనెక్టివిటీ కూడా అయితే అందిస్తున్నారనమాట. సో AI కనెక్టివిటీ ఫీచర్స్ ద్వారా మీరు ఏమన్నా ఇన్ఫర్మేషన్ కావాలనుకుంటే మొబైల్ యాప్ ద్వారా కూడా మీరు మెసేజ్ అయితే చేయొచ్చు అని చెప్తున్నారు. అంటే మీకు మీ బైక్ లో ఉన్న స్టేట్ ఆఫ్ ఛార్జ్ కానివ్వండి, నా రైడింగ్ స్టైల్ ఏంటి అంటే ఈ బైక్ లో ఉన్న డేటా ఏదైతే ఉందో అనలైజ్ చేసుకుంటుందన్నమాట. మీరు ఇప్పటివరకు రైడ్ చేస్తున్న ఇన్ఫర్మేషన్ అంతా కూడా అనలైజ్ చేసుకొని మీకు సజెషన్స్ కూడా ఇస్తుంది అని చెప్పి వీళ్ళైతే హైలైట్ చేస్తున్నారు. ఇక ఇప్పుడు ఈ బైక్ లో మొత్తం మూడు వేరియంట్స్ ఇస్తున్నారు. బేస్ వేరియంట్ వచ్చి ఎవోర్ EX1 అనమాట, మిడ్ వేరియంట్ వచ్చి ఎవోర్ EX2, టాప్ వేరియంట్ వచ్చి ఎవోర్ EX 2S అనమాట. ఇందులో బేస్ వేరియంట్ వచ్చి మీకు 7.5 కిలోవాట్ల పీక్ పవర్ ఎలక్ట్రిక్ మోటార్ ని అయితే ఇస్తున్నారు. టాప్ స్పీడ్ వచ్చి 100 కిలోమీటర్లు ఉంటుంది. సున్నా నుండి 40 కిలోమీటర్ల వేగాన్ని వచ్చి 3.2 సెకండ్లలో రీచ్ అవుతుంది. IDC రేంజ్ వచ్చి 160 కిలోమీటర్ల వరకు క్లైమ్ చేస్తున్నారు, 3.24 కిలోవాట్ల బ్యాటరీ ప్యాక్ కెపాసిటీ తో అనమాట. ఇక ఇందులో మీకు రివర్స్, ఎకో, సిటీ, స్పోర్ట్ మోడ్స్ అనేవి అయితే ఉంటాయనమాట. ఇక ఈ బైక్ ని మీరు 20 టు 80% ఛార్జ్ చేయడానికి మూడు గంటల సమయం అయితే పడుతుందని చెప్తున్నారు. దీంతో మీకు 750 వాట్ ఛార్జర్ అయితే అందిస్తున్నామని చెప్తున్నారు, ఇందులో మీకు ఆన్ బోర్డ్ ఛార్జర్ అయితే లభిస్తుంది అనమాట. అలాగే బేస్ వేరియంట్లో మీకు వెహికల్ డయాగ్నోస్టిక్స్ సిస్టం కానివ్వండి, హాంకింగ్ మీటర్ వంటి ఫీచర్స్ అయితే ఉండవు అని చెప్తున్నారు. టచ్ స్క్రీన్ డిస్ప్లే అనేది కూడా బేస్ వేరియంట్లో లభించదు. డిస్ప్లే సైజ్ వచ్చి 7 ఇంచ్ ఎల్సిడి డిస్ప్లే అయితే లభిస్తుంది అనమాట. కాల్, ఎస్ఎంఎస్ వంటి అలర్ట్ ఫీచర్స్ బేస్ వేరియంట్లో అయితే లభించవన్నమాట. జిపిఎస్ అయితే లభిస్తుంది బట్ నావిగేషన్ అనేది బేస్ వేరియంట్లో అయితే అందించట్లేదు. సో బేస్ వేరియంట్ యొక్క ప్రైస్ వచ్చి ₹1,35,000, బట్ ఇంట్రడక్టరీ ప్రైస్ కింద మొదటి 10,000 యూనిట్స్ కి ₹1,25,000 కి ఈ బైక్ అయితే అందిస్తామని చెప్తున్నారు. ఇక రెండో వేరియంట్ వచ్చి

title: 260 km Range- Avore Electric Bike Launch India - Mvs AutoTelugu
transcription: ఎవర్ EX2 అన్నమాట. ఇందులో కూడా మీకు 7.5 kw ఎలక్ట్రిక్ మోటార్ ఏ ఉంటుంది. బట్ ఇందులో ఏంటంటే బ్యాటరీ ప్యాక్ కెపాసిటీ అయితే ఎక్కువగా ఉంటుందన్నమాట. 5 kw బ్యాటరీ ప్యాక్ కెపాసిటీ తో 255 km సర్టిఫైడ్ రేంజ్ అయితే క్లెయిమ్ చేస్తున్నారన్నమాట. ఇందులో మీకు ఛార్జర్ కూడా రేటింగ్ మారుతుంది, 1500 w ఛార్జర్ అయితే లభిస్తుంది అన్నమాట. ఈ బైక్ ని మీరు రెండు గంటల్లోనే 80% ఛార్జింగ్ అది చేసుకోవచ్చని చెప్తున్నారు. ఇందులో కూడా మీకు 7 ఇంచ్ డిజిటల్ ఎల్సీడీ డిస్ప్లే అనేది లభిస్తుంది. ఇక ఎవర్ EX2 వేరియంట్ చూసుకున్నట్లయితే, ఈ బైక్ ఒక ఎక్స్ షోరూమ్ ప్రైస్ ₹1,49,000 నుంచి అయితే స్టార్ట్ అవుతుంది అన్నమాట. ఇక మూడోది ఎవర్ EX2S. ఇది వచ్చేసి 10.5 kw పీక్ పవర్ ఎలక్ట్రిక్ మోటార్ ఉంటుంది. 114 km టాప్ స్పీడ్ అయితే క్లెయిమ్ చేస్తున్నారు. సున్నా నుండి 40 కిలోమీటర్ల వేగాన్ని 2.8 సెకన్లలోనే రీచ్ అవుతుంది అని చెప్తున్నారు. ఇందులో మీకు అడిషనల్ మోడ్స్ అనేవి యాడ్ అవుతాయి అన్నమాట. ఎకో, పాంప్ ప్లస్, సిటీ, స్పోర్ట్స్, అపెక్స్, SWS మోడ్స్ అనేది ఈ వేరియంట్ లో మాత్రమే లభిస్తుంది. ఇక చార్జర్ కూడా 1500 w ఛార్జర్ title: Leading Change Webinar Clip
transcription: Hi, and welcome. This is Leading Change from Where You Are, Empowered Strategies for Navigating Transitions. My name is Cassie Blossey. I'm the co-founder of Sageburg Consulting, I'm a nonprofit executive leader, education policy is the core of my background and experience and I love working in the community, specifically around change management in nonprofits and small businesses. One of the things that is really important about nonprofits is that they're so core to our community and, whether they like it or not, they also experience change pretty regularly, and in fact change is the only constant, right? So what I have seen in my experience is that nonprofits that set up systems to help them go through change, uh, experience much more um, long-term success and they see fewer disruptions in their actual services, and so they can meet their impact and mission. So today, we're going to talk about a couple of key areas of change. These three are the top types of change that I see in nonprofits and small businesses every day. Uh, the first one is one that we have a little bit more control over and we'll talk about the next two because they tend to give us a little bit more anxiety, so let's start with planned. Planned change has to do with change that you can anticipate, something that you know for sure is coming up. That can be a retirement, the end of a temporary role, maybe it's the end of a grant, maybe it's something that you knew you were going to start and then had a very clear end date. So when you're talking about planned, uh, change, one of the things that's really important is making sure you have really good communication systems and thinking about, "Okay, we know that this transition's going to happen in March, so we should start setting us, ourselves up for success by thinking about that transition, maybe in January, how are we making sure that everything will be successful once that change happens?" So, you have a lot more control in this area of change. The next two, as I mentioned, not our favorite, but you can still be successful. Emergent change is the unfortunate change that happens when there's something sudden, it's unexpected, sometimes it comes with additional risk, for example, sudden illness or a natural disaster.

transcription: There are some organizations that I've seen that have experienced a natural disaster like a flood and have had to figure out what am I going to do? It's really important to think about what are the different ways that we can be creative and shift on a dime. So, in emergent change especially, you may not be able to predict the specific incident and whether or not it happened. But, you can set up your your organization for success by thinking about what are our predictable factors here? We know that if we have a brick and mortar building, anything can happen. A tree could fall on the roof, something could break. So, what are our plans for if we need some sort of, you know, change in location or or something along those lines. So, it's not about focusing on what isn't plannable, it's about taking those pieces and thinking about, I can do this one piece. Imposed is something that folks don't really think about as change management. But, it is. And you can also take some ownership and take some control of imposed change. And these are things that typically arise from an external influence. So, this is a change in policy, a reorganization. It's something that is imposed upon your team, your organization, or something along those lines. So, a key risk in this area, especially for leaders, is the issue when a policy or a change comes up, and maybe you don't agree with it. This happens a lot to leaders. And they're tasked with then communicating to their teams or to their stakeholders. Well, here's how we have to change, and here's how we need to plan for it together. title: Sustainability Strategy Masterclass: Purpose and Key Ingredients
transcription: Just going back to priorities in your sustainability strategy, are you addressing the economic, the social, the environmental, or is the focus really on the environmental side, or the social side? And that's something that is really important to decide up front, what is the purpose of this strategy? And once you've understood that, what are the goals? So, I often see organizations start with a headline target like, "We'll be net zero by 2050." And I don't think that's quite the right way of doing it, because a lot of the time, you don't have the data to know whether that's realistic. So, when I say goals, I don't mean necessarily putting time bound specific targets that you might not have the information to make. So, a goal could be something like by the end of 2026, we will understand our carbon footprint and be in a position to set a net zero target. Or it could be by the end of 2027, everyone in our organization will be carbon literate. So, when you set the goals that you're setting in your strategy need to be appropriate for where your organization is at. And then, finally, the purpose of having a sustainability strategy is to communicate what your organization's priorities and goals are, not just to the people working inside your organization, but also to your customers, to your supply chain, to potential stakeholders that are looking to invest, or regulators might be looking to have this information. So, a really core benefit that I have seen of having very public sustainability strategies for a lot of our clients is that it then makes it easier for their supply chain to understand what information they're going to need. And it just helps create that collaboration in getting that data in place, in understanding where emissions are coming from, where water is being used, and actually working together to make the change, because sustainability is a really complicated problem. If it was simple, we'd we'd have solved climate change. We wouldn't be worrying about these events. And so, creating visibility through a sustainability strategy is a great way to get people working together on solving what is really one of the biggest problems and challenges that we are facing as a as a global society.

And it's important that any vision statement for your organization's sustainability strategy is aligned to the overall vision statement of the business, because if your organization is, say, in manufacturing and your vision is about providing the most circular economy components that you can provide to your customers, that's that's quite aligned. That you you're looking to use resources effectively, whereas if you had a vision statement that was about people using public transport, that's not really aligned to the core business of a manufacturing company and it and it can be jarring. title: Getting started with Claude Cowork
transcription: Claude Cowork meets you where your work happens and allows you to delegate complete tasks to Claude. If it's on your computer, Claude can find and edit it. If it's in the cloud, Claude connects through services like Google Drive, Notion, and Slack. If it's in the browser, Claude is there too, through Claude in Chrome. Describe what you need done, and Claude does it. You can watch it work, steer when it matters, or step away and come back to the results. Claude Cowork is generally available in the Claude Desktop app on macOS and Windows for Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users. To get started, open Claude Desktop and click the Cowork tab. In a regular Claude chat, you work with Claude step-by-step. In Cowork, you hand off tasks, and Claude handles the rest while you focus on other work. First, give Claude access to a folder on your computer. Select the folder directory or project you want Claude to operate in. It asks permission before making changes to your file system. Claude can now read, create, and edit files in that folder directly. You can favorite the folders you go to most or select multiple folders to connect disparate data sources. Second, connect your tools. Cowork supports connectors that link Claude to services. These let Claude pull context from where your work already lives. Third, if you've set up Claude in Chrome, Cowork can use it for browser-based tasks, reading web pages, extracting data from sites, and navigating across tabs. Under settings, you can also click the Cowork tab and set global instructions that apply to every session, like context about your role or directions to create files as Word docs instead of markdowns. One thing to keep in mind, your Cowork sessions are stored locally on your device, and the Desktop app needs to stay open while Claude is working on a task. Let's start with something really simple.

questions.answer: Give Claude access to a folder on your computer.
options: Connect your Google Drive account directly.
Set up global instructions in the Settings menu.

options: It automatically backs up the entire folder.

questions.answer: By favoriting folders or selecting multiple folders.
options: By creating cloud-based backups of the directories.
By pinning folders directly to the system tray.
By syncing folders via Google Drive only.
By setting up automated folder-sharing links.

questions.question: What role do connectors play in Claude Cowork?
questions.answer: They link Claude to services to pull context from where your work already lives.
options: They allow Claude to bypass firewalls and access private databases.
They automatically encrypt all files stored in Claude's folder.
They speed up the processing of markdown files.
They sync your system settings across multiple devices.

questions.question: Which browser-based tasks can Claude Cowork perform if Claude in Chrome is set up?
questions.answer: Reading web pages, extracting data from sites, and navigating across tabs.
options: Installing browser extensions, managing passwords, and clearing cache.

ऐ! ये कंटेंट क्रिएशन शुरू करने के लिए प्रोफेशनल सॉफ्टवेयर, एडवांस्ड एडिटिंग या एक्सपेंसिव गियर नहीं चाहिए। बल्कि चाहिए सीक्रेट नंबर वन - द माइंडसेट शिफ्ट। बहुत से लोग को लगता है कि कंटेंट क्रिएशन शुरू होता है एक कैमरा या ऐप से। बट एक्चुअल में वो शुरू होता है आपके दिमाग से। तो कैमरा तू मुझे दे दे, दिमाग से शूट कर लियो तू। अबे मेरा मतलब ये है कि शुरू करने से पहले आपको खुद क्लेरिटी लानी पड़ेगी कि आप किसके लिए कंटेंट बना रहे हो, आप क्या वैल्यू दे रहे हो और कोई आपका कंटेंट क्यों देखे। जब एक बार आपको ये 'वाई' का जवाब मिल जाता है ना, तो कंटेंट बनाना बहुत आसान हो जाता है। क्योंकि अब आप सिर्फ व्यूज चेज नहीं कर रहे हो, आप कनेक्शन बिल्ड कर रहे हो। आप रियल वैल्यू दे रहे हो एक्जैक्टली उन लोगों को जिनको उसकी ज़रूरत है। यानी कि परफेक्ट कंटेंट स्ट्रेटेजी। जो भी क्रिएटर्स लंबे टाइम तक टिकते हैं ना, (Yeah boy) रेलेवेंस में लंबे टाइम तक टिकते हैं ना वो वही होते हैं जिन्होंने ट्रस्ट बिल्ड किया है। ट्रेंड से चलने वाले क्रिएटर्स मुश्किल से 5% होते हैं जो बाद में सस्टेन कर पाते हैं। तो इसीलिए क्रिएट विद इंटेंशन्स, क्रिएट फॉर रियल पीपल, नॉट जस्ट व्यूज। क्योंकि व्यूज की रेस में आप कहीं ना कहीं खुद को, खुद की स्टाइल को ही खो दोगे। और वो ना हो, उसके लिए बहुत ज़रूरी है - टू फाइंड योर वॉइस। देखो, हर क्रिएटर कॉपी करने से ही शुरू करता है एंड दैट्स कंप्लीटली ओके। हाँ, ये देख इसने तेरी वीडियो कॉपी करी। अबे ये सब कॉपी करते हैं। ... वीडियो रुला दूँगा इनकी। तो देखो, कॉपी करना बहुत ही नॉर्मल है। ऐसे ही तो हम सब सीखते हैं। लेकिन बहुत ज़रूरी है कि आप जल्द से जल्द अपनी एक स्टाइल फाइंड आउट कर लो वरना आप वही कॉपी की भीड़ में खो जाओगे। और लोग किसी कॉपी को क्यों देखेंगे अगर उनके पास रियल ओरिजिनल बेटर वर्ज़न एक्ज़िस्ट करता है तो? अब आपका सवाल होगा कि यूनिक वॉइस लाएँ कहाँ से? AI से? हाँ, ये तो सबसे इम्पोर्टेंट है कि AI यूज़ मत करना वॉइस के लिए। अपनी रियल आवाज़ का इस्तेमाल करो भले ही आपको अभी खराब लग रही है, धीरे-धीरे इंप्रूव कर लोगे। बट रियल आवाज़ रखो। अब अपनी यूनिक स्टाइल क्रिएट करने का एक सिंपल थ्री-स्टेप फॉर्मूला है। स्टेप नंबर वन, इन...

title: How to Master the Art of Content Creation in 2026
transcription: लिमिटेड, जो क्रिएटर्स तुम्हें पसंद हैं, उनके जैसी वीडियोस बनाओ। और बनाते-बनाते उनकी स्टोरी टेलिंग, उनकी स्ट्रक्चरिंग को समझो। स्टेप नंबर टू: इंटीग्रेट। उनके स्टाइल में अपने आइडियाज को इंटीग्रेट करो। अपनी थीम, अपना म्यूजिक चॉइस, अपने ह्यूमर के स्टाइल बीच-बीच में डालो। और जब आप ये चीज अच्छे से करने लगो, देन कम्स द स्टेप नंबर थ्री, इनोवेट। एक्सपेरिमेंट करना शुरू करो। कुछ वीडियोस में कंप्लीटली अलग अपने स्टाइल से ही कंटेंट बना दो। हो सकता है कुछ वीडियोस अच्छी परफॉर्म ना करें, कुछ वीडियोस अच्छी परफॉर्म कर जाएं। तीन-चार वीडियोस बनाओगे, तीन-चार डिफरेंट स्टाइल्स एक्सपेरिमेंट करोगे, तब जाकर कोई एक क्लिक करेगी। मेरा तो एक ही बार में क्लिक हो जाता है। हैं? वो कैसे? ऐसे। गंदा जोक था ये वाला। देखो, आपकी वॉइस का मतलब ये नहीं है कि आप क्या बता रहे हो, बल्कि ये है कि आप कैसे बता रहे हो। जैसे आज तक बहुत सारे लोग एडिटिंग को स्क्रीन पे बैठ के ट्यूटोरियल की तरह बोरिंग तरीके से समझाते थे। मैंने उसी कंटेंट को थोड़े फन, एंटरटेनिंग वे में प्रेजेंट किया और रिजल्ट आपके सामने है। चलो, मतलब जोक्स मारने हैं ना? तेरे से तो बेटर ही कर लूंगा। अब इसका मतलब ये नहीं है कि सब फनी कॉमेडी ही करो। यही तो मेन पॉइंट है भाई। हो सकता है आप रॉ रियल में ज्यादा अच्छे हो। हो सकता है आप सिनेमैटिक कंटेंट में ज्यादा अच्छे हो। जिस भी चीज में आप अच्छे हो, उस पे डबल डाउन करो। क्योंकि एल्गोरिदम्स, फिल्टर्स, कॉपी-पेस्ट से भरी आज के इस सोशल मीडिया पे ऑथेंटिसिटी ही है जो आपको सबसे अलग बनाएगी। लेकिन मैक्सिमम लोग आज के इस कॉम्पिटिटिव टाइम पे भी फोन उठाकर बस वीडियो बना दे रहे हैं जबकि इट इज वेरी इंपॉर्टेंट टू अंडरस्टैंड द क्रिएटिव प्रोसेस। तीन वर्ड्स की सिंपल सी प्रोसेस है और इसमें से एक भी चीज मिस नहीं कर सकते। प्लान, क्रिएट एंड रिफ्लेक्ट। कैमरा उठाने से भी पहले नोटबुक लो और अपना कंटेंट प्लान करना शुरू करो। वो तो जब आइडियाज आते हैं बना लेता हूं, प्लान क्या करना? ऐसे तो बन गए कंटेंट क्रिएटर। बैठके पहले आइडियाज प्लान करो आपकी नीश में क्या चल रहा है, आपकी ऑडियंस को क्या चाहिए और कुछ अपने पर्सनल एक्सपीरियंसेस भी। Notion, Trello, Google Sheets यूज़ कर सकते हो अपने कंटेंट कैलेंडर को ऑर्गेनाइज करने के लिए। आपके पास कम से कम एट अ टाइम अगले 10 वीडियोस का आईडिया होना चाहिए। इससे आप कभी आइडियाज, क्या बोल रहा हूं मैं? इससे आपके पास कभी आइडियाज खत्म नहीं होंगे और आप कंसिस्टेंट रह पाओगे। मैक्सिमम लोग कंसिस्टेंट इसलिए नहीं रह पाते क्योंकि उनके पास आइडियाज ही नहीं होते। वो एक वीडियो बना लेते हैं फिर सोचते हैं कि अब अगली क्या बनानी है, अच्छा ये वाली वीडियो हो गई अब नेक्स्ट क्या बनाऊं? तो वो कंटेंट क्रिएशन में आइडिएशन के लूप में ही फंस के रह जाते हैं और वीडियो बना ही नहीं पाते। देन द नेक्स्ट स्टेप इज़ टू क्रिएट। वाह! कितना अच्छा एक्सप्लेन किया 'क्रिएट', मज़ा आ गया। हां, ये जितना सिंपल लग रहा है उतना ही मुश्किल है। अगर आप परफेक्ट वीडियो बनाने की कोशिश करोगे कि मैं पहले सिनेमैटोग्राफी, एडिटिंग, स्क्रिप्ट राइटिंग, स्टोरी टेलिंग सब कुछ सीख जाऊं फिर वीडियो बनाऊंगा, तो कभी नहीं बना पा रहे आप वीडियो। इंस्टेड, आपका मेन ऐम होना चाहिए वीडियो बनाना। बनाते-बनाते खुद ही सीख जाओगे यार। इनिशियली सब कुछ परफेक्ट करने की कोशिश मत करो। आप Epidemic Sound थोड़ी हो।

transcription: हैं? बस अपना कंटेंट बनाते हुए ध्यान देना कि उसमें एक हुक हो, फिर रियल वैल्यू एंड एंड में एक छोटा सा CTA और ये सब चीजें व्यूअर को एक परफेक्ट इमोशन के साथ परोसने के लिए ज्यादा कुछ नहीं चाहिए। बस चाहिए अच्छा म्यूजिक। फ्री तो नहीं मिलता, कितना अच्छा होता ना अगर कोई होता जिसे हम बोल देते कि भाई इस सिचुएशन के लिए मुझे परफेक्ट म्यूजिक लाके दे दे और वो दे देता। वेल, वेल, वेल। अब यह पॉसिबल है, एपिडेमिक साउंड के असिस्टेंट फीचर के साथ। सिंपली बस इसको जाकर बोल दो की, "Give me a perfect music for intense suspense scene" और ये लो मिल गया परफेक्ट म्यूजिक। अब इसी म्यूजिक को आपको किसी और स्टाइल या इंस्ट्रूमेंट में कंवर्ट करना है तो उसके लिए है एपिडेमिक का अडैप्ट फीचर। मान लो कोई रॉक म्यूजिक है। आपको इंडियन क्लासिकल स्टाइल में चाहिए। है ना क्रेजी? title: How to Master the Art of Content Creation in 2026
transcription: या आप मेरे फैन हो गए इसलिए देख ली। कुछ भी हो सकता है। अब देखो यार स्टोरी टेलिंग शॉर्ट में समझाना बहुत ही मुश्किल है। इसका सबसे बेस्ट तरीका है कि आप यूट्यूब वीडियोज़ को, मूवीज़ को, वेब सीरीज़ को, इनको देखो, एनालाइज़ करो, ऑब्ज़र्व करो और इनको ब्रेक डाउन करके स्टोरी टेलिंग को सीखो, ताकि आप भी अपने कंटेंट में ऑडियंस से कनेक्ट कर पाओ। बट एंड में बात वही आ जाती है कि एक बार तो ये चीज़ कोई भी कर लेगा। बट सबसे बड़ा सीक्रेट है इसी चीज़ को कंसिस्टेंटली कर पाना। और कंसिस्टेंसी को ना बहुत लोग तो गलत ही समझ लेते हैं। उन्हें लगता है कंसिस्टेंसी का मतलब होता है हर रोज एक वीडियो आनी चाहिए। बट मान लो आप वीक में एक वीडियो अपलोड करते हो तो फिर हर हफ्ते एक वीडियो अपलोड करो। उस चीज़ पे कंसिस्टेंट रहो और इम्प्रूव करते रहो हर वीडियो के साथ। जब आप कंसिस्टेंटली दिखते हो तो आप लोगों के लिए फैमिलियर बनते हो। फैमिलियारिटी से ट्रस्ट बनता है और ट्रस्ट से कम्युनिटी। बट सबसे बड़ा सीक्रेट पता है क्या है? इवॉल्विंग योर कंटेंट। अगर आपकी ऑडियंस के साथ-साथ आपका कंटेंट इवॉल्व नहीं हो रहा है, आप नए आइडियाज़ ट्राई नहीं कर रहे, अपने फॉर्मेट्स ट्राई नहीं कर रहे, तो भाई कुछ टाइम बाद लोग छोड़ देंगे आपको। क्योंकि इतने कंटेंट से भरे इंटरनेट पे लोगों के पास हज़ारों ऑप्शन्स हैं। लोगों को रोज़ कुछ नया चाहिए, उनको रोज़ कुछ नया मिल भी जाएगा। इसी चीज़ को फॉलो करते हुए मैंने अपनी रिव्यू सीरीज़ निकाली, व्हिच इज़ समथिंग न्यू ऑन माय चैनल। मेरी यूज़ुअल वीडियोज़ से कम्प्लीटली हट के एंड पीपल लव्ड इट। अब कई बार हो सकता है लोग अच्छा रिस्पॉन्ड ना करें, वीडियो फ्लॉप हो जाए, बट वही तो असली मज़ा है कंटेंट क्रिएशन का। हर नई वीडियो एक नया चैलेंज, एक नया एंटीसिपेशन, एक नया एक्साइटमेंट, एक नया डिप्रेशन लेके आती है। और अगर आपको पसंद नहीं है कि हर बार सेम चीज़ मेरे साथ बार-बार हो रही है तो भाई, सॉरी बट कंटेंट क्रिएशन आपके लिए नहीं है। आप कुछ और देख लो। सो, अब आपने ये वीडियो यहाँ तक देख ली है तो आई होप यू नो हाउ टू मास्टर द आर्ट ऑफ़ कंटेंट क्रिएशन। देखो हाँ, ये एक लंबी जर्नी है, बट इम्पॉसिबल नहीं है। काफी बार इस जर्नी में आपको लगेगा कि यार नहीं होगा मेरे से, मेरे बस की नहीं है, तो उस टाइम के लिए ना, मेरी बस ये एक बात याद रख लेना। आज से 2 साल पहले हज़ार सब्सक्राइबर्स के साथ मैं गिव अप करने ही वाला था। इस यूट्यूब के सपने को हमेशा के लिए छोड़ देने वाला था, इस क्रिएटिव साइड को अपनी ज़िंदगी से हटा देने वाला था। बट आज मैं उसी सपने को जी रहा हूँ। अगर वो 2 साल पहले वाला अभय हार मान गया होता ना, तो आज आप मेरे को ये सब चीज़ें बोलते हुए नहीं सुन रहे होते। आज ये वीडियो एक्ज़िस्ट नहीं करती। आज आप एक्ज़िस्ट नहीं करते एज़ एज़ मेरे सब्सक्राइबर। तो भाई सिंपल सी बात है, सीखो, मेहनत करो, इम्प्रूव करो, रेस्ट लो, ब्रेक लो, बट गिव अप नहीं करना। बाकी इस वीडियो से अगर आपको कुछ भी सीखने मिला हो, थोड़ी सी भी इंस्पिरेशन मिली हो तो लाइक, शेयर, कमेंट कर देना, मुझको अच्छा लगेगा, मुझे भी इंस्पिरेशन मिल जाएगी। बाकी मैं मिलता हूँ आपसे अगली वीडियो में, तब तक के लिए टाटा, बाय बाय।

সেগুলো সিপিডি কোর্স কি না সেটা আমাকে দেখতে হবে। সিপিডি কোর্সগুলো কিন্তু মিনিমাম ৫০ ঘণ্টা, বাকি যত কোর্স আছে আপনি ৭০, ৮০, ৯০ ঘণ্টাও অনেকে করে নিয়েছে শুনছি, কিন্তু করে নিতেই পারেন কোনো অসুবিধা নেই, যত বেশি করবেন তত আপনার স্কিল ডেভেলপমেন্ট হবে। তার সঙ্গে আর একটা গুরুত্বপূর্ণ যে খুব সম্ভবত ৯০% আমি যা দেখছি সারা ভারতবর্ষের সিচুয়েশন, টেট আমাদের দিতে হবে। তো যেহেতু টেট আমাদের দিতে হবে, এমন কোর্সগুলো সিপিডি কোর্সগুলো বেছে নেব যেগুলো আমাদের টেট দিতে সুবিধা হবে বা টেটের কিছু নলেজও গ্যাদার হবে, সেই বিষয়টাও আজকে আলোচনা করবো। যেমন ৫০ ঘণ্টা যেটা আছে সেটা হচ্ছে ম্যান্ডেটরি করা হয়েছে সিপিডি কোর্সের এবং এটা প্রতি বছর করতে হবে। এই বছর করে নিলাম মানে না, প্রতি বছর কোর্স পালটে দেবে তারা সেই অ্যাপস এর মধ্যে এবং সেই অ্যাপস এ গিয়ে আমাদের কোর্সগুলো করতে হবে এবং প্রতি বছর কী কী কোর্সগুলো দেওয়া হবে সেগুলো জানিয়ে দেওয়া হবে। এনরোলমেন্ট হওয়ার শেষ তারিখ হচ্ছে এবছর ৩১শে আগস্ট অর্থাৎ ২০২৬-২৭ শিক্ষাবর্ষের এনরোলমেন্টের শেষ তারিখ হচ্ছে ৩১শে আগস্টের মধ্যে কিন্তু এনরোলমেন্ট করে নিতে হবে। এবং অনেকগুলো কোর্স কিন্তু শেষ হয়ে যাবে ১৫ই সেপ্টেম্বর, কিছু কিছু কোর্স কিন্তু ৩১শে আগস্ট বা জুলাই মাসেও, এই ৩১শে জুলাইয়ের মধ্যেও কিন্তু কিছু কোর্স শেষ হয়ে যাচ্ছে। তাই তড়িঘড়ি করে কিন্তু আমাদের এই কোর্সগুলো করতে হবে এবং এই কোর্সগুলো আমরা করছি কিনা সমস্ত ডিআই, সরি ডিআই নয়, স্কুল ইন্সপেক্টর এসআই এবং এআইকে দায়িত্ব দেওয়া হয়েছে, তারা স্কুল ওয়াইজ মনিটারিং করবেন যে সমস্ত শিক্ষকরা এনরোলমেন্ট করলেন কিনা বা তারা কোর্সগুলো করলেন কিনা। তাই এবার কিন্তু আমাদেরকে এই কোর্সগুলো কিন্তু করতেই হবে। তো কীভাবে করবো, কীভাবে সিপিডি কোর্সগুলো বেছে নেব, সেই পুরো ব্যাপারটা আমি স্ক্রিনে দেখাবো, তাই ভিডিওটা চলুন দেখে নিন পুরো ব্যাপারটা। তো আমি আমার মোবাইল স্ক্রিনে চলে এসেছি। মোবাইল স্ক্রিনে এই যে দীক্ষা অ্যাপ, দীক্ষা কোর্সে যাবেন না, প্রথমে দীক্ষা অ্যাপে ক্লিক করবেন। এই যে দেখতে পাচ্ছেন, এখানটায় দীক্ষা অ্যাপে ক্লিক করার পর এখান থেকে আপনাকে নিয়ে যাবে ও দীক্ষা কোর্সে আপনাকে যেতে হবে। সেটা কীভাবে সেটাও আমি দেখিয়ে দিচ্ছি চলুন। আমরা দীক্ষা অ্যাপে চলে এসেছি।

title: Diksha CPD Courses for Primary and High School Teachers। Diksha Courses for Teachers।
transcription: ল্যামে এই যে নিচের দিকে লেখা আছে দেখুন দীক্ষা কোর্স এই জায়গাটায় আপনি ক্লিক করবেন। এই জায়গাটায় ক্লিক করলে কিন্তু আপনি দীক্ষা কোর্সে চলে যাবেন। দীক্ষা কোর্স অ্যাপটা খুলে গেছে। তো এখানে যে এক্সপ্লোর কোর্সেস লেখা আছে না এটা আপনার ফোনে কিন্তু নিচের দিকে দেখাবে। যেহেতু আমার স্ক্রিন রেকর্ডার অন আছে এবং আমি ফোনের মোডটাকে চেঞ্জ করে নিয়েছি, সেই জন্য এটা এরকম দেখাচ্ছে। তো এইখানে আপনি ক্লিক করবেন, এক্সপ্লোর কোর্সেসে। এই জায়গাটায় ক্লিক করলে কিন্তু আপনি চলে যাবেন। লে আপনাকে কিন্তু এরকম একটা এতে নেবে। এখানে আপনার ফোনে কিন্তু অন্যরকম দেখাবে। এইখানে আপনি দেখবেন ফিল্টার করতে হবে আপনাকে। দেখুন এখানে ফিল্টার করবেন এই এই জায়গাটায় দিলে আপনাকে এই যে ক্লাস দেওয়া আছে, ক্লাসে এই ক্লাস লেখা টায় এটা তে ক্লিক করলে আপনার বিভিন্ন ক্লাসের কোর্সগুলো বেরোবে এবং সেখানে লেখা আছে দেখুন সি পি ডি। সিপিডি এই জায়গাটায় কিন্তু ক্লিক করবেন। এখানে ক্লিক করে অ্যাপ্লাই ফিল্টার করে দেবেন দিলে সমস্ত সিপিডি কোর্সগুলো কোন কোন গুলো রয়েছে সেটা কিন্তু দেখাবে। যেমন দেখো, দেখানো হচ্ছে এখানে আইসিটিসি এসসিইআরটি হরিয়ানা, এটা হরিয়ানার ক্ষেত্রে। আচ্ছা পেডাগোগি লিডারশিপ ট্রেনিং প্রোগ্রাম, এটা হেডমাস্টারদের জন্য। তারপরে যে কোর্স গুলো দেখাচ্ছে দেখুন, প্রত্যেকটা কোর্স কিন্তু সমস্ত টিচারদের জন্য। এখানে নিচে লেখা আছে দেখবেন এই যে যেমন কোর্সটা দেখাচ্ছে রিফ্রেসার ট্রেনিং এখানে সিপিডি কিন্তু লেখা আছে এই নিচের দিকে এই জায়গাটায়। তার মানে এটা কিন্তু একটা সিপিডি কোর্স। তারপরের কোর্সটাও সেরকম দেখুন এম এস ফাউন্ডেশন লিটারেসি এটাও একটা সিপিডি কোর্স। নিউট্রিশন সার্ভে এটাও একটা সিপিডি কোর্স, এটা প্রাইমারি থেকে টুয়েলভ পর্যন্ত যেকোনো টিচাররা করতে পারবে। পার্সোনালাইজড এডাপ্টিভ লার্নিং পাল, এটাও সিপিডি কোর্স। এরকম পরপর জীবন কৌশল, এটা বাংলায় দেওয়া রয়েছে সিপিডি করে একচুয়ালি ওটা আসামি ভাষায় দেওয়া রয়েছে। এনহান্স টিচার স্কিল ফর স্টুডেন্ট ক্যারিয়ার, এটাও সিপিডি কোর্স। এরকম পরপর সিপিডি কোর্সগুলোকে আপনার কাছে কিন্তু নিয়ে যাবে। না হলে এক্সপ্লোর কোর্স করে পুরোটা সার্চ করতে থাকবেন। নিচে লেখা আছে সিপিডি কোর্স বলে এবং কোনটা কত ঘণ্টার সমস্ত ডিটেলসে আপনি পেয়ে যাবেন। যেমন ধরুন আমি এই এই প্রোগ্রামটা দেখতে চাইছি। এই প্রোগ্রামটা কোর্স ডেসক্রিপশনে গেলে এই যে কোর্স ডেসক্রিপশন সমস্ত ডেসক্রিপশন দেওয়া আছে। কোর্স ১০ ঘণ্টার কোর্স এটা কিন্তু ৩১শে জুলাইয়ের মধ্যে কিন্তু এই কোর্সটা শেষ হয়ে যাবে লেখাই আছে। এরকম কিছু কোর্স আছে ২০২৭ এর সেপ্টেম্বর পর্যন্ত আছে। কিছু কোর্স আছে নেই বেশিদিন, ৩১শে আগস্টের মধ্যে শেষ হয়ে যাচ্ছে। তো এইভাবে আমাদের সমস্ত কোর্সগুলো কিন্তু করে নিতে হবে যেগুলো সিপিডি কোর্স এগুলো কমপক্ষে ৫০ ঘণ্টা করতে হবে। ভিডিওটা ভালো লাগলে সবাইকে শেয়ার করে দেবেন। চ্যানেলে নতুন হলে চ্যানেলটা সাবস্ক্রাইব করে নেবেন। থ্যাংক ইউ ফর ওয়াচিং।

title: 🎓 How to Become a Company Secretary (CS) in 2026 | Complete Step-by-Step Guide | Neha Patel
transcription: CSEET में टोटल चार सब्जेक्ट्स होते हैं जो कि मैं आपको स्क्रीन में दिखा देती हूं। एंड जैसे की मैंने आपको बताया की इसमें से स्टार्टिंग के तीन पेपर्स आपको लिखने हैं एंड लॉ का जो पेपर है वह आपका एमसीक्यू बेस्ड होगा। बट वह भी आपको सेंटर में जाकर करना है। CSEET ऐसा स्टेज है की जो आप एक्चुअल में खुद से पढ़कर भी क्लियर कर सकते हो। बट मैं रिकमेंड करूंगी की आप कोई कोचिंग या फिर यूट्यूब से लेक्चर्स देखो ताकि आपको इन डेप्थ सीएस की नॉलेज मिले, उसका करिकुलम पता चले, वे ऑफ़ आस्किंग क्वेश्चंस पता चले। एंड मेक श्योर करना कि आप इसमें राइटिंग प्रैक्टिस बहुत सारी करो तो आपके लिए CSEET क्लियर करना इजी हो जाएगा। जैसे ही आप CSEET क्लियर कर लेते हो, उसके बाद आपको एक ट्रेनिंग करनी पड़ती है जो की होती है थ्री डेज ओरिएंटेशन प्रोग्राम - टीडीओपी। यह आप आईसीएसआई वेबसाइट में जाकर अपने आप को रजिस्टर कर सकते हो और घर बैठे-बैठे भी टीडीओपी दे सकते हो या फिर अपने आसपास के कोई आईसीएसआई सेंटर में जाकर भी टीडीओपी दे सकते हो। जैसे ही सीएस एग्जीक्यूटिव में रजिस्टर करोगे उसके 30 डेज के अंदर आपको टीडीओपी खत्म करनी पड़ती है। नाउ सीएस एग्जीक्यूटिव इज वन ऑफ़ द टफेस्ट स्टेज ऑफ़ सीएस। CSEET क्लियर होने के बाद आप सीएस एग्जीक्यूटिव देते हो। एंड सीएस एग्जीक्यूटिव साल में दो बार होता है, जून में होता है एंड दिसंबर में होता है। एंड यहां पर दो ग्रुप्स होते हैं। ग्रुप वन में ये चार सब्जेक्ट्स हैं। ग्रुप टू में ये तीन सब्जेक्ट्स हैं। यह सातों के सातों सब्जेक्ट्स आपको राइटिंग में है। कुछ भी एमसीक्यू नहीं है। मेरे टाइम पर तीन पेपर्स एमसीक्यू हुआ करते थे एग्जीक्यूटिव में बट अभी इट्स कंपलीटली राइटिंग। आपके पास ऑप्शन है की आप कोई एक ग्रुप पहले, तो आप ग्रुप टू भी पहले दे सकते हो, ग्रुप वन भी दे सकते हो। या फिर आप दोनों ग्रुप एक साथ दे सकते हो। इट इस कंपलीटली अप टू यू। मैं रिकमेंड करूंगी की दोनों ग्रुप एक साथ दो, इसके काफी बेनिफिट्स होते हैं। ऑल इंडिया रैंक दोनों ग्रुप एक साथ देने पर ही आती है। आपको सेट ऑफ़ का बेनिफिट मिल जाता है की अगर एक ग्रुप में मार्क्स कम आए और दूसरे में ज्यादा, वो मार्क्स एडजस्ट हो जाते हैं। तो अगर आप एग्जीक्यूटिव क्लियर करना चाहते हो तो हर एक पेपर में आपको 40 परसेंटेज मार्क्स लाना पड़ेगा, दैट इस 100 में से 40। एंड ग्रुप वाइज देखा जाए तो एवरेज 50% आपको लाना पड़ेगा। जैसे ग्रुप वन में 400 में से 200 लाना पड़ेगा, ग्रुप टू में 300 में से 150 आपको लाने पड़ेंगे। तब जाकर आप एग्जीक्यूटिव क्लियर कर पाओगे। एंड यही सेम पासिंग परसेंटेज CSEET का भी है की इंडिविजुअल सब्जेक्ट्स 40 एंड एवरेज 50। यही सब में, प्रोफेशनल में भी यही है। दिस इस योर एग्जाम पासिंग परसेंटेज स्ट्रक्चर। नाउ गाइस, एग्जीक्यूटिव में यू हैव टू बी वैरी केयरफुल बिकॉज़ यहां पे जो लेवल ऑफ़ क्वेश्चंस आपसे पूछे जाते हैं वह कंपलीटली डिफरेंट होते हैं जो हम एक्चुअल में ट्वेल्थ में पढ़ते आए हैं। तो यहां पे आपको मेक श्योर करना है की आप पास्ट ईयर के क्वेश्चंस बहुत रेगुलर बेसिस पे सॉल्व कर रहे हो। आप राइटिंग प्रैक्टिस और टेस्ट काफी रेगुलर बेसिस पे दे रहे हो। आप लेक्चर्स डेली बेसिस पे देख रहे हो, बैकलॉग्स नहीं क्रिएट कर रहे हो और रिवीज़न कंसिस्टेंटली कर रहे हो। सेल्फ स्टडी पर भी अच्छा खासा टाइम इन्वेस्ट कर रहे हो। अगर आप डिटेल्ड एग्जीक्यूटिव की स्ट्रेटजी जानना चाहते हो तो मैंने काफी सारे वीडियोस बनाए हुए हैं प्लस ऑल इंडिया रैंक सीरीज जो की 30 डेज की है, वह भी मेरे यूट्यूब चैनल पर लाइव है। अगर आप ऑल इंडिया रैंक लाना चाहते हो तो वो सीरीज जरूर देखना, उसमें मैंने सारे

transcription: meri strategies aur tips discuss ki hai with study routine. Ab agar aap CS executive clear kar jaate ho toh ye bohot hi badi baat hai bohot acchi baat hai. CS Executive clear karne ke baad aapke paas do option aata hai. Ek option toh ye aata hai ki aap apni training start kar do jo ki practical training hoti hai 21 months ki. Aapko actual me corporate ya fir firm me jaake isko karna hota hai. Toh ye option humari ICSI deti hai ki aap isko Executive ke baad bhi start kar sakte ho ya Professional ke baad bhi start kar sakte ho. Jab bhi start karo 21 months ki hoti hai. Toh ye yahan pe aapko option aata hai ki Executive ke baad aap training start karo ya toh aap Professional do. Mai recommend karungi ki training start kar do aur sath me Professional de do. For example agar aap June 26 me Executive clear karte ho toh aapke paas option aata hai June 27 me Professional ko appear karne ka, ek saal ka gap toh rehne hi wala hai, toh usme aap apni ek saal ki, 12 months ki training bhi khatam kar sakte ho, and ek group ke liye bhi prepare kar sakte ho Professional ka. Toh ye zyada strategically dekha jaye toh jaldi aapki training bhi khatam ho jayegi and fir aapka Professional bhi khatam ho jayega. Agar aapko training Executive ke baad nahi deni hai toh aap seedha ek saal ke baad Professional me dono group ke liye appear karna, tab jab aapka Professional clear ho jayega uske baad fir aap 21 months ki training start kar sakte ho, it is completely up to you. Ab jaise hi aap Professional me aate ho toh yahan pe bhi again do group hote hai. Group 1 me char subjects jo ki ye rahe, Group 2 me teen subjects jo ki ye rahe. Yahan pe jo do paper hai, wo elective hote hai. Now elective matlab ki aap dekh ke answer likh sakte ho, but that doesn't mean ki wo easy hone wala hai, bacche isi subject me fail hote hai, because kahi se bhi wo question aapko puch sakta hai. Toh Professional me jaise hi aap aaoge aapko actual me saara pata chal gaya hoga ki ICSI ka mindset kya hota hai, ICSI kis level ke questions puchta hai, kaise aapko writing karni hai, but elective aisa paper hai jisme bacche, you know, ghabra jaate hai aur bacche stuck ho jaate hai. Toh jaise hi Professional me aap aaoge you have to be very cautious of elective. Now, Professional bhi aap clear kar loge na fir bhi aap apne naam ke aage CS nahi laga paoge. Kyunki iske baad ek aur training hoti hai jo ki hai CLDP, Corporate Learning Development Program. Now ye training aapko karni padti hai jo ki actual me offline hoti hai, 30 days ki hi hoti hai, 15 days online, 15 days offline. Yahan pe aapko actual me center me jaake rehna hoga and wahan pe aapko sikhaya jayega kaafi, kaafi interesting cheeze, professionalism sikhayi jayegi, fir company law ke concepts ke baare me bhi aapko bataya jayega, and kaafi saare competitions hote hai, bohot hi maza aata hai. Mai toh bolungi ki aap sab ek baar residential CLDP ka experience lena. Jaise hi aapka CLDP training jo hoti hai, wo khatam hogi na, usi ke baad hi aapko convocation me bulaya jayega and aapko milegi CS ki degree and aap apne naam ke aage CS laga sakte ho.

transcription: तो यह पूरा प्रोसीजर है सीएस बनने का। सीएसइइटी के बाद टीडीओपी फिर सीएस एग्जीक्यूटिव फिर 21 मंथ्स की ट्रेनिंग, प्रोफेशनल एंड देन सीएलडीपी। एंड देन आपको मिल जाती है आपकी डिग्री और उसके बाद फिर आप एंप्लॉयमेंट तो वैसे भी स्टार्ट कर ही सकते हो बट आप अपना खुद का फर्म भी स्टार्ट कर सकते हो जिसमें यू आर एक्चुली ऑथराइज्ड टू साइन द मिनट्स एंड द डाक्यूमेंट्स व्हिच अ सीएस कैन साइन। अब बात कर लेते हैं रिसोर्सेज की, अगर आप सीएस क्लियर करना चाहते हो तो आपको कौन से-कौन से रिसोर्सेज की जरूरत पड़ेगी। नंबर वन ऑब्वियसली इट इज़ गोइंग टू बी योर आईसीएसआई मॉड्यूल्स जो कि आप रजिस्टर करते हो वैसे ही कुछ दिनों में 10 से 15 दिन के अंदर आईसीएसआई आपके घर पे मॉड्यूल्स भिजवा देता है। तो वो आपको निग्लेक्ट नहीं करना है। उसको आपको लाइटली नहीं लेना है। सेकंड विल बी योर क्लासेस के नोट्स। जो सर आपको जहाँ से भी पढ़ा रहे हैं, खुद के नोट्स बना के पढ़ा रहे हैं, तो वो नोट्स भी आपको रिफर करने होंगे। थर्ड विल बी योर पीवाईक्यूज़ जो कि होंगे पास्ट ईयर क्वेश्चन पेपर्स एंड फोर्थ विल बी टेस्ट सीरीज़। ये चारों चीज़ अगर आपके पास है मॉड्यूल, क्लासेस के नोट्स, पीवाईक्यूज़ एंड टेस्ट पेपर्स, इट इज़ मोर देन इनफ टू गेट एन ऑल इंडिया रैंक इन सीएस। दिस इज़ कमिंग फ्रॉम समवन जिसने तीनों स्टेजेस में रैंक लाई है एंड ट्रस्ट मी इसके अलावा आपको और कुछ नहीं चाहिए। मैंने कैसे किया था? मैंने सीए और सीएमए के पेपर्स भी रिफर किए थे क्योंकि हमारे क्लासेस में वो भी करवाए जाते थे। ट्रस्ट मी उसमें भी मुझे काफी हेल्प हुई थी कि मैं अगर टफ लेवल सॉल्व कर रही हूँ तो जो हमारा लेवल है टैक्स या फिर अकाउंट्स में, वो मुझे काफी ईजी लगता था क्योंकि मैं ऑलरेडी टफ लेवल सॉल्व कर रही थी। तो जो कॉमन सब्जेक्ट्स हैं सीए, सीएमए में उसके भी पीवाईक्यूज़ आप रिफर कर सकते हो। बट उसके अलावा आपको कोई एक्स्ट्रा बुक लेने की जरूरत नहीं है। टेस्ट सीरीज़ के लिए मैं आपको रिकमेंड करूंगी रैंकर्स वेव जो कि मेरा खुद का प्लेटफार्म है जिसमें हज़ारों बच्चे ऑलरेडी सीएस बन चुके हैं, जो कि इतने सालों से स्टक थे, वो रैंकर्स वेव में आने के बाद क्लियर हुए क्योंकि यहाँ पे हम डिटेल्ड चैप्टर वाइस आपको टेस्ट सीरीज़ देते हैं प्लस मॉक पेपर्स देते हैं, 24*7 डाउट सॉल्विंग सपोर्ट होती है, राइटिंग प्रैक्टिस सेशंस लेते हैं, इसी के साथ ही साथ मॉड्यूल के पीछे के क्वेश्चन सॉल्व करवाते हैं। सो, इट इज़ ऑल इन वन प्लेटफॉर्म फॉर योर राइटिंग प्रैक्टिस एंड इसमें 50% ऑफ भी चल रहा है तो आप स्पेशल 50 कूपन कोड का यूज़ करके रैंकर्स वेव में एनरोल कर सकते हो। काफी सारे बच्चे हमको ट्रस्ट करते हैं जैसे कि आप खुद रिव्यू देख सकते हो एंड आई ऑल्सो वांट यू टू बी अ पार्ट ऑफ़ रैंकर्स वेव। अगर मैं स्ट्रेटेजी की बात करूँ तो आपका डेली रूटीन जो लेक्चर्स और रिवीज़न है वो दिखना चाहिए कि आप डेली लेक्चर्स के साथ ही साथ रिवाइज़ भी कर रहे हो। थोड़े टाइम बाद जैसे एक-दो महीने के बाद मेक श्योर करना कि पीवाईक्यू सॉल्विंग आप स्टार्ट कर दो। टेस्ट देना तो आप दूसरे दिन से ही स्टार्ट कर सकते हो जैसे ही आपका कोई चैप्टर ख़त्म हो जाता है एंड सेल्फ़ स्टडी के लिए लास्ट का एक से दो महीना रखना जिसमें लेक्चर्स-वेक्चर सब ख़त्म हो गए हों और फिर आप सिर्फ़ सेल्फ़ स्टडी कर रहे हो। सो गाइज़, अगर आप भी 2026 में सीएस करना चाहते हो तो कमेंट में सीएस लिख देना। मुझे बहुत अच्छा लगेगा देख के कौन-कौन सीएस स्टार्ट करना चाहता है। रियली वांट टू नो। बाकी ये वीडियो अगर आपको हेल्प की होगी तो डू लेट मी नो। कुछ और डाउट रहेगा तो वो भी मुझे कमेंट सेक्शन में बताना। हम मिलते हैं दूसरे वीडियो में। आई एम ऑलवेज देयर विथ यू इन योर सीएस जर्नी। बाय-बाय, बेस्ट ऑफ़ लक!

title: How to think like a lawyer | Zero-L from Harvard Law School
transcription: Imagine I asked you, what do you learn in law school? Well, you've decided to take this course, so maybe you're more informed than the average person. So instead imagine I asked your college roommate or your parents, assuming they're not lawyers. The image that may come to mind of law school is sun-deprived, bespectacled law students surrounded by large numbers of dusty books, reading intently so they can memorize a bunch of law cases. And don't get me wrong, we do make students read a lot from books, and there's some memorization involved. But that image of someone learning the law by just memorizing things that are already out there is not at all what law school is really about. If it were, law school would be much less fun, and also much less useful. The law is always changing. So if you just learned a number of dry rules, much of what you learned might be outdated by your fifth year in practice. The chief value of legal education is not to know stuff, but to know what stuff to look for, where to find it, how to interpret what you find, what to think when some stuff says one thing, and other stuff says another. And how to use what you find to give legal advice. Let me put this very tangibly for you. If you call up a lawyer on anything other than a very simple question, and without pausing, she quickly gives you a straightforward answer, you should fire her. She's not doing a very good job for you. She's just not thinking like a lawyer. That's a phrase you'll hear a lot in law school, and while we might over-use it a bit, it does capture something important. Law is mostly about questions, choices, and analysis, about thinking and not so much about simple answers. That is the main thing we try to teach you in law school. Yes, we want to teach you a good amount of content about the law. To use an example from a course I teach, civil procedure, we want you to know what claims without subject matter jurisdiction can get jurisdiction by way of being joined to other claims through 28 U.S.C. 1367. If that sounds a bit intimidating at first, that's very normal, it is. But by the end of 1L fall, that knowledge will be at the tip of your brain, or at least somewhere in there.

title: Admiral McRaven: The Letter His Mother Wrote Him Before He Left for SEAL Training
transcription: [Applause] I'm going to say three words which you're all going to know immediately and associate with the Admiral. Make your bed. [Laughter] Nine years ago, you made the commencement address here at the University of Texas, and that commencement address went viral. It's become iconic. Everybody can summon those words as an admonition, almost. How did that speech come to you, Bill? Yeah. So Bill Powers, when he was the president here, had invited me to be the commencement speaker, I don't know, three or four months before May. And obviously, you know, anytime you're invited to be a commencement speaker, it's quite an honor. Uh but I had a day job. So I was still I was running the university, I'm sorry, I was running the Special Operations Command. So I started writing the speech about, uh, yeah, maybe two weeks before uh I was supposed to give it, and I'd kind of been mulling some ideas over in my head. So I started writing it on the weekends, a little bit here, a little bit there. And I had this great theme and I thought I was going to pull it all together, and then the Wednesday before the Saturday that I was supposed to give the speech, I realized the speech didn't work. I mean, it wasn't wasn't a good speech. And I I went downstairs. I'd been writing upstairs. I went downstairs, I see Georgeann and I go, "Oh, my God. It, it doesn't work." [Laughter] "It's, it's not a good speech." I said, "I don't know what I'm going to do. I mean, I'm giving the speech in a couple of days." And she says to me, she said, "Well, why don't you write about something you know?" And I thought, "Well, there's an interesting concept." Um. And I told her, I said, "Yeah, but the only thing I know is how to be a Navy SEAL." And she said, "Well, write about that." But at the time, you know, you may recall there had been a number of kind of administration officials that had been, you know, scheduled to give commencement addresses and then the student population kind of voted them down and they didn't end up doing it. And I thought, "You know, if I talk about being a Navy SEAL to uh university students here and, you know, 8,000 students were graduating, I think, that year and 25,000 uh family members," I thought, "I I I'm going to be in uniform. I don't know how this is going to go."

title: Admiral McRaven: The Letter His Mother Wrote Him Before He Left for SEAL Training
transcription: But, uh, I decided to go ahead and do it that way. And the reason I did was it occurred to me that SEAL training, which is six months long, really was a microcosm of life. I mean, it was about the challenges that you had every day in SEAL training were the same sort of challenges you were going to face in life. Uh, you were going to fail, uh, you had to build relationships, there were going to be bullies out there, there were bad things that happened in that six months that to me after, you know, now almost 37 years after I had gone through SEAL training, I realized that it really was a reflection of life writ large. So, I started drawing on the lessons, um, you know, from SEAL training to write the speech. And then, of course, I had to put in kind of chronological order. People always ask me why did I put make your bed first, and the answer was, because that's the first thing we did every day. I mean, you had to get up every morning in SEAL training and make your bed because it was going to be inspected. And, as I've told folks before, the value of that of the idea that, um, you know, you're going to get up, you're going to take a little pride in it, and it encourages you to do another task and another. And also about the little things in life. And that was what one of the instructors said, "Look, if if you can't even make your bed to exacting standards, how are we ever going to trust you to lead a complex SEAL mission? Learn to do the little things right and you'll learn to do the big things right." But what I didn't say in the speech, and I reflected on it later, um, was really later in my life. And, of course, I made my bed every day in the military, but in Iraq and Afghanistan, it actually took on a a little bit of a different meaning, particularly when I was in Afghanistan. So, I was a three-star admiral in Afghanistan, was the second ranking guy in Afghanistan, and I lived in what we referred to as a B-hut, made by the Navy Seabees. And it was just a plywood room, about, you know, half the size, oh, shoot, about a fourth of the size of this stage. And in my plywood room was a bed. That was it. The latrines, the heads were outside, there was no shel-, just a bed, a rack, by name, in Navy parlance. And every morning, I would get up, I'd go do my PT, I'd come back, and I'd make the bed. title: Admiral McRaven: The Letter His Mother Wrote Him Before He Left for SEAL Training
transcription: beautiful cursive writing. Dearest Bill, you know, you're heading off to, she didn't know what SEALs were, but you're heading off to this training. And I'm thinking, you know, my mother thought the world of me, you know. She knew I was just the most competent, most capable young man in the world. And she starts off and she says, 'you know, you know, I, I really worry about you. I don't know that you're tough enough for this military training.' So, I'm reading this. She goes, 'you know, this is,' I think her words were, 'this is harsh military training, and you've lived a country club life.' We lived on a nine-hole municipal golf course. Actually, we didn't live on the golf course, but we were close to it, right? And, but somehow we lived the country club life. And so, as I'm reading this, I'm going on, 'What?' And then I get to the, you know, the punchline. She goes, 'and, oh, by the way, you're spoiled.' Underlined. I'm like, 'What?' I thought my mother thought I was the toughest, most competent, capable guy, and she thought I was a little snowflake because she and my father and a lot of folks were part of the greatest generation. And to those men and women that served in World War II and Korea and Vietnam, those of us in the '70s, we were soft, little, like I said, little snowflakes. And thank God I didn't read that letter before I went to SEAL training. I'm, I'm not sure I would have made it through. Um, but what it did was it reinforced with me the fact that every generation thinks the next generation isn't good enough because they didn't walk three miles in the snow to get to school or whatever. Well, I'm telling you, this generation is absolutely good enough to get us out of whatever problems we're in, and I think they will. And so, um, I always remain optimistic, you have to. And all you got to do, back to why was I able to lead so well, I said I was inspired by the soldiers. Same reason I've got, you know, faith that we'll be fine because I'm inspired by the young folks that I meet at LBJ school, I'm inspired by the kids I meet, you know, whenever I'm traveling. So, we're going to be fine. We're going to be just fine.

transcription:
Now, Susie, you mentioned that you've, you know, you've come from a different background. You worked in the corporate space, you worked in technology. Um, and you've had to shift from kind of that corporate mindset to a small business owner, someone who is now looking at corporate marketing to marketing your own brand, marketing yourself, marketing your small business. I'd love to know, like, what is one shift that you personally had to navigate making that transition? And what can you offer to other women in this room that are making that shift as well?

It was so hard. I don't know how many other folks left corporate and suddenly had to come out and start talking about themselves. So, I spent a lot of time on that messaging at my at my company. And it was the company's voice, it was the company's style, and it was the company's message. And it was great. I was good at it, right? It was awesome.

And then suddenly, the company wasn't there anymore. Social media was new when I was working in corporate. I never posted my own thoughts and feelings about the world because everything I said was going to reflect back on my company. How was how were they going to look at this, right? I was working for somebody else, it was their brand. I came out and suddenly said, "I am my brand. I can talk about anything I want to talk about because I am my brand." It was scarier than heck, I hated it, I didn't want to talk about myself, I didn't want to sell myself, I didn't want to market myself. It was really intimidating. And so, that was my biggest kind of hurdle as I came into this, right? I had to worry about my skills, I had those. I had to worry about my pricing, I figured that out. But talking about me and putting myself out there was a huge mental shift for me. And I wrote a blog post for the Sunnyvale Chamber of Commerce all about going my own experience going to get photos taken of myself and how terrifying it was and how important it was to get those photos to tell my story. And I was talking about it, I was using my voice, and it was great, and it felt good. And then I got to my about me, and I switched into, "Susie McFaddin is an internationally published award-winning photographer who blah blah blah." And the folks who reviewed it for me said, "That's great, but it didn't sound like you as soon as you started talking about yourself."

I don't know if y'all remember this, but when Facebook and social media first started, we all had our profile photos that had somebody's weird hand on our shoulder because we cut somebody out of the photo. I love overalls. I'm creating photos where my clients look their best, many of them are in suits, business wear, and I am running around in overalls, a tank top, and I'm barefoot, right? It's not about me. That's my brand. The big clunky glasses are my brand. My politics are my brand, right? I want people to know who they're coming to see, and that I offer a safe, inclusive space for them to get their, their photos taken, that that's a no judgment zone, right? All of those things that I couldn't do when I was corporate, are suddenly front and center to say, "This is who I am, and this is who you're going to work with." And, might I lose somebody who reads some of my, my values and politics and says, "Ooh." Great, bye-bye. Go with, go with grace. You will find somebody that you connect with more. And, that to me, is what is so much fun about being a small business and being a solopreneur, is embracing who you are, and I love working with my clients to put a face to that, so that when you go out and make your social media posts about you, and get all of that traction, and people saying, "This person is awesome, and oh, by the way, they also do this." title: This Week in Review | Fed Meeting, US GDP, Eurozone GDP (July 31, 2026)
transcription: Hello and welcome to This Week in Review. This is our weekly segment that's designed to highlight a few important developments that you might have missed this week, and we'll talk about what they mean for markets, and, most importantly, the potential impact for investors. To stay up to date with our latest market insights, subscribe to our YouTube channel or visit fisherinvestments.com. Now, let's review what happened this week. First, the Fed meeting. On Wednesday, the Federal Open Market Committee, or FOMC, voted to hold the interest rate steady at 3.5 to 3.75%. This was the fifth straight meeting without an interest rate change. It was also a split decision, and three members voted to hike rates by 25 basis points. Headlines quickly seized on the story of a divided Fed, but we wouldn't really read too much into that. Differing opinions among Fed officials tells us very little about what the committee will do next, and dissenting votes don't make a rate hike more or less likely in the meetings ahead. Some investors may also worry that Chairman Kevin Warsh's decision to step back from so-called forward guidance may make monetary policy harder to predict or less transparent. We see that differently. Central banks can, and often do, change their minds without notice based on changing economic data or fundamentals. So rather than trying to guess their next move, we think investors are better served by keeping their focus on the broader fundamentals driving markets. Central bank decisions are just one of many forces shaping the global economy and capital markets, and while we believe a rate hike would be a mistake, the talk today is of small hikes. And, really importantly, even a hike or two from here would leave policy rates within a range that this bull market has already successfully navigated. Additionally, when we look around the developed world, yield curves remain steep and healthy. For long-term investors, that's perspective worth holding on to.

title: This Week in Review | Fed Meeting, US GDP, Eurozone GDP (July 31, 2026)
transcription: Next, US GDP. On Thursday, the US Bureau of Economic Analysis released its official first estimate for US second quarter 2022 GDP. It came in at 1.5% annualized growth, which is a slowdown from what we saw in Q1, where we saw 2.1% annualized rate. But the report still shows moderate expansion that was driven largely by very resilient consumer spending. When data tends to fall in a moderate range, there may be plenty of opinions about whether it's truly positive or just good on paper. So with that in mind, we believe it's really critical for investors to remember this. Stocks are forward-looking. GDP is backward-looking. Stocks don't wait for economic data or what happened in the preceding quarter. Instead, they pre-price all widely known information and move in advance of the economy. So as the Ukraine war continues and some inflation remains elevated, slower economic growth may actually worry those who assume that you need robust GDP for strong stock market returns. However, history shows this isn't the case. The US stock market has often had very nice positive returns, even during periods of modest economic growth. In fact, fears about a slowing economy can actually be a positive for stocks because they set a lower bar for reality to surprise to the upside. Finally, Eurozone GDP. This Thursday, we got the first estimate of second-quarter GDP for the Eurozone. It grew at 1.8% annualized. That's a notable increase from the flat reading we saw in the first quarter, and it landed well above market expectations. Growth factors included strong business investment and a recovering industrial output. On a year-over-year country-by-country basis, Spain led the region with annual GDP growth of 2.7%. Spain was followed by the Netherlands at 1.3%, Italy at 1%, and Germany at 0.9%.

title: This Week in Review | Fed Meeting, US GDP, Eurozone GDP (July 31, 2026)
transcription: After the first quarter, which featured some pressures from the ongoing war in Iraq and a 13.2% drop in Ireland's GDP, expectations for GDP growth were low. That set the stage for Eurozone stocks to climb a wall of worry. We feel that that wall is still higher than the US's today, and just as in the US, stocks don't need a perfect economy. They just need reality to be better than feared. Some also worried that the European Central Bank, or ECB's, recent 25 basis point hike, which was in response to some rising inflation, could hinder growth and maybe apply some pressure to stocks. However, we believe what really matters here is the yield curve. So, despite the ECB's rate hike and expectations for additional hikes later this year, the Eurozone yield curve remains nicely positive, which has supported healthy loan growth. We think this should be a tailwind for Eurozone stocks going forward. So, while GDP growth across the pond might be a little slower, markets appear to be pricing in the region's adaptability to challenges. Renewed Iraq war-related volatility or tariff concerns are certainly potential headwinds for Q3, but there's also good reason to believe the Eurozone is actually primed to do better than feared and to continue supporting this global bull market. That's it for this week. Thanks for tuning into This Week in Review. If you're looking for more insights, don't miss our other series. It's called Three Things You Need to Know This Week. We release it every Monday. You can also visit fisherinvestments.com anytime for our latest thoughts on markets. Thanks again for joining, and don't forget to hit like and subscribe.

title: Clorox (CLX) Stock Analysis 2026 – Graphs, Risks, Opportunities & Valuation ✅
transcription: Clorox is a good example of a defensive consumer staples business that the market once priced for certainty, then sharply repriced when that certainty broke down. In the pandemic era, investors were willing to pay a premium for bleach, disinfecting and household staples because demand looked unusually strong and durable. In hindsight, that was one of the market's big mistakes. It capitalized peak demand as if it were normal demand. Then the opposite happened. The August 2023 cyberattack followed by ERP-related shipment disruption in fiscal 2024 reminded investors that even a boring staples company can suffer real operational volatility. But Clorox also had real successes. Fiscal 2024 gross margin rose to 43.8%, adjusted EPS reached $6.10, and operating cash flow climbed to $1.04 billion as cost savings and recovery actions took hold. Today the stock looks much less loved. Clorox is trading around $132.85 with a trailing PE of about 21.8x. Against management's fiscal 2025 adjusted EPS outlook of $6.55 to $6.80, the stock is trading at roughly 19 to 20x forward earnings. The quarterly dividend is $1.22 or $4.88 annualized, which puts the yield near 3.7% at the current price. For a company that historically often attracted a much richer multiple because of brand strength, resilience and dividend dependability, that is a meaningful derating. The market is no longer paying up for Clorox as a premium safe haven. It is pricing it more like a mature business that has to prove earnings quality again. The reason the multiple is compressed is not that the brands stopped mattering. It is that fiscal 2025 is messy. In Q1 FY25, net sales fell 15% to $1.39 billion, organic sales were down 15%, and gross margin slipped to 38.8% from 42.1%. Management kept full-year guidance, but said results were likely to land toward the lower end because earlier order fulfillment problems caused consumption and market share losses.

transcription: That is the key issue around the current price. Investors are asking whether this is a temporary transition year or evidence that Clorox has become a slower, less predictable earnings story. Looking forward, the valuation debate is becoming more interesting. On one hand, the Gojo acquisition, completed on April 1st, 2026, adds Purell, expands Clorox's health and hygiene exposure, supports its long-term 3% to 5% sales growth target, and is expected to bring at least $50 million of run-rate cost synergies, with EPS neutral in year one and accretive in year two. On the other hand, the deal is being funded primarily with debt, so the market will want proof that Clorox can integrate Gojo cleanly while stabilizing the legacy business. My view is that today's valuation already reflects a lot of disappointment. If management restores cleaner organic growth and shows that Gojo improves the quality of the portfolio, the stock can re-rate higher. But until that happens, Clorox will likely remain a "show-me" staples name rather than regain its old premium multiple. Let's go straight into the risks, because with Clorox, the question in 2026 is not whether consumers still need bleach, trash bags, cat litter, or water filters. The real question is whether the company can stabilize demand, protect margins, and execute cleanly while the business is going through operational change and portfolio expansion. The biggest risk is volume pressure. In fiscal Q2 2026, net sales fell 1%, household sales fell 6%, lifestyle sales fell 5%, and management said earlier order fulfillment issues led to consumption and market share losses that keep full-year expectations near the low end of guidance. Reuters also noted pressure from shoppers trading down to cheaper alternatives. The second major risk is execution around the ERP transition. Clorox has described fiscal 2026 as being distorted by inventory shipped ahead of consumption before the US ERP implementation. Management said that retailer inventory drawdown should create about a 7.5 point sales headwind this year and reduce EPS by about 90 cents. Even though the final US ERP phase was completed in January, that does not automatically remove the risk. These kinds of transitions can still create friction in forecasting, replenishment, retailer relationships, and on-shelf availability, and in a staples business, even short disruptions can hurt share.

Clorox's 10-K is also very clear that lower priced private label products can pressure sales mix and profitability, while larger retailers can demand lower pricing, higher trade discounts, and more promotional support. Management sees long-term strategic benefits, but the deal is expected to be neutral to adjusted EPS in year one, which means the near-term burden falls on execution. If the core business remains soft, a debt-funded acquisition can reduce flexibility. And investors should not forget cyber risk, either. Clorox's 2026 risks are less about brand relevance and more about stacked execution pressure. Softer branded demand, ERP-related disruption, margin volatility, retailer pressure, and a larger balance sheet commitment all hitting at the same time. Now the opportunity side, because with Clorox, the upside is not just about waiting for a defensive stock to bounce back. The real opportunity is that the company may be building a better business mix than the market is currently giving it credit for. In the short term, the biggest opportunity is simple. Reported results should look cleaner once the ERP distortion is behind the company. Management said the major drag on fiscal 2026 is transitory and tied to retailer inventory movements around the system change, while the final US ERP phase was successfully completed in January. That matters because when a temporary operational distortion rolls off, investors can start focusing again on the underlying business rather than noisy comparisons. Second, health and wellness looks like a real source of upside. In Q2, that segment still delivered sales growth, helped by strong professional products shipments, and management continues to position Clorox around health, hygiene, and well-being. That is important because this is already one of Clorox's stronger areas, and it gives the company a more attractive growth profile than a pure slow-growth household staples story. transcription: Clorox highlighted multiple launches across the portfolio, including Clorox Pure, new Scentiva bleach offerings, Glad ForceFlex Max Strength LeakGuard bags, and new Burt's Bees products. For a staples company, that matters because better innovation can improve mix, support shelf space, and help the company earn better pricing without relying only on broad inflation. Longer term, the biggest upside is clearly Purell. Clorox completed the Gojo acquisition on April 1st, adding a category leader with nearly $800 million in annual sales, more than 80% of revenue tied to a broad B2B distributor network, and roughly 20 million installed soap and sanitizer dispensers that support recurring demand. Clorox also says the deal supports its long-term 3% to 5% sales growth target, should generate at least $50 million of run-rate cost synergies, and should become EPS accretive in year two. So the upside framework is clear: cleaner comparisons, stronger execution in health and wellness, innovation that improves the core business, and a bigger platform in professional and institutional hygiene. If Clorox delivers on that mix shift, the stock can gradually be valued less like a troubled staple and more like a higher quality health and hygiene compounder. Looking at analyst ratings, the message is pretty cautious. Clorox has zero strong buy ratings, only two buys, 14 holds, two sells, and one strong sell. So this is clearly not a stock the Street sees as a high conviction idea right now. What that tells us is that analysts still respect the business, but they are not ready to fully trust the earnings story. Clorox has strong brands, defensive categories, and a long history of cash generation, which is why the stock is not being treated like a broken company. But at the same time, the large number of hold ratings shows that most analysts want more proof before becoming more bullish. The market is likely waiting to see cleaner execution, more stable organic performance, and evidence that recent strategic moves actually improve the quality of the business over time. Until that happens, analysts seem to view Clorox as stable, but not especially exciting. Clorox is currently seen as a wait-for-proof stock, resilient enough to avoid broad bearishness, but not strong enough yet to inspire major conviction.

title: Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS) Q2 2026 Earnings Explained | Why the Market Misread the $0.95 EPS Loss
transcription: Navitas Semiconductor's second quarter 2026 earnings triggered a sharp market reaction, but the headline tells only part of the story. Investors focused on a reported GAAP loss of 95 cents per share, a result that appeared to miss expectations by roughly 22 times. At first glance, that looked alarming. However, a closer examination of the financial statements reveals a very different picture. The reported loss was driven almost entirely by a one-time non-cash accounting adjustment rather than a deterioration in the underlying business. Once that accounting impact is removed, the operational performance appears considerably stronger. The key comparison begins with two earnings figures. While GAAP earnings showed a loss of 95 cents per share, the non-GAAP loss was only 4 cents per share. At the same time, revenue exceeded expectations by approximately 7%. The difference between those two earnings figures was a $203 million, one-time, non-cash SPACC earn-out accounting charge tied to the company's 2021 SPACC transaction. This adjustment had no impact on cash flow or ongoing operations, and has now been fully recognized, meaning it will no longer affect future financial statements. Operationally, the quarter showed meaningful progress. Revenue reached $10.53 million, representing 22% sequential growth and finishing at the high end of management's guidance. Looking ahead, management projected another 28% increase in revenue during the third quarter. The operational loss also improved modestly, declining from $11.7 million in the previous quarter to $11.4 million. Viewed through that lens, the underlying business improved rather than weakened. Much of the market reaction reflected a comparison between a GAAP result and non-GAAP expectations, effectively comparing two different accounting measures. Once those figures are separated, the operating trend becomes much clearer. Understanding Navitas also requires understanding its position within AI infrastructure. While AI discussions often focus on GPUs and computing power, every AI data center ultimately depends on efficient power conversion.

transcription: Electricity must be converted multiple times before reaching processors, and traditional silicon becomes increasingly inefficient during those conversions. Navitas addresses that challenge through power semiconductors built on gallium nitride, or GaN, and silicon carbide, or SiC. Both materials provide higher efficiency and greater power density than conventional silicon. Rather than remaining focused on lower-margin consumer charging products, the company has shifted its strategy toward higher-margin AI infrastructure and industrial power applications. An important competitive advantage is that Navitas offers both GaN and SiC technologies, whereas many competitors specialize in only one material. The quality of recent growth can also be evaluated across several financial metrics. Revenue increased to $10.53 million, supported by stronger demand across high-power products. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 39.5%, improving by 0.5 percentage points sequentially, and 1 percentage point from the prior year, as product mix shifted toward higher-value applications. The balance sheet remains another notable strength. Navitas finished the quarter with $557 million in cash and cash equivalents, and no outstanding debt. During the quarter, the company also raised approximately $373 million through an equity offering priced at $21.89 per share. Management indicated those proceeds will support manufacturing capacity expansion and potential acquisitions. Inventory increased from $14.9 million to $19.5 million as the company intentionally accumulated TSMC wafer supply in preparation for anticipated AI-related demand. Perhaps the most significant strategic milestone during the quarter was management's announcement that the Navitas 2.0 transformation was completed one full quarter ahead of schedule. Historically, approximately 90% of company revenue came from legacy mobile and consumer applications, while only 10% originated from newer, high-power markets. By year-end, management projects high-power products and AI infrastructure will account for roughly one-third of total revenue, with legacy mobile becoming largely immaterial.

Management dismissed those lawsuits as attempts to slow competitive momentum, arguing that established competitors often resort to litigation when market share comes under pressure. Regardless of that interpretation, the legal proceedings introduce additional uncertainty that investors will continue monitoring. Analysts also pressed management on several key topics. Questions regarding 800V deployment timelines received consistent and confident responses, with management reaffirming its 2027 outlook, despite reports of isolated project cancellations. Questions surrounding the Magnachip strategy were similarly addressed, with management explaining that the initiative is designed to secure dedicated 8-inch wafer capacity, rather than transition toward an IP licensing model. However, management declined to provide detailed breakdowns of revenue by high-performance computing, data centers, or the percentage of future revenue already backed by committed orders versus programs still undergoing qualification. While strategic direction was discussed openly, more granular financial visibility remained limited. Ultimately, the investment thesis continues to revolve around one central question: whether the industry's transition toward 800V AI infrastructure unfolds on schedule. If deployment progresses as expected, Navitas's dual GaN and SiC portfolio, combined with its $557 million cash position, could support continued expansion until operational break-even. If deployment slips significantly beyond current expectations, rising operating expenses and ongoing legal costs could pressure financial performance for longer than anticipated.
