title: The Highest-Paid Podcasters Of 2026
transcription:
Today on Forbes, the highest paid podcasters of 2026.

When Jay Shetty started his podcast, On Purpose, in 2019, he remembers people telling him he was too late. The medium was already saturated, they said, with little room for growth. And wasn't he really just a content creator?

Seven years later, the 38-year-old self-help guru hosts one of the most popular podcasts in the world, competing not only with the biggest TV, radio, and internet-native talk shows, but blurring the lines between them entirely. Just as many people watch his lengthy interviews with celebrities, including Michelle Obama and Matt Damon, on YouTube, as listen on the iHeartMedia Network. Distribution deals that Forbes estimates paid Shetty $21 million over the past 12 months.

And when those deals expired this year, Shetty landed a new kind of contract, in which the audio and video of his show will not only be distributed by Spotify, it will also stream on Netflix, with the two companies combining to pay him an estimated $100 million over the next 3 years. Shetty tells Forbes, quote, "When I started, video wasn't normal for a podcast. Now we have the four largest streamers bidding for the show. To see that kind of interest and enthusiasm was pretty amazing, for me and for the industry overall."

The impressive thing about mega-deals like Shetty's is that, unlike the makers of movies, TV, or other forms of entertainment, podcasters retain ownership of their shows' underlying IP, meaning networks and platforms are paying millions just to license it as a distributor and ad sales partner for a set number of years. That's one reason why premium streaming giants like Netflix, Hulu, and Tubi had largely ignored the industry's rise over the past decade, allowing YouTube to grow into the largest podcasting platform in the world.

But beginning in 2025, hoping to cut into YouTube's dominance over engagement time, the streamers have made a splashy entrance. Industry dealmakers say that after Netflix's initial $1 million to $2 million bids for top podcasts were roundly rejected, the streamer adopted a strategy similar to the one it used previously to capture market share in scripted television: overpaying to lure talent away from incumbent platforms. Offers of $10 million or more per year, on a one- or two-year trial term, eventually convinced marquee shows from Spotify, iHeart, and Barstool Sports to sign on. Goalhanger, a UK-based podcast network, reportedly landed $19 million from Netflix to stream just 40 episodes of its daily talk show, The Rest Is Football, during the World Cup. title: The Highest-Paid Podcasters Of 2026
transcription: We think about video podcasts like the modern talk show, but instead of having a single brand-defined show, you have hundreds of them. Yet podcasts are ascendant because of their inherent differences from traditional television. They are much cheaper to produce, can run year-round, and make the bulk of their money from host-read advertisements inserted into the audio and video recordings. For the highest-end shows, brands will pay premium prices for a trusted host's personal endorsement or to target their audience's specific demographic. Joe Rogan reigns as the world's highest-paid podcaster, earning an estimated $82 million this year by pairing deep listener trust with massive scale, releasing around 15 episodes per month, and attracting more than 80 million downloads and views, according to one data provider. In 2024, Spotify rewarded him with a new three-year contract that could reach $250 million. For most podcasters, landing a $100 million-plus deal like SmartLess's from one of the major networks, mainly Spotify, SiriusXM, or iHeart, is still the ultimate prize. Deals are paid out as a guaranteed advance with a revenue-sharing model in place for any additional profits generated above this break-even point. But competition between networks is what drives the guarantees above $30 million per year for a select handful of elite talent. At that rate, ad sales are unlikely to make back much profit for networks on the shows, if any. Still, networks justify their biggest deals in other ways, including subscriber acquisition, attracting blue-chip sponsors, and using talent as brand ambassadors. For example, Wondery's top podcasters, New Heights hosts Jason and Travis Kelce, who are number seven on our list with estimated earnings of $35 million, appeared on a panel for parent company Amazon at the Cannes Lions Festival in June. Talent, meanwhile, are using their mega-deals and IP control to create mini-networks of shows under their umbrella, such as Alex Cooper's Unwell at SiriusXM, or Charlamagne tha God's Black Effect Podcast Network at iHeart. Cooper, the host of the Call Her Daddy podcast, is number eight on our list with estimated earnings of $32 million. And Charlamagne, who hosts The Breakfast Club, is number 10, with estimated earnings of $27 million. For full coverage and to see the whole list released on Thursday, check out Matt Craig's piece on Forbes.com. This is Kieran Meadows from Forbes, thanks for tuning in.

transcription: All right, let's dive in. Today we're going to unpack a really chaotic weekend that, honestly, pushed American democracy right to its limits. We're going to look at how a direct, pretty unprecedented showdown between the president and the Supreme court unfolded, and in doing so, tested the very foundations of the rule of law. So where did this all kick off? Well, it started right here with this absolutely explosive social media post. I mean, in a single message, the president didn't just defy the nation's highest court, he actually claimed their ruling against him somehow made him even more powerful. This post right here set the stage for a major constitutional confrontation. So, how did a constitutional conflict like this ignite so quickly? The thing is, this whole confrontation just escalated over the course of one single chaotic weekend. Let's walk through the timeline. Okay, just look at how this played out. On Friday, the Supreme Court comes out and rules the president's tariffs are unconstitutional. Now, these were tariffs he levied under a specific law for national emergencies. But then, just hours later, he openly defies them, announcing a new 10% tariff anyway. By Saturday, he's on social media, hiking it up to 15%. And then, by Monday morning, we get that post where he claims the court's decision actually expanded his authority. We're talking 72 hours where a Supreme Court ruling was not just ignored, but completely flipped on its head. And this, right here, really gets to the core of the whole thing. On one side, you have the court's official judgment, a clear check on executive power. And on the other, the president's direct rebuttal, basically saying he doesn't need Congress. It's that classic constitutional friction point, right? The judiciary's check on power being met with a declaration of unchecked authority. And look, this whole showdown wasn't just some abstract debate about the constitution. It had immediate, very real world consequences for the economy and for America's standing on the world stage. The international reaction was swift and, frankly, pretty bewildered. The head of the European Parliament's Trade Committee, Bernd Lange, he just called it pure tariff chaos. And his statement really captures that global feeling of instability, which led the EU Parliament to immediately propose pausing a major trade deal with the US. And the fallout wasn't just limited to Europe. Officials from India, who were literally about to finalize their own trade agreement, they postponed their trip to the US. And at the same time, back home, all this uncertainty sent shudders through the financial system, with the stock market falling pretty sharply. Now, what's really fascinating here is how the American public already felt about all this. Even before this constitutional crisis blew up, a poll from ABC News and the Washington Post showed that nearly two-thirds of Americans already disapproved of the president's handling of tariffs in the first place.

title: Heather Cox Richardson Video Summary: Supreme Court Expands Presidential Power (June 29, 2026)
transcription: For over a century, unassuming buildings like this have served as the quiet engine rooms of the American government. Inside, thousands of civil servants do the unglamorous work of regulating markets and keeping the country running. Starting in the late 19th century, Congress began building a specific feature into these independent agencies. They were intentionally designed as bipartisan bodies, deliberately insulated from the direct control of the President. The logic was simple. Keeping the air clean, ensuring consumer products are safe, and stopping monopolies requires technical expertise that doesn't change with every election. By keeping the executive branch at arm's length, Congress created a buffer. It guaranteed that decisions affecting public safety and financial security were driven by scientists and economists rather than political favors. In a single morning, with a landmark 6-to-3 decision, the Supreme Court erased over 90 years of established legal doctrine. President Trump immediately hailed the decision as a monumental victory, calling it the largest expansion of presidential power in over a century. He is correct about the scale of the change. The ruling legally grants the President the power to fire the head of any independent agency at any time for any reason. To understand how a foundational power of the United States government was dismantled overnight, we have to look at the legal theory that made it possible. The test case began in March 2025. The President abruptly fired Rebecca Slaughter, the last remaining Democratic member of the Federal Trade Commission. Since 1935, the standard for removing someone from these commissions was strict. You had to prove neglect of duty or malfeasance. But Trump argued he could fire her because her presence was inconsistent with his administration's priorities. This defense relies on the unitary executive theory, a framework conservative strategists have built since the 1980s. The core argument: as head of the executive branch, the President holds absolute authority over everything within it. No other branch can limit his control. By neutralizing Congress's ability to shield these agencies, this theory bypasses the legislative process. It takes national regulatory power and concentrates it into the hands of one person.

This strategy fits alongside the court's 2024 decision, granting the president broad immunity for official acts. Throughout his second term, the administration has worked to fit its power grabs within the protective boundaries of that framework. The Loper decision is the final link in the chain. A president who is virtually immune from prosecution now has absolute, unquestioned control over the officers running the nation's regulatory infrastructure. In a six-to-three decision, the court sided with the president. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson issued a fierce warning, noting that this ruling undoes decades of political practice. The dissenters wrote that this decision elevates the president above his co-equal branches, granting him a level of power unknown even to the English Crown. On a functional level, this marks the return of the spoils system. We have already seen the administration fire civil servants perceived as political enemies and install members of the president's inner circle in their place. title: Day 1 Highlights | 2026 Bahrain Pre-Season Test 1
transcription: F1 is back for the first official test session of the season. All 11 teams and 22 drivers are present for 6 days of running across 2 weeks at the Bahrain International Circuit. McLaren entered the 2026 season as reigning back-to-back Constructors' Champions, and it was Oscar Piastri in the car for the morning of Day 1. The Aussie, who had battled for last season's Drivers' Championship until the very final round, was on the pace from the off in Bahrain. Despite McLaren running just over half the number of laps of Mercedes in Barcelona, the Woking-based outfit were raring to go in Bahrain. Piastri, second fastest in the morning session, just 2/10 of a second behind Max Verstappen. The Australian gave Turn 10 a wide berth following Aston Martin's Lance Stroll, but completed 54 laps before the lunch break. 2025 World Champion Lando Norris took over for the afternoon session, topping the Day 1 times with a 1:34.669. The Brit added a further 58 laps to McLaren's total, ensuring they ended the day with well over 100 tours of the circuit. George Russell was the only driver other than the title protagonists to win a Grand Prix in 2025, the Brit victorious on two occasions at Canada and Singapore. And the Silver Arrows were in fine form throughout shakedown, logging 500 laps in Barcelona, more than any other team. On to Bahrain, and Mercedes were again getting the laps in. Russell ran the morning session, completing 56 laps, before teammate Kimi Antonelli took over for the afternoon. The Brit did have a little trouble at the off-camber Turn 10, running wide on three separate occasions. transcription: Second practice in Monte Carlo. F1's finest with another hour of track time ahead to really get to grips with the Circuit de Monaco. Many have touted Ferrari as the team to beat on this narrow, twisty course, where downforce rather than extreme speed rules. And so it proved in FP1 when Charles Leclerc had been fastest from teammate Lewis Hamilton. The seven-time world champion, playing catch up in this session, he flirted with disaster on an early quick lap. Oh, you just feel it's a place that you can split a Formula One car in two if you get it wrong. It's that difficult and that high speed with no barrier margin. Three times a winner on these streets, he continued to push throughout the session, locking up approaching the Nouvelle Chicane, and then taking a whole bunch of curb at the same spot the next time around. My word, that's more curb than I've seen so far down at that chicane, I think. Hamilton on the, on the edge of rear grip, pings it over the curb, bounces through. And it was the Briton with the bragging rights in this session. His lap of 1 minute 13.026, more than a tenth quicker than Leclerc's best effort for P2. The teammates even had a little race after the flag. Great foretaste perhaps for Sunday's main event. Max Verstappen had not been entirely happy with his ride in FP1, despite a decent P3 performance. This time out, he seemed much more hooked up, especially on the soft tires, and managed the same placing again. Only this time, he was a bit closer to the Scuderia drivers. Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar, who crashed out of FP1, was P6 this time around, his mechanics working wonders in the interim. There was a hairy moment for George Russell early doors. Oh my word, the car getting loose through the first part of the swimming pool. He will need an underwear change. He was later blocked on a fast lap by a slow-moving Gabriel Bortoleto. The Briton believes he's had more than his fair share of bad luck so far this season, but was upbeat coming into the weekend, feeling the odds would even out across the year. He's currently P2 in the drivers' championship, some 43 points behind Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli, but he was one place ahead of the Italian in second practice, P4 after the hour. It was a short session for reigning world champion and defending Monaco master, Lando Norris, who encountered a technical problem...

వికెట్స్ కోల్పోతే, చేజింగ్ కోసం 235 టార్గెట్ తో వచ్చిన కృనాల్ పాండ్య టీం దీన్నైతే చాలా ఈజీగా అండ్ కంఫర్టబుల్ గా చేజ్ చేసిందని చెప్పాలి. ఇందులో మెయిన్ పాత్ర పోషించింది ఆర్సిబి కెప్టెన్ అయిన రజత్ పటిదార్. తనైతే లాస్ట్ త్రీ మంత్స్ నుంచి ఇంజురీ తో ఎంత బాధపడుతున్నాడో మన అందరికీ తెలుసు. ఇంకా పర్సనల్ గా నన్ను అడిగినా రజత్ పటిదార్ ఈ సీజన్ అంత బెస్ట్ ఇస్తాడని డౌట్ గానే ఉంది. లాస్ట్ త్రీ మంత్స్ నుంచి ఎలాంటి క్రికెట్ కూడా ఆడలేదు. బట్ రావడం రావడంతోనే తన ప్రాక్టీస్ మ్యాచ్ లో తనేంటో ప్రతి ఒక్కరికి ప్రూవ్ చేశాడని చెప్పాలి. జస్ట్ తను ఆడిన 25 బాల్స్ లోనే 74 రన్స్ చేశాడు. సో తను ఆడిన బ్యాటింగ్ స్టైల్ చూసుకున్నా వేరే లెవెల్ లో ఉంది. బిగ్ బిగ్ సిక్సర్స్ తో మ్యాచ్ నైతే వన్ సైడ్ చేశాడని చెప్పొచ్చు. ఇంకా తనతో పాటు ఆర్సిబి ప్లేయింగ్ 11 లో నెంబర్ త్రీ ఎవరొస్తారో చాలా

transcription: డౌట్ ఏముంది! బట్ ఈ మ్యాచ్ వల్ల ఒకటి అయితే క్లారిటీ అయిపోయింది. నెంబర్ త్రీ పొజిషన్ లో మాక్సిమమ్ పడిక్కల్ వచ్చే ఛాన్సెస్ ఎక్కువగా ఉన్నాయి. ఎందుకంటే లాస్ట్ టూ త్రీ మంత్స్ నుంచి తను డొమెస్టిక్ లీగ్స్ లో ఎలా ఆడుతున్నాడో మనం చూస్తున్నాం. ప్రతి మ్యాచ్ సెంచరీతో అదరగొడుతున్నాడు. సో అదే ఫామ్ ని ఇక్కడ కంటిన్యూ చేస్తూ తను ఆడిన జస్ట్ 33 బాల్స్ లో 63 రన్స్ అయితే చేశాడు. ఇంకా వీళ్ళిద్దరితో పాటు కృనాల్ పాండ్యా కూడా బెస్ట్ బ్యాటింగ్ చేసి మ్యాచ్ నైతే ఈజీగా గెలిచారని చెప్పాలి అగైనెస్ట్ విరాట్ కోహ్లీ టీమ్. మరి ఆర్సీబీ బ్యాటింగ్ లైనప్ అండ్ ప్లేయర్స్ ఇలా ఉంటే, అండ్ బౌలర్స్ ఎలా ఉన్నారని చూసుకుంటే, మెయిన్ గా శ్రేయస్ శర్మ, భువనేశ్వర్ అండ్ అభిమన్యం అండ్ మంగేష్ యాదవ్. ఈ ఫోర్ బౌలర్స్ అయితే వేరే లెవెల్ బౌలింగ్ చేశారంట ఆర్సీబీ ఫస్ట్ ప్రాక్టీస్ మ్యాచ్ లో. మరి ఇందులో ఇంట్రెస్టింగ్ నేమ్స్ ఏమున్నాయని చూసుకుంటే, మంగేష్ యాదవ్. మంగేష్ యాదవ్ దగ్గరి నుంచి న్యూ బాల్ తో అండ్ డెత్ ఓవర్స్ లో అయితే యార్కర్స్ తో భయపెట్టించాడంట ప్రతి ఒక్క ఆర్సీబీ బ్యాటర్స్ ని. సో మరి తను డైరెక్ట్ గా ప్లేయింగ్ 11 లో చూస్తామంటే ఇదైతే 100% ఫిక్స్ అయిందని మేనేజ్మెంట్ నుంచి అయితే ఇన్ఫర్మేషన్స్ కూడా వస్తున్నాయి. సో యశ్ దయాల్ ప్లేస్ లో మంగేష్ యాదవ్ ఫస్ట్ మ్యాచ్ ఆడబోతున్నాడు అగైనెస్ట్ ఎస్ఆర్హెచ్. ఇంక మరి ఆర్సీబీ టీం ప్లేయింగ్ 11 ఎలా ఉండబోతుందో అని చూసుకున్నా, ఇందులో త్రీ చేంజెస్ అయితే పక్కాగా ఉండిపోతాయి, ఇదైతే కన్ఫర్మేషన్ వచ్చింది టీమ్ మేనేజ్మెంట్ నుంచే. ఇందులో డఫీ, మంగేష్ యాదవ్ అండ్ ఫిల్ సాల్ట్. వీళ్ళు ముగ్గురైతే ప్లేయింగ్ 11 లో మాక్సిమమ్ ఉండబోతున్నారు. సో దీన్ని బట్టి చూసుకుంటే జాకబ్ డఫీ కి అయితే ఫస్ట్ ప్లేయింగ్ 11 లో ఛాన్స్ వచ్చేదే లేదు. మరి ఈ త్రీ ప్లేయర్స్ తో మీ ప్లేయింగ్ 11 ఎలా ఉంటుందో కింద కామెంట్ చేయండి. ఇంకా మన సెకండ్ అండ్ ఇంపార్టెంట్ టాపిక్ విషయానికెళ్తే ఎస్ఆర్హెచ్ టీం ప్రాక్టీస్ మ్యాచ్ 2 ఎలా జరిగింది, అండ్ ఈ మ్యాచ్ వల్ల మన ఎస్ఆర్హెచ్ ప్లేయర్స్ కి అండ్ మన ఎస్ఆర్హెచ్ టీం కి మరి ఎలాంటి ఇంపార్టెంట్ పాయింట్స్ తెలుసుకున్నామో చూసుకుందాం. మెయిన్ గా ఈ వీడియోలో స్టార్టింగ్ లోనే నేనైతే ఒకటి చెప్పబోతున్నా. మనం మాట్లాడుకున్న లాస్ట్ ప్రాక్టీస్ మ్యాచ్ 1 లో నేనైతే శివంగ కుమార్ గురించి అయితే మెన్షన్ చేయలే. సో దాని గురించి ఆ వీడియోలో అయితే మోర్ దెన్ 30 ప్లస్ కామెంట్స్ వచ్చాయి మావ, శివంగ కుమార్ గురించి ఎందుకు చెప్పలే అని. మెయిన్ గా తన గురించి ఫుల్ డిటైల్డ్ వీడియో ఒకటి చేద్దాం అనుకున్నా అందుకే తన గురించి ఆ వీడియో లో మెన్షన్ చేయలే. బట్ ఈ వీడియోలో నేనైతే తన గురించి ఫుల్ క్లారిటీ అయితే ఇచ్చేస్తా. మనం చాలా వీడియోస్ నుంచి అయితే చాలాసార్లు చెప్పుకున్నాం. శివంగ కుమార్ వన్ ఆఫ్ ది బెస్ట్ బౌలర్ అండ్ బెస్ట్ ఆల్ రౌండర్ అవ్వబోతున్నాడు ఎస్ఆర్హెచ్ టీం కి ఈ సీజన్ లో. సో ఎందుకంటే తన బౌలింగ్ యాక్షన్ చూసుకున్నా సేమ్ టు సేమ్ నూర్ అహ్మద్ లెక్కనే ఉంటుంది. ఇండియాలో కుల్దీప్ యాదవ్, సిఎస్కె టీం లో నూర్ అహ్మద్ అండ్ ఎస్ఆర్హెచ్ టీం కి శివంగ కుమార్. సో వీళ్ళు ముగ్గురు టాప్ క్లాస్ బౌలర్స్ ఉన్నారు ఎందుకంటే వాళ్ళ యాక్షన్ తో అండ్ వాళ్ళ అక్యురెసీ తో. మెయిన్ గా శివంగ కుమార్ అయితే లెఫ్ట్ హ్యాండర్స్ కి చాలా డేంజరస్ గా మారిపోతున్నాడు. తను వేసిన బాల్ ఎప్పుడైతే లోపలికి వెళ్తుందో చాలా కష్టంగా ఉంటుంది ప్రతి ఒక్క బ్యాటర్స్ కి. బట్ రైట్ హ్యాండర్స్ కి అంతే ఎఫెక్టివ్ గా ఉంటుందని నాకైతే డౌట్ ఉండేది. బట్ ఈ టూ ప్రాక్టీస్ మ్యాచెస్ వల్ల ఒకటి అయితే క్లియర్ అయిపోయింది. తనైతే ఎస్ఆర్హెచ్ ప్లేయింగ్ 11 లో బెస్ట్ అండ్ ఇంపార్టెంట్ ప్లేయర్ గా మారిపోయాడని నాకైతే అర్థమైపోయింది. సో మాక్సిమం అర్షద్ డూబే కూడా చాలా ఇంపార్టెంట్ స్పెల్స్ చేశారు కాబట్టి, శివంగ కుమార్ అండ్ అర్షద్ డూబే వీళ్ళిద్దరినీ ఫస్ట్ మ్యాచ్ లో చూసే ఛాన్సెస్ కూడా ఉన్నాయి. అండ్ మెయిన్ గా శివంగ కుమార్ దగ్గర నుంచి ఎంత బౌలింగ్ పొగుడుతున్నామో, తన బ్యాటింగ్ కూడా అలానే ఉంటుంది మావ, అదైతే పక్కా. ఈ ప్రాక్టీస్ మ్యాచ్ లో అయితే...

transcription: బ్యాటింగ్ ని మనం చూద్దాం. బట్ చాలా డొమెస్టిక్ మ్యాచెస్ లో వచ్చి చాలా మ్యాచెస్ ని ఫినిష్ చేశాడని చెప్పొచ్చు. సో మ్యాక్సిమం తననైతే ఫస్ట్ మ్యాచ్ లో ప్లేయింగ్ లెవెల్లో ఉండే ఛాన్సెస్ transcription: Some, some people call me a survival expert. Well, as a survival expert, I want to clear up a common misconception. Survival is not something we just do in the woods. So, I would like to help give you some advice to survive whatever is coming next. And while I do not know what your future holds, I can tell you that the world is changing at a terrifying and fascinating pace. You know, so, here I am, I'm 47 years old, I'm not properly old yet, and, I've seen some crazy stuff. I remember watching the Berlin Wall come down live on television as a child. I remember hearing about the internet for the first time, and I thought it was a fake. I thought, I didn't understand that. I was an adult the first time I ever saw an email. I was married when 9/11 happened. And the year before I went to law school, this thing called YouTube was invented. I was practicing for 3 years before I ever got my first social media account. I've seen 7 US wars, 6 recessions, and I've survived one global pandemic so far. I'm only 47. I don't know what the next 40 years holds for you. But, I doubt any of us are going to get through it without seeing terrible and amazing things. We don't know what these changes are going to be, but we do know they're coming. You need to be ready to grab the opportunities that are going to come in this changing world. And, you need to be ready to survive the storms. Money is freedom, money is power, money is flexibility.

Go big or go home, right? You know, and I did not get that job. I did not, I did not get that job.

but I walked away from that convinced that it was going to be easier to steal people's clients than it was to get a job.

title: YouTuber ‘Reckless Ben’ BREAKS SILENCE amid legal battle over missing Legos | Jesse Weber Live
transcription: Tonight, Reckless Ben is here. Yeah, in just a minute, the YouTube star is going to talk with us exclusively about his big legal win in the mystery of the missing LEGO. Yep, a judge just granted him the right to talk again. This is a big development. I got to give you a background though, a quick look at how this whole LEGO legal drama unfolded, okay? It all started when an Oregon family entrusted a franchise of a chain called Bricks & Minifigs to sell their reportedly $200,000 Star Wars LEGO set on consignment. But, the franchise was apparently sold, and the LEGO owners say they never got their LEGO, they never got paid. Now, the family sued the franchise claiming their agreement was breached, that Bricks & Minifigs stole the LEGO collection, and that is when Reckless Ben got on the case. He allegedly traveled to Utah where the franchise executive lives, reportedly started documenting attempts to make contact at his property, posted videos, all going viral. The executive apparently called police, led to Ben getting arrested twice, and as we reported, Bricks & Minifigs also filed a lawsuit against Ben. And, that brings us to this week. Ben is facing a total of four criminal charges. They're all misdemeanors. Provo, Utah, he's charged with disorderly conduct, also reportedly commercial obstruction for allegedly going to the Bricks & Minifigs corporate headquarters. Ben tells us he was there to ask for the LEGOs back. Over in American Fork, Utah, he's charged with stalking and residential picketing for allegedly going to the franchise owner, Josh Johnson's house. Now, Reckless Ben just scored a big legal win. This is when a Utah federal court, this judge lifted the ban that had been on him, posting videos related to Bricks & Minifigs. This was a TRO. However, the revised order still prohibits Ben from coming within 100 meters of any Bricks & Minifigs stores or offices, prevents him from making any threats. Now, we've reached out to Bricks & Minifigs for a statement today, but we haven't heard back. The company has maintained it does not have the LEGO, and in a statement to local media, they said that this issue in its civil case against Ben, real name, Ben Schneider, is going to be addressed through private mediation. It hopes to resolve everything in the coming weeks. But for now, Ben says he got his freedom back, his freedom of speech back. He's already made a new, a new YouTube video. Here's an exclusive sneak peek.

transcription: ജീൻ ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റിനെ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് സ്ഥാപിക്കാൻ പ്രേരിപ്പിച്ച യുദ്ധം ഏതാണ്? ചോദ്യം ഇതാണ് ജീൻ ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റിനെ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് സ്ഥാപിക്കാൻ പ്രേരിപ്പിച്ച യുദ്ധം ഏതാണ്? ഉത്തരം സോൾഫെറിനോ യുദ്ധം. 1859 ൽ നടന്ന സോൾഫെറിനോ യുദ്ധമാണ് ജീൻ ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റിനെ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് സ്ഥാപിക്കാൻ പ്രേരിപ്പിച്ചത്. ഏതാണ് യുദ്ധം? സോൾഫെറിനോ യുദ്ധം. മറന്നുപോകരുത് സോൾഫെറിനോ യുദ്ധം. നമുക്ക് അടുത്ത ചോദ്യത്തിലേക്ക് കടക്കാം. ജീൻ ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റ് എഴുതിയ പ്രശസ്തമായ ഗ്രന്ഥം ഏതാണ്? ജീൻ ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റ് എഴുതിയ പ്രശസ്തമായ ഗ്രന്ഥം ഏതാണ്? ഉത്തരം എ മെമ്മറി ഓഫ് സോൾഫെറിനോ എന്താണ്? എ മെമ്മറി ഓഫ് സോൾഫെറിനോ. ജീൻ ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റ് എഴുതിയ പ്രശസ്തമായ ഗ്രന്ഥമാണ് എ മെമ്മറി ഓഫ് സോൾഫെറിനോ. അടുത്ത ചോദ്യം. ഇന്ത്യൻ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് സൊസൈറ്റിയുടെ ആസ്ഥാനം എവിടെയാണ്? ഇന്ത്യൻ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് സൊസൈറ്റിയുടെ ആസ്ഥാനം എവിടെയാണ്? ഉത്തരം നോക്കൂ ന്യൂഡൽഹി. ഇന്ത്യൻ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് സൊസൈറ്റിയുടെ ആസ്ഥാനം വരുന്നത് ന്യൂഡൽഹി ആണ്. പ്രധാനപ്പെട്ടൊരു ചോദ്യമാണ് ഇന്ത്യൻ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് സൊസൈറ്റിയുടെ ആസ്ഥാനം വരുന്നത് ന്യൂഡൽഹി. അടുത്ത ചോദ്യം. ഇന്ത്യൻ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് സൊസൈറ്റിയുടെ ഇപ്പോഴത്തെ പ്രസിഡന്റ് ആരാണ്? ഇന്ത്യൻ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് സൊസൈറ്റിയുടെ ഇപ്പോഴത്തെ പ്രസിഡന്റ് ആരാണ്? ഉത്തരം ഇന്ത്യയുടെ രാഷ്ട്രപതിയാണ്. ഇന്ത്യയുടെ രാഷ്ട്രപതിയാണ് ഇന്ത്യൻ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് സൊസൈറ്റിയുടെ ഇപ്പോഴത്തെ പ്രസിഡന്റ്. അപ്പൊ ഇപ്പോഴത്തെ രാഷ്ട്രപതി ആരാണ്? ശ്രീമതി ദ്രൗപദി മുർമു. ഇന്ത്യയുടെ നിലവിലെയും പതിനഞ്ചാമത്തെയും രാഷ്ട്രപതിയായിട്ടുള്ള ശ്രീമതി ദ്രൗപദി മുർമു ആണ് ഇന്ത്യൻ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് സൊസൈറ്റിയുടെ ഇപ്പോഴത്തെ പ്രസിഡന്റ്. അടുത്ത ചോദ്യം നോക്കിക്കോളൂ. ഇന്ത്യയിൽ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് പ്രവർത്തനം ആരംഭിച്ച വർഷം ഏതാണ്? ഇന്ത്യയിൽ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് പ്രവർത്തനം ആരംഭിച്ച വർഷം ഏതാണ്? ഉത്തരം വരുന്നത് 1920. ഇന്ത്യയിൽ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് പ്രവർത്തനം ആരംഭിച്ച വർഷം 1920

transcription: ഉത്തരം പറയണം. മലയാളക്കരയിൽ ജെആർസി പ്രവർത്തനം ആരംഭിച്ച വർഷം. മലയാളക്കരയിൽ ജെആർസി പ്രവർത്തനം ആരംഭിച്ച വർഷം. ഉത്തരം നോക്കിക്കോളൂ, 1920. 1920 ലാണ് മലയാളക്കരയിൽ കേരളത്തിൽ ജെആർസി പ്രവർത്തനം ആരംഭിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നത്. അടുത്ത ചോദ്യത്തിലേക്ക് കടക്കുന്നു. കേരളത്തിലെ ആദ്യത്തെ ജൂനിയർ റെഡ്ക്രോസ്സ് യൂണിറ്റ് ആരംഭിച്ച ജില്ല ഏതാണ്? കേരളത്തിലെ ആദ്യത്തെ ജൂനിയർ റെഡ്ക്രോസ്സ് യൂണിറ്റ് ആരംഭിച്ച ജില്ല ഏതാണ്? ഉത്തരം വരുന്നത് കണ്ണൂരാണ്. കണ്ണൂരിലാണ് കേരളത്തിലെ ആദ്യത്തെ ജൂനിയർ റെഡ്ക്രോസ്സ് യൂണിറ്റ് ആരംഭിച്ചത്. കേരളത്തിൽ കണ്ണൂരിലാണ് ജെആർസി യൂണിറ്റ് ആദ്യമായിട്ട് ആരംഭിക്കുന്നത്. അടുത്ത ചോദ്യം. റെഡ്ക്രോസ്സിന്റെ അന്തർദ്ദേശീയ സമിതിക്ക് നോബൽ സമ്മാനം ലഭിച്ച വർഷം. റെഡ്ക്രോസ്സിന്റെ അന്തർദ്ദേശീയ സമിതിക്ക് നോബൽ സമ്മാനം ലഭിച്ച വർഷം ഏതാണ്? ഉത്തരം, 1944. റെഡ്ക്രോസ്സിന്റെ അന്തർദ്ദേശീയ സമിതിക്ക് നോബൽ സമ്മാനം ലഭിച്ച വർഷം 1944 ആണ്. റെഡ്ക്രോസ്സിന്റെ സംസ്ഥാന തല പ്രസിഡന്റ് ആരാണ്? റെഡ്ക്രോസ്സിന്റെ സംസ്ഥാന തല പ്രസിഡന്റ് ആരാണ്? ഉത്തരം നോക്കാം, സംസ്ഥാന ഗവർണ്ണറാണ്. റെഡ്ക്രോസ്സിന്റെ സംസ്ഥാന തല പ്രസിഡന്റ് സംസ്ഥാന ഗവർണ്ണർ. അടുത്ത ചോദ്യം. ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റ് അന്തരിച്ച വർഷം. ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റ് അന്തരിച്ച വർഷം. ഉത്തരം, 1910. 1910 ഒക്ടോബർ മാസം മുപ്പതാം തീയതിയാണ് ഹെൻറി ഡ്യൂനന്റ് അന്തരിച്ചത്. എപ്പോഴാണ്? 1910 ഒക്ടോബർ 30 ന് അദ്ദേഹം അന്തരിച്ചു. അടുത്ത ചോദ്യം. ഐ ആർ സി എസ് ന്റെ പൂർണ്ണരൂപം എന്താണ്? ഐ ആർ സി എസ് ന്റെ പൂർണ്ണരൂപം എന്താണ്? ഉത്തരം, ഇന്ത്യൻ റെഡ് ക്രോസ് സൊസൈറ്റി. ഐ ആർ സി എസ് ന്റെ പൂർണ്ണരൂപം എന്താണ്? ഇന്ത്യൻ...

transcription: റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സ് സൊസൈറ്റി എന്നാണ് IRCS ൻ്റെ പൂർണ്ണരൂപം. അടുത്തത് ICRC, ഇതിൻ്റെ പൂർണ്ണരൂപം എന്താണ്? ICRC യുടെ പൂർണ്ണരൂപം എന്താണ്? ഉത്തരം, International Committee of the Red Cross, എന്താണ്, International Committee of the Red Cross, ICRC-യുടെ പൂർണ്ണരൂപം ഇതാണ്, International Committee of the Red Cross. മറന്നുപോകരുത്, IRCS - Indian Red Cross Society, ICRC - International Committee of the Red Cross. അടുത്ത ചോദ്യം, സ്കൂളുകളിൽ ജൂനിയർ റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സിന് ഗ്രേസ് മാർക്ക് അനുവദിക്കാൻ തുടങ്ങിയ വർഷം? സ്കൂളുകളിൽ ജൂനിയർ റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സിന് ഗ്രേസ് മാർക്ക് അനുവദിക്കാൻ തുടങ്ങിയ വർഷം? ഉത്തരം വരുന്നത് 2005. 2005 ലാണ് സ്കൂളുകളിൽ ജൂനിയർ റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സിന് ഗ്രേസ് മാർക്ക് അനുവദിക്കാൻ തുടങ്ങിയത്. ഏത് വർഷമാണ്? 2005ൽ. അടുത്തത്, റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സ് സൊസൈറ്റിയുടെ പ്രധാന പ്രമേയം അല്ലെങ്കിൽ മുദ്രാവാക്യം എന്താണ്? റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സ് സൊസൈറ്റിയുടെ പ്രധാന പ്രമേയം അല്ലെങ്കിൽ മുദ്രാവാക്യം എന്താണ്? ഉത്തരം സർവീസ്, സേവനമാണ് റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സ് സൊസൈറ്റിയുടെ പ്രധാന പ്രമേയം. അപ്പൊ ഫ്രണ്ട്സ് ഈയൊരു വീഡിയോ നിങ്ങൾക്കെല്ലാവർക്കും യൂസ്ഫുൾ ആയെന്ന് കരുതുന്നു. JRC യുമായി ബന്ധപ്പെട്ട അടിസ്ഥാന വിവരങ്ങളാണ് നമ്മൾ നോക്കിയത്. എക്സാമിന് ചോദിക്കാൻ സാധ്യതയുള്ള കുറച്ചു ചോദ്യങ്ങളാണിത്. അപ്പൊ നമുക്കിനി നിങ്ങൾക്കായുള്ള സ്പെഷ്യൽ ക്വസ്റ്റ്യൻ നോക്കാം. ചോദ്യമിതാണ് ലോക റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സ് ദിനം എന്നാണ്? ലോക റെഡ് ക്രോസ്സ് ദിനം എന്നാണ് ആചരിക്കുന്നത്? അപ്പൊ ഈ ചോദ്യത്തിന്റെ ഉത്തരം ഇപ്പൊ എല്ലാവർക്കും കിട്ടിയിട്ടുണ്ടാവും. അവരെന്ത് ചെയ്യുക? പെട്ടെന്ന് തന്നെ അത് കമൻറ് ബോക്സിൽ രേഖപ്പെടുത്തുക. ഒപ്പം നിങ്ങളുടെ പേരും കൂടി ആഡ് ചെയ്യാൻ മറക്കണ്ട. പ്രധാനപ്പെട്ട ചോദ്യമാണ് എല്ലാവരും അറിഞ്ഞിരിക്കേണ്ടതാണ്. അറിയാത്തവർ എന്താ ചെയ്യാ? പെട്ടെന്ന് തന്നെ പോയി ആ ചോദ്യത്തിന്റെ ഉത്തരം നോക്കി പഠിച്ചു വയ്ക്കുക കേട്ടോ. അപ്പൊ ഇതുപോലെ നിങ്ങൾക്ക് കൂടുതൽ വീഡിയോസ് ആവശ്യമാണെങ്കിൽ ചാനൽ മറക്കാതെ ഒന്ന് സബ്സ്ക്രൈബ് ചെയ്തു വച്ചോളൂ, ബെൽ ഐക്കണും എനേബിൾ ചെയ്യാൻ മറക്കണ്ട. ഈ വീഡിയോ നിങ്ങൾക്ക് യൂസ്ഫുൾ ആയിട്ടുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ നിങ്ങളുടെ ഫ്രണ്ട്സിലേക്കും ഷെയർ ചെയ്തു കൊടുത്തോളൂ. വീഡിയോ ലൈക് ചെയ്യാനും സബ്സ്ക്രൈബ് ചെയ്യാനും മറക്കരുത്. താങ്ക് യു ഫോർ വാച്ചിങ്.

transcription: ଭିତର ଦେଲାଟାରେ? ବୋପଦେବଃ ପ୍ରଥମତଃ କିମ, ବୋପଦେବଃ ପ୍ରଥମତଃ କିମ ପଢିତୁମ ଆଚରଣବାନ, ଓକେ। ତ ଏଇଟା ହବ କଣ ନା ପ୍ରଥମ ହେଇଯିବ ବୈଦେଶିକ ବନ୍ତଃ ତମାନଙ୍କର ହେଇଯିବ କରେକ୍ଟ ଆନସର। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ରହିବ ତମାନଙ୍କର ୟୁନିଟ-3 ର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ, ୟୁନିଟ-3 ର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ଦେଲା ଉପମନ୍ୟୁଃ କ୍ଷୁଧାର୍ତ୍ତଃ ଓକେ ସନ କଣ ଖାଇଦେଲେ? ନା ଉପମନ୍ୟୁଃ କ୍ଷୁଧାର୍ତ୍ତଃ ତତ୍ କାନି ଅଭକ୍ଷୟତ୍ ଉପ ଉପମନ୍ୟୁ ଭୋକରେ କଣ ଖାଇଦେଇଥିଲେ ନା ଅର୍କପତ୍ରାଣି ବା ଅରଖ ଲେଖିଦଉଛି ଏଠାରେ ଅରଖ ପତ୍ର। ଉପମନ୍ୟୁ ଭୋକରେ କଣ ଖାଇଦେଇଥିଲେ ପିଲାମାନେ? ନା ଅରଖ ପତ୍ର। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ରହିଲା ତମାନଙ୍କର କଥମ ଉପମନ୍ୟୁଃ, କଥମ ଉପମନ୍ୟୁଃ ଆ କଣ ଅଛି ନାଗଛତ୍ ଓକେ? ତ କଥମ ଉପମନ୍ୟୁଃ ଆଶ୍ରମ ନାଗଛତ୍, ଏଇଟା ତ ପିଲାମାନେ କରିପାରିବ। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ରହିବ ତମାନଙ୍କର ତିନି ନମ୍ବର ଓକେ, କ୍ୟା ପ୍ରୀତି ଅସ୍ମାତ୍, ଓକେ। ଏଇଟା ତମାନଙ୍କର ଗୁରୁଭକ୍ତିହାଃ, ଗୁରୁ ଲେଖିଦଉଛି ପିଲାମାନେ, ଆନସର ଗୁଡିକ ମୁଁ ଏଠି କହିଦଉଛି ଗୁରୁଭକ୍ତିହାଃ। ପିଲାମାନେ, ମେମ୍ବରସିପରେ ସବୁ ଅଲରେଡି ଆପଲୋଡ ହେଇସାରିଲାଣି, ୫୦ ରୁ ଉର୍ଦ୍ଧ ପିଲାମାନେ ବର୍ତ୍ତମାନ ନେଇସାରିଲେଣି ଓକେ। ତମାନେ ଯାଇ ଦେଖି ମଧ୍ୟ ପାର। ଯଥାଶୀଘ୍ର ଜଏନ ଅପସନ ଉପରେ କ୍ଲିକ କର, ଆଉ ବେଶୀ କିଛି ଡେରି କରନି। ଜଏନ ଅପସନ ଉପରେ କ୍ଲିକ କରି ପିଲାମାନେ ବହୁତ କମ ପ୍ରାଇଜ ଅଛି, ତମାନେ ମେମ୍ବରସିପ ପିଲାମାନେ ଲେଖିଦଉଛି ଏଠାରେ, ମେମ୍ବରସିପ ପିଲାମାନେ ନେଇଯାଅ। ବହୁତ କମ ପ୍ରାଇଜ ତମାନଙ୍କର ରହିଛି। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ରହିବ ତମାନଙ୍କର ନୈତତ୍ ଓକେ। ଏଇଟା ସନ୍ଧିବିଛେଦ କଲେ କଣ ହବ ଇତି? ଏଇଟା କଣ ହବରେ ପିଲାମାନେ ନ ଯୁକ୍ତ ଏତତ୍, ନ ଯୁକ୍ତ ଏତତ୍ ତମେ ଏଠାରେ କରିପାରିବ। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ରହିବ ତମାନଙ୍କର ଚାରି ନମ୍ବର ଦେଲା ମାତୃଭାଷାୟା ତମାନଙ୍କର ସ୍ଵମାତୃଭାଷାୟା ଉତ୍ତରମ ଲିଖତ, ଓକେ। ତ ସ୍ଵମାତୃଭାଷାୟା ନିଜ ମାତୃଭାଷାରେ ଉତ୍ତର ଲେଖିବା। କହ, କହ କବିକୁଳସ୍ୟ ଲଲାଟଃ ମୁକୁଟମଣିଃ? କିଏ କବିକୁଳ ଲଲାଟର ମୁକୁଟମଣି ଅଟନ୍ତି? ଏଠି ତମାନଙ୍କୁ ଲେଖିବାକୁ କୁହାଯାଇଛି। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ଦୁଇ ନମ୍ବର ଦେଲା, ସର୍ବଦମନଃ ଇତି ବାଳସ୍ୟ ନାମ କେନ ଉକ୍ତବାନ? ଓକେ, ତ ସର୍ବଦମନର ଯେଉଁ ନାମ ଦିଆଯାଇଥିଲା ସର୍ବଦମନ, ଏଇଟା କାହା ମାନଙ୍କ ଦ୍ଵାରା ଦିଆଯାଇଥିଲା, ନା ଋଷିମାନଙ୍କ ଦ୍ଵାରା ଦିଆଯାଇଥିଲା। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ହବ ତମାନଙ୍କର ରକ୍ଷାକରଣ୍ଡକେ କା କୋ ସିଦ୍ଧଃ ଅସ୍ତି? ରକ୍ଷାକରଣ୍ଡକରେ କୋଉ ପ୍ରକାର ଔଷଧ ଥିଲା ତମାନଙ୍କର ଏଠାରେ ପିଲାମାନେ କରିପାରିବ। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ହବ ତମାନଙ୍କର IV ରେ, IV ରେ ଦେଲା କସ୍ୟା, କସ୍ୟା ଉଟଜେ ମୃତ୍ତିକା ମୟୂରଃ ଆସୀତ? ଓକେ, କଣ ହବରେ ନା ପ୍ରଥମ ତପସ୍ଵୀ, ଯେଉଁ ମୃତ୍ତିକା ମୟୂରଟି ଆଣିବାକୁ ଯାଇଥିଲା କାହାର କୁଟୀରରେ ଥିଲା? ନା ପ୍ରଥମ ତପସ୍ଵୀ କୁଟୀରରେ। ନେକ୍ସ୍ଟ ହବ ତମାନଙ୍କର ଓକେ, ଏଇଟା ତମାନଙ୍କର କଣ ହବ ଭିଟା ସିଂହସ୍ୟ ଗର୍ଜନେନ? ସିଂହସ୍ୟ ଗର୍ଜନେନ ହେଇଯିବ ତମାନଙ୍କର ଲାଷ୍ଟ କରେକ୍ଟ ଆନସର। ତ ଫାଇନାଲି ପିଲାମାନେ ମୁଁ ସବୁ କୋସିନର ୧୦୦ ତୁ ୧୦୦ % କରେକ୍ଟ ଆନସର ଡିସକସନ କଲି, ତମାନଙ୍କର ୧୦୦ % ପିଲାମାନେ ତମାନଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ଏକ୍ଜାମରେ ହେଲ୍ପଫୁଲ ହବ। ସାଙ୍ଗସାଥୀମାନଙ୍କୁ ନିହାତି ଭାବରେ ଶେୟାର କର। ଆଉ ମେମ୍ବରସିପ ନେଇନଥିଲେ ଯଥାଶୀଘ୍ର ଜଏନ ଅପସନ ଉପରେ କ୍ଲିକ କରି ପିଲାମାନେ ମେମ୍ବରସିପ ନେଇଯାଅ। ବହୁତ ପିଲାମାନେ ଅଲରେଡି ମେମ୍ବରସିପ ନେଇସାରିଲେଣି ଓକେ। ତମେମାନେ ମଧ୍ୟ ନେଇଯାଅ। ଓକେ ଥାଙ୍କ ୟୁ ଫର ଵାଚିଙ୍ଗ ଭିଡିଓଟିକୁ କମ୍ପ୍ଲିଟଲି ଵାଚ କରିଥିବାରୁ, ଏତିକିରେ ରହୁଛି ପିଲାମାନେ ଜୟ ଜଗନ୍ନାଥ।

transcription:
Hello, everyone, Jai Jagannath. Welcome to Educare. 
ତ ନବମ ଶ୍ରେଣୀ ଛାତ୍ରଛାତ୍ରୀମାନେ ତମର ଇଣ୍ଟରନାଲ୍ ଆସେସମେଣ୍ଟ ୱାନ୍‌ର ଏକଜାମ୍ ଅଛି। ତ ତାପାଇଁ ମୁଁ ମ୍ୟାଥମେଟିକ୍ସର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନପତ୍ର ନେଇଆସିଛି। ତ ସମସ୍ତେ ଏ ଭିଡିଓଟିକୁ ଲାଷ୍ଟ୍ ଯାଏଁ ଦେଖ ଏବଂ ସମସ୍ତେ ଏ କୋଶ୍ଚିନ୍‌କୁ ପ୍ରାକ୍ଟିସ୍ କରିକି ଯାଅ। ବହୁତ୍ ଇମ୍ପୋଟାଣ୍ଟ ରହିଛି ପିଲାମାନେ। ଆରି ଭିତରୁ ବି ପଡ଼ିବ। ତ ସମସ୍ତେ 
ପ୍ରାକ୍ଟିସ୍ କରିକି ଯାଅ। କେହି ମଧ୍ୟ ଭିଡିଓଟିକୁ ମିସ କର ନାହିଁ। ଏବଂ ଯୋଉମାନେ ଆମ ଚ୍ୟାନେଲ୍‌ରେ ନିଉ କରିକି ଅଛ ସମସ୍ତେ ଚ୍ୟାନେଲ୍‌କୁ ସବସ୍କ୍ରାଇବ୍ କରିଦେବ। ଭିଡିଓଟିକୁ ନିଜ ସାଙ୍ଗମାନଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଶେୟାର କରିବ ଲାଇକ୍ ମଧ୍ୟ କରିଦେବ। ତ ପିଲାମାନେ ସମସ୍ତେ ଭିଡିଓଟିକୁ ନିଜ 
ସାଙ୍ଗମାନଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଶେୟାର କରିବ ଲାଇକ୍ ମଧ୍ୟ କରିବ। ସମସ୍ତେ ଲାଇକ୍ କରିବ ଏବଂ ପିଲାମାନେ କହିରଖୁଛି ଏ ଭିଡିଓର ଡେସ୍କ୍ରିପସନରେ ଆମ 
ସୁପର ସିଲେକ୍ସନ ଗ୍ରୁପର ଲିଙ୍କ୍ ଅଛି। ସେଇଠି କ୍ଲିକ କରି ମଧ୍ୟ ଜଏନ ହେଇପାରିବ। ତ ଜଏନ ହେଲା ପରେ ତମେମାନେ ସୁପର ସିଲେକ୍ସନ ଗ୍ରୁପ ମଧ୍ୟ ପାଇପାରିବ। 
ସିଲେକ୍ସନ କୋଶ୍ଚିନ୍ ମଧ୍ୟ ପାଇପାରିବ। ତ ପିଲାମାନେ ୟେ ରହିଲା ତମର ଇଣ୍ଟରନାଲ୍ ଆସେସମେଣ୍ଟ ୱାନ୍ ମ୍ୟାଥମେଟିକ୍ସ କ୍ଲାସ ଆଇଏକ୍ସର କୋଶ୍ଚିନ୍। 
ତ ୨୦୨୬-୨୭ କପିରାଇଟ୍ ଓଷ୍ଟା। ତ କୋଶ୍ଚିନ୍ କ’ଣ ଅଛି ଚାଲନ୍ତୁ ଦେଖିବା। ନିମ୍ନଲିଖିତ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଗୁଡ଼ିକର ଉତ୍ତର ଗୋଟିଏ ଶବ୍ଦ ବା ବାକ୍ୟରେ ଲେଖ। ସେଟ୍‌ର ସେଟ୍ ତତ୍ତ୍ଵର ସ୍ରଷ୍ଟା କିଏ? ତା’ପରେ ଯଦି x+1 
, 2 = 3, y-1 ତେବେ y ର ମାନ କେତେ? ଯଦି In = 1, 2, 3, 4, 
...., n ତେବେ I20 - I16 ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ କର। ତା’ପରେ ଯଦି A = a, b, c, d, ସ୍ମଲ a, b, c, d, ସେଟ୍ ହୁଏ ତ B ସେଟ୍ = ସ୍ମଲ c, d, e, f ହୁଏ ତେବେ A ୟୁନିୟନ B ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ କର। ତା’ପରେ v ନମ୍ବର: ଶୂନ୍ୟ ସେଟ୍‌ର ଏକ ଉଦାହରଣ ଦିଅ। 
ତା’ପରେ ପିଲାମାନେ ୟୁନିଟ୍ II। ତ ୟୁନିଟ୍ II କୁ ଯିବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ କହିରଖୁଛି ପିଲାମାନେ, ଯୋଉମାନେ ଆମ ଚ୍ୟାନେଲ୍‌ର ମେମ୍ବରସିପ୍ ନେଇନାହାଁନ୍ତି ଜଲଦି ଜଲଦି ଜଏନ୍ ଅପ୍ସନ ଉପରେ କ୍ଲିକ୍ କରି ମେମ୍ବରସିପ୍ ନେଇଯାଅ।

लोग प्रिंस के लाश के सामने बैठ के उसके गांव में नाच रहे थे। ये गिनवा रहे थे कि खान सर का फीस महंगा है कि सस्ता है। अरे हरामियों, कोई लाश पड़ी है न्याय के लिए सालों, तुम लोग टीचर हो! एक थ्योरी आई थी कि आपको शायद ट्रैप करने के लिए पुलिस या किसी ने... खबर भिजवाया गया ना, कि आपकी मां जो हैं, वो आखरी सांस ले रही हैं, बात कर लीजिए। आज़ाद भारत में पहली बार किसी इंसान को गिरफ्तार करने के लिए इतना जी-जान लगाया गया था। चाहे मीडिया हो, टीचर हो, प्रशासन हो... आप रक्षाबंधन मनाते हैं, त्रिपुंड लगाते हैं, लेकिन ईद नहीं मनाते हैं उस तरह से। और ये सब मार्केटिंग पीआर का हिस्सा होता है... मेरे जीवन में बस एक ही कमी है, कि मेरी बहन नहीं है। तो हम शुरू जब किए थे, तो पांच ही राखी होती थी। ये हज़ार राखी एक दिन में हुई है। एक सवाल आया, खान सर गरीबी बेचते हैं। तो अमीरी बेचें? ये चोट्टा वो कह रहा है जो 4-4 हज़ार में पीडीएफ बेचता है। लोग कहते हैं कि आस्तीन में सांप पाल रहे थे, हम आस्तीन में सूअर पाले थे। आप दिखाते हैं कि आप प्रोग्रेसिव इंसान हैं, लेकिन आप पिछड़ी सोच के आदमी हैं और इस बार भी उनके धर्म का, बुर्के का, ये सारी चीज़ें आई। यार हमको ये नहीं समझ में आता, हमारी मेहरारू को देखने के लिए एकनी को कौन सा चूल मचल रहता है! पाकिस्तान भागने का इरादा तो नहीं था आपका? transcription: रोल-रोल बड़ा एक बढ़िया किए। तो अंजना जी के नहीं, कंचना जी के फैन हो गए। हां, कंचना जी। अरे महाराज! तेज प्रताप यादव कहे कि हम खान सर का समर्थन नहीं करते, इनको जेल में होना चाहिए। भरोसा है कि ये हत्या करवाया है और उसको जेल जाना चाहिए। जुगनुओं ने पी रखी थी शराब, भर-भर के सूरज को गालियां दी कि तुम क्या ही चमकते हो, हमको देखो, हम क्या चमकते हैं। रोशन सर ने कहा कि हम भी सस्ता पढ़ाते हैं। एक ₹200 का सवाल है सर, हम भी ₹100 में सर पढ़ाते हैं। अभिनय मैथ्स सर ने भी यही जिक्र किया, यही बात अवध ओझा भी कह रहे थे। ये लोग 50 करोड़ जॉइनिंग लेते थे, ये सब लोग अपना पेनड्राइव और रिकॉर्डेड कोर्स हजारों में बेचते थे, लॉकडाउन से पहले। खान सर फर्जी रेवेन्यू ऑफिसर, फर्जी इनकम टैक्स ऑफिसर, फर्जी एयर फोर्स विंग कमांडर, नीरज को वो राफेल उड़वा देते हैं जबकि उसका नाम मेरिट में नहीं है। अब लोग मजाक उड़ा रहे हैं कि नीरज राफेल उड़ा रहा है, सुखोई उड़ा रहा है। जिस नीरज नाम के लड़के का और ये जो रेवेन्यू ऑफिसर था, इनकम टैक्स ऑफिसर था, इसपे हमने केस किया है, ये एक नंबर का धूर्त और कमीना, हरामी आदमी है ये। एक टीचर हैं, जिनके लिए आपने मुखिया चुनाव का प्रचार तक किया था, उन्होंने यूट्यूब पर वीडियो बनाकर सबसे ज्यादा आपको एक्सपोज़ किया। वो 12वीं पढ़ा ऑर्केस्ट्रा में लौंडा नाच करने वाले को हम मुखिया बना दिए, वो भी तो फर्जी रिजल्ट था? title: Ransom Note Clues Revealed | Jesse Weber Live
transcription:
6 months ago tonight. This is after 84-year-old Nancy Guthrie disappeared from her Tucson-area home. The Pima, the Pima County Sheriff's Office has finally released the alleged ransom notes that were supposedly sent by these alleged kidnappers. Now, as you may know, these notes have been the source of more than a little controversy in the months since Today Show host Savannah Guthrie's mother vanished, mostly because we still don't know if they're real. And though the cops still won't verify their authenticity, because of something that I'm going to get into in just a little bit, it is important to read them in full. So here we go. The first alleged note that was apparently sent on February 2nd says this, "Hello, Savannah. We have your mother, Nancy. She is safe but scared. She will be held for ransom and once payment is received, she will be released unharmed. We will be holding her for a maximum of 7 days. You will need to send Bitcoin in the amount of $4 million USD, United States Dollars, before 5:00 p.m. on Thursday the 5th. If payment is not received, the ransom will be increased to $6 million USD, which will need to be paid by 5:00 p.m. on Monday the 9th. Once payment is received to the Bitcoin address below, she will be released within 12 hours of deposit to a safe drop-off location back in Tucson. If payment is not received by the last deadline on Monday the 9th at 5:00 p.m., she will be killed. Your mother is aware of this, and her life is in your hands. It is in the best interest of everyone to have this completed as soon as possible. You will not be able to contact me from here on out. There will be no negotiation. Do not play games. Law enforcement will not be able to help you. She had a white smartwatch on the floor of the foot of her bed, and the white floodlight in back yard was destroyed."

Then you have the second alleged note. Very different, very different tone. This was apparently sent on February 6th, so 3 days before the deadline from that first note. It says, "Guthrie family, we did not fully grasp the seriousness of her physical condition. We never intended to hurt her, that was not our intention. She perished shortly after she was taken. We believe it was heart-related. She is buried in nature now. Nothing you could have done could have changed the outcome. We want your family to know this, and hope you can find peace. We are truly sorry."

Now, despite the fact that the Sheriff's Office couldn't authenticate the notes, they are now asking for the public's help in finding whoever wrote them. Said in a press release, quote, "These communications reveal distinctive patterns of word choice, syntax, and phraseology that reflect the writer's unique linguistic style. We believe these distinctive linguistic characteristics may be recognizable to someone who knows or has interacted with the note's writer."

transcription:
...somebody who took her or was part of the investigation know that detail. So, when I'm looking at these notes and you raise a good point, they are distinctive. They are bizarre. Big question I've heard today is: is it from AI or did a person write it? And it's phrased so weird, "USD", "US dollars". It's like, is that person from here or, or is there an international connection?

Yeah, those are, that's a great question because, you know, AI certainly could be in play. But when you do that comparative analysis against note number two, let's take a look at that one as a whole. The Guthrie family is now addressed. Why, why the, why the sudden shift away from Savannah?

You know, now we're going back to the Guthrie family and here's what's really stark that jumps out: the word "we" again. The word "we" jumps out five times in the second note. "We did", "We never", "We believe"—

What does that, what does that tell you? What does that tell you?

Well, it, it tells me that there's an emotional shift, uh, in whoever put these notes together. title: How to protect your investments from an AI bubble | The Economist
transcription: Why is investor confidence in AI now wobbling? In recent weeks, we've seen big companies announce that they're going to spend absolutely jaw-dropping amounts of money investing in AI. And whereas previously, investors were cheering those announcements, actually lately, we've seen the stock market wobble in response. It seems like they're getting a bit worried about whether they're going to get returns on all of this money that companies are spending on this new technology. So what exactly is it that's making the stock markets jittery? Well, it's not just that investors are worried about the amounts that companies are spending, although those amounts are vast. It's kind of this feeling that we've been here before. So there are lots of times throughout history where you've had a new technology emerge and it looks like it's going to transform the world. So take railways or canals or electricity or the internet. And in all of those cases, the new technology actually did transform the world. But in the early stages, when it was just coming out, investors got overexcited. They ended up bidding up companies' share prices out of all proportion with their underlying profits. Um, and they also ended up picking the wrong firms, you know, not buying the companies that would actually benefit from this. And then even when the new technology was really successful, a lot of investors lost an enormous amount of money. And there's kind of this worry that something similar is happening again, that AI might be this transformative technology, but share prices have been bid up out of all proportion with underlying profits. So we're at a very nervous moment. What is it then that investors can do to avoid getting stuck? This is something of a puzzle because you might think the obvious answer is, "Okay, shares are too pricey, so I'm going to sell my shares." Professional investors often don't have that as an option. For example, if I manage a stock fund and I tell clients, "invest in my fund and I'm going to invest in stocks," I can't just suddenly sell them and sit on a pile of cash. I, I might actually not be allowed to, even if I am, my clients are going to ring me up and say, "What are you doing? This isn't what I'm paying you for."

title: How to protect your investments from an AI bubble | The Economist
transcription: Even for individual investors who can make the decision to sell their stocks, it's not necessarily a good idea. So take a previous boom, the dot-com boom, which ended in a crash. There were lots of wobbles on the way up, and at each wobble, nervous investors might have decided to sell their stocks. But actually, over the course of that boom, share prices rose by a factor of 12, so you would have really regretted selling your stocks on the way up. And in fact, even after share prices plunged, at the bottom of the crash, investors who had just held on through the ups and the downs would still have made money. Those who had sold out early wouldn't. So selling your stocks isn't necessarily the right thing to do, even if you think share prices are too expensive and you're worried about a crash. title: ICML 2026 | AI Governance Needs ISO-like Interoperability Protocols | Spotlight Presentation
transcription: Good morning, everyone. My name is Rafia Islam, and I'm here to present our position paper, AI Governance Needs ISO-like Interoperability Protocols, Not Just Laws. Our main claim is simple: laws alone cannot make AI governance work across borders. We need shared technical standards to go with them. Let me walk you through why. Here is the problem we start from: AI rules are splitting apart across countries. The European Union has a binding law, the EU AI Act. It sorts systems into four risk levels and requires formal checks before and after release. China takes a registration and security route. Companies must file their algorithms and pass security review for public-facing systems. The United States has no single federal law. It uses sector rules and voluntary guidance, mainly the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. ASEAN offers regional principles, but these are not enforceable. So, we have four regions, four very different philosophies. The strange part is that the underlying systems, the data, and the risks are often the same; only the rules differ. This creates what we call a standardization vacuum. Picture one foundation model with the same weights and the same behavior. Send it to two countries. In one, it is labeled high-risk. In the other, low-risk. Nothing about the model changed, only the border changed. Why does this happen? Because there is no shared technical language for describing AI risk. Without the language, every country classifies the same system in its own way. The result is compliance uncertainty, repeated assessments, and blocked cross-border deployment. And this acts like a hidden trade barrier. Large companies can absorb the cost of dealing with many rule books. Small and medium firms cannot. So, fragmentation quietly favors the big players.

title: ICML 2026 | AI Governance Needs ISO-like Interoperability Protocols | Spotlight Presentation
transcription: So, here is our position. We are not against laws. Laws are necessary. They set the thresholds. They decide what counts as acceptable AI behavior and they carry the enforcement power. But laws are not enough on their own. They cannot guarantee that thousands of different systems in different countries are all measured the same way. That gap needs a second layer. We call it a complementary technical layer. It is a shared, machine-readable way to describe AI risk. In short, laws define what is acceptable, and standards show how you prove it in practice. The two work together. One without the other leaves the job half done. We are not guessing that this works. We have a precedent: GDPR, the European privacy law. GDPR succeeded worldwide, but not because of legal text alone. It succeeded because standards made it actionable. Companies use ISO 27001, a security management standard, to turn legal duties into concrete controls. They also used privacy by design, which builds privacy into systems from the start. Together, the law plus the standards turned an abstract mandate into daily practice. One honest heads up here: ISO 27001 governs how an organization runs its operations. AI is harder because AI governs model outputs, and those outputs are unpredictable and can change over time. So, GDPR guides us, but AI needs standards that can handle that extra uncertainty. This brings us to our proposal: machine-readable AI risk manifests. Think of it as a nutrition label for an AI system. It is a modular JSON file, similar to a software bill of materials. A computer can read it, check it, and compare it automatically. It is not just a document for humans to skim. It travels with the model as a compliance credential. So, one manifest can move across borders. It can plug into MLOps pipelines, into procurement systems, and into regulatory review. As you can see on the right, it is structured data: fields like system identity, intended use, and a risk class that is tagged per jurisdiction. Build it once, reuse it everywhere. We are not asking for hundreds of fields on day one. We propose a minimum baseline of three dimensions, all reported in one shared vocabulary.

title: ICML 2026 | AI Governance Needs ISO-like Interoperability Protocols | Spotlight Presentation
transcription: First, fairness. Report at least one global fairness metric, name the demographic groups, and state your mitigation. Second, sustainability. Report training and inference energy, and disclose the hardware context because energy numbers mean nothing without it. Third, lineage. Give a verifiable record of data sources and hash the data source artifacts so they can be audited later. One important point, these three do not force every country to agree on legal thresholds. They simply let each country read its own rules through one common layer, same data, one format, many interpretations. Now let me address two fair objections. First objection, standards will slow down fast moving research and hurt innovation. Our reply, this assumes that having no standards keeps you nimble. It ignores the coordination cost that fragmentation already imposes at scale. Teams already redo the same work for every jurisdiction. Second objection, compliance requirements favor large established companies and hurt small firms. Our reply, uncoordinated fragmentation already costs small actors more because they must navigate many incompatible regimes. So the real question is not whether standards exist. It is how they are designed. Our answer is to make them modular, versioned, and outcome-oriented. They specify what you must demonstrate and how you must be lit. That is infrastructure, not gatekeeping. So what do we recommend concretely? Three things. One, build open, modular, extensible protocols with low cost paths, reference implementations, and capacity building for the global south and for smaller firms. Two, put stewardship in a multi-stakeholder body such as ISO, IEC, or IEEE releasing major versions on multi-year cycles with room for local modules. Three, treat standards as coordination infrastructure. Embed them in certification, in sandboxes, or and in procurement. They complement the law. They never replace it. The goal is a shift from siloed compliance to interoperable conformance. Comply once, reuse everywhere. That is our position. AI governance needs ISO-like interoperability protocols, not just laws. Thank you for listening. I'm happy to take your questions.

transcription: Hi everyone, I'm Nico Köhnitz and I'd like to introduce MLOx, open-source MLOps for the rest of us. MLOx is a control plane for self-hosted AI infrastructure. Today, even large organizations struggle with MLOps, and for individuals or small teams, the gap is even bigger. You rely on managed cloud platforms, which are powerful but complex, expensive, and often lead to vendor lock-in. Or you try to build your own stack, which requires significant DevOps expertise and a lot of glue code. In practice, many teams face the same constraints. They don't have the time to operate complex cloud setups. They don't want to commit to a single hyperscaler or multiple ones, and they lack the resources to build and maintain a full system from scratch. MLOx is designed exactly for this setting. The core idea is simple: make it possible to run a complete, secure, and observable ML system on your own infrastructure without needing a dedicated DevOps team. So, the problem is when building machine learning systems, you typically deal with three layers. First: infrastructure - servers, runtimes, security. Second: services - databases, pipelines, tracking, registries, serving. And third: integration - configs, secrets, dependencies, and monitoring. Each of these layers is already complex on its own, and while there are many tools available, most of them focus on just one piece of the puzzle. So what happens in practice is that teams end up stitching together everything themselves, often with fragile scripts and ad-hoc setups. And that leads to a key observation: most tools solve one piece, but the user actually needs the whole system. So what MLOx does, MLOx addresses this by structuring the problem into three parts. First: servers - you define and manage infrastructure, choose a backend like Docker, Kubernetes, or native execution, and monitor it. Second: services - you install and manage components like MLflow, Airflow, or MLServer, including configuration and secrets. And third: wiring.

title: MLOX presentation @ CAIN 2026
transcription: This is where MLOxs becomes interesting. It understands services and how they connect, resolves dependencies, and links everything together. So, instead of manually integrating components, you work off at the level of systems, not individual tools. Right now, lifecycle management is intentionally simple, mostly add and remove, because the focus is on reducing complexity, not adding more layers. The architecture follows a simple but important idea. Users can interact with MLOxs through the CLI, UI, or TUI. So, in practice, they don't need to write configuration files themselves. Under the hood, these interactions are translated into a structured configuration, including servers, services, and their relationships. So, a session loads this configuration together with state and secrets, and builds an internal infrastructure graph. This graph represents how all components are connected. From there, different backends, such as Docker, Kubernetes, or native execution, translate this into actual deployment actions. So, MLOxs acts as a kind of a middle layer, not adding complexity, but absorbing it and exposing a simpler interface. Another important aspect is extensibility. Through a system, a plug-in system, new services, integrations, or even backends can be added without changing the core system. So, MLOxs currently supports multiple backends. Docker is the most complete and stable today. Most services run on Docker. Kubernetes is already supported and being extended with more services. There's also a native mode for lightweight setups and a connector backend for hybrid or external integrations. On top of that, the system is structured in layers: infrastructure, services, integrations, and plug-ins. This makes it possible to grow the ecosystem over time without turning the core idea into a monolith. So, the goal is not to build everything into MLOxs, but to provide a structured way to integrate everything else. Let me give you a very simple example. title: MLOX presentation @ CAIN 2026
transcription: Then you can deploy a specific model version to a target server with a single command: mlox model deploy, then the version and the registry and the model, and the target server. What happens under the hood is more interesting. MLOx automatically connects the model registry, retrieves artifacts, configures the serving layer, for example, via MLServer, and ensures everything is deployed securely. So instead of manually wiring together multiple components, you define what you want, and MLOx handles how it connects. So why is this useful? Well, from early usage and feedback, a few patterns emerged. First, integration is the real bottleneck, not individual tools. Second, simplicity wins, especially for small teams. Third, transparency matters. People want to understand what is happening. And fourth, self-hosting becomes viable once complexity is reduced. So in terms of positioning, MLOx sits somewhere between fragile custom custom-built pipelines and large cloud-native MLOps platforms. It tries to combine the flexibility of the first with some of the structure of the second. So looking ahead, there are a few main directions. First, security: better networking, firewall integration, and more advanced certificate handling. Second, features and platform: especially deeper Kubernetes support and improved service integrations. And third, simplicity: lighter alternatives to existing tools, smaller default setups, and potentially separating monitoring into its own application. The guiding principle here is important: not just more features, but more secure and more minimal. So as a takeaway, to summarize, MLOx abstracts servers, services, and their wiring into a single consistent system. It is open-source, self-hosted, and extensible, and designed for teams that need complete systems, not isolated tools. And since this is an early-stage project, we are actively looking for contributors, collaborators, and feedback, and also open to partnerships and funding discussions. If this resonates with you, I'd be very happy to connect. Thank you.

title: CVPR 2026 : CrowdGen
transcription: Let's talk about this paper titled Generative Adversarial Perturbation with Cross-Paradigm Transferability on Localized Crowd Counting. We have seen evasion attacks on all kinds of vision tasks, classification, face recognition to name a few, but crowd models are relatively less explored. They are more complex than the classification task, but they inherit the same weakness that other deep vision models suffer. And most importantly, they are widely deployed in real life scenarios such as public safety, retail analytics and so on. So an undercounting attack could be a safety risk. As we can see a clean example on the right, while passed by a model it outputs 428 people and their locations. However, if small adversarial perturbation is added, it slashes this prediction by over 40% and we get 285 people. So, the previous studies on crowd models are mostly patch-based attacks and they are limited to only density map-based models. So naturally, the question emerges is that can adversarial perturbations transfer across heterogeneous localized crowd counting paradigms such as density map and point regression models? So, to accomplish this attack, we design a perturbation generator that takes clean image as input and outputs the perturbation noise, and this noise is added to the clean image to produce the adversarial image. For black-box transferability, we design a loss function keeping the transferability, imperceptibility and effectiveness goal in mind. Our hypothesis is that even though these models vary by outputs, they share similar backbone architecture such as VGG, ResNet and same weights. So, we our, we hypothesis that this drives the transferability. On the other hand, the crowd scenes are low-frequency dominated, so we suppress the high-frequency and magnitude of the noise for, for subtle perturbation. And lastly, the effectiveness between two paradigms of models come from model-specific loss. So, density map models do the density suppression, and point regression-based models perform logit suppression. Together, this combined loss govern the training. So, this is a sample instance of adversarial examples, where adversarial perturbations are added to the clean images for various lighting conditions.

title: VeriSHAP 5min Summary Presentation
transcription: Hi there, I'm David, and in the next few minutes, I present a short summary of our paper VerifySHAP, or VerySHAP for short, on computing provable bounds for the exact Shapley values of neural networks. SHAP is a popular feature importance technique that can help us explain deep neural networks. The goal is, for example, to find out what influence an input feature, such as the arrow in this image, has on the prediction a neural network makes. SHAP provides such importance scores by computing what is called the Shapley value of each input feature. So, for example, for this arrow feature, we look at a combination of the other features, once with the arrow present, here in yellow, and once with the arrow absent, here in pink. We then use a value function V to mask out the missing features and evaluate the network on that new input with the masked-out features. We then subtract the network output we get when the arrow is absent from the output we get when the arrow is present to compute what is called the contribution delta of this arrow feature. However, SHAP does not only look at one such combination of input features, but looks at all of the combinations of the other input features that we can have. This means that computing Shapley values requires enumerating an exponential number of these feature combinations that are also called coalitions. Because this clearly does not scale very well, previous work has investigated different statistical estimators that only sample a certain number of coalitions. While this is a lot more scalable, these techniques don't necessarily tell us how far off they are with an individual estimate, which can be problematic in sensitive applications. Additionally, for empirically evaluating these SHAP estimators, we need to know the ground-truth exact Shapley values. For these reasons, we introduce VerySHAP, a new algorithm for computing the exact Shapley values of neural networks faster on higher-dimensional feature spaces, and computing guaranteed lower and upper bounds on Shapley values using ideas from neural network verification. The key idea from neural network verification that we leverage is bound propagation. Bound propagation allows us to propagate an entire set of input features, such as this entire coalition space, through the contribution function. And then we obtain a guaranteed lower bound and a guaranteed upper bound on the contribution. We can then plug these bounds into the SHAP equation, and obtain a guaranteed lower bound and a guaranteed upper bound on the Shapley value itself.

title: VeriSHAP 5min Summary Presentation
transcription: While this bound can be rather loose, the way we did it here, since we bound over the entire coalition space, we can iteratively refine the coalition space using a branch and bound approach to create more and more granular partitions of the coalition space. We can again apply bound propagation for each of these partitions to compute guaranteed Shap bounds, and the finer we make that partition, the tighter these bounds get. As we show theoretically, these bounds are indeed guaranteed to contain the true Shapley value at every iteration. We also show that this algorithm eventually recovers the exact Shapley value after finitely many iterations. Another important insight is that, for a linear model, you don't have to do any splitting to compute the exact values. This also has implications for neural networks, as it means that VeriShap can also terminate early for piecewise linear networks, such as ReLU networks, with the exact Shapley value. This also happens in practice, as demonstrated by this MNIST example. Here we compute the exact Shapley value of a ReLU network in 512 iterations, which is way fewer than would be required for enumerating all coalitions. This example also shows that the Shap bounds are useful in their own right. So, for example, the Shapley bounds in iteration 278 already provide us with essentially the same information as the exact values, while taking less time to compute. We compare VeriShap to the previous state-of-the-art algorithm for computing exact Shapley values that is called ExactShap. As this table shows, VeriShap is able to compute exact Shapley values for substantially larger search spaces of up to 2 to the power of 25 coalitions. For computing tight Shap bounds, VeriShap even scales to 60 input features in some cases. We also compared VeriShap to statistical Shap estimators, showing that VeriShap can be advantageous over estimators when high accuracy is required. Additionally, we use VeriShap to compare different Shap estimators on datasets where it was previously infeasible to compute the ground truth Shapley values for neural networks. To summarize, we presented VeriShap, an algorithm for computing guaranteed bounds on Shapley values that, furthermore, eventually recovers the exact Shapley values. We use bound propagation and branch and bound to scale computing exact Shapley values to up to 25 input features and computing tight bounds for even up to 60 input features. Thank you very much for listening. Our paper is on arXiv, the link is in the video description, and if you have questions, please feel free to reach out.

title: Short Introduction of NeighborMAE (CVPR 2026)
transcription: Hello everyone, I'm Liangcong from KU Leuven. I'm glad to present our work, Neighbor MAE: Exploiting Spatial Dependencies between Neighboring Earth Observation Images in Masked Autoencoder Pre-training. The main idea of this work is simple. In Earth observation, images are not isolated samples. They are observations of the continuous Earth's surface. So instead of training masked autoencoder on each image independently, we ask whether neighboring images can provide useful spatial context for masked autoencoder pre-training. Masked image modeling has become a popular self-supervised learning strategy for Earth observation. The model masks parts of an image and learns to reconstruct the missing region. However, most existing MIM methods reconstruct a single image tile independently. This is a simplification of Earth observation data because satellite and aerial images are naturally spatially connected. Neighboring images often share useful information, such as terrain structure, land use, continuity, roads, buildings, and infrastructure patterns. At the same time, neighboring views may also differ in acquisition time, viewpoints, or sensor conditions. This means neighboring images provide varied signals, shared spatial context, and natural variations. Therefore, we ask: can neighboring images provide useful context for masked image modeling? To answer this question, we propose Neighbor MAE, which extends MAE from single image reconstruction to joint reconstruction of neighboring Earth observation images. The method has five main components. First, neighbor sampling: we use geospatial metadata to sample neighboring Earth observation images based on the intersection over union of the spatial footprints.

title: Short Introduction of NeighborMAE (CVPR 2026)
transcription: Images with sufficient overlap are treated as neighbors. Second, relative position encoding. We embed the patch position in a shared normalized coordinate system, which allows the Transformer to understand the spatial relationship between patches from different images. Third, joint reconstruction. Instead of encoding one image independently, we concatenate the visible patches from both neighboring images and feed them into the same MAE encoder. Then the decoder reconstructs the masked region of both images jointly. Through self-attention, the model can learn dependencies across neighboring views. Fourth, dynamic masking ratio. If two neighboring images overlap strongly, reconstruction becomes easier because one image may reveal information about the other. To keep the pretext task challenging, we increase the mask ratio when the IoU between the neighboring images is high. Finally, visibility-aware loss weighting. Some masked pixels in one image may already be visible in the neighboring images. This can create a shortcut when the model simply copies the visible contents. To avoid this, we reduce the reconstruction loss weight for pixels that are visible from the neighbors when copying is too easy. Together, this design allows Neighbor MAE to learn from neighboring images effectively and efficiently. We compare Neighbor MAE with original MAE under the same training conditions. The evaluation includes diverse downstream Earth observation tasks, including image classification and semantic segmentation. We evaluate both linear probing and fine-tuning. As shown on the right, Neighbor MAE consistently improve over MAE across all downstream benchmarks.

title: Short Introduction of NeighborMAE (CVPR 2026)
transcription: This results suggests that neighboring images provide useful contextual information and that NeighborMAE learns more transferable representation than standard MAE. Next, we analyze where the improvements come from. A key question is whether NeighborMAE works simply because it sees more pixels or because neighboring images provide more useful spatial context. To answer this, we compare different ways to extend the input view using the same extra token budget, approximately two times the base input used by standard MAE. The result shows that simply using a larger tile gives only limited improvement. In contrast, neighboring images provide stronger gains because they introduce richer spatial variations rather than a fixed larger field of view. The best performance comes from multi-temporal neighbors, which combines spatial variations from neighboring regions and temporal variations from different observation. This supports our main claim. The gain does not come merely from increasing input size. It comes from learning spatial and temporal dependencies between neighboring Earth observation images. In conclusion, this work highlights an overlooked signal in masked image modeling for Earth observation, the spatial dependencies between neighboring images. We propose NeighborMAE, a spatially aware MIM framework that jointly reconstructs neighboring EO images, which learns stronger and more transferable representation. Our experiment shows consistent improvement over MAE across diverse downstream task and the ablation study confirms that neighboring views provide more useful context than simply enlarging the inputs. Thank you for your listening.

transcription: The final award of the evening is the Ramon Guiteras Award, our highest honor, recognizing outstanding contribution to both the art and science of urology. President Palmer, President-elect Reed, past and future presidents, fellow awardees, and guests. Thank you. Shira Ruben, my official AUA handler, tells me that the Guiteras Award has been given since 1970, but that only three people in its history have swept all three AUA awards: the Gold Cystoscope, the Hugh Hampton Young, and the Guiteras. Pat Walsh, who hired me as his first resident and regretted it ever since, Darracott Vaughan, who hired me as his first faculty member and withdrew the offer after a disastrous interview, and Bill Catalona, my chief resident, who for 50 years has been telling me how wrong I am. Now we're four. That is humbling company. Shira also says that the only reason that I can say this with a straight face is that until 1975, the Gold Cystoscope Award was given to the best golfer in the AUA, which would have ruled out all four of us, except maybe Bill. Before I go further, I have been nominated four times for the Guiteras Award. The North Central Section, where I did the bulk of my work on robotic surgery, nominated me three times. transcription: I'm not supposed to know any of this, but I do. And there is... I want to say something that I do not often say. I am an immigrant. The fact that the son of an Indian teacher can stand here holding the Guiteras, well, I'm not holding it, it's... but it's not a story about me. When Raj and Padma Vattikuti decided to fund a robotic surgery program at Henry Ford, they were not buying equipment. They were making a bet on a person. No money, no money. No money, no mission. This award belongs to those who bet on an underdog. Novick gave me my first chance, Pat Walsh picked me for the Hopkins residency and stood my, stood by me until I went to the dark side of robotics, a debt that I carry to this day. Bill Catalona kept me from being fired more than once, not because Bill necessarily saw anything in me, but because Bill likes to fight a good fight. John Barry was my weather vane for ethics and morality and also taught my children how to fish. Peter Carroll, my younger and smarter brother, has been a steadfast advocate for 30 years, in seasons where that cost something. Craig Rogers has taken the Vattikuti Institute to places I never imagined and is now taking on the mantle of enhanced nerve-sparing. Larissa Rodriguez has, you might say, no interest whatsoever in nerve-sparing, but a deep interest in making life better for the next generation of urologists. I hope to spend the next, the next year helping Larissa and Craig. They are not the future, they are the present. To most everyone here 50 years ago, I was an underdog. To one person, I was not. title: Alex Morehead - CS Postdoc Symposium 2026
transcription: I'm Brandon Anderson. I'm a upper postdoc fellow here at NERSC, also in the SciDAC AI and computing systems group. And today, I'll be presenting a AI foundation model for 3D molecules and materials, also known as EquiM. So, first off, foundation models. This is a very popular term these days. Models like ChatGPT, we're all familiar with. These are some examples of foundation models, right? AI models that are trained on a vast quantity of data and can be applied across a range of tasks once it's trained. And for science, we're interested in these types of models because we'd like to build, for example, universal algorithms for many different types of scientific data we care about. So, in this case, in this work, we're going to focus on chemical systems, so molecules and materials. Um, what would it take to build a foundation for molecules and materials? Um, so the way we look at that is, we want to understand how do we represent the data, molecules and materials. So, in this work, we're going to argue for breaking down the representation of molecules and materials as atomic systems with 3D points in space and types of atoms, for example, element types attached to them. And if we have a if we have a foundation model that's trained on these collections of atoms, that could be applied across a range of tasks. For example, it can be a universal generative and predictive algorithm. It can generate new molecules and materials, it also predict properties of existing molecules and materials. And can share information across those different tasks. You could use this in drug discovery, battery research, and many other areas. Now, how would you actually build this if you had a collection of atoms and a bunch of datasets with those atoms in? There's two main approaches to building foundation models in the AI community these days, many others, but the two main ones are autoregressive models and bidirectional models. So, BERT is an example of a bidirectional model and ChatGPT is an example of an autoregressive model. Autoregressive models, you're just predicting one token after the other. And bidirectional models means you can corrupt some tokens in your, like for example, sentences and ask the model to predict back the missing words in the sentence at any position. So, it doesn't assume any kind of ordering when you're doing this bidirectional modeling. And for scientific applications, we're going to argue that that's really important, that we don't want to assume that there's a specific chemical ordering of atoms in these molecular or material systems. So, we lean towards bidirectional models in this work.

It can perform both generation of new molecules and materials, and prediction of properties like energies, forces, and so on, of existing molecules and materials. It's visualized here in the top right-hand corner. Like most foundation models in the AI literature, it's trained in two stages. The first stage is pre-training, and we'll talk about how that's performed in a little bit, and second is fine-tuning. So the idea is you want to train your model on a vast quantity of data during pre-training, so it sees as much as possible, and you want the pre-training task, what it's actually trying to do, to be as generic as possible so it can learn rich information about your input data. And then when we fine-tune it, you want to adapt it to specific, related tasks in your domain, like property prediction. And this is all driven, that, that pre-training phase I mentioned, is driven by what is called flow matching, which is this really popular technique in the generative AI literature. Basic idea of flow matching is you have two different probability distributions, or data distributions, and you're trying to learn an AI model that will basically map samples from one distribution and push them to the other distribution. So, why would you want to do that? This is really convenient for data generation. For example, you could have your first data distribution be something like a Gaussian, something you can readily and quickly sample from, and then the second distribution could be like a real dataset, like of molecules and materials. So if you want to generate new molecules and materials, you can sample from the Gaussian, use your trained AI model, and it can basically turn that Gaussian sample into a real molecule or material. Now empirically, how does Sadam-1 do? So, we tested across a range of tasks. First, we're going to talk about the pre-training tasks, which are these generative tasks: How well can we generate small and large molecules, kind of split into two different tasks. For small molecule generation, we're almost at a perfect, um, chemical validity, um, chemical and structural validity rate according to this tool called PoseBusters, which is well-known in the AI literature, um, essentially 99%, better than any other method in the AI literature. And we also find something, you know, quite interesting, which is that training on both molecules and materials is better than training on just molecules alone. So, there's some mutually beneficial information the model is learning when it sees both types of chemical systems during pre-training.

title: Ultrasound-CLIP(CVPR 2026)
transcription: Hello, everyone. I'm Jiayin Jin from Hangzhou City University. Today, I'm excited to present our CVPR 2024 paper, UltrasoundCLIP: Semantic-Aware Contrastive Pre-training for Ultrasound Image-Text Understanding. Ultrasound is one of the most widely used imaging modalities in clinical practice. However, ultrasound vision-language learning remains under-explored because of heterogeneous diagnostic attributes and weak image-text alignment. To address this problem, we propose a semantic-aware ultrasound vision-language framework, together with a large-scale ultrasound image-text dataset. Unlike natural images, ultrasound images are highly challenging for vision-language learning. First, ultrasound diagnosis involves heterogeneous diagnostic attributes. For the same lesion, radiologists may describe multiple diagnostic attributes, such as echogenicity, margins, internal characteristics, and calcification. Second, ultrasound images from different organs often look visually similar, even though they correspond to completely different anatomical structures and diagnostic semantics. Because ultrasound image-text pairs often exhibit weak semantic alignment, directly applying conventional CLIP-style contrastive learning is insufficient for ultrasound understanding. This motivates the need for semantic-aware ultrasound representation learning. To address these challenges, we first construct US365K, the first large-scale dedicated ultrasound image-text dataset. The dataset contains over 364,000 image-text pairs collected from more than 11,000 clinical cases, spanning diverse organs and pathological findings. More importantly, we introduce UDT, which stands for Unified Ultrasound Diagnostic Taxonomy. UDT standardizes both anatomical hierarchy and ultrasound diagnostic attributes, providing structured semantic knowledge for ultrasound understanding. This taxonomy serves as the semantic foundation of our framework.

Now, if you're not in medicine or research, you might hear the word conference and picture doctors sitting through endless PowerPoint presentations and drinking too much coffee. And yes, there is definitely some of that going on here. And for organizations like GHLF, these meetings are not just about networking, they are about making sure the patient perspective is present in rooms where important healthcare decisions and innovations are taking shape. So today, I want to pull back the curtain a little bit and explain what actually happens at conferences like EULAR, why they matter for patients, and some of the major themes already emerging this year, including artificial intelligence and the growing excitement around CAR T and cell therapies for autoimmune diseases.
