transcription: For decades, treatment has largely focused on suppressing the immune system continuously over time. But researchers are increasingly asking, could we someday fundamentally reprogram the immune system itself? Now, a very important caveat here, these therapies are still early on, they are complex, they are very expensive right now and they are certainly not around the corner for most patients. But the excitement in the research community is real. I'm meeting with some of these doctors, some of these scientists, and I could feel the excitement. And one of the valuable things about conferences like EULAR is getting an early sense of where medicine may be heading over the next decade. So, stay tuned to see what more is coming in the world of CAR-T. Another major theme at EULAR this year is artificial intelligence and digital health. AI is now showing up across almost every part of rheumatology research, including imaging analysis, predicting disease flares, identifying patterns in large data sets, remote monitoring of patients, and personalized treatment selection. Now, whenever people hear AI, there's often a tendency to jump immediately to extremes. Either AI will solve everything or AI is going to replace everything. Neither is realistic. The more practical reality is that AI may increasingly become a tool that helps clinicians make better, faster, and more personalized decisions for patients. For example, AI may eventually help identify which patients are most likely to respond to certain therapies or which patients may be at higher risk for complications. That could improve care dramatically. But there are also important questions, such as data privacy, bias in algorithms, and access to technology. Technology is there to support, rather than replace, human relationships in the healthcare world. So, this is an area with enormous promise but also important caution. title: [CVPR 2026] MoECLIP: Patch-Specialized Experts for Zero-shot Anomaly Detection
transcription: Zero-shot anomaly detection, which aims to detect anomalies in unseen categories, has recently attracted significant attention. In this work, we propose MOE-CLIP: Patch-Specialized Experts for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection. To perform zero-shot anomaly detection, existing studies primarily use pre-trained CLIP models and apply adapter fine-tuning methods to adapt them to the anomaly detection task. However, conventional approaches process all patches in a monolithic, patch-agnostic manner, without considering the unique characteristics of each patch, such as background patches or anomalous patches. To address this, we propose MOE-CLIP, a mixture-of-experts-based CLIP adaptation method that dynamically selects the most suitable expert for each patch. However, simply applying a mixture-of-experts framework leads to a functional redundancy problem among experts, where multiple experts learn highly similar representations instead of diverse knowledge. Therefore, we further propose FOFS and ETF loss, which encourage each expert to learn distinct and complementary knowledge. Here is the framework of our proposed MOE-CLIP. First, the mixture of LoRA experts module is inserted into the vision encoder layers, enabling dynamic expert selection and adaptation according to the characteristics of each image patch. The approach for achieving expert specialization, FOFS, is a technique applied at the input stage that enforces role separation among experts through the LoRA A matrices. Specifically, it decomposes the input feature space into multiple orthogonal subspaces, forcing each expert to observe only its own unique information without physical overlap with other experts.

title: [CVPR 2026] MoECLIP: Patch-Specialized Experts for Zero-shot Anomaly Detection
transcription: In addition, we introduce ETF loss, because even if FOFS provides different inputs to each expert, there is still a risk that the experts' final outputs may become similar again during training. Motivated by the phenomenon known as neural collapse, ETF loss regularizes the final output vectors of the experts, so that they become geometrically well separated and uniformly distributed in an equiangular manner. In summary, FOFS is responsible for input level separation, while ETF loss enforces output level separation. Through this synergy, each expert becomes specialized in handling its own distinct image patch regions. Comprehensive experimental results across 14 benchmark datasets, spanning industrial and medical domains, demonstrate that MoE-CLIP outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. When we analyzed which image patches each expert attends to, we observed that, in this example, expert one mainly focused on anomalous patches, expert two captured the overall object regions, expert three attended to background regions, while expert four did not focus on any particularly meaningful area for this image. These results indicate that different experts learn distinct roles and collaboratively contribute to anomaly detection. Due to its patch specialized expert design, MoE-CLIP delivers more accurate and fine-grained anomaly localization than existing methods. By incorporating FOFS and ETF loss, we observed a significant reduction in similarity among experts, demonstrating that the proposed methods effectively mitigate redundancy between experts. Thanks for watching this video.

transcription: My name is Katie Linden, and I'm the CEO at Exercise and Sports Science Australia, or ESSA. And I'm here today at our national conference, Activate, where we have over 800 clinicians from around the country here today to discuss research, emerging practice, and innovative models of care. My name is Jackson Howie, I'm a PhD candidate from the Centre for Heart Rhythm Disorders at the Adelaide University. I presented some of our work in pacemaker patients. It was a simple clinical question looking at the relationship between pacemaker-detected physical activity and objective exercise tolerance. When the GST legislation was first introduced, exercise physiology was an emerging discipline. title: Dr. Dutton Address to the Senate Standing Committee on Agriculture and Forestry
transcription:
Dr. Dutton, you now have the floor.
Good morning. I'm an associate professor at Dalhousie University in department called Community Health and Epidemiology. I'm also a member of a research group called PROOF, with members across Canada and the US, who have a goal of identifying policy options to reduce household food insecurity in Canada. I want to open by pointing out that household food insecurity is a specific scientific concept. It sounds like it should be the opposite of food of food security, but it isn't. Household food insecurity is the inadequate or insecure access to food due to financial constraints at the household level. Food security has been used to refer to everything from our ability to produce enough food domestically to feed our population, food supply chain, access to food banks. Food security therefore is a term inclusive of many problems that have to do with food and people sometimes conflate action on anything related to food with solutions to household food insecurity, which is not correct. This inappropriate combination of household food insecurity with issues grouped under the banner of food security complicates the language for people in government trying to grapple with the problem of household food insecurity. So some find it helpful to think about food insecurity as part of consumption poverty uh and so is related to challenges attributable to general affordability, cost of living, labor market outcome inequality, housing, like we like we just heard. Statistics Canada measures household food insecurity using a specific questionnaire that's been agreed upon by researchers to accurately measure household material circumstances. Uh that means efforts to decrease that measure will improve the lives of Canadians by improving their health and decreasing healthcare command for uh healthcare demand, excuse me. For reference, about one in four people in Canada are in food insecure households. I know this standing committee has heard from government employees from AAFC and ESDC, ESDC and others uh who have also emphasized that food insecurity is tied to income and I heard it all morning, so that's great. This is consistent with decades of research on food insecurity. Uh PHAC recently published reviews on what impacts food insecurity in Canada and came to the same conclusion. Food insecurity is improved by actions that decrease financial hardship. Those reviews identified that giving households food through in-kind mechanisms does not make much of an impact on food insecurity. The idea that giving a household food does not impact food insecurity is a major sticking point for many people, because it sounds unintuitive.

title: 'How Much Reparations Have You Personally Paid?': Rep. Gill Confronts NPR CEO With Her Past Tweets
transcription: Should taxpayer-funded media promote highly ideological social views? Should race be treated as the central lens for understanding America? Those are questions that cut through political spin very quickly. And this is where the hearing became more significant than a single viral moment. For many conservatives, the issue is no longer just disagreement with certain media narratives. It's the belief that institutions like NPR have gradually shifted from journalism into activism. Whether that perception is fully fair or not, it's clearly growing. Many Americans now look at coverage surrounding race, gender, policing, and social justice, and feel those issues are often framed from one ideological perspective, rather than explored as open debates. The repeated "I don't recall" answers also became politically damaging because they created the impression that controversial statements were embraced publicly during one political moment, then softened later under scrutiny. Fair or unfair, it came across to many viewers as evasive rather than reflective. But this is where the conversation becomes more complicated. Supporters of NPR would argue that covering issues involving inequality or social tensions is part of journalism, not activism. And to be fair, not every progressive framing automatically means political bias. Some of these debates are legitimate public issues that media organizations are expected to cover. Still, the larger problem here is trust. Once audiences begin to feel that major institutions no longer represent them fairly, skepticism grows very quickly, especially when taxpayer funding is involved. And politically, Republicans understand why these hearings resonate. They tap into a broader frustration among voters who feel cultural institutions increasingly treat traditional beliefs or dissenting opinions as morally suspect, rather than simply different viewpoints. At a broader level, this hearing didn't fully resolve the debate over media bias or public funding, but it did expose how deep the divide has become between legacy institutions and a large segment of the American public. And that trust gap is now becoming one of the defining political issues in the country. If you want political analysis that focuses on the arguments, the policy implications, and the deeper institutional stakes without turning everything into outrage, that's what we focus on here.

title: Ramayana Trailer REVIEW | Deeksha Sharma
transcription: इतने सारे लीक्स में रामायण का ट्रेलर देखने के बाद अब ऐसा क्या ही बाकी बचा है जो मैं आपको नया बता दूंगी? सच बोलूं, बहुत कुछ। इतना ज्यादा हाइप भी नहीं करना चाहिए था ना क्योंकि रियल ट्रेलर में कुछ वर्ल्ड क्लास है तो थोड़ा बहुत चीजों में 50-50 फील आ रहा है। तो चलो शुरुआत उसी सवाल से कर लेते हैं जिससे हर कोई बचना चाहता है। सुबह 4:00 बजे ट्रेलर कौन डालता है? नहीं-नहीं, यह वाला नहीं, इससे भी बड़ा जरूरी दूसरा सवाल। भगवान राम के बिना रामायण कैसी और राम के लिए रणबीर कपूर का ही सिलेक्शन क्यों? क्या वाकई में मजा आ रहा है रणबीर को ऐस भगवान राम के रोल में देखकर? देखो यह बात किसी से छुपी नहीं है जब से ट्रेलर के क्लिप्स वायरल होना शुरू हुए थे और अब फाइनली ऑफिशियल वीडियो भी आ गया है, हर किसी ने यश को ऐस रावण टोटली एक्सेप्ट कर लिया है। नो इफ, नो बट, किसी दूसरे एक्टर का नाम तक नहीं लिया जा रहा है जो इस फिल्म में रावण बन सकता था या फिर यश से ज्यादा बेटर तरीके से एग्रेशन, गुस्सा, घमंड, इन सारे एक्सप्रेशन को डिस्प्ले कर सकता था। सबसे बेस्ट डिसीजन था ट्रेलर को यश के सीन के साथ शुरू करना। देखते ही अलग एनर्जी सी फील होने लगती है। उनके डायलॉग्स उनके चेहरे को पूरी तरह मैच कर रहे हैं। यश और रावण मेड फॉर ईच अदर हैं। चाहे आप इस बात को कितना भी कंट्रोवर्शियल क्यों ना समझो लेकिन हां, इस ट्रेलर के बाद काफी लोग ऐसे होंगे जो रावण की वजह से रामायण देखने जाएंगे। लेकिन इस तरीके का कॉन्फिडेंस लोगों को रणबीर के ऊपर फील नहीं हो रहा है, फिर चाहे वो 144p वाला वीडियो हो या फिर 4K एचडी का ट्रेलर। दिक्कत वीडियो क्वालिटी की नहीं है, एक्टर से एक्सपेक्टेशंस की है। ऑनेस्टली ट्रेलर में रणबीर के सीन्स ऑन-ऑफ टाइप के हैं। जब वो ब्लाइंड फोल्ड वाला सीक्वेंस आया, इतनी खुशी हुई ना अंदर से। यह है वो इंडियन सिनेमा विजन जिसके आगे अंग्रेज भी अपनी नजरें नीची कर लेंगे। लेकिन जैसे ही ट्रेलर में आंखों से वो पट्टी हटी, रणबीर पे भरोसा थोड़ा डगमगा सा जाता है। वो भगवान से धीरे-धीरे इंसान जैसे लगना शुरू हो जाते हैं। नोटिस किया, ट्रेलर में जो पास वाले शॉट्स हैं, वो काफी डाले गए हैं जिनका परपज था गॉड वाइब्स लेकर आना, पब्लिक का सर रिस्पेक्ट में झुकाना। बट ईमानदारी से बोलूंगी एक बात, मैंने सोशल मीडिया पे कुछ फैन मेड पोस्टर्स, एआई जनरेटेड इमेजेस देखी हैं जो रणबीर को भगवान राम के रूप में कई ज्यादा डिवाइन तरीके से प्रेजेंट करती हैं। मैं क्या बोलना चाह रही हूं वो शायद आप सौरभ राज जैन को स्क्रीन पे देखकर जो महसूस करते हो, उसे रामायण में रणबीर से कंपेयर करके अच्छे से समझ जाओगे। देखो जैसे शूर्पणखा का रोल है, उसमें रकुल प्रीत का अचानक आना आपकी एक्सपेक्टेशंस को क्रॉस कर जाता है। प्रेजेंटेशन जितना सोचा था उससे भी ज्यादा बेटर निकला। यही सेम बात अरुण गोविल के लिए भी कही जा सकती है। बट वो सेम फार्मूला रणबीर के केस में उतना फिट नहीं बैठ रहा है, उसका उल्टा हो रहा है फिलहाल। याद रखना इस शब्द पे खास जोर दिया है मैंने, फिलहाल। क्योंकि ऐसा भी नहीं है कि ट्रेलर देखकर आप रणबीर से अंधा हेट करने लग जाओ, सीधा उनकी कास्टिंग पे सवाल खड़े करने लग जाओ, या फिर इतना अंधा भी नहीं होना है कि एक्सपेक्टेशंस को मार ही डालो, जो है, title: Ramayana Trailer REVIEW | Deeksha Sharma
transcription: बचाना था, सच्ची बताना। पता नहीं क्यों हर बार जब रामायण का कंटेंट आने वाला होता है, लोग आदिपुरुष का ज़िक्र करने लग जाते हैं। बट इस बार ट्रेलर में विजुअल्स की क्वालिटी देखने के बाद आपको बड़े हॉलीवुड प्रोजेक्ट से कंपैरिजन शुरू कर देना चाहिए। जिस तरह क्रिस्टोफर नोलन की फिल्म का टिकट खरीद के आप थिएटर नहीं सीधा दूसरी दुनिया में पहुँच जाते हो, ठीक वैसे ही रामायण ने खुद का हिस्टोरिकल वर्ल्ड क्रिएट किया है। लेकिन सच ये है कि ट्रेलर में जो मॉन्स्टर्स क्रिएट किए गए हैं, वो टीज़र से तो बेहतर हैं लेकिन एकदम बेस्ट रिजल्ट से काफी दूर हैं, वर्क इन प्रोग्रेस लग रहा है, टीवी सीरियल जैसा वाइब आ सकता है कुछ लोगों को। और जिस तरह ट्रेलर का कलर फिक्स किया है, उसी तरह बाकी छोटी-मोटी चीज़ों को रिलीज आने तक संभाल लिया जाएगा। लेकिन मुझे बिल्कुल समझ नहीं आ रहा है, कुछ लोगों का साई पल्लवी को जबरदस्ती डाउनग्रेड करना। माता सीता की पहचान ही यही है कि उनसे जुड़ी सिंपल चीजें भी बहुत बड़ी बन जाती हैं। कितने अच्छे से ड्रेस सिलेक्शन किया है ट्रेलर में साई पल्लवी के सारे सीन्स का। उनके एक्सप्रेशंस देखकर एक प्योर डिवाइन एनर्जी सी आ गई है आँखों में। डायलॉग्स भी बहुत रियल, नेचुरल और इमोशनल फील दे रहे हैं। साई पल्लवी, रणबीर के सीन्स बिल्कुल वैसे हैं, जैसा आप इस एनिमेटेड फिल्म को देखकर फील करना चाहते थे। वैसे अब रियलाइज हुआ मुझे, क्यों वो दिल्ली वाले इवेंट के बाद हर कोई ट्रेलर के म्यूजिक के बारे में बात करते नहीं थक रहा था। लास्ट में देखा, कैसे शोर, सन्नाटा साथ में फील हो रहा था। कहीं से तो न्यूज़ उड़ी है, टी-सीरीज़ ने रामायण के दोनों पार्ट्स के म्यूजिक राइट्स 75 करोड़ में खरीदे हैं और ऑनेस्टली ट्रेलर का बीजीएम सुनके ये प्राइस मुझे तो डिस्काउंट जैसा लग रहा है। देखो एज टोटल, इस ट्रेलर ने रामायण की हिस्ट्री को अच्छे से इकट्ठा कर लिया है। बहुत तगड़ी डिटेलिंग कर रहे हैं नितेश तिवारी जो छोटी-छोटी चीजों में साफ़ नजर आ रहा है। ट्रोल करने वाले चाहे कुछ भी बोले, बट रामायण की फिल्म मेकिंग अपने सब्जेक्ट को डिसरिस्पेक्ट बिल्कुल नहीं कर रही है, उल्टा एक फैमिलियर सब्जेक्ट को भी नया सा फील दे दिया है, एक्साइटमेंट आने लगा है। काफी लोग सवाल कर रहे थे ना कि रामायण का हाइप सिर्फ इसीलिए है क्योंकि वो रामायण है, उसका सब्जेक्ट हर किसी के साथ कनेक्ट करता है, इसके अलावा फिल्म की टीम ने अलग से इसमें क्या ऐड किया है? कास्टिंग 100 में 100 नंबर, ऑडियो सुनके सुकून आता है, एक्शन बहुत बड़े स्केल का होगा और इमोशंस सच्ची में भगवान के करीब ले जाते हैं। और कुछ चाहिए? सुबह 4:00 बजे उठकर नई जनरेशन के बच्चे इंडियन फिल्म के ट्रेलर का वेट कर रहे हैं, कुछ तो अच्छा किया होगा ना? जब गालियां देने में इतना आगे रहते हो तो क्रेडिट देने में कंजूसी क्यों करना? लेकिन इस बात से भी इनकार नहीं कर सकते कि फाइनल क्वालिटी में अभी काफी काम करना पड़ेगा क्योंकि क्रिएचर्स वगैरह थोड़े आर्टिफिशियल लग रहे हैं, उनमें रियलिटी वाली बात नहीं है। लेकिन एक चीज़ मेरे दिमाग में जरूर आ रही है, जो बिना बोले मैं रह नहीं पाऊँगी। अगर रामायण पार्ट वन भगवान राम के बारे में ज्यादा है और इसमें रावण का स्क्रीन टाइम काफी कम होगा, उसके बावजूद यश ने अगर इस तरह पकड़ बना ली है फिल्म पे तो फिर सोचो फिल्म के पार्ट टू में क्या होगा? जब रामायण का फोकस यश पे शिफ्ट करेगा, रावण तो हार जाएगा लेकिन क्या यश को रणबीर हरा पाएंगे? कोई भी यार नहीं, कोई ट्रोल नहीं, अगर आप एक जिंदा सिनेमा लवर हो तो फ्रैंकली दो बातें जरूर लिखकर बताओ, जो आपको ये ट्रेलर देखकर सबसे पहले दिमाग में आईं। टीज़र के बाद ट्रेलर में क्या सुधर गया और आगे क्या सुधारा जा सकता है? दिल खोलके कमेंट करके जरूर बताना। मेरी मानो तो इंडियन सिनेमा का नया जन्म हो चुका है दोस्त। बोलो जय श्री राम। टेक केयर, बाय-बाय।

title: Ramayana Trailer Review | Yogi Bolta Hai
transcription: तो फाइनली वो दिन आ गया जिसका सब लोग वेट कर रहे थे। रामायण का, नाना, नमित मल्होत्राज़ रामायण का एक प्रॉपर ट्रेलर इज़ आउट नाउ ऑन सोशल मीडिया। वो भी ढेर सारे लीक्स के बाद। यार, आप ट्रेलर लॉन्च इवेंट एंड ट्रेलर को सोशल मीडिया पे अपलोड एक साथ करोगे तो ये लीक्स करना फिर उस लीक्स को हटाने के लिए एक एजेंसी को हायर करना ये सब नहीं होता। बट एनीवेज़, पैसा है तो करो ख़र्चा। राजामौली ने मस्त काम किया था भाई। इवेंट रखा और जिस टाइम पे इवेंट में ट्रेलर दिखाया था वाराणसी का, उसी टाइम पे सोशल मीडिया पे डाल दिया था। एनीवेज़, ट्रेलर आया है तो भाई बात करना तो बनता है। वेल, हेलो, मेरा नाम है योगी और हमारी मुलाकात बार-बार होगी। सबसे पहले अब मैं यहाँ खुल के कह सकता हूँ कि रावण का जो लुक अभी आपने ट्रेलर में देखा या लॉर्ड परशुराम का जो ग्लिम्प्स आपने अभी ट्रेलर में देखा या इवन कुंभकरण, वो हमने क्रिएटर इवेंट में मुंबई में देखा था नमित मल्होत्रा जी के घर। आई मीन इसके अलावा भी बहुत कुछ देखा था, ऐरावत वाली लड़ाई और कुछ एक कैरेक्टर्स। तो वही कुछ एक सेम कैरेक्टर्स इसमें भी दिखाए गए हैं एंड आई मस्ट से कि इस 4 मिनट के ट्रेलर में रावण के कैरेक्टर में यश बस कमाल ही करते नज़र आ रहे हैं। सी, आई एम नॉट ग्लोरिफाइंग रावण, बट आई एम टॉकिंग अबाउट यश की परफॉर्मेंस। एंड पूरा ट्रेलर देखने के बाद आई कैन प्राउडली से कि जितनी भी कास्टिंग की गई है वो एकदम ऑन पॉइंट लग रही है। अब देखो कोई बोलेगा कि रावण का कैरेक्टर इतना मस्त एक्शन वगैरह करते हुए दिखाया है, अग्रेशन में दिखाया है और रणबीर एज़ श्री राम को एकदम ठंडा सा दिखा दिया। भाई, वी आर नाउ हैबिचुअल टू सी मेनस्ट्रीम एक्टर्स इन टॉक्सिक मेल पर्सनालिटी। कबीर सिंह में शाहिद का अग्रेशन देख लो आप, रणबीर कपूर को एनिमल में पसंद किया गया था क्योंकि वो अग्रेशन से भरा हुआ था, यश को केजीएफ में पसंद किया गया था क्योंकि अगेन अल्फा मेल मस्क्युलिनिटी, मार्को में उन्नी मुकुंदन को, द बॉयज़ में होमलैंडर को, सेम विद पुष्पा, सेम विद अदर ग्रे शेड्स एंड एंटी-हीरो टाइप कैरेक्टर्स क्योंकि वो अग्रेशन एंड मार-धाड़ एंड टॉक्सिसिटी से भरे हुए थे एंड आजकल लोगों को वही पसंद भी आता है भाई। यहाँ रणबीर राम हैं भाई, वो जैसे थे वैसा ही प्रेजेंट किया गया है शांत title: Ramayana Trailer Review | Yogi Bolta Hai
transcription: कुबेर द्वार को तोड़ देना फिर कुबेर की नगरी में आने के बाद वो जटाएं यार वो एंड दैट फाइट सीक्वेंस इस ऑन अनदर लेवल भाई। अपेरेंटली रावण अपने भाई कुबेर के राज्य को ही लंका में कन्वर्ट करता है उस पर विजय पाकर तो जहां वो वाइट एंड ब्लूइश एंड गोल्डन बिल्डिंग स्ट्रक्चर आपको दिख रहा है वो लंका ही है। उसके बाद वो महल के बालकनी में आकर सबको अपने किंग होने की घोषणा कर रहा है। दिस इज व्हाट वी कॉल्ड प्रेजेंटेशन। जो बर्फ में या हिमालयन पहाड़ियों में जो लड़ाई दिखाई गई है वो इंद्र के राज्य को लेकर उनसे सिंहासन छीनने वाली लड़ाई होगी। जहां इंद्र को तो नहीं दिखाया गया लेकिन वो ऐरावत वाला सीन भी बहुत ब्यूटीफुली डिजाइन किया गया है। वन मोर थिंग आई नोटिस कि इन्होंने जो राक्षस क्रिएचर्स हैं उनका कलर थोड़ा ह्यूमन्ली रखा है। पिछले टीज़र में जैसा था वैसा नहीं है एंड इवन ट्रेलर के क्रिएचर्स में देखोगे तो वो माथे पे वाइट एंड लाल टीका वगैरा दिया गया है तो चेंजेस तो किए गए हैं लोगों की बातों को ध्यान में रखते हुए। इवन कुछ एक सीन्स तो आई रियली लव्ड जैसे दैट मिथिला में श्रीराम का धनुष बाण उठाने वाला वो सीन। शूर्पणखा के एंट्री एक रथ पे हो रही है जिसमें वाइट लायन जैसे कुछ क्रिएचर्स है। आई मीन इसमें काफी अच्छे से एक मीनिंगफुल क्रिएटिव लिबर्टी ली गई है। एंड अगेन आई कैन से रकुल प्रीत सिंह एज़ शूर्पणखा डैम्न गुड कास्टिंग। एक और सीन बहुत ही ज्यादा खूबसूरत लगा मुझे, जटायु और रावण का युद्ध भाई ये सीन जिस तरह से ट्रेलर में दिख रहा है ना आई कैन ऑनेस्टली इमेजिन। यस, ऑनेस्टली इमेजिन कि ये सीन इस फिल्म का वन ऑफ द बेस्ट विजुअल सीन होगा। विवेक ओबेरॉय का विद्युतज्वा कैरेक्टर एंड रावण का एक फाइट सीक्वेंस भी हम देखते हैं ट्रेलर में। विद्युतज्वा एक्चुअली शूर्पणखा का पति होता है। और भी कई सारे कैरेक्टर्स हैं इसमें जो रिवील होते हैं एंड कास्टिंग किस-किस की है उसके ऊपर मैं ऑलरेडी एक डिटेल वीडियो बना चुका हूं तो वो चेक आउट जरूर कर लेना। इस ट्रेलर में कैकसी यानी रावण की मदर, रावण का भाई कुंभकरण को भी दिखाया गया है। मंथरा है, राजा दशरथ है, मारीच है। इवन भाई, लास्ट सीन में रावण का हायना जैसा दिखने वाला पालतू जानवर भी दिखाया गया है जिसका नाम क्रोधा रहता है जिसको इनके कॉमिक बुक्स में भी दिखाया गया है एंड दैट सीन एंड दैट रेज एक्सप्रेशन बाय यश इज एब्सोल्युटली कमेंडेबल। वैसे इतना सब दिखाने के बाद भी एग्जैक्ट रिलीज डेट अभी भी रिवील नहीं की गई है यानी दिवाली में तो आएगी पिक्चर लेकिन कौन से दिन वो नहीं पता फिलहाल। तो भाई, डेट जो भी हो, द वर्ल्ड इज नॉट रेडी फॉर दिस। अच्छा मेकर्स, अगर आप ये मेरा वीडियो देख रहे हैं तो वो जो एक शॉट है जहां रावण दौड़ते हुए कुबेर के सैनिकों की ओर भाग रहा है वो विजुअली थोड़ा पता नहीं क्यों बट ऑकवर्ड सा लग रहा है। इफ यू कैन फिक्स इट, प्लीज फिक्स इट। बाकी मेरे सब्सक्राइबर्स और व्यूअर्स से विनती है कि अगर आपकी भी कोई राय है तो कमेंट में जरूर बता देना। मिलते हैं अगले वीडियो में। बाय।

title: Moondru Mudichu - Best Scenes 1 | 25 July  2026 | Tamil Serial | Sun TV
transcription: ஃபுல் மூன் சேல் காலை 9 மணியிலிருந்து இரவு 12 மணி வரை. ஜூலை 29 ஒரு நாள் மட்டும். ஏங்க கடைக்கா? கையில் பேக்கெல்லாம் பலமா இருக்கு. உனக்கு என்ன வேணும் இப்போ? நாங்க எங்க போய்ட்டு வந்தா உனக்கு என்ன? பின்னாடியே மோப்பம் பிடிச்சிட்டு வரதுக்கு பேரு மனுஷன் இல்ல. அதுக்கு வேற பேரு. என்னன்னு சொல்லவா? அதுவும் சரிதான். ஏன்னா நல்ல பெரிய இடமா எல்லாம் புடிச்சு முந்தானையில் முடிஞ்சு வச்சிருக்க. என் பங்காளி வீட்டுலதான் காசு, பணம், சொத்துன்னு எல்லாம் கொட்டிக் கெடக்க. அப்ப இதுவும் பேசுவ, இன்னமும் பேசுவ நீ. பேச மட்டும் செய்ய மாட்டேன். நீ ஓவரா பேசினா செயல்லயும் காட்டுவேன். அசிங்கப்படுறதுக்கு முன்னாடி வழியை விட்டுட்டு போயிரு. ஏம்மா ரோட்ல பார்த்து ஒரு நலம் விசாரிக்கிறது எல்லாம் ஒரு குத்தமா? நீ வேணும்னா அங்க நிக்கிற நாலு பேரை கூப்பிட்டு கேட்டு பாரு. இப்போ உனக்கு என்ன வேணும்? ஏய் உன்கிட்ட எனக்கு என்னடி வேணும்? என் நெஞ்சு அப்படியே கொதிக்குதுடி. அதுக்கான பலி தீக்குறதுக்குதான்டி இங்க வந்திருக்கேன். மரியாதையா பேசு. ஏய் உனக்கெல்லாம் என்னடி மரியாதை? நீ பாட்டுக்கு போலீஸ்ல என்ன பிடிச்சு குடுத்துட்டு மெட்ராஸ்க்கு ஓடி போய்ட்ட. உன்னை விட்ருவேன்னு நினைச்சியாடி நீனு? விடமாட்டேன்டி. ஏய் ஜெயில்ல இருந்து வந்ததுல இருந்து உன்னை தீர்த்துக்கட்டதான்டி வெயிட் பண்ணிக்கிட்டு இருக்கேன். இப்ப கூட நான் உன் கண் முன்னாடிதானே நிக்கிறேன்? உன்னால என்னடா பண்ண முடியும்? என்னது டா போட்டு பேசுறியாடி நீனு? ஏய் திமிருதான்டி உனக்கு. ஏய் நீ ஒன்னும் மெட்ராஸ்ல என் பங்காளி வீட்டுல ஒன்னும் பாதுகாப்பா இல்லடி. இப்ப என் கிராமத்துல என் முன்னாடி நின்னுகிட்டு இருக்க. அதை மறந்துட்டு பேசுறடி நீ. என்ன? If you look at the history of espionage in the United States, Cuba is the only country that consistently has implanted and embedded spies in our system without even paying them. So, this is the hard work of foreign policy and it requires every administration to sort of balance these these two competing tugs against us. Well, we hear a lot about tensions with China. title: HULK vs. SPIDERMAN Fight Scene | Spider-Man: Brand New Day (2026) Savage Hulk Return Breakdown!
transcription: God, please, look at me. No, girl. Only Hulk. Savage Hulk is back and the big green rage monster might have just exposed a massive flaw in Doctor Strange's spell. Yeah, bro. Spider-Man: Brand New Day didn't just give us Spidey fighting Professor Hulk. It brought back the proper, old-school Hulk. The uncontrollable version we haven't really seen in the MCU for years. And I've got to know: What's next for Hulk? Come on, you already know we've got you covered. Let's get into it. To understand why Hulk loses control again, we got to go back to Avengers: Endgame, where Bruce revealed that he'd finally combined his intelligence with Hulk's strength, putting the brains and the brawn together to create Professor Hulk. After years of Banner and Hulk fighting for control, they'd finally found some kind of balance, and it seemed like the days of Bruce randomly transforming into a giant rage monster were over. Then, during the Shang-Chi post-credits scene, Bruce appeared in his human form again while wearing a device around his wrist. She-Hulk later revealed that this was an inhibitor, designed to suppress his gamma radiation and keep Hulk locked away. That technology becomes massively important in Brand New Day because Peter's superpowers have started changing. So he tracks Bruce down at his university looking for answers. Obviously, Bruce doesn't remember Peter thanks to Doctor Strange's spell, meaning Peter has to speak in code while asking how somebody might control powers that have suddenly become unpredictable. Bruce tells him about the inhibitor, and Peter then does what Peter Parker always does by casually building his own version of technology created by one of the smartest men on the planet. Peter creates an inhibitor designed to suppress his arachnid DNA and control the changes happening to his powers. He also builds a universal inhibitor that could theoretically suppress somebody else's powers, planning to use it against Jean Grey and stop her.

Bruce warns him that this kind of technology could be dangerous. MJ says how this is the kind of thing you put on a monster. title: PE Fund Journal Entry Bible | Private Equity Accounting Interview Guide
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Most candidates memorize PE journal entries and still fail the interview. Why? Because the interviewer is not testing debit and credit only. They are testing cash, NAV, investor capital and LP reporting. Take one private equity fund case: commitment $100 million, capital called $20 million, investment made $15 million, fund expense $1 million, management fee $2 million, fair value $18 million, exit $18 million, distribution to LPs $5 million. Here is the scoreboard. After every entry, ask: did cash move? Did NAV move? Capital activity or performance? What reaches LP reporting? First, capital call. The fund calls 20 million from LPs. Debit cash 20 million, credit investor capital 20 million. Cash increases, investor capital increases, but performance has not improved. This is capital activity, not income. Capital call brings cash, it does not create profit. Second, investment made. The fund invests 15 million into a portfolio company or SPV. Debit investment 15 million, credit cash 15 million. Cash goes down, investment asset goes up, but there is no immediate gain. Cash became investment, that is the trap. Investment made is not an expense and it does not automatically increase NAV. Third, fund expense. Assume 1 million of audit, legal or admin expense. Debit fund expense 1 million, credit expense payable or cash 1 million. This hits P&L, so NAV reduces. LP reporting shows fund level expense impact. The trap: fund expense is not capital activity. It reduces NAV because it hits P&L.

title: PE Fund Journal Entry Bible | Private Equity Accounting Interview Guide
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Credit cash 5 million. Cash leaves the fund. Investor capital reduces, but distribution does not automatically mean profit. It may be return of capital, realized gain, income, recallable distribution or a mix. That affects DPI, LP statements, capital accounts and callable capital. The trap: distribution is the cash event. Classification tells the performance story. Eighth, profit allocation. At period end, fund performance flows into investor capital accounts. Debit P&L or income summary, credit investor capital. This updates the capital account, and the capital account becomes the investor level story. A fund accountant does not stop at P&L. They explain how performance reaches each LP. Now the strategy layer. Different PE strategies add different support schedules. LBO may add SPV books, debt and interest. Fund of funds may add underlying fund investments. Private credit may add interest, PIK, non-accrual or impairment. Real estate may add rent and valuation marks. Distressed may add write downs. But the core logic stays the same. Cash, asset, P&L, NAV, capital account, LP reporting. Before answering any PE journal entry question, ask: Did cash move? Did NAV move? Did P&L move? Capital activity or performance? Realized or unrealized? Accrual or payment? What changed investor capital? What reaches LP reporting? A weak candidate memorizes journal entries. title: Journal Your Best Reality ✨ How to Manifest Your Dream Life Through Writing.
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Have you ever felt like you were just one step away from the life you actually want to live, but you just cannot seem to grab it? We have all been there. You have these big dreams and deep desires, but they feel like they are stuck in some alternate reality that you can only see from a distance. Well today, I want to share something with you that completely shifted everything for me. It is not magic and it is not just wishful thinking. It is the intentional practice of journaling to attract your best reality. I used to think journaling was just for recording what happened during my day like a diary, but once I realized it could be a tool for creation, my whole world changed. First, let us talk about why this actually works. When you put pen to paper, you are doing more than just writing words. You are focusing your energy, and giving your subconscious mind a clear roadmap. Most of the time our brains are cluttered with thousands of random thoughts, but journaling forces you to slow down and get specific. It is like sending a clear signal to the universe saying, 'this is exactly what I am ready for.' Your brain has a filtering system called the reticular activating system, and when you write down your desires, you are essentially telling that system what to look for in the real world. The first thing I always do before I start writing is get into a state of gratitude. You cannot manifest from a place of lack because the energy of wanting something often carries the heavy feeling of not having it. So, I start by listing three things I am genuinely thankful for right now. It could be as simple as a good cup of coffee, a supportive friend, or even just the fact that I have a quiet moment to myself. This shifts your vibration from 'I need' to 'I appreciate' which is the perfect foundation for attracting more. Now, let us get into the most powerful part of my routine, which is called scripting. Scripting is basically writing about your future as if it is happening right now, in the present tense. Instead of saying, 'I want to have my dream job,' you would write, 'I am so incredibly happy and fulfilled in my new career.' You have to get detailed. What does your office smell like? How does it feel when you see your name on that door? Who are you celebrating with at dinner tonight? The key is to involve all your senses. When you write these details, your brain starts to believe it is a memory rather than a distant hope. This bridge between your current reality and your desired one is where

title: How Data Centers Actually Work
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Every email you send, every video you stream, and every file stored in the cloud exists somewhere physically. Behind the internet is a network of buildings filled with servers, electrical infrastructure, and cooling systems working continuously to keep data moving. These buildings are called data centers. In this video series, we are going to explain how data centers actually work from a mechanical and electrical perspective, focusing on the systems that keep servers powered, cooled, and operating without interruption. This first video provides the big picture overview. We will explain what a data center does, why these facilities consume so much energy, and why mechanical and electrical systems are the most critical part of the building. In the following videos, we will begin breaking down each system in greater detail. At its simplest level, a data center is a facility designed to store, process, and distribute digital information. Inside the building are rows of servers, which are specialized computers responsible for storing, computing, and network traffic. Unlike office computers that operate intermittently, servers operate continuously. They run 24 hours a day, every day of the year. This creates an important reality. Servers consume large amounts of electricity, and nearly all of that electrical energy eventually becomes heat. While most people think of data centers as IT facilities, from an engineering perspective, they are really energy conversion buildings. Electricity goes in, computing work is performed, and heat comes out. The entire facility exists to manage that process safely and reliably. Every data center, regardless of size, must solve three fundamental problems. The first is continuous power. Servers cannot simply shut down when power is lost. Even brief interruptions can cause data loss or service outages affecting thousands or even millions of users. As a result, power systems must remain available even when equipment fails or utility power is interrupted. The second problem is continuous cooling. Because servers generate heat constantly, cooling systems must also operate continuously. If cooling stops, temperatures can rise quickly, forcing equipment to reduce performance or shut down to protect itself. Cooling in a data center is not about comfort. It is about equipment survival. The third problem is continuous operation.

title: How Data Centers Actually Work
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: And those concepts will be covered in a later video in this series. Although data centers appear complex, most of the infrastructure falls into three major system groups. The first group is electrical systems. Electrical infrastructure brings power into the building and distributes it safely to server equipment. This includes utility connections, switchgear, backup power systems, and power distribution equipment. The goal is simple. Power must always be available. The second group is mechanical cooling systems. Mechanical systems remove the heat generated by servers. Depending on the facility, this may include chillers, cooling towers, pumps, air handling units, or specialized cooling equipment located directly at the server racks. The objective is to keep equipment operating within safe temperature ranges at all times. The third group is controls and monitoring systems. Controls tie electrical and mechanical systems together into one operating environment. These systems monitor temperatures, power usage, equipment status, and alarms, allowing the facility to automatically respond to changing conditions or equipment failures. In modern data centers, controls and monitoring are just as important as the physical equipment itself. Data centers are often misunderstood because they look similar to commercial buildings from the outside, but operationally, they are very different. In an office building, occupancy changes throughout the day, cooling loads rise and fall, and equipment cycles on and off. In a data center, electrical loads are constant, cooling demand is continuous, and systems rarely shut down. Failure tolerance is also very different. A comfort cooling failure in an office building creates discomfort. A cooling or power failure in a data center can create immediate operational risk. Because of this, data centers typically include redundant equipment, multiple power paths, and system designs that allow maintenance without shutting the facility down. Now that the big picture has been established, the next step is understanding how energy actually moves through a data center. In the next video, we will walk step-by-step through the electrical side of the facility, following power from the utility connection all the way to the server rack. After that, we will cover how heat is removed, how airflow is managed, and why redundancy drives nearly every design decision in modern data centers. Understanding this foundation makes the rest of the systems much easier to follow, and provides the context needed to understand why data centers are designed and constructed the way that they are. Check out our HVAC, electrical, and plumbing construction forms to help you run your business, and explore our online courses for in-depth training.

title: Apple’s Journal App Helped Me Organize My Entire Life
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Most of us have thoughts we don't want to keep floating around in our heads all day. Ideas, reminders, things we need to do tomorrow, things we're worried about, things we don't want to forget. For a long time, I tried keeping all that in paper journals. I actually loved them, I probably bought way too many of them over the years. But eventually, I ran into one problem: I didn't always have them with me when I needed them. And that's when something interesting started happening. Over the past few months, Apple's Journal app has quietly turned into something different for me. It's not just a journaling app anymore, it's basically become my digital notebook. The place where I organize my thoughts, capture ideas, and keep different parts of my life in one place. So, in this video, I want to show you how I set it up, how I organize my journals inside the app, and why it's slowly replacing paper notebooks for me. But I'm curious about something first. Has Apple's Journal app replaced your paper notebook yet? Or are there things still holding you back? Let me know in the comments. And if you enjoy calm tech videos about productivity and intentional living, hit that like button and subscribe. It really helps the channel. All right, let's get into it. I've always liked paper journals. There's something satisfying about finishing one and keeping it on a shelf. It feels like you actually own it. It's not locked away inside an app somewhere. And writing with a pen just feels natural. You can jot something down quickly, cross things out, draw arrows, sketch little ideas. Things that don't always feel as fluid when you're typing. In the past, I tried using digital journaling apps, but I usually ended up going back to paper. But paper journals eventually started becoming inconvenient for one simple reason: I didn't always have them with me. If I had an idea while I was out somewhere, on the train, traveling, or just away from home, I couldn't write it down unless the notebook happened to be nearby. Another issue was organization. At one point, I tried using a bullet journal system with calendars, indexes, and sections, but maintaining all that just started to feel like a chore. Searching for something I wrote weeks earlier could be frustrating unless everything was perfectly indexed, which I usually didn't keep up with. With the Journal app, that problem basically disappears. Everything is automatically dated, everything is searchable. And most importantly, it's always with me. I always have my phone nearby, and most of the time, my iPad is within reach, too. And once Apple brought the Journal app to the iPad with Apple Pencil support, it started giving me many of the same benefits that the paper journals had. I can still jot things down by hand, sketch quick ideas, or cross things out. But now, it lives everywhere I go. Over time, I started organizing the app into different journals. Right now, I have five journals, but three of them are the ones I use the most. I have separate places for different parts of my life, so I know where things belong. The first one is called Personal Log. This works like a traditional journal. I write about my life, things that are on my mind, things that make me happy, things that bothered me,

transcription: or just general reflections about the day. This is the journal where I usually use the Apple Pencil on the iPad because it feels like the closest thing to writing in a physical notebook. The second one is called daily work log. This is where I keep quick notes related to work, things I need to remember, ideas for projects, notes from meetings, or small bites of information like names or phone numbers. It's not extremely structured, but that's okay. Everything inside the journal is work related, so it's easy to find. Then I have a journal for YouTube ideas. Whenever an idea for a video pops into my head, whether it's a topic, a headline, or just something I use to experiment with on the channel, I drop it into the journal so I don't lose the idea. Organizing things this way just makes sense to my brain. If I have a work thought, it goes into the work journal. If it's personal, it goes into the personal log. If it's a YouTube idea, it goes into that journal. It keeps everything simple and easy to find. There are a few things that make this system work really well. The biggest one for me is iCloud syncing. I can write something quickly on my phone and later continue it on my iPad without even thinking about it. It just appears there automatically. I also like that you can create multiple journals inside one app. With paper notebooks, I'd either have to carry several of them or divide one notebook into sections, which usually got messy. Another big advantage is search. If I want to find something I wrote weeks ago, I can just type it and it pops up instantly. The app is also extremely simple. It's free, it syncs across devices, and you can lock it with Face ID or Touch ID, so everything stays private. As far as routine goes, I usually write in the personal log in the morning with the Apple Pencil. Sometimes I'll write down what I dreamed about, how I'm feeling that day, or what I have on my plate. At night, I'll sometimes open the work log and dump out everything I was working on that day so I'm not thinking about it for the rest of the evening. And throughout the day, if an idea pops into my head, I just capture it. There are still a few things I'd like Apple to improve, though. One feature I'd love to see is templates. Things like lined pages, dotted pages, or bullet journal layouts would make it feel even closer to a real notebook. It would also be interesting if journals visually looked more like actual notebooks that you could customize or decorate. The Apple Pencil support has improved, but it still isn't perfect. For example, switching to the Apple Pencil eraser doesn't always work consistently for me, and sometimes there's still a delay while writing. We're only a few months away from WWDC, though, so there's a good chance Apple could introduce updates to the app in the future. For me, Apple's Journal app isn't just a journaling app anymore. It's basically my digital notebook. It's where I organize ideas, capture thoughts, reflect on my day, and keep different parts of my life in one place. And because it's always with me, it actually gets used more than my paper journals ever did. But I'm curious what you think. Do you still prefer paper notebooks, or have you moved everything digital? Let me know in the comments, and if you enjoyed this video, don't forget to like and subscribe. Thanks for watching, and I'll see you in the next one.

transcription:
इसकी साइंस है, इसे ग्राउंडिंग कहते हैं। जब तुम नेचर के साथ फिजिकली कनेक्ट हो जाते हो, तो तुम्हारा नर्वस सिस्टम लिटरली काम हो जाता है। ट्री की बाक का टेक्सचर फील करो हाथों से, उसकी ठंडी या गर्म फीलिंग महसूस करो, उसकी एनर्जी सेंस करो। दो मिनट भी करो तो एंजाइटी का वो टाइट फीलिंग चेस्ट में ढीली पड़ जाती है। और प्रैक्टिकली बात करें तो जब तुम पेड़ के साथ खड़े हो, तुम प्रेजेंट मूवमेंट में आ जाते हो। पास्ट नहीं, फ्यूचर नहीं, बस अभी। बस यही तो चाहिए था मुझे।

तो क्या मैं 100% एंजाइटी फ्री हूं आज? नहीं यार, ऑनेस्टली नहीं। थॉट आते हैं, नर्वस होती हूं। बट फर्क ये है, अब मैं उनका प्रिज़नर नहीं हूं। अब मैं जानती हूं कि ये सिर्फ एक थॉट है, ये मेरी रियलिटी नहीं है। ये तीन चीजें, टैरो फॉर सेल्फ रिफ्लेक्शन, सिंगल पॉइंट मेडिटेशन और ट्री ग्राउंडिंग, ये मेरी डेली टूलकिट बन गई है। कोई बड़ा इन्वेस्टमेंट नहीं, कोई कॉम्प्लिकेटेड प्रोसेस नहीं, बस थोड़ी सी कमिटमेंट और थोड़ा सा प्रैक्टिस। अगर तुम भी इस जगह पे हो जहां मैं थी, प्लीज ट्राई करो। स्टार्ट छोटा करो, एक दिन 5 मिनट, बस इतना।

ये वीडियो आपको हेल्पफुल लगी हो, तो लाइक जरूर करना और उन्हें शेयर करना जिन्हें लगता है कि इन्हें ये चाहिए। कमेंट में बताओ आप एंजाइटी से कैसे डील करते हो? मैं जेन्युइनली पढ़ती हूं सारे कमेंट्स। अपना ख्याल रखना। मिलते हैं नेक्स्ट वीडियो में। बाय।

title: Moving Forward | My Anxiety Story (Part 7)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: What if understanding anxiety and panic attacks is not enough to beat it? For a long time, I believed that if I just learned enough about anxiety, if I became aware of its existence and its causes, it would eventually disappear. But knowledge alone didn't change much. The real change started only when I began taking action. Welcome back, or just welcome if this is your first time here. My name is Luka, and this is part seven of my anxiety story. In this video, I'll talk about the moment when I realized something important: it is not enough to simply learn a lot about our enemy, although that is certainly the first and essential step. To ultimately defeat it, or to overpower it to the point where there is no battle at all, we must create a solid plan and strategy, and then truly begin with active preparations. So, how do I stand on my own two feet again? How do I run freely without fear? All of us secretly hope that our problems will solve themselves, that someone will appear with a magic wand and make everything disappear. We just need to be patient, and it will happen. And yes, sometimes life really does work that way. Sometimes, someone unexpectedly helps you, sometimes a problem gets resolved by someone else. Sometimes, time slowly erases things. But the truth is, situations that get solved like that are actually very rare. When it comes to anxiety and panic attacks, you can be 100% sure of one thing: they will not disappear on their own. And if you do nothing, the situation will most likely only get worse. So, if we want to win the lottery, we first have to buy a ticket. That's when the first steps of self-help begin. And that's exactly what I did. My psychiatrist gave me advice and guidance on how to live with anxiety and panic attacks, how to slowly expose myself to the things that scared me, how to face those fears step by step. And I actually put many of those tips into practice. When my mind finally felt free enough to move forward, my real self-help journey began.

title: Moving Forward | My Anxiety Story (Part 7)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: The first step was reading books about anxiety and panic attacks. I intentionally keep those uh these two together because, in my case, they were like a perfect love couple. I wanted to understand my enemies better and find multiple ways to deal with them. At the same time, around that period, YouTube started filling up with all kinds of mental health gurus. Some of them had a really great advice. How to overcome a panic attacks, and various self-help methods for those kinds of situations. And honestly, I found many of their tips and ideas fascinating and useful. Some things and explanations were already familiar and logical to me, as I believe they are to most of you watching this. But you know how sometimes you keep some- something you already know in some forgotten corner of your brain, in the irrelevant section. Then, you get thrilled when someone else tells you that same thing or reveals it like some grand wisdom, and then you might actually accept it and start applying it, but as someone else's brilliant advice. That is actually the experience we get when learning from books or videos. And now, we arrive at the most important part of the whole process. Action. What happens if your progress is based only on reading and listening? We keep discovering new ideas, tips, and methods, we we get excited again and and again by brilliant insights from other people, but after a while, we start asking ourselves, if I have learned so much about anxiety and panic attacks, and all the tips on how to overcome them, why don't I feel better? The answer is very simple. If you don't apply the knowledge you have, it is completely useless. And that applies to any knowledge we acquire but don't use. But there is another important thing. Just like a specific medicine doesn't work the same for everyone, not every method for overcoming these unpleasant situations will have the same effect. Basically, we have to find what works for us.

There certainly is, and I will be talking about that as we go along in the upcoming videos. Now, let me give you another comparison about anxiety. Imagine you are a small, skinny kid, and on your way to school, or in the park, or even inside the school, there is a bully who keeps bothering you. Slowly, you start to hate going to school, you stop enjoying the park, you stop enjoying time with friends. Even walking to the local store becomes stressful. Things that should be normal parts of your life start turning into hell. So you begin avoiding those places, you take longer routes, you make excuses to calm your mind. That bully is anxiety, and panic attacks are the extra punches that come with it. So, what are your options? You can tell your parents, which is which is actually a good idea, but depending on how they react, sometimes that can even make that can even make things worse. Another option is to do nothing, keep taking the hits, waiting for school to end, waiting for that phase of life to pass. But if we do nothing, we can't expect expect any improvement. Your confidence will drop even lower, and every future encounter with that bully, or even the thought of meeting him, will create even more fear. What will your life look like? Will that affect your confidence? Of course it will. Now, are those really all the options for overcoming these kinds of challenges? Probably not. There are many variations, but there is one specific path that I prefer over, over, over all others, and for challenges like this, I believe is the best one, at least for me. The path is actually a, a, a process of gradually building yourself up, a real process of physical and mental strengthening, a process that also builds your confidence over time, a process that builds a solid foundation for any future growth. And the ultimate goal is to become physically and mentally stronger until the day comes when that bully just walks right by you and doesn't even notice you anymore, or at least doesn't see you as a target anymore, or maybe he just nods and says hello. He's still around, you still see him sometimes, but you feel nothing. Maybe the only thought that comes to your mind is, "Wow, I used to be afraid of that guy." Let's repeat this one more time. The bully is anxiety, those anxious thoughts and worries that disturb your life, and the punches he throws are panic attacks. In this story, the role of parents is played by professionals: psychiatrists, psychologists, and also by close friends and people who truly care about you. title: Exercise Burnout & Anxiety: My Recovery Story
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: What if your healthy exercise routine is secretly fueling burnout? Mine did, wrecking my nervous system, spiking anxiety, and turning sleep into a nightmare. I literally ran into my doom. A few tweaks to my routine, however, kept my cardio fitness soaring while calming my nervous system and restoring sleep. The changes I will share are backed by 40 years of scientific research proven to help runners and cyclists of all ages, and they're easy. Stick around, I'll reveal the symptoms I ignored and how I fixed them to reclaim my energy using the CAT, hockey stick, ego approach. Hello, all. I am Daniel, father of two, corporate and weekend warrior, and had a severe burnout last year. First, let's talk about the sneaky symptoms, all equally important, which indicated that I was on the verge of nervous system collapse, and I completely ignored because I thought I was invincible. Number one, changes in level of tiredness. Legs like lead, stiff even after rest. You start to also have post-run highs, crashing in the afternoons with headaches, or even directly after the run, not experiencing the euphoria you normally feel. This is hard to identify because you think, "This is just normal tiredness." Be alert of increases in duration and frequency. Any increase is a red flag. Number two, skyrocketing heart rate. My runs pushed me to max zones way too often. What was moderate became intense. Your body is basically screaming, "Slow down." Number three, sleep quality goes down. Exercise should help sleep, right? Nope, mine tanked. And this is essentially because too much exercise stimulates hormones to be elevated at the wrong times, leading to anxiety and body still on edge at night. For example, cortisol levels are elevated throughout the day and night. Number four, moody without workouts. Skip a run, felt off, guilty, irritable. Turns out it's hormone havoc from overdoing it, not just missing the endorphins.

title: Exercise Burnout & Anxiety: My Recovery Story
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I will deep dive into my sleep routine in a future video, but here's the quick blueprint. Winding mentally down at work around 5:00 to 6:00 p.m. No heavy or triggering workloads. At home, fuel up with a solid evening meal. No skipping. Do meditation or do other mindfulness exercises and boost with supplements like magnesium bisglycinate or phosphatidylserine for that Zen shutdown. Number two, reverse hockey stick. Manage your cortisol levels. Don't eliminate cortisol. Restore its natural rhythm. Upside down hockey stick. Peak high in the morning, then taper gradually to low by bedtime. Maximize the AM surge with hydration, sunlight exposure around 10 to 15 minutes, and light exercise after waking. Also take your coffee in the morning if you are a coffee drinker. During the day, monitor stress and ease off heavy tasks by 4:00 to 5:00 p.m. Try chamomile tea or a short break. At home, fully unplug. No emails or emotional triggers to ensure a smooth wind down. Number three, ego be gone approach. Dial down workout intensity. I quit cold turkey for a month during peak burnout. Nearly fainted on a walk. Post-recovery, easy walks, then moderate runs. Your smartwatch tracks it. Drop to 4 days a week using Phil Maffetone's MAF method. Build sustainable stamina without the crash. Gym? Lighter weights, no heavy squats. But here's the twist. These fixes run deeper than you think with hidden pitfalls and game-changing easy tweaks I discovered the hard way. Want that surge of energy, razor-sharp clarity, and unbreakable strength back? You'll need the full story, including the one mistake that almost derailed my recovery forever. See you in the next video. I am on a mission to create a community to support each other through sharing experiences and mental health hacks. Please hit the like button, subscribe, and comment so that others can find this content. Thanks for watching.

अटैक आया। और उसके बाद जो है, एक अजीब सी घबराहट होने लगी, अजीब सा टेंशन लगने लगा। लेकिन, वो एक दिन था, लेकिन उसके बाद ये मुझे कई बार और हुआ। तब तक मैं श्योर नहीं था कि मुझे एंग्जायटी ही है, पैनिक अटैक ही हैं या हार्ट से रिलेटेड कोई समस्या है। अब ये पैनिक अटैक ना इतनी डरावनी होती है कि ऐसा आपको लग रहा होता है कि शायद ये हार्ट अटैक है। क्योंकि इसके सिम्टम्स और हार्ट अटैक के सिम्टम्स बहुत हद तक एक जैसे ही होते हैं। तो अचानक मुझे ऐसा लगने लगा कि शायद ये हार्ट अटैक है। मैं उस दिन तो किसी तरीके से डॉक्टर के पास गया और उन्होंने मुझे मेडिसिन दी और मैं उस दिन कुछ नहीं हुआ नॉर्मल हो गया। लेकिन फिर सेम यही चीजें नेक्स्ट वीक या फिर उससे 15 दिन बाद मेरे साथ हुआ। उस दिन मुझे ये काफी लंबे समय तक रहा, मतलब मैंने मेडिसिन ले ली उसके बाद भी ये मेरे साथ चलता रहा। रात का ही टाइम था, सेम वही टाइम के आसपास। और फिर मुझे एहसास हुआ कि ये डेफिनेटली कुछ ना कुछ समस्या है। एक तरफ माइंड कह रहा था हार्ट से रिलेटेड कोई इशूज हैं, एक तरफ माइंड कह रहा था नहीं हार्ट का रिलेटेड इशूज नहीं हो सकता शायद कुछ ऐसी कोई चीज होगी, गैस बन रहा होगा कुछ और होगा। लेकिन उसके बाद जो कुछ हुआ ना, वो शायद मैं आपको क्लीयरली ऐसे बोलूँगा ना तो आप शायद समझ नहीं पाएंगे। अगर आप एंग्जायटी में हैं या आपको पैनिक अटैक आते हैं, तो आप उसको फील कर सकते हैं, आप समझ सकते हैं कि हाँ क्या हो रहा होगा। क्योंकि आपके हाथ पैरों पर पसीना आने लगता है, आपको घबराहट होने लगती है, ऐसा लगता है जैसे कि बस आपके पास कुछ आखिरी पल बचे हुए हैं और आपके साथ आज ही कुछ ना कुछ हो जाएगा और शायद आपका आखिरी दिन है, अजीब अजीब तरीके के थॉट्स चलते हैं और आपका माइंड ना बहुत ही अजीब सा हो जाता है। तो दिमाग में ना एक बात आया कि अगर मान लो, आखिरी दिन हुआ तो आपको ऐसा लगेगा कि यार पता नहीं पूरी जिंदगी बची है, अभी ये जी क्या है और इस एज में आप चले जाओगे। तो आपको अपने आसपास लोगों का ख्याल आने लगेगा, फैमिलीज का ख्याल, अगर आप पर कोई डिपेंडेंट है तो उसका ख्याल, आपकी रिस्पांसिबिलिटी, हर चीज के बारे में आपको अजीब-अजीब ख्याल आने लगते हैं।

मुझे क्या दिक्कत है? पता चल जाए मुझे बस। तो हॉस्पिटल पहुँचा। हॉस्पिटल पहुँचा, तो उन्होंने ईसीजी किया और उसके बाद जो है शायद बीपी वगैरह भी चेक किया था उन्होंने। और फिर वो आप डॉक्टर आपस में बात करने लगे। उन्होंने मुझे एक फिर दवाई दी और उनमें से किसी ने आके बोला, उन्होंने मतलब उनके अब बोलने का अंदाज ये था कि कुछ नहीं, पैनिक अटैक है। उस पल एक एक चीज़ समझ में नहीं आती है जब वो डॉक्टर आपको ये कहता है ना कि कि पैनिक अटैक है, तो आपको ऐसा लग रहा होता कि यार ऐसे कैसे हो सकता है? बॉडी आपकी ये सारे सिम्पटम्स दे रही है जो हार्ट अटैक से रिलेटेड है और मशीनें आपकी कह रही होती हैं कि यार आप फिट हो। आपको लग रहा होता है कि डॉक्टर शायद गलत हैं। लेकिन यहाँ से ना आपको समझना पड़ेगा कि एंजाइटी की समझ आपको डेवलप करनी पड़ती है। क्योंकि ये फेज सिर्फ एक बार नहीं आएगा अगर आपने छोड़ दिया इसको तो। ये बार-बार आता है और ये आता ही रहता है अगर आपने इसको सही मायनों में नहीं ट्रीट किया या छोड़ दिया। क्योंकि मैं ये करके देख चूका हूँ भाई। इसलिए बोल रहा हूँ। एक्सपीरियंस है और उस एक्सपीरियंस के बेसिस पे आपके साथ बता रहा हूँ, तो प्लीज अगर आपके साथ ऐसा होता है तो इसको हल्के में मत लीजिए। अपनी लाइफ के बहुत ही प्रेशियस टाइम, बहुत ही कीमती समय आप यूँ ही बर्बाद कर रहे हैं। तो देखिए, सबसे पहली चीज़ क्या है ना कि आपको ये समझना पड़ेगा कि एक्चुअली में जो मेंटल हेल्थ है वो बहुत जरूरी है। अगर आपके साथ ऐसा हो रहा है तो जान लीजिए कि आप पागल नहीं हैं और ना ही ऐसा है कि कोई ये जानलेवा बीमारी है। बस जरूरत ये है कि आप एक मुश्किल दौर से गुजर रहे हैं और आपको उसे पहचानना है। तो अगर आप इस दौर से गुजर रहे हैं ना, तो तुरंत आपको मदद लेना चाहिए। किसी प्रोफेशनल काउंसलर काउंसलर से आपको बात करना चाहिए।

transcription: Hi. Today I want to tell you about the day I realized something was very wrong. For months, my daughter had been waiting to go to a big Disney show in Rome, and she was so excited. Really counting down the hours and the days. But when the moment came, as we were getting ready to leave, my body just stopped. I started to feel like I was going to faint, I was sweating, I felt sick to my stomach, and honestly, I thought I had a virus because I didn't even know what a panic attack was yet. I just knew that I didn't have the energy to drive for an hour, find parking, find dinner, deal with the crowds, deal with the loud music, and then drive us both back home. So, eventually my dad ended up taking her to the show so she wouldn't miss it, thank God. But I still remember sitting at home and feeling so much guilt. I felt like a failure because I couldn't be there for her. I felt sad that my dad had to do it on my behalf when he had work the next morning. And if you have ever felt that mom guilt because your anxiety is stopping you from being the parent you want to be, please listen to me. You're not a bad mother. You're just a person whose nervous system is overwhelmed and there is a way back. When I was at my lowest point as a single mother, I had to find ways to heal that were simple, fast, and free because I couldn't afford to pay for therapy. And these are the five things that saved me at the very beginning. First of all, I stopped fighting the panic. I learned that when a panic attack starts, if I fight it, if I resist it, it just stays longer. So I started saying to my body, "Okay, I feel you. You can go through." And I just imagined this kind of wave of electricity going through me. And when I stopped resisting, the attacks started coming less often. Second, Bach Flower Rescue Remedy. This was my safety net. I kept it in my bag everywhere I went. At grocery store, train, social situations. And it helped me feel like I had an escape because the moment I could feel a panic attack arising, I knew I could rely on the remedy to stop it then and there. Third, I had to remove the triggers. So I had to stop putting things in my body that made my heart race

transcription: I had to cut out caffeine, I know, don't hate me, but coffee just makes things worse. Cigarettes, again, don't hate me, but trust me, it makes things worse even if you think it it helps. Alcohol, Diet Coke, anything that could again trigger my nervous system. I was using them to survive the exhaustion, and probably like me, you might be thinking that cigarettes were a huge help, but they weren't, they were just making anxiety much worse and removing them helped from the very beginning. EFT tapping, this is a very simple technique where you tap on specific points on your body to calm your brain, and it's based on the meridian points, a little bit like acupuncture. I can do this anywhere, even in a bathroom stall to feel safe again, and even my clients afterwards have used EFT to prevent panic attacks. I will be sharing a mini online course in the next few days, so feel free to subscribe if you want to stay on top of everything I will share. And I also had to learn to say no. I had to learn to say no to things that were draining my energy. Social dinners, extra work, staying up late, everything that was not in line with what I needed at the time. I realized that my rest was not a luxury, it was a requirement for my recovery, and years later when I discovered Human Design, I finally understood why my energy works this way. transcription: If you're watching this right now, I already know something about you. You didn't just stumble across this video. You searched for it. Yeah, I know that feeling because I lived it. And honestly, at my worst, I was probably in a darker place than you are right now. So, if you can give me a few minutes, I want to tell you my story. Not the cleaned up version, the real one, because I think it might be exactly what you need to hear today. Back in 2019, life was actually pretty solid for me. I was that sports guy, always outside, playing every single day, super active, full of energy. Sure, there was normal stress like anyone else, but nothing that felt overwhelming. I thought I was living the good life. Then, February 18th, 2019 hit, and everything just flipped. That morning, I woke up and my whole body felt hot, like I had a fever, but when I checked my temperature three different times, it was completely normal. My energy just crashed out of nowhere. I told myself, "It's probably just tiredness, it'll pass by tomorrow." So, I still dragged myself to the ground and played for a couple of hours trying to act normal. But deep down, something felt seriously off. It was like my body was warning me that something bad was coming. That same night, my brother's friend was throwing a party just a mile away. I wasn't feeling it at all, but my older brother convinced me to come along. "We'll eat quick and head straight back home." The second we walked in, everything started looking blurry and weird, like I was in a dream. I turned to my brother and said, "Man, something is really not right. I'm getting super anxious." He told me to just sit down, eat with everyone, and we'd leave soon. But I could barely hold myself together. 10 minutes later, my heart exploded. It started pounding so hard I could feel

transcription: feel every single beat in my throat, in my ears, everywhere. Sweat was pouring down my face, my back, my whole body. I genuinely thought, 'This is it. I'm dying right here in front of everyone.' Everyone else was laughing and chatting like nothing was happening, but I couldn't take it anymore. I jumped up and ran the entire mile home on foot, heart still racing the whole way. When I burst through the door, my mom took one look at my face and panicked. We rushed straight to our family doctor. My heart rate was 155, blood pressure was through the roof. He asked if I was stressed. I said, 'Yeah, a little.' He gave me acid reflux medicine and some multivitamins, told me not to worry, and sent me home. But that night, that was my first real panic attack. I didn't sleep even for 1 minute. The next morning, I just broke down crying in front of my mom, begging her, 'Please take me to another doctor or I'm going to die.' She started crying, too. The very next day we went to a different doctor. All the blood tests came back completely normal. He gave me a sleeping pill for a month and said, 'Just reduce your stress.' When I looked up that pill online, I saw it was actually prescribed for anxiety and depression. That's when it clicked. This whole thing was anxiety. Suddenly, it all made sense, because I had over 85 plus different symptoms hitting me at the exact same time. I was terrified every single minute that I was about to have a heart attack. The dizziness was constant, like I was standing on a rocking boat even when I was sitting still. My legs felt so weak I was scared they'd give out any second. My heartbeat was pounding so loud in my ears, I couldn't hear anything else. I was losing weight rapidly, my blood pressure stayed high, I had this burning pain in my stomach, my chest and left arm hurt constantly, muscles were tight everywhere, I couldn't sleep at all, and whenever I did pass out, I'd have these terrifying nightmares that felt so real. The worst part, I became scared to even step outside the house, because going out would trigger massive panic attacks that left me shaking. I started googling every single symptom like a maniac.

transcription: Every weird feeling, every pain, I type it in and convince myself I had some deadly disease the doctors were missing. I changed more than 35 different doctors in six months, got my blood work done 15 times, MRIs, CT scans, everything you can imagine. All normal. But I still didn't believe it. I went to three different psychiatrists. They put me on antidepressants and sleeping pills. The sleep got a little better for a while, but nothing else changed, and those antidepressants completely killed my libido, so I stopped taking them. Then the sleep disappeared again. Plus, I had read so many horror stories online of people stuck on those meds for 8, 10, even 15 years and still suffering. I told myself, "I don't want that life. There has to be another way." That's when I decided to stop fighting the anxiety and actually try to understand it. I finally accepted, after more than a month of struggling, that this really was anxiety, not some hidden, deadly illness. The moment I accepted it, that constant background worry started dropping. I stopped Googling every little symptom like my life depended on it. I even wrote down all 80 to 85 of my symptoms in a notebook and started understanding each one properly instead of panicking. I got really lucky because my aunt is a neurosurgeon. She was pregnant at the time and came home for three months of maternity leave. She sat with me every day and explained every single symptom in real medical terms: why my heart raced, why I felt dizzy, why the chest pain happened, everything. That conversation was the total game-changer for me. After that, I took full control. I completely changed my diet, started using natural herbs like ashwagandha and brahmi that actually helped calm my nervous system, did yoga and breathing exercises every single day, and tried different meditation techniques until I found what worked for me. Slowly, my sleep started coming back.

I actually sat down and created six different 30-day lifestyle and diet plans, each one custom-made for exactly what I was dealing with at that moment. For six straight months I followed them religiously, no excuses, no skipping days. And slowly, week by week, everything kept getting better. The symptoms started fading one by one. Some days were still tough, but the bad days became fewer and fewer. Then one day in January 2021, it just hit me. I realized I hadn't felt a single symptom in weeks. No racing heart, no dizziness, no fear, nothing. I was completely out of it. It didn't happen overnight, but after all those months of steady work, I had finally made it through. It's been over four years now, and I'm living a totally normal life, actually better than before, with zero meds and zero dependency on anything. When I look back today, I feel so damn proud because I beat something that keeps most people trapped for 10 or 20 years. On this channel, I'm going to break down every single symptom, one by one, in future videos, exactly how I fixed each of them, step-by-step. I'll also share some really powerful tips and tricks that honestly took me years to figure out and you won't easily find anywhere else on YouTube. So, if you're watching this right now and you're struggling, I want you to hear me loud and clear. No matter how bad your anxiety feels today, if I could beat it, you can beat it too. If this story gave you even a little bit of hope, do me a favor, smash that like button, subscribe, and turn on notifications because I'm dropping new videos every single week. title: Bipolar Disorder, Depression, Anxiety and Faith: Stories of Recovery | Fresh Hope
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Me dijo que tenía la mente enferma y que eso no significaba que mi fe era débil. Yo vivo con trastorno bipolar tipo uno. Nadie me dijo sobre el trastorno bipolar. Hay días buenos y hay días muy difíciles, y ambos son parte del proceso. De hecho, por medio de la ansiedad Dios usa esta situación para poder transformar nuestro corazón. Yo pude conocer Fresh Hope. Es un ministerio que me enseñó y me recordó de que no estoy sola, de que se puede salir de esta situación y de que hay esperanza. Yo no soy ansiedad generalizada, tú no eres depresión, tú no eres tu diagnóstico, tú eres una hija, un hijo de Dios. Fresh Hope me enseñó que no estoy dañada ni soy mala cristiana por necesitar ayuda. Aprendí que Dios también obra a través del tratamiento, el acompañamiento y el descanso. Mi diagnóstico no me define. Elijo la esperanza. Y en Fresh Hope encontré un grupo de apoyo, hermanas que oran por mí, muchas herramientas, lo cual me ha ayudado a salir adelante. Y en Fresh Hope pude aprender a vivir siempre con esperanza a pesar de los desafíos y las luchas. Fresh Hope me enseñó a vivir y a sentir que no estoy solo, que mi diagnóstico no me define como persona, que puedo vivir con propósito aun en medio del proceso. He aprendido a hablar, he aprendido a pedir apoyo, a tomar mi tratamiento sin vergüenza y a confiar en que Dios no me ha soltado nunca de su mano. Hoy sé que la recuperación es lenta pero no es lineal. Es posible y cada pequeño avance cuenta. Vivo con depresión, vivo con ansiedad generalizada, pero la depresión y la ansiedad no viven en mi vida. Si yo pudiera decirle algo a un familiar que tiene un ser querido que vive con un diagnóstico... que no está solo, hay esperanza. La recuperación es posible, y no tiene por qué caminar solo. Si pudiera decirle algo a alguien recién diagnosticado, le diría estas tres cosas. Uno, hay esperanza. Dos, la recuperación es posible. Tres, no tienes que caminar esto solo.

मतलब वो सेम डे जब मैंने बात बताई, उसने पूरा दिन ड्यूटी भी नहीं करी। वो इमीडिएट भाग गया लंच से पहले ही और डॉक्टर के पास जाकर बताया, "सर, मैंने ये ये रिपोर्ट कराई। डॉक्टर ने कहा हाँ, हाँ ये तो आप कह रहे हो काफ़ी लो है आपका।" तो उसने मेरी बात मानी और उसने विटामिन डी के शॉट्स लेने, इंजेक्शन लिए थे। शॉट्स लिए, बी 12 के इंजेक्शन वगैरह लिए, तो उनका मेरे ख्याल से ड्रिप भी चढ़ी थी आयरन के लिए। आप मानोगे नहीं 15 दिन में कह रहा है, "सर, मेरे को सब कुछ बढ़िया लग रहा है। कोई दिक्कत नहीं हो रही।" तो मैंने बोला देखो कई बार क्या होता है ना अगर आपको एंग्जायटी नहीं भी है ना और बी 12, डी3 की डेफिशिएंसी की वजह से अगर आपको प्रॉब्लम आती है, तो ये थोड़ा ठीक होने के बाद भी ना हल्की-फुल्की एंग्जायटी रह जाती है या फिर रहती ही है, कोई चेंज नहीं आता। बट उनके में चेंज आ गया था क्योंकि वो डेफिशिएंट थे और डेफिशिएंसी की वजह से उनको इतने सारे सिम्टम हो रहे थे और वो खुद से दिमाग़ लगा-लगा के अपने आपको एक एंग्जायटी का पेशेंट समझ रहे थे। अब खुद से सब कुछ समझने लगोगे फिर तो नैया डूबती ही है। अब कहते तो वही है ना कि जो तैरता है वही डूबता है। तो उनके साथ भी वही हो रहा था, स्मार्ट बन रहे थे। अब इस स्मार्टनेस के चक्कर में खुद अपने डायग्नोसिस भी करें और खुद डॉक्टर के पास जाके बैठ गए। डॉक्टर के पास जाके भैया अगर आप उनको इतनी कंप्लेंट करोगे, इतनी एक्यूरेट कंप्लेंट करोगे तो वो खुद कहेगा भाई मेरा तो काम आसान कर रहा है यार। किसके पास टाइम है इतना, हिंदुस्तान में 150 करोड़ जनता है। तो ठीक है अच्छा तू एंग्जायटी के सिम्टम बता रहा है तो दवाई खाओ, ठीक हो जाएगा। तो दवाई भी खा रहा था। आप मानोगे नहीं जैसे उसका एक मिथायक्लोबिन इंजेक्शन आता है 2.5 हज़ार एमसीजी का और विटामिन पहला लगा ना अगले दिन ही उसकी आँखें चमक गई थी। फिर जब दूसरा शॉट लगा एक हफ्ते बाद, मैंने बोला अब 1 महीना ट्रीटमेंट करा लो और मेरे को 1 महीने बाद बताना आपका क्या है क्या नहीं। तो मैंने पूछा, "हाँ जी, बताओ एक महीने बाद।" कह रहा, "सर, मेरी तो ठीक हो गई एंग्जायटी।" मैंने बोला, "कोई सिम्टम आ रहे?" कह रहा, "सर, कुछ भी नहीं आ रहे।" मतलब जीरो सिम्टम है, लाइफ बिल्कुल पहले जैसे नॉर्मल हो गई। तो मैंने बोला, "एंग्जायटी की टेबलेट्स का क्या हुआ?"

title: The Anxiety Trick No One Talks About (True Student Story)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Have you ever caught yourself trapped in a loop of your own thoughts, lying awake at 2:00 a.m., replaying a conversation from years ago, convinced everyone secretly hates you? If you have, know this: you are not broken, you are not weak. Alex felt exactly what you're feeling right now. Alex was a first-year student. Good grades, tight friend group, a hard-earned scholarship, but underneath, his mind was a battlefield. Picture it: 6:00 a.m., Alex on the dorm floor, heart hammering like it might crack a rib. No fire, no danger, just a presentation due at nine. Here's what nobody tells you about panic: it doesn't need a reason, it just needs a nervous system running on empty. Alex missed that presentation. Then three more. Isolation crept in slowly, the way it always does. Skipped classes became skipped meals. Let that sink in. One of the sharpest minds in his program was disappearing, not from lack of ability, but from a mind stuck in survival mode. Stay with me, because the breakthrough in phase three is a tool most people ignore completely, and the quiet decision Alex made in the final month decides whether any of us can break free from our own mental traps today. One, naming the enemy. Alex thought something was medically wrong. Racing heart, shaking hands, walls closing in during lectures. The amygdala, the brain's alarm system, can't tell a tiger from a test. It floods the body with adrenaline and waits for you to run. Alex wasn't losing his mind; his mind was just aimed at the wrong target. The turning point? A counselor gave him one sentence: "Name it, don't become it." Instead of "I am anxious," he learned to say, "Anxiety is visiting." The fight wasn't in the classroom; it was between his ears. Two, rebuilding from the ground up. Naming it didn't erase it. Isolation is where anxiety thrives, and Alex knew it. So he built tiny, deliberate acts of discomfort: sitting in the library instead of his room, speaking one sentence in class, texting a friend back with shaking hands. This is behavioral activation.

Today, I'm talking about the reactivation of Epstein-Barr. If you've ever been struggling with this relentless fatigue despite sleeping well, if your blood work comes back so called normal, but you're really feeling anything but, or if you've had mono in the past and never quite felt the same afterwards, today's video may provide a missing piece to what you've been searching for. Well, let's start with the basics of Epstein-Barr, EBV. This is part of the herpes family. You've probably heard this as mononucleosis or just simply mono or you may have heard this as just kissing disease. Most people are exposed to Epstein-Barr virus at some point in their life and by some estimates as much as 90% of people adults carry this. Now in many cases, the initial infection just passes and the virus becomes dormant in your body, especially in your B cells, which are again are part of your immune system. But here's the key, Epstein-Barr virus never fully leaves your body, it simply just goes into an inactive state. So, while Epstein-Barr virus can remain dormant really for years, certain stressors or triggers can cause it to wake up and then become reactive and when that happens, your immune system has to mount a response. This often looks and feels like chronic fatigue, autoimmune flare ups and some people muscle aches and joint pain and brain fog and sometimes even low-grade fever or even swollen lymph nodes.
