title: The Morning After I K*ll Myself
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: The morning after I killed myself, will I still wake to my mother's prayer, her voice trembling softly between incense and faith, as if God still listens to tired women before sunrise? Will I still hear my father's familiar scolding for not waking up early enough, those small ordinary rants I once mistook for irritation, never realizing they were love wearing a rough voice? Will I still receive those annoying texts from my manager, those weekend meetings I hate with all my heart, and still secretly laugh at how life never asks whether we are tired before demanding more? Will my best friend still wait outside her house for me, ready to pull me away from this suffocating city life, just for an hour, just to remind me that breathing is still possible? Will my mother still save strawberries for me because she remembers what I like, even when I forget what it feels like to be loved? Will my father still stand outside the main gate of our house if I come home late from work, pretending he was just walking outside after having dinner, when really he was waiting to make sure I returned safely? Will those annoying relatives still ask those annoying questions about my marriage, my future, my life, as if they know anything about the storms a quiet person survives without making a sound? No. The day after I leave, none of it will reach me. Not the daily noises that make me frustrated every day. Not the love hidden inside that noise. Not my loved ones waiting for me to reach home safely. Not my parents worrying about my safety. Not the ordinary little things that look so small until I imagined a world without them. And maybe that is the tragedy of hopelessness. It does not always come because life has no love in it. Sometimes it comes because pain grows so loud that it drowns out the love that was there all along. While I was losing hope, everyone around me was still quietly holding hope for me.

title: The Morning After I K*ll Myself
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: In my mother's prayers, in my father waiting at the gate, in my friends' unfinished plans, in the strawberries that were kept aside for me, in the people I thought I was a burden to. And if you, too, have been standing at the edge of your own darkness, thinking no one would notice if you disappeared, look again. Sometimes hope does not arrive like sunlight. Sometimes it arrives like a mother calling your name from the next room. Sometimes it arrives like a father asking if you have eaten. Sometimes it arrives like a friend saying, "Come downstairs, I'm waiting." Sometimes it arrives as one more morning you did not ask for, but was still given. And maybe you do not need to believe in forever right now. Maybe all you need is to stay for one more prayer, one more scolding, one more annoying text, one more late-night gate opening, one more plate of cut fruit, one more stupid laugh, one more ordinary day that does not know it is saving your life. So, if today you have no hope left, borrow some. Borrow it from the people who still love you, even when you cannot love your life. Borrow it from the version of you that still wants to stay, even if only a little. Borrow it until it becomes your own, because the day after you leave, the world will keep moving, but it will move with a missing piece, and that missing piece will be you. So stay, not because life is easy, not because pain is small, not because tomorrow is promised to be beautiful. Stay because even now, in ways you do not fully see, you are still being waited for by someone, somewhere.

title: Just Do It - Spoken Word by Paul Harris Steward ft Ansel King
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Thank God I don't look like what I've been through. Tell you the truth, I'm lucky that I'm even standing right here in front of all of you. I was 14 years old the first time, the first time those thoughts crossed my mind, but see, I was too worried about leaving my mother and my little brother behind. In high school, it was bad. No, in college, it was worse. Shit, I don't even know how I made it through my 20s and 30s because those thoughts used to float through my mind, but I used to be able to push them out right in time. Tell you the truth, I did not know that anything was wrong. I'm from Chicago. I was raised to be strong, never show any weakness. What happens in this house stays in this house. My mom said, "Boy, you better always keep your business to yourself." So, I thought that meant even if it jeopardized my mental health. See, I've come to the conclusion that my happy moments, my happy moments in my life, they're like waves, they never stand still. I've been in denial and hurting for 32 years and it hasn't been easy to heal. But it seems like the older I got, the thoughts stopped floating. In my mind, those demons would stay and play every day, got me going through it. They're no longer whispering, now every day they're screaming, telling me to just do it. I can't outrun it. I read the books, took the meds, sat in therapy trying to understand my head, but some nights the darkness wins, and I'm exhausted from fighting it. I tell my family I'm fine, but I don't know how to explain. Someone said, "Paul, don't worry, they're just passive, intrusive thoughts. It's only dangerous if you make a plan." Well, I remember the day I held that pen in my hand. On my calendar, I circled October 14th, 2021, and I wrote, "just do it." And this time, it wasn't just a cry for help. This time, it wasn't just words of my mouth, I swear to God, y'all, this time I wouldn't chicken out. I had already been in the house for two weeks by myself. I look at my clock, and I realize I only had eight minutes left. I pick up my phone one last time, and then I saw her. She was on The Breakfast Club doing an interview, and she said, "Come out of those dark rooms and get some help." It felt like she was talking to me. It felt like she understood my pain. So, for the rest of my life, I'll say her name. Jenifer Lewis, Jenifer Lewis, Jenifer Lewis saved me because her words stayed in my head to the point where I started seeing my mom at the edge of my bed. My mom said, "I miss you baby, but I'm not ready to see you yet." Bro, that night my mom fought for me. Dog, my mom fought for me. She took me out of his hands. She gave me enough strength. The next morning, I checked myself in because my heart was dark, and so was my soul.

title: Just Do It - Spoken Word by Paul Harris Steward ft Ansel King
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: I was in a room with no windows on a 72-hour hold. Now I'm standing in line. I got a good job, master's degree, money in the bank, but I'm humble, cuz now I'm standing in line and I'm raising my tongue like everyone else. But I'm lying to the doctors, keeping my secrets to myself because I'm worried about y'all judging me. Hear that? I was almost not here because I was worried about y'all judging me even though I know that all pain wants to be free. Look, I don't think y'all understand. I was safe in the hospital. But every second I was making a new plan. I asked the doctor, I said, "Why do I continue to hurt? When will these fucking pills start to work?" The doctor said, "Paul," he said, "Paul, I know that it's hard, but bro, you also have to do your part." Oh, so I knew what I had to do. I sat up on that couch. I said, "All right, doc, I'll tell you." I was molested when I was ten... I said, "I was molested when I was ten, twice." For the last 32 years I've been holding that secret in. The doctor said, "Good job, Paul. What else?" I said, "Damn! You wanna hear more?" The doctor said, "That's the only way you're ever gonna walk out that door." And the first time I was ready to let it go. It's not me. It's not me. It's when it comes down, I can't talk or have anyone around. On November 26, 2010, my mom called me and I sat in that dark room with those demons. I just looked at my phone. I called her back ten minutes later, and some nurse said she's gone. The doctor said, "Good job, Paul." I said, "Wait, there's one more thing I need to let go. Something I've been holding in, something I've never told my best friend. Yo, I'm a good dude. I really try to be a good person. But when it comes down, when those demons come around, I can't talk or have anyone around. On October 5, 2020, my little brother, my only sibling, Jeremy Jermaine Stewart, he was coming to New York to see me in just two days. So all my social coins I tried to save. He called me and I sat in that dark room. I thought, "I'll just see my little brother tomorrow." But like a fool, I forgot that time is something that we can't borrow. I woke up the next morning in my bed. I read a text message, "Paul, your little brother's dead."

transcription: I asked the doctor. I said, "Doctor, don't you think this is too much for anyone to hold in, for anyone to handle?" He said, "Yeah, Paul, but the truth is, you have a fucking chemical imbalance. He said, "Your highs don't balance with your lows." If diagnoses feels like a sentence, hear me say. You haven't figured it out yet. I'm talking about MDD, major depressive disorder, and I'm not talking about you losing $20 and you mad as fuck. I'm talking about being in bed for 3 weeks and you can't get up. Depression is like drowning in a kiddie pool but you're stuck, but everyone around you like, "Why won't he stand up?" I don't want y'all to feel sorry for me because at the end of the day, I'm still here, even with depression, still here, living with anxiety. I don't always love my reflection, but I'm fighting for my life quietly. Still here. Right. I made it. But I think about those who've lost the battle. Ian Alexander Jr., he was 26 years old. Y'all remember the cat from the Ellen Show, tWitch? He was 40 years old. The young guy from the Disney show, Lee Thompson Young, he was 29 years old. I met a woman in Orlando. She said her son went to the graveyard in the middle of the night and he shot himself in the head. He was 21 years old, Jabril Muhammad. So, I know there may be someone here. You smile when you're in a crowded room, you learned how to laugh real loud when everyone wants you to, but deep down inside you're hurting, you're drowning. I understand that you're going through it. I just ask that you do like I did. Pick up the phone. Just do it. I bet it feels like running through pain. I've cried in silence, felt the shame. Got broken by my own mind, but I'm learning that expressing it is how I stay alive. I talk to friends, I write it down, I let the sadness speak, because oppressing all these feelings is almost ending me. I don't need judgment, I need space to feel everything I feel and still be okay. I'm still here, even with depression, still here, living with anxiety, medication, therapy, progression. title: A Prison Called My Mind
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Thud. Thump. Thud. Thump. The steady, heavy sound of a heartbeat echoes in the quiet room, looping like a ticking clock of anxiety. The beat drops in slow, heavy, mournful piano chords blended with vinyl static. Step inside the vestibule where shadows wear my face. I rent a room in ruin in a quiet crowded space. The blueprints of my sorrow were drafted in my youth, a self-inflicted torture built to barricade the truth. They think freedom is a pardon from a cell of iron bars. They've never felt the prison of beneath a million stars. My consciousness is solitary, padded with regret. Every mirror is a guard that I can't quite outrun or let go of the whispers that bleed through the drywall, predicting every stumble, orchestrating every fall. The key was swallowed years ago, dissolved in bitter acid. Now I sit in silence, paralyzed and flaccid. Trapped inside an echo chamber, spinning out of phase, navigating hallways in a permanent twilight maze. In a prison called my mind, the warden wears my eyes. He feeds me daily rations made of fabricated lies. No walls of grey concrete, just the weight of what could be. I built the cage myself and threw away the sanity. Oh, let me out. Let me face the open sky. Serving life in hard times in a prison called my mind. I pace the perimeter of all the things I never said, a graveyard of intentions resting heavy in my head. There's a library of every single look that made me shrink and a reservoir of ink from every time I dared to think that maybe I was more than just a tenant of my doubts. The fire starts to flicker every time the oxygen runs out. My heartbeat's like a metronome for grief I can't release, trading bits of sanity for moments of a fragile peace.

category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: This is me in my 20s. A mind too loud, out pacing my breath. Running in circles with anxiety's depth. Depression would sit like a weight on my chest, a body on edge that never found rest. Irritated, agitated, out of place, wearing a calm but losing the race. Unbalanced steps on a thin tightline, losing my body while chasing my mind. I ate what I knew, what I thought was right. Meats on my plate and dairy at night. Ice cream melting to soften the day, gallons of milk as years slipped away. Feeding the habit and quieting the ache, numbing the signals my body would make. Chasing a comfort that would never stay, holding me gently then drifting away. But something inside was trying to speak. A truth in my body steady but weak. A whisper beneath all the noise and the fear calling me closer, I couldn't yet hear. I didn't know then what I know today, that the mind can lead you further and further astray. When it grips too tight, when it won't unwind, you lose the body, ah, you lose the divine. Now, this is me nearing my 50s. Breath more steady, movements more free. Vegan, mostly raw, alive in the skin, feeding my body, woo, from deep within. Vegetables and fruits and nuts and seeds, with light fueling my days, restoring my night.

title: From Anxiety to Alignment: A Spoken Word Healing Journey
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: What I consume now nourishes me, body and spirit in harmony. My mood loving, calm, at ease, a gentle flow like a warm summer breeze. Forgiving my past and releasing the fight, stepping into my truth and into my light. My mind, I no longer a cage I defend, but flexible thoughts that bend and extend. No longer the ruler, no longer the way, I learned how to move it gently aside each day. Because we have choices more than we see, not bound by the past or who we thought and were taught to be. We can stay stuck in patterns that ache, or rise with intention in each choice we make. We can stay suffering and call it fate, or open a door we thought was late. Get the mind out of the way and let it rest, so the body can speak what it knows is best. Get the mind out of the way and release the control, so the spirit can rise, remember it's whole. Get the mind out of the way and soften the fight, so healing can flow without force, without smite. And now I look forward with wonder, not fear, to the woman I'll meet each passing year. My 70's calling, steady and wise, with stories and laughter and truth in her eyes. My 100's waiting, vast and free, a lifetime of healing unfolding in me. So I ask you now, as you stand in your day, what choices are you making? What are you choosing, your way? What life are you shaping with each breath you take? What version of you are you ready to wake?

title: Quiet Desperation
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: forget what excitement even feels like. Not pleasure, not distraction. Real excitement. The kind that makes you feel awake, the kind that reminds you there's still fire in you somewhere. And maybe that's why so many people are constantly overstimulated now. Constant music, constant scrolling, constant noise. Because silence forces confrontation. Silence asks questions entertainment can temporarily drown out. Questions like, is this really the life I want? When did I stop being curious? Why do I feel lonely even around people? What part of myself did I abandon just to fit into this version of adulthood? The truth is, a lot of people aren't depressed because life is impossible. They're depressed because they've disconnected from meaning. Human beings can survive pain. We've always survived pain. But meaninglessness? Meaninglessness empties people out. It turns days into repetitions instead of experiences. That's why some of the most exhausted people aren't the ones working the hardest. They're the ones living without emotional connection to what they do. And I'm not saying everybody needs to quit their job tomorrow and disappear into the mountains to find themselves. Sometimes the change starts smaller than that. Sometimes it starts with honesty. Honest conversations, honest reflection. Honest admissions like, "I'm not happy," or "I've been pretending for years." That kind of honesty is terrifying because once you see the truth clearly, you can't unsee it anymore. But maybe that discomfort is necessary. Maybe dissatisfaction isn't always a flaw. Maybe sometimes it's a signal. A warning light on the dashboard of your spirit telling you that you've been living too far away from yourself for too long. Because people think the greatest tragedy is failure. I don't think so. I think the greatest tragedy is becoming emotionally absent from your own life. Waking up one day, realizing you spent decades being responsible, but never truly alive. Safe, but never fulfilled. Admired, but never understood. That's quiet desperation. It doesn't destroy you all at once. It erodes you gradually, quietly, politely. And maybe the solution isn't to become louder. Maybe it's to become more real. To stop performing strength every second of your life. To stop treating your deeper desires like inconveniences. To stop abandoning yourself just because the world rewards conformity more than authenticity. Because at the end of the day, people can survive chaos. People can survive heartbreak. People can survive failure. But surviving a life that never felt like yours in the first place, that leaves a different kind of wound. And I think deep down, most people already know exactly what I mean.

title: The Truth About Recovering From Depression (That Changed Me)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: People often ask me when I finally got better, as if there was one magical morning when I opened my eyes and everything felt different. As if healing arrived all at once, like flipping a switch. Darkness one moment, light the next. But that's not how it happened, and honestly, that's not how healing usually works. My depression didn't leave overnight. It left quietly, slowly, almost invisibly, like the tide pulling away from the shore. One day, the water would retreat and I'd catch a glimpse of the beach beneath it. I'd laugh at a video, reply to a message, cook a simple meal, take a walk outside. For a few hours, life felt manageable. Then the tide would return. Not violently, not dramatically, just enough to make me wonder if I'd imagined those better moments. For a long time, that cycle frustrated me. Whenever I felt better, I expected it to stay. Whenever I felt worse, I assumed I was back at the beginning. I didn't realize healing was happening underneath it all. I remember mornings when getting out of bed felt impossible. Not because I was physically tired, because mentally, everything felt heavy. Simple tasks felt enormous: brushing my teeth, taking a shower, answering a text. Things that seemed effortless for everyone else felt like climbing a mountain. And the hardest part was knowing what I was supposed to do. I knew exercise could help, I knew fresh air could help, I knew routines could help. But depression has a way of turning simple actions into impossible missions. Knowing and doing become two completely different things. It's like having a map but no energy to start the journey. Then one day, something happened, something that would seem completely insignificant to most people. I got up and took a shower.

transcription: Without spending 30 minutes arguing with myself first, without lying on the floor trying to gather motivation, without negotiating every step, I simply stood up and did it, and afterward I cried, not because I was sad, because I suddenly realized how long it had been since anything felt easy. That tiny moment became important, not because it fixed everything, because it proved something, it proved I was still capable of moving forward, even if the steps were small. Recovery taught me something I wish more people understood, healing is not a straight line, it's messy, some days feel like progress, other days feel like you're right back where you started, you can have a great week and then wake up on Tuesday feeling exactly like you did 6 months ago, that doesn't mean you've failed, that doesn't mean you're broken, it simply means you're human. For a long time I measured healing the wrong way, I looked at entire days, entire weeks, entire months, and when they weren't perfect, I assumed nothing was changing. Eventually, I started measuring healing differently, I measured it in moments, the moment I answered a friend's phone call instead of ignoring it, the moment I admitted I wasn't okay, the moment I sat outside and felt the warmth of the sun, the moment I tasted a meal and actually enjoyed it, small moments, ordinary moments, but together they became evidence, evidence that I was still here, evidence that I was still fighting, evidence that recovery was happening, even when I couldn't see it. Then something unexpected happened, the good days started showing up more often, at first it was barely noticeable, maybe one extra good day each month, then one extra good day each week, slowly the balance began to shift, the difficult days didn't

title: The Truth About Recovering From Depression (That Changed Me)

transcription: disappear. But they stopped controlling everything. And eventually, I stopped counting. I stopped checking whether I was healed yet. I stopped searching for a finish line. Because healing isn't about reaching perfection. It's about building a life that feels possible again. A life where difficult days don't erase all your progress. A life where setbacks aren't proof of failure. A life where hope becomes stronger than fear. Today, I won't tell you healing is easy. Because it isn't. I won't tell you there's a secret shortcut. Because there isn't. And I won't tell you that positive thinking alone solves everything. Because sometimes the struggle runs deeper than that. What I will tell you is this. You are allowed to heal slowly. You are allowed to take your time. You are allowed to have setbacks. You are allowed to celebrate tiny victories. And you are allowed to call that progress. Because progress isn't always dramatic. Sometimes progress is simply getting out of bed. Sometimes progress is drinking water. Sometimes progress is surviving a difficult day. And sometimes progress is choosing to try again tomorrow. My depression didn't leave overnight. But one day, I noticed it had become quieter. One day, I realized I was making plans for the future again. One day, I looked in the mirror and recognized the person staring back at me. Not perfect. Not completely healed. Not finished. But present. Still here. And after everything I had survived, that meant more than I can explain. Because sometimes being still here isn't a small thing. Sometimes it's the greatest victory of all. And if you're still here too, keep going. The tide may not disappear overnight. But little by little, it can move farther away. And one day, you'll look back and realize you've traveled much farther than you ever thought possible.

title: Senior Depression Doesn't Look Like Sadness—Watch for This Instead
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: If your mom or dad has seemed more worn out lately, more on edge, or just kind of distant, most of us chalk it up to getting older. That's just what happens, right? But honestly, a lot of the time, that's not what's going on at all. And missing what's actually happening can make things so much harder down the road. So today, I want to walk you through five signs that your parent might be struggling with depression, not just aging, and what you can realistically do to help. Here's the thing about depression in older adults. It's one of the most missed diagnoses in the country. And the reason it keeps getting overlooked, it doesn't look the way we expect it to. There's usually no breakdown, no "I think I'm depressed." It disguises itself as stuff that just looks like normal aging. That's exactly how it slips by everyone, including doctors. So let's go through the signs, one at a time. Sign number one: fatigue and low energy. The first sign is a kind of bone-deep exhaustion. Not "I didn't sleep great" tired, more like a heaviness that just follows them around, no matter how much rest they get. Maybe they're sleeping in more than usual, napping constantly, or they just seem completely drained by the smallest things. Now, yes, some tiredness comes with age. That's real. But when it shows up out of nowhere, or keeps getting worse week after week, that's not something to brush off. It's the change you want to pay attention to, not just the tiredness itself. Sign number two: irritability, not sadness. This one catches families completely off guard. When most of us picture depression, we picture someone crying, shutting down, saying they feel hopeless. But in older adults, it often comes out as irritability, snapping over little things, getting frustrated way faster than usual, seeming angry for reasons nobody can quite figure out. So if your parent has gotten noticeably more short-tempered lately, and that's just not like them, please don't write it off as them being grumpy. There may be a lot more going on underneath that. Sign number three: losing interest in the things they love. Think about what your parent used to love doing. Maybe it was tending to their garden, watching their shows, cooking a big Sunday dinner for whoever could make it. And now, they just don't. They're not interested. They don't even bring it up anymore. Losing that spark for things they once genuinely enjoyed, that's one of the clearest signals of depression at any age. Doctors actually have a name for it: anhedonia. It means you've lost the ability to feel pleasure from things that used to make you happy. When the stuff that used to

transcription: to light them up just doesn't anymore, that's worth taking seriously. Sign number four: pulling away from people. Seniors dealing with depression tend to quietly retreat from the people they care about most. They stop picking up the phone. They cancel plans. They go silent in conversations they used to love being part of. And here's what makes this so hard. Loneliness and depression don't just co-exist, they fuel each other. The more isolated your parent gets, the worse the depression becomes. And the worse the depression gets, the more they pull back. It's a cycle, and it's really tough to break without someone stepping in from the outside. Sign number five: saying they feel like a burden. This is the one I want you to hold onto most. Start really listening for things like, "I don't want to be a bother," or, "You've all got enough going on without worrying about me," or even, "What's the point anymore at my age?" Those aren't just throw-away comments. Those aren't just venting. Those are warning signs. When a parent starts talking like they're a burden to the people they love, that means they need real support, and they need it sooner rather than later. Please, don't let those words just hang in the air unanswered. What to do. Okay, so you recognized your parent in some of that. Now what? Three things you can actually do. First, have a gentle, low pressure conversation. You don't have to have all the answers. You don't have to fix anything. Just sit down with them and say something like, "Hey, I've been thinking about you. You seem like you might be going through something. How are you really doing?" That kind of moment matters more than most people realize. Second, bring it up at their next doctor's appointment, and be specific. Ask for a depression screening. Don't assume the doctor will bring it up because, most of the time, they won't. And third, look into therapy. A lot of seniors have no idea that Medicare actually covers mental health visits. And with online therapy being so widely available now, it's easier than ever, especially for parents who don't drive or have a hard time getting around. I've linked some resources in the description to help you get started. Before you go, I want you to hear this. Depression is not a normal part of getting older. It is not just something your parent has to accept and live with. It is treatable. And the sooner it's caught, the better things can get. If this was helpful, share it with someone who might really need it right now. And subscribe. Every week we talk about real, practical mental health topics for seniors and the families who show up for them. I'll see you in the next one.

The champagne is long since gone flat, the confetti swept away, and the echoes of Auld Lang Syne have faded into the ether. We stand now at the precipice of a new year, yet I, like so many others, feel inexplicably stuck. The dawn of 2026 was heralded with such promise, such optimism. The arbitrary flip of the calendar's page seemed to offer a tabula rasa, a chance to shed the skin of years past and emerge, phoenix-like, into the new. We scribbled resolutions on scraps of paper, whispered promises to the universe, and clinked glasses to the future. Yet here we are, mere weeks later, watching as our best-laid plans begin to list precariously, like a ship taking on water. Old habits, it seems, have die-hard convictions. They creep back into our lives like ivy, their tendrils insidiously wrapping around our good intentions, threatening to strangle them before they can bear fruit. I had sworn to eschew the snooze button, to embrace the dawn with the vigor of a Benedictine monk. Yet my alarm clock and I remain locked in our eternal pas de deux, those nine tantalizing minutes of stolen slumber too sweet a temptation. The gym membership card, once a badge of honor, a testament to my commitment to physical renewal, now languishes in the dark recesses of my wallet. The meditation app, downloaded with such gusto, has been relegated to a distant corner of my smartphone's home screen, its daily reminders met with increasing indifference.

category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: But why does this happen? Are we merely weak-willed, or is there some deeper psychological underpinning to our annual dance with resolution and relapse? Dr. Timothy Pychyl, a professor of psychology at Carleton University in Ottawa, Canada, posits that the problem lies not in our lack of willpower, but in our failure to understand the nuances of habit formation and change. He asserts, "We don't know how to make lasting changes in our behavior. We initiate change through goal-setting, but we don't follow through on those goals." In essence, we are seduced by the idea of instant transformation, duped into believing that change is a binary switch to be flicked, rather than a dimmer slowly ratcheting up the brightness over time. We fail to appreciate the cyclical nature of change, the ebb and flow of progress and setback. Moreover, our resolutions often hinge on negative self-perceptions, obsessing over perceived flaws that must be fixed. This negative reinforcement can be a powerful motivator initially, but it lacks the staying power of positivity. When we inevitably stumble, we are left with nothing but our old familiar friend, self-loathing. So, what is the antidote to this January ennui? How do we break the cycle and forge ahead with our resolutions? Firstly, let us reframe our resolutions, not as drastic changes to be implemented overnight, but as journeys of incremental growth. A daily walk, however short, is still a step forward. A single meditation session, however brief, is still a moment of mindfulness. Secondly, we must cultivate self-compassion. It is inevitable that we will stumble, that we will fall back into old habits. But rather than allowing these setbacks to define us, we must treat them as temporary detours on our journey.

title: Depression Starts in the Gut? The Hidden Truth Nobody Tells You
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Have you ever felt heavy without knowing why? Have you ever woken up tired, even after a full night of sleep? Have you ever felt sadness, but there was no clear reason? What if the answer is not in your thoughts, but in your stomach? Yes, you heard that right. Your gut, your digestive system, may be deeply connected to your emotions, your mood, and even depression. Welcome to Universal Wisdom. Today, we explore a powerful truth that most people never notice: the secret link between your gut and your mind. This is not just motivation; this is science, awareness, and deep understanding. Take a slow breath, and listen carefully, because what you are about to hear may change how you see your body forever. The second brain inside you. Inside your body, there is a system so intelligent that scientists call it the second brain. This system lives in your gut. It controls digestion, but it also communicates constantly with your brain. Every second, signals travel between your stomach and your mind. If your gut is healthy, your mind feels calm. If your gut is disturbed, your emotions become unstable. Think about this: when you feel nervous, your stomach tightens. When you feel fear, digestion slows down. When you feel stress, your appetite changes. This is not coincidence. Your gut and brain are in constant conversation. And when this communication breaks, emotional imbalance begins. The hidden cause people ignore. Many people try to fix depression by changing thoughts only. They try positive thinking, motivation, distraction, but they ignore the physical root. transcription: Hi, I'm Chris Avery, I'm the founder of Michaux Media. And this journey for me started back in 2010 while I was deployed to Afghanistan. My mom at the time had sent me a care package, and tucked inside that care package were these stamps featuring this man named Oscar Michaux. Now my mom knew that I had a passion for TV and film, but what she didn't know was that this subtle introduction would drastically change my life. Oscar Michaux lived as a black man during the Great Depression and the segregation of the Jim Crow South. During that time, and despite all of that, he somehow managed to produce, finance, and self-distribute over 40 of his own films entirely independently. He was a maverick who didn't ask for permission. His legacy of self-determination and independence is the absolute inspiration for Michaux Media. Right now, the modern film industry is facing its own unique challenges. Currently, over 85% of the media produced doesn't return its investment, and less than 10% even manages to break even. Hollywood is losing millions because they are bound by outdated production models that fail to engage modern audiences. They are trying to solve a 21st-century problem by gatekeeping 20th-century methods, and it's costing them everything. Michaux Media exists to capture a shift. We want to bet on modern mavericks just like Oscar Michaux. We are building an accelerator platform to de-risk, scale, and monetize creative media before committing massive investment, and shift the power dynamics back to the independent creator. Our platform operates on a four-phase model. First, we host a development sprint designed to test the validity of a project. Second, based on the results of the validation process, we use an internal VC-style model to invest in those ideas that are great and excellent and will go above the mark. And third, we use the most advanced yet financially accessible tools to create proof of concepts. And fourth, we distribute our final result to our pre-vetted and highly curated direct audience. And now is the time for this shift. We are witnessing massive disruption in the entertainment industry. Independent creators are breaking box office records, and we've already seen this in artists like Markiplier and his Iron Lung movie.

title: VCs See 100s of Decks a Week — Here's How to Not Get Rejected in 5 Seconds
transcription: The greatest lie ever told in Silicon Valley is build it and they will come. We love to imagine if you code a brilliant product, users will magically appear, and venture capitalists will throw term sheets at your feet. Investors see countless high-performance products fail because no one ever finds out they exist. Without a distribution plan, a startup is effectively an expensive hobby. Most founders assume investors reject them because their idea is bad. In reality, investors reject them because their pitch deck is completely confusing. Industry veteran Guy Kawasaki points out a classic mistake: cramming slides with 10-point font. If you are reading tiny text aloud to an investor, they read ahead, tune out, and the pitch is dead on arrival. You have to understand the psychology of the person across the table. Venture capitalists see hundreds of pitches a week. They are actively looking for a reason to say no so they can move on to the next one and save time. A pitch deck's utility is limited to surviving that initial wave of skepticism and securing a 30-minute meeting. To survive, you have to clear two psychological hurdles. Hurdle 1: Do I care? To get a yes, your problem statement has to be stupidly simple. If you use MBA jargon to describe a synergistic paradigm, you lose. You need to state exactly how many hours or dollars your user is currently wasting because your product doesn't exist yet. The solution slide should offer immediate relief to that exact pain point. Investors don't want a complex technical schematic of your software architecture here. They want to see the pain disappear. This diagram shows three concentric circles of market size: total addressable market, serviceable available, and serviceable obtainable. This clears Hurdle 2: Is this a real business? Calculate market size here without sounding delusional about capturing all of it day one. That requires detailing your go-to-market strategy. Founders often spend weeks polishing product screenshots and maybe 10 minutes thinking about customer acquisition. A brilliant business model is entirely uninvestable if you can't articulate exactly how your first 100 or 1,000 customers are going to find you. Next is Hurdle 3: Is there proof?

title: VCs See 100s of Decks a Week — Here's How to Not Get Rejected in 5 Seconds
transcription: Investors want to see traction, but the definition of traction changes depending on what stage you're pitching. If you are raising a pre-seed round, completing 100 in-depth customer interviews counts as perfectly valid proof. But if you are raising a seed round, investors expect to see active, measurable usage of a live product. You don't need grid lines, legends, or 12 colors to present traction. Strip everything away. Highlight a single core metric that proves your growth. Investors want to see milestones. How $2 million unlocks your next major growth threshold. Finally, hurdle 4: can you win? If you look at investor in the eye and say, "We have no competitors," they hear, "There is no market." It's an instant red flag. Acknowledging your competition proves that the problem actually exists and people are trying to solve it. It immediately shifts the conversation to why your specific team has the unfair advantage required to completely dominate them. A funded deck builds an airtight chronological case that this specific team can execute a proven strategy. To force that level of clarity, Guy Kawasaki coined the 10-20-30 rule. A pitch should have 10 slides, take 20 minutes, and use no font smaller than 30 points. The logic is brutal but effective. If you have to shrink your text to make it fit on the slide, you are trying to cram too many concepts into one space. Early stage founders often think they need slick corporate graphic design or inflated revenue projections to look professional. In reality, clarity beats aesthetics every time. Before you send your deck anywhere, check these four boxes: Can someone understand the problem in 5 seconds? Is your font 30 points or larger? Do you have a clearly defined go-to-market strategy? And is your team's advantage obvious? Building a startup is hard enough. Ignore the fake guru advice, and let factual clarity earn you that next meeting.

title: GEW and The Experience Gap
transcription: The traditional model of higher education is a passive one. You spend years in wood-paneled rooms like this, absorbing information and waiting to be evaluated by a single focal point of authority. But the moment you graduate, that model breaks. You enter a job market that demands prior experience, yet you can't get that experience because no one will hire you without it. It's the universal paradox of the modern graduate. Most students respond by polishing a resume and submitting it to an online portal, hoping to be chosen from a stack of thousands. This path relies entirely on relinquishing control and waiting for someone else to grant you permission to start your career. In an economy that moves as fast as ours, relying on that passive strategy of waiting to be chosen is a losing bet. The traditional line is simply moving too slowly. If you look at how the most significant career opportunities are actually created, they are rarely assigned by a teacher or a hiring manager. They are discovered by people who notice a problem and step in to fix it before they are asked. This suggests a different logical step after graduation. Instead of spending months finding a job, what if you spent a week building a solution to a problem that already exists? There is a sharp contrast in mindset here. A traditional applicant is looking for an empty slot to fill. A creator is looking for a functional gap in the market, and designing a way to close it. Our current economy is full of powerful tools, but short on people who know how to apply them to specific, messy problems. That gap in the market is exactly where students can transition from being consumers of a curriculum to creators of real-world value. Historically, launching a new venture was a high-stakes game. It required massive capital, a team of specialized engineers, and the backing of a large institution. But as this chart shows, the cost of developing a new product has exponentially collapsed, dropping towards zero. Modern artificial intelligence, cloud services, and no-code tools erased those old gates, making infrastructure accessible to anyone with an internet connection. This toolkit has expanded the definition of an entrepreneur. It is no longer a label reserved for business school students. It is now a functional set of skills. For tradespeople scaling a service, artists automating their sales, or educators reaching new students. For example, a student might notice that a local nonprofit struggles with a repetitive administrative bottleneck. Using AI tools, that student can now build a lightweight, functional prototype to solve that specific problem in a single afternoon. Technology has democratized the power to build. This means the primary barrier to entry is no longer capital or a degree. It is the individual decision to hit start. Even with the tools available, most students stay on the sidelines because they feel they lack professional experience. They are waiting for a level of authority that no textbook can give them.

title: Why Shark Tank Rejections Often Create Billion-Dollar Businesses
transcription: Television framing suggests that a golden key, and investor's approval, is the only way a startup can scale. Yet a growing list of multi-million dollar companies share a counterintuitive origin story. Their trajectory only accelerated after their golden opportunity publicly shattered. Over the last decade, business reality television has engineered a very specific cultural myth: the idea that a panel of billionaires possesses a flawless intuition for predicting market winners. The audience is sold a clean, dramatic narrative. A broadcasted handshake equates to instant wealth and market dominance, while a harsh rejection signifies the immediate death of a company. Behind the cameras, the reality of these negotiations is heavily obscured. Real pitches often last anywhere from 45 minutes to two and a half hours, but editors aggressively splice these marathons down into 8-minute segments designed purely for pacing and conflict. The resulting broadcast is a highly engineered media product. It is optimized for entertainment, capturing dramatic confrontations rather than providing a definitive verdict on a company's fundamental market value. The manipulation of the narrative extends beyond the editing bay. A significant percentage of filmed pitches are completely scrapped by producers, meaning many founders endure the entire gauntlet only to never make it to the airwaves. The psychological toll of the process is severe enough that immediately following a rejection, founders are ushered into a room with a show-appointed psychiatrist to evaluate their mental state before they leave the studio. Even for those who survive the pitch and secure a deal, the instantaneous on-screen handshake is largely theatrical. It is immediately followed by months of grueling off-camera due diligence. During that period of intense scrutiny, the most heavily guarded secret of the production comes to light. Roughly two-thirds of the agreements made on television completely collapse in the real world. Consider the case of HyConn. The founder secured a massive 1.25 million dollar agreement on-air, only to see the entire deal evaporate once the camera stopped rolling and the investor decided to aggressively alter the terms of the agreement. Founders are legally prevented from discussing these collapsed deals or leveraging their television appearance to attract other backers because they are bound by strict non-disclosure agreements enforced by the production company. A televised handshake is a flimsy illusion of success. A startup's true test does not happen in the studio. It begins the exact moment the production crew leaves the room. title: I Spent 5 Days at Techstars Startup Week Abuja. Here's What Happened
transcription: My team won the pitch competition at Techstars Startup Week Abuja. 5 days, 1 idea, 1 MVP built from scratch. And this video is the full story. Every day, every lesson, every moment. Let's go! Techstars Startup Week is a 5-day entrepreneur-led event that brings founders, developers, investors, and creators together to learn, connect, and build their ideas. This year, it took place in Abuja, and I attended every day from start to finish, participating in sessions, workshops, panels, and networking events, while actively building with my team. Day 1 was all about ideas and community. Walking in, I immediately felt at home among like-minded innovators. We had meaningful conversations about the Nigerian startup ecosystem and the importance of building products that truly matter. By the end of the day, our group was formed, and we agreed on an idea that we would work on collectively. Day 2 was focused on knowledge. We attended sessions on AI ethics, cloud infrastructure with AWS, and a deep dive into MedGemma, Google's open-source AI model. We were also assigned a hands-on project to work on. Day 3 was all about execution. We remained fully focused on building our MVP. I completed the landing page for our product and worked closely with a senior engineer on my team to review it. That experience taught me a great deal. Day 4 was focused on depth. We explored startup leadership, financial discipline, and we had a panel with four senior tech experts who discussed AI, the Nigerian market, the japa syndrome, and the importance of giving back to community. Meanwhile, our MVP was nearly complete. Day 5 was pitch day. Before the pitch began, we had sessions on startup funding, storytelling, and robotics. After the sessions, the room went quiet, and it was time for each team to pitch their ideas. I didn't want to be the only one to describe what this week felt like. I wanted you to hear from someone who experienced it first-hand. So, at the end of the event, I interviewed Victoria to capture her perspective. Here is what she shared. Okay, I'm Victoria Ofuasia. I am a researcher, I'm a reinforcement learning researcher, also a backend developer, and I build communities.

title: Uber's Original Pitch Deck: The Slides That Raised Millions
transcription: When you walk into a venture capital pitch, you are stepping into a room defined by heavy skepticism. Every word you say and every slide you show is either building a bridge of trust with the people across the table, or giving them another excuse to say no. The reality of fundraising is that you don't actually win these meetings, you survive them. You keep the conversation alive just long enough to earn a second meeting, by systematically identifying and removing every single reason an investor might hesitate. In 2008, Garrett Camp and Travis Kalanick raised a $200,000 seed round using this presentation. That check grew into an operation valued at $140 billion, even though the deck looks like a rough draft. It runs 25 slides long, ignoring modern advice on brevity. It lacks complex financial models, and barely mentions a business plan. On paper, it should have been discarded during the brutal 3-minute skim test that most VCs use to filter their deal flow. The UberCab deck suggests that at the seed stage, the specific sequencing of trust and psychology can be more influential than the quality of the graphic design. Most founders fall into the trap of the McKinsey-style presentation. They lead with dry market sizing, abstract industry jargon, and theoretical frameworks. It is a logical approach that often feels disconnected from the actual problem being solved. Uber used a structure we call the flipped pyramid. Instead of starting with the math, they hooked the audience with raw, relatable frustration first, saving the spreadsheets for later. They avoided transit industry jargon entirely. Instead, they forced investors to recall the shared misery of trying to hail a cab in a major city. They evoked specific visceral pain points: the 45-minute wait times with zero status updates, and that helpless feeling of standing on a street corner in a downpour hoping an empty car might eventually pass by. Only after they established that emotional wound did they introduce the solution. This direct mapping, linking a technological feature like automated dispatch to a specific human frustration, makes the product feel inevitable. Notice the lack of dense text on these slides. By using simple icons as visual anchors, the deck prevents the investor from reading ahead. It forces the founder to remain the primary storyteller in the room.

title: Uber's Original Pitch Deck: The Slides That Raised Millions
transcription: Leading with emotional pain helps bypass an investor's critical defenses. By the time you get to the logic of the solution, they are already looking for a reason to believe it works. Even with a great hook, you can still lose an investor if your financial projections seem delusional. Most pitch decks rely on aggressive hockey stick growth charts that assume a perfect market with zero friction. For a veteran venture capitalist, these charts often signal that a founder is naive to the actual risks of the business. Uber's slide 20, the potential outcomes slide, was a calculated play on credibility. It offered a psychological antidote to the typical skepticism founders face. The best case scenario still promised the massive billion-dollar scale investors need to justify a seed-stage check. But the right side of the slide offered a dose of brutal honesty. It admitted that the company might fail to scale and remain a tiny, 10-car boutique service for executives in San Francisco. Acknowledging a grounded worst case indicated that the founders understood market friction, which served to build a new level of credibility with the room. Transparency regarding potential failure tends to raise an investor's floor of trust, removing the lingering hesitations that often stall a deal. This is why Uber's original deck remains mandatory study material at places like Y Combinator. It isn't a template for design, it's a template for communication. Its legendary status comes from what the founders ruthlessly excluded. They stripped away the corporate fluff and the empty buzzwords to focus entirely on the substance of the problem and the logic of the solution. The next time you update your own pitch deck, try to cut one slide instead of adding one. Force yourself to find that same level of narrative clarity. Surviving the pitch room requires you to apply this level of psychological precision to every piece of your material. That is the goal of our Capital Kit. It includes the VC-ready 16-slide pitch deck templates, and a 16-page slide-by-slide instruction guide, built on the same psychological principles used by the world's most successful founders. transcription: Uh, hackathons chhodo, competitions chhodo, challenges chhodo, every event, every class, sab ko hata do. Mere ko jo cheez mila hai na yahaan pe, yeh jo cheez hai, yeh matlab unmatched hai. Mere ko jo dost mile hai, jo hum aapas mein baatein karte hai, ek room mein bas saare log, ek floor ke saare log ek hi room mein pade hai, char-paanch room ke log bas gappe-shappe maar rahe hai, chai peene jaa rahe hai. Ek debugging sessions ho rahi hai. Har koi productive karne ki soch raha hai aur matlab disappointments aati hai hackathons mein aur yeh sab karne pe. Par jab main pehle tha, jab main Kota mein tha, main akela rehta tha aur yahaan pe mere ko motivation dete hai log. Like, ho jaayega, agle baar ho jaayega, yeh sab. Ek emotional support, knowledge ki, knowledge sharing yeh sab bahut achha hota hai matlab, yeh maine experience kara hai, main apne khud ke experience se bata raha hoon. Like, yeh saari cheezein na mere heart ko abhi aise melt kar chuki hai ki un logo ko chhod ke main jaane hi nahi wala hoon. Agar jab jaunga to main is baar to pakka royunga. Maine aaj tak kabhi kisi farewell mein, kisi dost ko ya kisi college ko, kisi school ko chhodte hue nahi roya, par is baar like, I'm definitely gonna cry. Ab aap mere se puchoge tumhe Scaler ne kya diya? Education mein? Nahi, itna nahi bol sakta hoon matlab, education diya hai, of course, but experience toh diya hai, experiences diye hai, mentors diye hai, opportunities diye hai, friends diye hai jo ek like, like family, kind of family ban chuke hai mere. Aur mere ko push diya, like, confidence toh friends ne diya, direction diya mentors ne. Matlab basically, VCs ne mere ko bahut zyada direction diya hai. Like maine Scaler ke mentor se itna zyada baat nahi kiya hai, par VCs ne mere ko bahut zyada ideation mein aur direction mein bahut kaam kiya hai. Main apna ye journey Scaler ke bina abhi imagine nahi kar sakta hoon. Ek saal ho gaya hai, and the best is yet to come. Bye!

title: 🏆 WINNER: Best Video Pitch & 4th Runner-Up Overall | PSC X Bicol Region
transcription: The heart of the Philippines, a broken system is hurting everyone. Farmers harvest with sweat and sacrifice, yet sell at prices too low to survive. Ang hirap po kasi kahit malakas ang ani ay mababa pa rin ang presyo na naibibigay sa amin. Yung ni-harvest ko ngayon may presyo pero hindi naman alam kung magkano ang pagbili niya. Presyo ng gulay is uh parang ang may gain doon is yung middleman. Mababa ang bili ng disposer sa farmer. Kasi mababa ang presyo pag hinarvest wala na, pupunta sa ano sa pamasahe wala nang matitira para sa amin. Buyers want local produce but face high cost and unreliable supply, and customers they pay more for less. This isn't just a gap, it's a broken chain that fails us all. Lalong lumalalim pa ang ugat ng problemang kinakaharap ng mga kababayan nating magsasaka lalo na nitong nakaraang buwan. Farmers face unfair pricing, limited market access and constant uncertainty. Buyers pay inflated cost and face inconsistent supply. Consumers struggle with affordability and freshness. This inefficiency hurts our economy, our health and our communities. But what if we could bridge this gap fairly, transparently and sustainably? Agrikita is a digital marketplace connecting farmers, buyers, consumers and organizations. We're not just an app, we're a movement to achieve the UN Sustainable Development Goals and transform Philippine agriculture. Agrikita empowers four key segments: smallholder farmers, local businesses, consumers, and support organizations. Farmers are verified through secure digital profiles, ensuring trust and authenticity. They can also create product listings with just a few taps, giving them direct access to reliable buyers.

तो यस, 100% देने चाहिए। चाहे सिलेक्शन हो या ना हो, इंटरव्यू तो देने चाहिए। देखो इससे क्या होता है कि अपने अंदर कॉन्फिडेंस आता है, क्वेश्चंस पता लगते हैं कि क्या-क्या पूछा जा रहा है, एनवायरनमेंट पता लगता है इंटरव्यूज का, थोड़ा हम फैमिलियर हो जाते हैं इंटरव्यू देते हुए और अपने खुद के वीक एरिया पता लगते हैं कि क्या हमने गलतियां करी हैं, क्या चीजें सुधारनी हैं। तो इंटरव्यू एक एग्जाम नहीं है कि भैया फेल हो गए तो बहुत बड़ी बात हो गई कुछ। लर्निंग है जिससे कि आप नेक्स्ट इंटरव्यू के लिए और अच्छा प्रिपेयर कर सकते हो। उसके बाद एक क्वेश्चन था कि R2R के बाद FP&A क्या होता है और क्या यह सैप का मॉड्यूल है क्या? तो FP&A सैप का मॉड्यूल नहीं है। FP&A की फुल फॉर्म है Finance Planning and Analysis और SAP एक सॉफ्टवेयर है, तो दोनों अलग-अलग चीजें हैं। FP&A प्रोसेस के अंदर काम होता है जैसे कि बजट बनाना, फोरकास्टिंग, एक्चुअल वर्सेस बजट एनालिसिस, मैनेजमेंट को इनसाइट्स देना। तो FP&A के लिए अकाउंटिंग प्लस एडवांस एक्सेल प्लस एनालिटिकल थिंकिंग स्ट्रांग होनी चाहिए। साथ ही साथ हर कंपनी की अलग-अलग रिक्वायरमेंट होती है, किसी को Power BI, SQL वगैरह यह सब भी चाहिए होते हैं। फिर एक क्वेश्चन है, आपने किस एज में काम स्टार्ट करा? तो मैंने ग्रेजुएशन जब मेरा लास्ट ईयर था, मैंने तब से ही स्टार्ट कर दिया था काम करना। सीए फर्म मैंने स्टार्टिंग में ज्वाइन करी थी और मेरा फिर दो साल डिले हो गया था मेरा ग्रेजुएशन कंप्लीट होना, तो 2020 में कंप्लीट हुआ था। तो काम मैं तब से कर ही रहा था सीए फर्म वगैरह में, तो मैंने यहां पर अपना टाइम ज्यादा वेस्ट करा। 2023 सितंबर में जाकर मैं Genpact ज्वाइन करा, मेरी पहली MNC। बट यस, ठीक है अभी जो भी है। नेक्स्ट क्वेश्चन है, फ्रेशर ग्रेजुएट्स MNC में जा सकते हैं? तो यस, बिल्कुल जा सकते हैं। कई सारे प्रोसेस हैं जैसे कि R2R, AP, AR, O2C, P2P तो फ्रेशर्स की हायरिंग चलती रहती है। LinkedIn और नौकरी पर आप अगर प्रोफाइल बनाओगे तो तो आपको कई सारे वॉक-इन्स और ओपनिंग्स दिख जाएंगे। देखो, एज़ अ फ्रेशर आपके पास अकाउंटिंग की नॉलेज होनी चाहिए अच्छी और इंटरव्यू का कॉन्फिडेंस होना चाहिए और इजीली इंटरव्यू भी क्रैक कर सकते हो। नेक्स्ट क्वेश्चन है कि एक्सेल, टैली, जीएसटी सीखने के बाद क्या सीए फर्म में एंट्री मिलेगी सेकंड ईयर स्टूडेंट को? तो बिल्कुल, अगर आपको ये चीजों की नॉलेज है, तो सीए फर्म में आपको इजीली एंट्री मिल जाएगी। देखो सीए फर्म में यार देखो इनिशियली सैलरी बहुत कम होती है। बट यस, आपको सीखने को काफी कुछ मिल जाता है, अगर आप अच्छी सीए फर्म में गए हो तो। अगर आपको अकाउंटिंग की नॉलेज है और लर्निंग एटीट्यूड है आपका, तो आपको आराम से सीए फर्म मिल जाएगी जहां पर आप काम सीख सकते हो। फिर एक क्वेश्चन था कि आजकल वीडियोस क्यों नहीं डाल रहे थे? पिछले मतलब शायद 4 महीनों से मैंने वीडियो नहीं डाली है और देखो, मैं अपने आपको खुद को मेरे को पता है कि यह सारे एक्सक्यूसेस थे, बट फिर भी बता देता हूं कि

Gym nahi ho pa rahi thi to night schedule kharab ho gaya tha, sleep schedule. Woh kharab ho gaya tha to routine bigad gaya tha aur bahut jyada patla ho gaya tha beech mein abhi thoda wapas main maintain karna chalu kar raha hun. Aur fir mera mann hi nahi kar raha tha apne aap ko matlab video banate hue matlab itna patla lag raha tha main, to halanki yeh saare excuses hain aur abhi wapas se routine sahi kar raha hun, koshish kar raha hun continuous video daalu wapas se ab. To yahi tha reason. Fir next question hai ki graduation ke alawa koi aur professional course kara hai kya? To dekho simply maine sirf B.Com kari thi jab maine MNC join kari, uske baad maine M.Com complete kari apni MNC jab maine join kar li thi uske baad. Uske baad next question hai ki CA firm se start karke MNC mein switch karein to 10 saal mein growth kya hogi? To dekho growth bilkul hogi, agar aap skill upgrade karein, hai na, apne comfort zone mein na rahein aur cheezon mein specialization lein, jaise ki jis bhi process mein aap kaam kar rahe ho uspar deep knowledge lo, hai na, team lead karne ki koshish karo, communication skills pe kaam karo, to 10 saal mein manager, SME level tak jana to aaram se possible hai. Fir next question hai ki night shift mein health kaise maintain karte ho? To dekho main yun nahi kahunga mere liye bahut easy hai. Main jo bhai khud ke liye apne liye follow karta hun woh hai fixed time hona chahiye sone ka jo ki hota nahi hai, but poori koshish yahi honi chahiye... junk food bilkul avoid karo, healthy khao, daily gym, walking, workout activities honi chahiye, hydration proper rakho, yahan sabse important hai bhai discipline, ho jata hai manage fir. Next question hai international aur US accounting ka scope kya hai India mein? To India mein international accounting ka scope kaafi sahi hai kyunki baahar ki companies outsource India mein hi karti hain kyunki yahan pe cheap labor hai, to graduates bhi easily entry le sakte hain MNCs ke through, Big 4 ke through. Fir ek question hai ki finance analyst ke kya-kya roles hain? Dekho alag-alag processes hain, alag-alag roles hote hain. AP mein invoicing ka dekhna hota hai, hai na, jo bhi humko pay karna hai. AR team receivables ka dekhti hai data, hai na, ki jo bhi paisa humko mangwana hai, jo bhi paisa hamare paas aana hai, uski invoicing dekhna aur bhi usme kai saare kaam hote hain. R2R mein reporting hoti hai, FP&A mein finance planning hoti hai, budgeting, forecasting, woh sab cheezein. Har process ka alag-alag role hota hai finance analyst ke. To guys yahi the saare questions jo mereko mile the meri YouTube community post mein, to agar kisi ka koi question miss ho gaya ho to tension mat lena, neeche comment mein daal dena next Q&A video ke liye, jo bhi questions, queries hon. title: Zero to Finance Analyst: The Complete Roadmap for Freshers & Career Switchers 💼📊
transcription: This isn't just another textbook, it's a literal step-by-step blueprint. It's designed specifically for students, freshers, and job seekers to zero in on the exact core skills that get you hired, helping you build this unshakable real-world confidence. Let's talk numbers, cuz, well, numbers don't lie. When you look at the 2024 job market, there is incredibly high demand right now for roles like MIS executive and finance associate. The starting salaries are really solid, and the career paths are crystal clear. But, and this is a big but, to unlock these roles, you've got to have the right skills. If you can master Excel pivot tables, VLOOKUP, data visualization, and real problem-solving, you immediately push yourself into those higher salary brackets. It's a total game changer. Moving right along to Section 2, Financial Modeling and MIS: The Core Skills Employers Want. So, the blueprint breaks down finance fundamentals without drowning you in corporate speak. It teaches you what's essentially the Holy Trinity of finance, how the three main financial statements talk to each other. Step one: your profit and loss net profit flows straight into your balance sheet equity. Step two: any changes in that balance sheet, they're explained by your cash flow statement. And step three: the closing cash in your cash flow has to perfectly match the cash on your balance sheet. Once you grasp this flow, you're literally speaking the language of business. But here's the best part. It doesn't just leave you with abstract concepts. You learn P&L analysis by looking at a real-world Domino's Pizza store, tracking the cost of cheese, flour, and staff wages. You build your very first Excel model by projecting revenues for a local chai shop. See what's happening? You're moving from passive reading to active execution. You're actually building the exact models companies rely on every single day. And then we get to MIS: Management Information Systems. Put simply, it's the art of getting the right data to the right people at exactly the right time so they can make smart decisions. Think about it. If you're the person who can build a dashboard tracking the KPIs that actually matter, like net profit margin, capacity utilization, or customer acquisition cost, you make yourself completely indispensable to the leadership team. Okay, onto Section 3, The Variance Secret Weapon: Finding the Why Behind the Numbers. Variance analysis, it sounds intimidating, but mathematically it's just your actual performance minus your budgeted plan. Super simple, right? But here's the catch: employers do not want human calculators. They want you to figure out the why. Why on earth did the company miss its target this month? Was volume down? Did we mess up the pricing? And, most crucially, how do we fix it?

title: Transgender Persons Amendment Bill 2026: Self-Identification Out, Medical Boards in - What Changes?
transcription: Second, and this is a part that's unusual, the bill also defines as a transgender person anyone who has been forcibly made to assume a transgender identity. Someone abducted, mutilated, castrated, subjected to hormonal procedures against their will. This is clearly aimed at a documented pattern of trafficking and coercion, particularly involving the Hijra community. But here's what falls outside the new definition: trans men, trans women, genderqueer individuals, and anyone whose identity is self-perceived rather than biologically or culturally determined. The bill's statement of objects and reasons puts it plainly. Protection under this Act is for those facing exclusion due to biological reasons, for no fault and no choice of their own. And it goes further: the definition shall not include, and it says, shall never have been so included, persons with different sexual orientations or self-perceived sexual identities. That last phrase is significant. It's not just prospective, it's retrospective. The government is not just changing the law going forward, it's saying this is what the law always meant. That raises an immediate legal question. Hundreds of people have already obtained identity certificates under the 2019 Act on the basis of self-identification. What happens to them? The bill doesn't say. And constitutional law experts are already asking whether a retrospective redefinition of this kind can survive judicial scrutiny, particularly given that the Supreme Court's NALSA judgment, which has never been overturned, explicitly recognized self-perceived gender identity as a constitutional right. Now to the procedural changes, and here, too, there's a gatekeeping concern. Under the existing law, a person applies to a District Magistrate for an identity certificate. The 2026 bill inserts a new step: a medical board, headed by a Chief Medical Officer or Deputy Chief Medical Officer, whose recommendation the District Magistrate must examine before issuing the certificate. The Magistrate can also bring in additional medical experts if they deem it necessary. Transgender rights lawyers point out that this is almost precisely the kind of medical gatekeeping the Supreme Court warned against in NALSA. The Court said gender identity is a matter of self-determination, not medical diagnosis. On the other side of the ledger, there is one procedural gain in the bill. A person issued an identity certificate will now have the explicit right to change their first name in their birth certificate and all official documents. That's a practical fix to a gap that had caused real problems, people caught in administrative limbo with mismatched documents.

title: Transgender Persons Amendment Bill 2026: Self-Identification Out, Medical Boards in - What Changes?
transcription: The third major area is penalties, and here, the government has a stronger case to make. The 2019 Act prescribed a maximum of two years in prison for offenses against transgender persons: forced labor, denial of access to public spaces, physical abuse, sexual abuse, economic abuse. Two years, across the board, regardless of the severity of the act. The 2026 amendment retains that two-year ceiling for those existing offenses, but builds an entirely new layer of serious crimes on top. If someone kidnaps an adult and causes grievous bodily harm through mutilation, castration, surgery, or hormonal procedures with the intent of forcing them to assume a transgender identity, the minimum sentence is 10 years, the maximum is life, the minimum fine is 2 lakh rupees. For the same offense against a child, the sentence is life imprisonment, mandatory, the minimum fine is 5 lakh rupees. Compelling anyone through force or deception to present as transgender and then exploiting them through begging or servitude: 5 to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment; for children, 10 to 14 years. The government's reasoning is that existing law, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Juvenile Justice Act, addresses bits and pieces of these wrongs separately. But no provision treats the full combination of abduction, bodily harm, and forced identity assumption as a single unified offense. The amendment creates that unified offense. But there is a tension that legal observers have noted. The bill creates life imprisonment for forcing someone into transgender identity. It still caps punishment at two years for physically or sexually abusing an actual transgender person. That disparity is likely to face hard questions in the Parliament. Here's where things stand. The bill has been introduced, it hasn't been passed. It will now go through the legislative process: committee scrutiny, debate, and a vote. What's already clear is that this amendment is not a minor technical fix. It touches the definitional core of the 2019 Act, removes the right the Supreme Court said was constitutionally guaranteed, adds a layer of medical authority over identity recognition, and creates a new criminal framework with punishments ranging from six months to life. The government says it is targeting benefits more precisely and building stronger protections against coercion. Its critics say it is using the language of protection to narrow who deserves it. Seven years ago, the NALSA judgment told the Indian state that every person has the right to define themselves. The question this bill puts before Parliament is whether that right still stands.

title: How Argentina Became The Most Hated World Cup Team
transcription: Argentina's World Cup, let's get into it. Argentina entered the 2026 World Cup as the defending World Cup champions, the reigning Copa América champions, and the number-one ranked team in the world. On paper, they looked unstoppable, and with this expected to be Messi's last World Cup run, millions of football fans from around the world were hoping for one last magical run. But as the tournament went on and Argentina kept winning, the controversy only continued to grow. The first major controversy of Argentina's tournament involved their supporters after their match in the round of 32. Cabo Verde was by far the surprise story of the tournament. They shocked the football world by holding Spain to a scoreless draw and earning their very first World Cup point. Their 40-year-old goalkeeper had about 50,000 Instagram followers before the Spain match, and after his incredible performance, he gained millions of followers overnight, currently sitting at nearly 30 million. So on July 3rd, when it came time for them to play Argentina in the round of 32, IShowSpeed, who is a Ronaldo fan, naturally was cheering for Cabo Verde and made that pretty clear. "Let's go! Cabo!" title: UEFA Finally Issues BOYCOTT Threat to FIFA!
transcription: Football could be on the brink of its biggest civil war in decades. UEFA has just issued one of the strongest statements we've ever seen against FIFA. And it's not just criticism, it's a warning. A warning that Europe's 55 Football Associations are prepared to boycott FIFA competitions if FIFA pushes ahead with its controversial new plan. If that sounds unbelievable, that's because it is. For years, FIFA and UEFA have disagreed over football calendars, tournament expansion and governance. But this time, the stakes are much higher. So what exactly has happened? It all started when FIFA unveiled a proposal to create a new commercial company called FIFA Forward Enterprise. The idea is for this company to manage the commercial side of the World Cup and other FIFA competitions. FIFA would still remain the majority owner, but it also wants to sell a minority stake to private investors. The goal? Raise billions of dollars to invest in football development around the world. On paper, FIFA says it's simply creating a smarter financial model, one that can generate more money for member associations and help grow the game globally. But UEFA sees it very differently. In an extraordinary statement released on behalf of all, all 55 European football associations, UEFA unanimously rejected the proposal. Its message couldn't have been clearer. The World Cup is not for sale. According to UEFA, football's greatest competition should never become an investment product for private shareholders. The organization says the World Cup belongs to players, national teams and supporters across generations, not investors looking for financial returns. And UEFA wasn't just angry about the proposal itself. It also criticized the way FIFA handled the entire process. According to the statement, such an important decision was developed behind closed doors and brought close to approval without meaningful consultation with the people responsible for governing the sport. That criticism goes beyond business. It's about trust. UEFA believes decisions that shape football's future should involve open discussions with confederations, leagues, clubs and national associations. Instead, it believes FIFA acted alone.

title: Supreme Court weakens Voting Rights Act by voiding Louisiana's congressional map
transcription: Hello, everyone. I'm Major Garrett in New York. Welcome to The Takeout. When it comes to voting representation in modern post-Jim Crow America, there are many ways to measure. Access at the voting booth is one. Numerical representation in Congress is another. The landmark 1965 Voting Rights Act addressed both head-on. Section 2 of that Act, which the Supreme Court eroded today, intentionally attempted to increase minority representation nationwide in Congress by allowing for the drawing of so-called majority-minority districts, even if the drawing of those district lines were unusual in geographic ways so as to knit together minority voting blocks. Now, in 1980, the Supreme Court restrained the interpretation of that Act by saying Section 2 only prohibited district lines that prevented minority representation on purpose. Congress stepped in in 1982 to say no, no, Section 2 barred district lines that had discriminatory effect. It didn't need to be on purpose. If the effect was discriminatory, it could be challenged in court. And that interpretation held for decades. Until today, when a 6-3 majority on the High Court ruled that the benefit of drawing district lines with the intent of increasing minority representation had to be weighed against other considerations, specifically Equal Protection Clause protections in the Constitution against discrimination suffered, in this particular litigation, by white voters, who sued to block creation of a second congressional district in Louisiana, which, as you can see here, stretches from Shreveport in the northwestern part of the state to Baton Rouge in the southeastern part of the state. With more on this decision, the dissent to it, and the possible political implications, we turn to our Chief Legal Correspondent, Jan Crawford. Jan, walk us through what happened. Well, I mean, Major, I think you've really kind of nailed all of it. I mean, it's going to make it much harder for people to justify these so-called majority-minority districts that, as you said, were designed to increase representation in Congress. The way people had done it was they would argue that we needed this district, you know, under Section 2, that key provision, the crown jewel of the Voting Rights Act. And so, therefore, you could consider race when you were drawing it, and do those kind of long lines like you just showed.
