title: Dr. Carina de Oliveira Mann (Innate Immunity)
transcription: Hi, I'm Karina de Oliveira Mann, and I'm an assistant professor at the Technical University of Munich in Germany, and I'm also a co-organizer of the next Keystone Symposia on Innate Immunity happening in January. Despite major advances in the field, we still lack fundamental understanding of how the innate immune system is activated at the molecular level, and in addition, translating this biology into the clinics has proven particularly difficult. So modulating innate immune responses is still an ongoing challenge, and this meeting is basically meeting that gap, bridging basic biology in the field with the newest developments in drug discovery and potential clinical applications. And in addition, if we think about the cross-talk between the innate and adaptive immunity, it's particularly exciting to see this joint meeting with the T-cell meeting, where we're going to see, live at the meeting, the cross-talk between innate immunity and T-cell biology, and how innate immunity can modulate T-cell responses in an intended or unintended way.

Sufficient funding for conducting clinical trials on immune diseases.

Measuring the speed of molecular activation during an infection.

By offering research grants specifically for T-cell engineering.

options: The chance to witness a debate on the classification of white blood cells.

title: How Mohammad Irfan Went From Street Hawker To India's Most Viral Protest Voice
transcription: सिर्फ पेट रोटी खा लेना ही जीवन नहीं है। शहरी सलम में जीवन नरक है। मैं कहता हूँ लोकतंत्र में ना अहंकार नहीं संवाद होना चाहिए और संवाद के दरवाज़े दोनों तरफ़ से खुले होने चाहिए। संविधान की शपथ में ना गरिमा शब्द का, व्यक्ति की गरिमा, राष्ट्र की एकता और अखंडता को सुनिश्चित, तो व्यक्ति की गरिमा, गरिमा, गरिमा नहीं गिरनी चाहिए सर। जय श्री कृष्णा सर, मैं इरफ़ान सर और आज मुझे आपसे बहुत सारी बातें करनी है सर। चार ट्रिलियन की अर्थव्यवस्था में ना पढ़े-लिखों का ही जीवन संवरा है? A voice that rose about the slogans at Jantar Mantar is now being heard in the country's political corridors. Mohammad Irfan, the hawker with little formal education whose speeches went viral during the student protest, met Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Monday. Rahul Gandhi said Irfan's understanding of the constitution and his desire to learn reflected the strength of India's youth. Hours after the meet, Irfan spoke exclusively to India Today's sister platform, The Lallantop, with a message that cuts across party lines. मैं आज राहुल गांधी से मिला तो मैंने उनसे यही कहा कि अगर सर आप जो हम आपसे अपनी मांगे रख रहे हैं, आप विपक्ष के बड़े नेता हैं और आज नहीं तो कल सत्ता में आएंगे, अगर आपने हमारी बातों के वादाखिलाफी की तो हम अपनी असहमति आपके खिलाफ भी रखेंगे। For Irfan, accountability does not stop with one government or one political party. और हम न्यूट्रल हैं, हम इस देश का भला चाहते हैं। He also spoke about the struggles of migrant workers. 2024 का एनसीआरबी का डाटा कहता है कि 1 लाख 70 हजार 746 मौतें हुई जिसमें 31% दिहाड़ी मजदूर थे और वजह एक थी कि घर में तंगी और मानसिक संतुलन डिस्टर्ब होना, आर्थिक तंगी थी। तो हम कैसे इग्नोर कर सकते हैं उस वर्ग को जो इस देश की बड़ी आबादी है और खून-पसीना लगा रही है इस देश के निर्माण में? हम कैसे इग्नोर कर सकते हैं उसे? From the streets of Jantar Mantar to the national spotlight, his story is not about political power. It's about the power of a citizen's voice to be heard. If you liked the video, do like, comment, share, and subscribe.

title: Leading Monaco’s Vision | Monaco Day 2026 - Davos WEF
transcription: Mr. Pierre-André Chiappori, Minister of Economy and Finance, ladies and gentlemen, Presidents and CEOs, ladies and gentlemen, dear guests, I am very pleased to be with you today in Davos to open the Monaco House. This is my first time here, in a place that is not only a global meeting point, but above all, a space for dialogue and serious work among women and men who make decisions, often in uncertain environments. Being in Davos means taking a step back, listening, confronting different perspectives, and recognizing that behind strategies, models, and trends, there are always human decisions taken by people with responsibilities, constraints, and convictions. Monaco is here today to contribute to a shared reflection on how the future is being shaped by asking the right questions and remaining attentive to the world and to the people within it. My role fits precisely into this approach. It is about positioning Monaco, but also about coordination, coordination between public and private actors, so that decisions are never disconnected from human, economic, and social realities. I firmly believe that public decisions influence private ones and that private initiatives, in return, feed public reflection and governance.

title: Report: U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro applied pressure to indict Democratic lawmakers over video
transcription: There's brand new reporting in the New York Times this afternoon about the turmoil inside the Department of Justice when it came to that failed attempt to indict six Democratic lawmakers who released a video reminding the men and women of the military that they do not have to obey any illegal orders. According to that reporting in the New York Times, in mid-January, the inquiry into the lawmakers had no sense of urgency, and that when lawyers for the lawmakers were contacted by federal prosecutors, they were told that they were not told of any law that had been broken, according to six people familiar with the matter. Times goes on to report that everything changed two weeks later when, quote, "Janine Pirro abruptly instructed her team to seek an indictment of the lawmakers." Her prosecutors then faced a decision that many in the Department under Trump have confronted: comply or resist. They chose the first. That attempt to indict, of course, failed last week, but as the New York Times notes, it stood, quote, "as an example of the chaos that has roiled the Department as it has grappled with the President's increasingly erratic demands, even in the face of little evidence." Want to bring in New York Times investigative reporter Mike Schmidt, whose byline is on that reporting we read from. Also joining us, former acting assistant Attorney General for national security at the Justice Department, Mary McCord. Um, Mike, first take us through what you and your colleagues are reporting today. Well, basically, what we're trying to show is that when this investigation started, these prosecutors reached out to the defense lawyers for the six lawmakers and said, "Look, uh, we're in the early stages, we're not even sure if we're in the first inning yet, we're not even sure what law we're investigating this under, not even sure if it's an investigation. Uh, you know, could could one of the lawmakers come in and talk? You know, would one of the lawyers want to come in and talk to sort of get this thing going?" That is as informal a way of starting an investigation as possible, especially after the President of the United States has called for them, you know, essentially called for them to be investigated for this and raised the possibility that they could be punished, you know, up you know, up to um you know, Seditious conspiracy. Seditious conspiracy and execution. So, it had a very, very informal feeling to it. And within two weeks, they there was a prosecutors before grand jury trying to indict them.

title: Iran has a new plan to kill Trump, Israel warns: Sources
transcription: A new Iranian plot to assassinate Trump. According to the Wall Street Journal, with new reporting this hour, Israel shared new intelligence with the US, which suggests Iran was plotting a new plan to kill President Trump. Now, Israel is not commenting thus far, but President Trump did bring this topic up multiple times yesterday. It was clearly on his mind. He talked about how his life could be at risk and mentioned specifically that he is Iran's top target. They want to take out the US leader, me. I'm on every list. I saw a thing this morning, I'm on every single one of their lists. I'm number one on the kill list for Iran. They're lovely people, I'm number one. I may be gone, too, because I'm their number-one target. It's out all over the place. I'm their number because they're scum. Were you aware of any credible threat by Iran against your life? Well, I have a threat all the time. I'm number one on their list, before you. But if I go, you go, right? Now, you see him there speaking on a plane here in that last clip. That was on board Air Force One, the old Air Force One, right, that he's gotten rid of because he has the new $400 million presidential jet that he was given by a foreign country, Middle Eastern country, Qatar. तो डेफिनेटली सीएस में कोई एंट्री बैरियर नहीं है, आप साइंस से हो, आर्ट्स से हो, कॉमर्स से हो, हर कोई सीएस कर सकता है। सेकंड, एलिजिबिलिटी जो है सीएस करने की वह होती है ट्वेल्थ, ठीक है? तो यहां पर दो तरीके से आप सीएस में आ सकते हो, नंबर वन इज की आप अपना ट्वेल्थ क्लियर करके सीएस में आ जाओ, सेकंड इस की आप ग्रेजुएशन करके सीएस में आओ। तो ट्वेल्थ की बात करें तो ट्वेल्थ के बाद आपको तीन स्टेजेस करने पड़ेंगे, पहला होता है सीएसइइटी जो कि आपका एंट्रेंस है, उसके बाद सीएस एग्जीक्यूटिव एंड देन सीएस प्रोफेशनल। अगर आप ग्रेजुएशन के बाद आना चाहते हो तो एंट्रेंस आपका एक्जेंप्ट हो जाता है, आप सीधा आपको डायरेक्ट एंट्री मिलती है एग्जीक्यूटिव में एंड देन प्रोफेशनल। मेरी पर्सनल रिकमेंडेशन यही होगी कि आप ट्वेल्थ के बाद से ही सीएस स्टार्ट कर लो अगर आप एकदम श्योर शॉर्ट क्लियर हो बिकॉज जब तक आप ग्रेजुएट होगे तब तक तो आप सीएस बन भी जाओगे, तीन ही साल का कोर्स होता है, दैट्स व्हाई। तो अभी हम बात करते हैं इसके पहले स्टेज की जो की है सीएसइइटी - सीएस एग्जीक्यूटिव एंट्रेंस एग्जाम टेस्ट। नाउ गाइस इसमें काफी ज्यादा चेंज आया है, अगर आप 2026 के पहले सीएस करने की सोच रहे थे ना, तो सीएसइइटी आप घर बैठे-बैठे एमसीक्यू में अपने कंप्यूटर में पास हो जाते, बट अभी आपको एक्चुअल में सेंटर्स में जाना पड़ेगा और आंसर लिखना पड़ेगा। एक्चुअल में तीन घंटे पेपर आपको देने हैं, चार सब्जेक्ट होता है एंड सेंटर में जाकर आपको पेपर देना होगा, बस एक ही पेपर है सीएसइइटी का जो कि अभी एमसीक्यू बेस्ड होगा वह है लॉ का पेपर, बाकी तीनों सब्जेक्ट्स आपको लिखने हैं तो यह सबसे बड़ा चेंज आपके एंट्रेंस लेवल पर ही आया है। जो सीएसइइटी है वो साल में तीन बार होने वाला है फेब में, जून में एंड अक्टूबर में।

title: How to think like a lawyer | Zero-L from Harvard Law School
transcription: But while this kind of content is important and useful, the main thing we're trying to teach you is a set of approaches, techniques, a disposition to dealing with real problems that will enable you to go out in the world and deal with any legal problem. Some of these may be problems related to courses you never took. Indeed, some may relate to legal issues that never existed when you went to law school. A lot of my work is on cutting-edge technologies, so I encounter these all the time, topics like in vitro fertilization and posthumous conception. So a key goal of law school is to make you into a legal Swiss Army knife, to have the tool for any problem you encounter, or at the very least to know where to find that tool. To be clear, that doesn't mean you're to become a hired gun. Instead, you're called upon and valued for your ability to exercise independent judgment on questions of law and on policy. Some of you will want to become trial lawyers. Others will want to go into public service. Others will want to become deal lawyers or go into business through law. Others still will want to work for advocacy organizations. Many of you will disagree about many legal questions, but law school will help you learn to disagree and to argue in ways that are more likely to convince others that you are right. Regardless, we want to enable you to give sound legal advice to your client, or perhaps, if you're engaging in cause lawyering, to figure out a legal strategy and find a client who might bring that case. As we will develop in a later segment, while there are many legal skills to learn, from oral advocacy to negotiation, from contract drafting to organizational design, there are five primary skills that every lawyer will need to bring to the table. First, digest the facts. Second, spot the relevant issue or issues. Third, determine the governing law. Fourth, apply the governing law to the facts to generate arguments and probabilistic assessments. And finally, work with the client to understand how the legal analysis fits in with the client's overall interests and goals. And this whole course is aimed at getting you started on mastering these skills.

title: FP1 Highlights | 2026 Belgian Grand Prix
transcription: and we can work on the car, nearly half an hour sooner than if it was left at the top of the Kemmel Straight. Current Drivers' Championship leader Kimi Antonelli felt aggrieved when he came across a slower moving Carlos Sainz exiting Turn 15. Sainz, what an idiot. I wonder if that's a man that's not completely happy at the moment. When you're not having the easiest of runs, sometimes little things can can frustrate you a lot more. Mercedes teammate George Russell is struggling for grip during his early excursions. Still got four-wheel sliding, tires not biting. Copy that. The Briton trails his Italian colleague by 25 points in the drivers' standings, the gap somewhat narrowed after the teenager failed to score in the last Grand Prix, having won the Sprint. Liam Lawson put a wheel in the gravel at Turn 14 and later went drifting through Turn 18. The Racing Bulls have been vying for best of the rest, with their consistent points in recent races. On that form, they're likely to jump ahead of Alpine, who sit a point above them in the constructors' race, due largely to Pierre Gasly's performances since day one, scoring in every round bar Austria this year. In this session, Arvid Lindblad was P9, Lawson P11, with Alpine's Franco Colapinto and Gasly P15 and P17 respectively. A decent outing for Gabriel Bortoleto, the Brazilian finished in the points last time out, and in this session was a creditable P10 at the flag. Teammate Nico Hulkenberg finished two places further back, he locked up at Turn 8, one of several drivers who took a few goes around to get their eye in. Sainz locked up both front wheels coming into the Turn 1 hairpin, both Williams drivers seemed downbeat during their Thursday media duties, the Spaniard admitting that the FW46 was not delivering, and calling this season a character-building year. Not often we get a sunny day on a Grand Prix weekend at Spa. Fernando Alonso took advantage, sitting out the session on the pit wall, as Jak Crawford was given another go in the Aston Martin. The two-time champion probably isn't missing much, no technical changes for the Silverstone-based team this time around, the much-anticipated upgrades are scheduled for Budapest next week. So it finished: Verstappen top from Hamilton, Leclerc, Hadjar, and Piastri, followed by Antonelli, Norris, Russell, Lindblad, and Bortoleto. P11 for Lawson, then came Hulkenberg, Bearman, Albon, Colapinto, Ocon, Gasly, Bottas, Perez, Sainz, Stroll, and Crawford.

What matters most is that we act fast because every day companies are collecting more data and building more capabilities.

transcription: ...ने खान सर ने खरीदने की कोशिश की, जिसमें दो टीचर, राकेश यादव सर और अभिनय सर ने खुलेआम कहा कि विवाद के दौरान कॉल आया और पीआर तंत्र फैलाने की कोशिश की। विवेक बिंद्रा जी ने दो चार पांच टीचर्स को बुलाया और वहां पे ये प्लान किया कि खान साहब को सपोर्ट करना है। सारे यूट्यूबर और टीचर आ रहे हैं और हमें वहां खान सर की इमेज को बचाने के लिए प्रयास करना है। ये ससुरे गए कहां सब तब? जितने साले किसी काम के नहीं है, उनको लगता है बिहार उनके बाप का है। कह रहा है कि तुमको बिहार से जाएंगे, तुम्हारे बाप का है बिहार? तू निकाल के दिखा देगा हमको। क्या पढ़ाई किए थे सर आप? फिर दुबारा काहे पूछ रहे हैं, पीजी किए हुए हैं। सोनू शर्मा और ओझा वाली क्लिप देखी है आपने? सोनू शर्मा का कौन फोन देखता है? कंप्लीट बेल मिल चुकी है। कैसा लगता है आजाद हो के? इतना कानूनी लड़ाई लड़ लिए हैं इस 40 दिन में ना, कि अब हम लॉ का बैच लाने जा रहे हैं। हैं? आपदा में अवसर खोज दिए। अगर मान लो कोई समझदार इंसान आप में और रोशन आनंद सर के बीच में मध्यस्थता कराना चाहे? उनका कहना है कि मध्यस्थता से हमको क्या है, हमको पब्लिसिटी मिल रही है। आप करना चाहोगे? बिहार में कई सारे यूट्यूबर्स ने आपके खिलाफ मोर्चा खोल दिया था। एक तो पत्रकार है जिसको वहां के लोगों ने नाम दिया है, सनब दुगला। उ कह रहा है कि हम ही वो पत्रकार हैं जो खान सर का घर पता करके आए, गोत्र पता करके आए, जात पता करके आए, धरम पता करके आए। अरे ससुरा तू नहीं, टीचर खोज रहा है कि जीजा खोज रहा है रे? ये सब कौन पता करता है? आप जानते थे कि इस केस में जब आप पहली बार बोलेंगे तो पूरा देश सुनेगा। आपने हमारा मंच क्यों चुना? आप क्रॉस क्वेश्चन पूछते हैं, चाहे सामने वाला कुछ भी हो। समय जब मुंह फेर लेता है तो कुत्ता भी शेर को घेर लेता है। जिन्हें लगता है खान सर खत्म हो गए? मैं समंदर हूं, मेरी उतरती लहरों को देखकर मेरे किनारे पर अपना घर मत बना लेना। मैं जब लौट के आऊंगा तो एक-एक इंच जमीन का हिसाब लूंगा।

The CCA offers unrivaled access, insight, and information for members and partners and stakeholders into the realities of operating community pharmacies, the experience our members have, and the opportunities for the future.

We need service design that's really patient-centered, that connects the different parts of the system together, and that supports pharmacists to really thrive in their new roles as prescribers.

title: Quiet Desperation
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: You ever notice how some people look completely fine on the outside? But something about them feels tired? Not physically tired. Soul tired. They wake up, go to work, answer texts, laugh at the right moments, pay bills, scroll their phone at night, and repeat the same cycle over and over again like a machine pretending to be a human being. And nobody notices because nothing is technically wrong. That's the terrifying part. Quiet desperation doesn't always look like a breakdown. Sometimes it looks like functioning perfectly while slowly dying inside. Henry David Thoreau once wrote that most men live lives of quiet desperation, and the older I get, the more disturbing that sentence becomes. Because desperation is easy to recognize when it's loud. When someone's screaming, spiraling, crashing out, everybody sees it. But quiet desperation, that hides behind routines, behind careers, behind relationships, behind smiling photos, and "I'm good" responses. It's the kind of suffering that learns how to behave, and I think a lot of people fall into it without even realizing it. It starts with tiny compromises, tiny betrayals of yourself. "I'll chase my dream later." "I'll settle for this job for now." "I'll stay in this relationship because at least it's familiar." And at first, it feels temporary, but temporary has a way of becoming permanent when fear gets comfortable. Years pass. Your responsibilities grow roots around you, and one day you wake up realizing you built an entire life around survival, but forgot to include yourself in it. That's why some people feel empty even after getting everything they thought they wanted. Because achievement without alignment creates exhaustion. You can win the game and still hate waking up in the morning. You can make money and still feel spiritually bankrupt. You can be surrounded by people and still feel emotionally isolated. Quiet desperation is the gap between the life you're living and the life your soul knows you were meant for. And social media makes it worse. Now everybody performs happiness like it's a full-time job. People don't even ask, "Am I fulfilled anymore?" They ask, "Do I look fulfilled?"

title: How to Create a Journal System in Joplin | Quick Guide 2026
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to create a journal system in Joplin. Joplin is a fantastic open source note-taking app that offers a lot of flexibility and customization for keeping track of your thoughts, goals, and reflections. Whether you're an avid journaler or looking to start this beneficial habit, Joplin can help you organize your entries in a way that makes them easy to manage and review. Let's start by setting up your journal notebook. To begin, you'll need to open Joplin desktop. Once you have the application up and running, take a look at the left sidebar. You'll find a button labeled "New notebook." Go ahead and click on that. A prompt will appear asking you to enter a name for your new notebook. In this case, you should name it simply "Journal." Naming your notebook distinctly helps maintain clarity and keeps everything organized as your digital journal grows. Now that you have your journal notebook created, you can start thinking about how to organize your entries effectively. A well-structured journal system can provide insights and make reference easier over time. One effective way to structure your journal notebook is to create subnotebooks for different aspects of your journaling practice. To do this, look at the file above your journal notebook. There, you will see an option to create a "new subnotebook." For starters, you might want to create a subnotebook titled "Daily entries." This section will be where you jot down your thoughts and reflections every day. It's a space for freeform writing, capturing everything from daily events to personal reflections. Next, consider adding a subnotebook for "Weekly reviews." This section is great for reflecting on the week that just passed. It offers a valuable opportunity to see how your thoughts and experiences have evolved over the past seven days, and help set intentions for the following week. Finally, there's the "Monthly reviews" subnotebook. Monthly reviews are vital for looking at the bigger picture. They allow you to track longer-term goals and assess progress over time. Reflecting monthly provides a macro perspective of your life, habits, and achievements. When you envision this structure in Joplin, it might look like a tree, with "Journal" as the trunk, "Daily entries," "Weekly reviews," and "Monthly reviews" act as the branches extending from it, providing a clear pathway for your thoughts to spread. By organizing your journal in this manner, you create a harmonious and systematic approach that enhances your journaling practice. This customized structure caters to different aspects of life reflection, and makes it simpler for you to navigate through your thoughts and feelings. Once everything is set up, you can start using Joplin to capture your life's details, review your growth, and make journaling an enriching experience.

title: Dax – “My Silence Was Crying for Help” (2026 Lyrics Video)
category: Mental Health Vlogs & Personal Video Diaries
transcription: Tomorrow it'll hurt a little less. My silence was crying for help. Every quiet moment said my name. I smiled so nobody would worry, while carrying invisible pain. My silence was crying for help, but nobody knew what to hear. Sometimes the strongest disguise is looking like you're doing fine. Maybe healing doesn't begin with the perfect words. Maybe it begins the moment you stop pretending you don't need anyone. If you've been hiding your pain because you're scared people will see you differently, listen carefully: you don't have to earn the right to be hurt. You don't have to reach your breaking point before your pain matters. Strength isn't measured by how much you can carry alone. Sometimes the strongest decision is letting somebody walk beside you. You deserve compassion on your hardest days. You deserve hope, even when you can't feel it. And if today all you can do is take one more breath, take it. Because healing doesn't always arrive like a sunrise. Sometimes it begins with one honest sentence: I need help. My silence was crying for help, now my voice is learning to heal. The pain may still be with me, but it no longer decides what's real. My silence was crying for help, and today I finally know the first step toward freedom is letting the truth be spoken. The world heard my words, but the people who truly love me finally heard my silence.

transcription: I've really enjoyed Carson's talk about OCD because I think a lot of what he described is is something that I see a lot in clinical practice and some of the challenges of working with people with OCD is is yeah it's very familiar and really helpful. Lots of new ideas, definitely. I feel like every talk has been kind of very thought-provoking and I've left each of them thinking, "Oh God, I really want to go and read more about that and learn more about it." So there's been lots that I thought I could integrate into my practice. The fact that, um, instead of having lots of speakers, there is just two per session, which means you can go into so much more depth in the topic that is covered and not just little tasters. I particularly enjoyed Silva Neves' yesterday, um, talking about sexuality in a really accepting way and really informative, and encouraging people to, uh, be open about what they don't know and really has made me think about my practice, how I ask questions about sexuality. We've had a lot of really diverse group of speakers. Um, I've enjoyed the balance between research and applied practice. Um, I've enjoyed the opportunity to meet other people, and that's why I come in person because I just think that being able to have those conversations, being able to go to a talk and then afterwards, discuss it with colleagues, that's just amazing. I've loved coming to these conferences and just networking, you always meet new people, always take some cards away with me. It's just brilliant, really. I think it's just a a really good opportunity to meet other sort of EMDR practitioners and and exchange ideas, hear about research, I think there's been some really good research that has been done. आपने एक्सपीरियंस शेयर करा, सबको अपने बुक के बारे में बताया, अपनी कंपनी के बारे में बताया, अपनी लाइफ स्टोरी के बारे में बताया। सर, कैसी फीलिंग आ रही है? मैम भी आई हैं आपके साथ? जी। मैम आपके साथ खड़ी हैं? नहीं-नहीं, मेरी फ्रेंड हैं वो आई हैं। अच्छा-अच्छा। देखिए, अच्छा लग रहा है। बहुत अच्छा लग रहा है क्योंकि जब एक मिडिल क्लास का बच्चा जब मेहनत करता है ना और साथ देता है लोग, इस तरह से लोग आते हैं। किसी-किसी की हिम्मत नहीं होती है। बहुत सारे बच्चे जानते हैं कि सर, हमें आपकी किताब पढ़नी है। हमें आपकी यूट्यूब पे वीडियो देखनी है। वो सब चीजें सुनकर बहुत अच्छा लग रहा है। और ऊपर वाले का बहुत आशीर्वाद है। अभी बहुत सारे बुक्स आने वाले हैं। और मैं थैंक यू बोलना चाहूँगा, Seven Network का थैंक यू बोलना चाहूँगा, S S G Iconic Awards का कि हम जैसे जो क्रिएटर होते हैं, जो बच्चे कुछ करना चाहते हैं ना, तो मिडिल क्लास से निकल के आते हैं, उनको सपोर्ट करते हैं, मोटीवेट करते हैं, आगे बढ़ाते हैं और इस तरह से इतने अच्छे लोगों के बीच में लाकर खड़ा कर देते हैं। थैंक यू अगेन। बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद। सर, आप तो लाइव एग्जांपल हैं कि मेहनत सच में रंग लाती है एक न एक दिन। हम लोग बोलते हैं कि मेहनत करते रहते हैं, मेहनत करते रहते हैं, गोल्स अचीव नहीं होते। नहीं, होते हैं गोल्स अचीव। एक बार जोरदार तालियां बजा दीजिए। थैंक यू सर। थैंक यू फॉर योर टाइम। आई विश कि आपकी ज्यादा से ज्यादा कॉपियां और सेल हो बुक की। थैंक यू। ओके। एनी वन ऑफ़ यू वांट्स टू कम? title: Transgender Persons Amendment Bill 2026: Self-Identification Out, Medical Boards in - What Changes?
transcription: A bill introduced in parliament on Friday could fundamentally change who the Indian state recognizes as transgender and who it doesn't. The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill 2026 was tabled in the Lok Sabha by Social Justice Minister Virendra Kumar. And while the government says it's about bringing clarity to a vague law, critics say it could quietly dismantle rights that took years of struggle to win. I'm Vrinda Tulsian and you're watching The Print. To understand what's changed and why it matters, we need to go back to where this all began. It's 2014. The Supreme Court delivers what becomes known as the NALSA judgment, a landmark ruling that recognizes transgender persons as a third gender, directs the government to provide reservations and welfare measures, and crucially holds that a person has the right to self-identify their gender, no surgery required, no medical certificate, no government approval. The court said the constitution guarantees it. That judgment set the stage for legislation, but getting a law passed took five more years, and they weren't smooth years. A 2016 version of the bill was met with protest from the transgender communities across the country. The core objection: it required a District Magistrate to certify whether someone was transgender. Activists said that handed a bureaucrat the power to decide something the Supreme Court had said was a fundamental right. After sustained pressure, the bill was revised. The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act was finally passed in 2019. It was imperfect, many in the community still had reservations, but it represented a floor, a legal baseline. It defined transgender persons broadly: anyone whose gender doesn't match the gender assigned at birth, including trans men, trans women, genderqueer individuals, those with intersex variations, and those with socio-cultural identities like hijra, kinnar, aravani, and jogta, and it explicitly said, under Section 4, Part 2, that a recognized transgender person has the right to a self-perceived gender identity. That section is now proposed to be deleted. So what exactly does the 2026 amendment propose? There are three major changes worth unpacking: the definition, the procedures, and the penalties. Under the new bill, the term transgender person would be restricted to two categories: first, people with specific socio-cultural identities—hijra, kinnar, aravani, jogta, eunuch—or people born with medically recognized intersex variations. Variations in chromosomes, genitalia, hormones, gonadal development, biological markers, in other words.

title: Leading Change Webinar Clip
transcription:
you don't have control over. But what you do have control over is yourself and how are you planning your own actions to mitigate some of the risk that's involved in the area that you don't have control over? And then obviously, picking up the things that you can control helps you to gain some ownership over how that change progresses in your organization.

So, a quick thing that gives me some clarity when I'm talking about change is thinking about my own change readiness. So, when you think about this, think about it in terms of the people engaged in change. Are they ready for this change? What do they need to be ready for this change? Process. Is your process, you know, collection in this particular area, is that ready for change? Is it a movable process? Is it easy to move or is it not? If you have a website, for example, and the process is completely contingent on how that website works, is it a flexible process or is it not? Because that may give you um an issue if you're trying to make a a pretty immediate change. Resources. Do you have the resources to put behind this change? And some changes do require monetary or resource changes. It could also be volunteerism or something like time and capacity. And then finally, communication. Are your communication systems set up to be transparent, communicate clearly, and provide the information that's actionable for folks to actually take it and move with it?

Another area that is important as a leader is thinking about your sphere of control. And we talked a little bit about this when I mentioned the imposed change, but essentially, you have a sphere of control that directs what direct actions you can take, those that you can shape the outcomes, and those that are outside of your control. So, we'll take a second and move into some more reflection about how you see your sphere of control shaped by an issue that you are working on right now.

title: Introduction to the Optim.AI™ test
transcription: Opti-My can be captured, the workflow of Opti-My can be captured in a four step process. So, basically we first start off with sample collection where we isolate live cancer cells from different tumor types such as biopsy resections, ascites or pleural fluids and blood or bone marrow aspirates. So, we then perform an ex vivo sensitivity test on the isolated cancer cells by treating them with 12 drugs in a mix of combinations based on proprietary design. So, we then measure the cell viability and use it for Opti-My analysis which then generates a final test report that ranks the top single, two, three and four drug combinations including any relevant clinical trial references. So, the main parameter that we are using is normalized cell viability or NCV score. This NCV score quantifies cell killing from zero to one after measuring the amount of viable cells left after drug treatment. So, NCV score of zero indicates that all cancer cells are killed, highlighting increased sensitivity to the treatment and vice versa if the NCV score is closer to one. Basically, I think as long as we can get a sample of the tumor tissue, we can test all cancer types. Yes. So, I think in our experience in our lab is more than 20 plus cancer types including cancer of unknown primary and some even very rare cancers we have also processed them before. Right now, for our Opti-My test we do short-term culture of the tumor cells. So, for hematological cancers we seed and within 24 hours we will do drug treatment. So, there is no real opportunity for the cells to have to grow or whether or not for them to die off too much. So, for solid cancers, it's a bit longer.
